Tribute.fullContent:
[[File:BS04-X13.jpg|thumb|320x320px]] '''Tribute ''' ({{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|召|しょう}}, ''Tenshō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS04]], possessed by certain Spirits of different colors. Cards with this effect have the following text: * {{Tribute|Cost X or more → [Zone]}}
After paying for the summoning cost, you must send all core from one of your Cost [X] or more Spirits to the [Zone]. The effect is essentially a sacrificial summon, and unlike most keywords in the game, which aims to assist the cards, Tribute aims to impose a summon condition to cards. Such summoning condition cannot be bypassed, except by certain effects like that of [[The MasterDragonRider Dark-Crimson]]. It mostly serves as a restriction to bring out powerful Spirits. From [[BS12]] onwards, Tribute that targets families instead of costs appeared. In Heroes Saga, a new variant, {{tk|Burst Tribute}}, was introduced with [[The SuperHero Lord-Dragon-Saviour]]. After that, the keyword vanished. There can be multiple reasons including how Burst as a free summon mechanic with condition has outshone the double restriction of Tribute (card cost + tribute cost). In Advent era, a lot of cards with Tribute are being remade into cards with {{tk|Advent}}, a new mechanic with a similar structure as Tribute but skipping the normal card cost by paying the cost with one Soul Core. In True-Rebirth era, Tribute combos used back in older generations are remade into the A sides and B sides of a Rebirth card, like [[The SevenShogun Beelzebeat X]] and [[The SevenShogun Asmodios X]]. == Official Q&A == ''Click [[Tribute/Q&A|here]].'' == Trivia == * Due to Tribute being used as a restrictive effect, the keyword was often possessed by Spirit cards with two symbols, which were deemed as powerful during the time of their release. * Even though the keyword has not been used ever since [[BS18]] and has become irrelevant ever since, as the official has the habit of remaking old cards with renewed effects while referencing their old effects, there are still effects referencing Tribute as far as 11 years after the last card with Tribute. == Cards That Have Tribute Effects == * [[:Category:Tribute|List of cards with Tribute]] * [[:Category:Tribute support|List of cards supporting Tribute]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Charge.fullContent:
[[File:BS21-X01.jpg|thumb]]
'''Charge''' (強化, ''Kyōka'') is a keyword which premiered in [[SD10]]. It's not restricted to a particular color. [[Rush]] acts as the counterpart of this effect. 

''The effect of charge is different for each color:''

* '''Red:''' Increase the limit of your "BP destruction effects" by +1000.

* '''Purple:''' Your "Core Removal" effects send +1 core to the Reserve.

* '''Green:''' Increase the number of bodies to be exhausted by your “opponent-targeting exhaustion effects“ by +1.

* '''White:''' Increase the number of bodies to be refreshed by your “Spirit-refreshing effects” by +1.

* '''Yellow:''' Your “BP- effect” decreases 1000 further.

* '''Blue:''' Your "opposing-deck-discarding effects" discard +1 card.

== General rules on Charge ==
* Pursuant to the updates of Rule Manual ver5.0, Charge is restricted to non-Ultimate effects. After the Ultimate era, the text also specifies "non-Ultimate effects".
* Charge can affect Grandwalker Nexuses' effects.
* One Spirit can have multiple Charge effects.
* When a Brave direct braves onto an Ultimate, its (When Summoned) effect can still be affected by Charge, as it's treated as a Brave effect.

== Specific rules regarding Charge of each color ==

=== Red ===
* Charge can only affect effects that specify a certain BP limit, such as "Destroy an opposing BP 5000 or less Spirit". It can't affect effects such as "Destroy the opposing highest BP Spirit".

=== Purple ===
* While not specified in the text, Charge only affects core removal effects that send cores from the Field to the Reserve, and doesn't affect sending cores from the Life to the Reserve.
* Charge doesn't affect effects that say "send cores from opposing Spirits until one core is left on each of them", and such.
* When an effect changes the locations of cores sent, such as by [[The EvilCapricornusDeity Stein-Bolg X]] (which sends the cores to Trash instead), Charge doesn't affect the core removal effects, as the cores aren't sent to the Reserve.

=== Green ===
* Charge also affects effects that heavy exhaust opposing cards.

=== White ===
* Charge doesn't affect effects that say "refresh '''''this''''' Spirit", and such.

=== Yellow ===
* If the Charge effect only activates after a BP decrease effect with a timing (e.g. "during this turn, "during this battle") activates, Charge doesn't affect that effect. However, under the same situation, Charge can affect BP decrease effects that don't specify a timing, such as the BP decrease effect of [[Small Phynx]].
* Charge can't affect effects such as "treat the Spirit as BP 1000", as they're not BP decrease effects.

=== Blue ===
* Charge doesn't affect effects that banish cards, as "discard" and "banish" are different.

Rush.fullContent:
[[File:BS19-X03.png|thumb]]
'''Rush''' (連鎖, ''rasshu'') is a keyword which premiered in [[SD11]]. It isn't restricted to any colors. [[Charge]] is its keyword counterpart. 

Rush encourages mixing colors, as it requires keeping a different color symbol on your Field to activate, designated on the card. Following the timing of the effect above Rush, as long as you have the conditions fulfilled, the Rush effect activates after. The actual effect of Rush varies from card to card.

Starting from [[BS24]], symbol conditions also start to include two or more symbols, and the effect also includes non-colored symbols, such as the Ultimate symbol.

The format for '''Rush '''is as follows:

* [Rush(Condition: '''[1 or more symbol]''')] (While you have '''[1 or more symbol]''', the effect below remains active.) '''[1 or more symbol]''': '''[effect]'''.
Since the introduction of Rush, the keyword has also inspired various derivative keywords: [[Six Heaven Rush]], [[Diva Rush]], and [[Six Pentan Rush]]. It is worth noting that none of these derivative keywords are treated as Rush by rule.

== Rules ==
* Even if the effect above the Rush effect can't activate, the Rush condition can activate if possible.
* The Rush effect doesn't activate at the same time as the effect above it, but simultaneously after it.
* If one effect has two Rush effects, the turn player chooses the activation order.
* When a Magic card with Rush is used, the symbol condition is checked at the moment the card is used. So the Rush effect can activate even when the symbol is gone at the moment of its activation.
* [[Dispersion]] can't affect the Rush effects on Magic cards.

Seal.fullContent:
[[File:Unknown copy.png|thumb|320x320px]] '''Seal''' ({{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD33]], acting as the main mechanic of the God-King era. Although it is not limited to any color, it occurs only on [[God-King]] Spirits. The keyword can activate at different timings depending on the card, and the action involved is always simply sending the Soul Core from the player's Spirit or the Reserve to the Life area. Seal is the first effect in the game which sends the Soul Core to the Life area. While the Soul Core is in the Life area, the player is considered to be {{Seal|During Seal}}, and can activate any effect that is required to be in that state. There are also a lot of other keywords that derives from Seal, which are featured below this page. == Official Q&A == ''Click [[Seal/Q&A|here]].'' == Other "Seal"-named Keywords == === High Speed Seal === '''High Speed Seal''' ({{ruby|神|しん}}{{ruby|速|そく}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Shinsoku fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD35]], possessed exclusively by [[The RabbitTwelveGodKing Mistral-Bit]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Flash -''' {{Seal|High Speed Seal}}
This card in Hand can be summoned by paying the cost with cores in the Reserve. In this case, cores to be put on this Spirit must also be from the Reserve. When you've done so, you can send the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from any of your Spirits to your Life. As the name suggests, the keyword is a combination of [[High Speed]] and Seal. Giving the Spirit an option to be summoned during the Attack Step adds a flexibility in when to send the Soul Core to Life. The ability to jump out at an unexpected timing is also fitting for Mistral-Bit, which is a rabbit. ------ === Constellation Seal === '''Constellation Seal'''({{ruby|星|せい}}{{ruby|座|ざ}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Seiza fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS38]], possessed a Nexus card of each color. Constellation Seal always activates upon deployment, needing the Soul Core to be on a Spirit of the "[[Galaxian]]" or "[[Astral Soul]]" family to be able to send to the Life area. The purpose of this variant of Seal is to ease the use of the "Galaxian" and "Astral Soul" family cards, which during that time were upgraded to include the use of {{Seal|Seal}} and {{Seal|During Seal}} effects, allowing the players to build decks without the need to include the "God-King" family cards, which were often very high cost and did not pair well with the play style of the "Galaxian" cards. For details, please refer to the [[Constellation Seal]] page. ------ === Burst Seal === '''Burst Seal''' (バースト{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Bāsuto fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS38]], possessed exclusively by [[The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{Burst|seal|After your Life is reduced}}
If your Life is at three or less, summon this Spirit card without paying the cost. Then, you can send the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]](Soul Core) from any of your Spirits to your Life. As the name suggests, the keyword is a combination of [[Burst]] and Seal, allowing the player to put the Soul Core back to the Life area, effectively nullifying the Life reduction and keeping the player in During Seal state without disturbance. It also means the card with Burst Seal is simultaneously treated as a card with the Burst keyword, and a card with the Seal keyword. Hence, the card with Burst Seal is subjected to effects which target Burst or Seal. For more information, please check out the [[Burst]] page. ------ === Super Seal === '''Super Seal''' ({{ruby|超|ちょう}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Chō fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS39]], possessed exclusively by [[The Super-TwelveGodKing Execeed Formula]]. Besides the usual "sending Soul Core to Life", Super Seal would also put the activating Spirit at the highest level during the turn, allowing it to possibly reach an unprecedented amount of BP and use abilities reserved for a higher level without needing to place much cores on that Spirit. ------ === Twinkle Seal === '''Twinkle Seal''' ({{ruby|煌|こう}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Kō fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS40]], possessed exclusively by a cycle of Spirits based on the twelve months on the calendar. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{Seal|Twinkle Seal}} (Your Attack Step)'''
When stacking a card onto this Spirit via {{tk|Advent}}, instead of sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, you can send it to your Life. Unlike any other "Seal"-named effects seen before, Twinkle Seal acts as a replacement effect, allowing the player to send the Soul Core to the Life area instead of the Trash when activating {{tk|Advent}}. This keyword was an attempt to incorporate the then-new mechanic, {{tk|Advent}}, with the cards of the God-King era. (Whether it was effective or not was another topic.) ------ === Pyroxene Seal === '''Pyroxene Seal''' ({{ruby|輝石|きせき}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Kiseki fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[Promo]] cards, possessed only by two Spirits, [[Execeed-Bereft]] and [[Gale-Phoenix-Bereft]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV3] {{Seal|Pyroxene Seal}} (When Attacks)'''
By sending [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from this Spirit to your Life, during this battle, treat this Spirit as Cost 6. Besides sending the Soul Core to the Life area, the keyword also treats the activating Spirit at a higher cost, allowing it to be an easier target for [[Advent]] while summoning the Spirit at a lower cost. ------ === Mystery Seal === '''Mystery Seal''' ({{ruby|謎|なぞ}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Nazo fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD47]], possessed exclusively by [[Medjeowl]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2] {{Seal|Mystery Seal}} (When Summoned)'''
You can exchange one of your Life cores for [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] on your Reserve. Unlike any of the previous "Seal"-named effects, Mystery Seal does not add the Soul Core to the Life area, but rather swap a core from the Life area with the Soul Core, which means the player would not be losing a core by sealing. ------ === Sky Seal === '''Sky Seal''' ({{ruby|天|てん}}{{ruby|空|くう}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Tenkū fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS47]], possessed exclusively by [[Horus' Sky Temple]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV2] {{Seal|Sky Seal}} (Your Turn)'''
When your "Sky"-named Spirit/Ultimate is summoned, you can send the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Reserve to your Life. This effect can only be used once per turn. Another Nexus that has the ability to seal, Sky Seal was introduced during a time when the Green God-King deck was reintroduced to the game, just like the purpose of Constellation Seal, Sky Seal was used to ease the deck space, allowing the player to choose not to put too many high cost "God-King" family cards just for the sake of sealing. As the new variant of Green God-King deck was also bound to the "[[The "Sky" cards|Sky]]"-named cards, Sky Seal is also designed to support this archetype specifically. ------ === Moonlight Seal === '''Moonlight Seal''' ({{ruby|月|げっ}}{{ruby|光|こう}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''Gekkō fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS72]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The MoonlightGodKing Arte-Mistral-Bit]] and [[The SheepTwelveGodKing Glorious-Sheep X]]. The effect is written as follows: * {{Seal|Moonlight Seal}} '''(Timing)'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) If you control any "Contractor Artemis", you can send the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from this Spirit/your Trash to your Life. Moonlight Seal is an alternative method of {{Seal|Seal}}, with the difference being that Moonlight Seal requires the presence of "[[The MoonlightContractor Artemis|Contractor Artemis]]", and also the first "Seal"-named keyword that can send the Soul Core to the Life from the Trash, making the keyword more fitting to be used in an environment where [[Manifest]] is more prominent. ------ === Seal Flag Contract Advent === '''Seal Flag Contract Advent''' ({{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}{{ruby|F|フラッグ}}{{ruby|契|けい}}{{ruby|約|やく}}{{ruby|煌|こう}}{{ruby|臨|りん}}; ''fuuin-furagu-keiyaku kourin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], possessed by part of the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remakes of the Twelve God-Kings. The general form of the effect writes: '''Flash -''' {{SF Advent|[Condition]|(Timing)}}
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By sending your [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Life, stack this from the Hand onto your target Spirit/Nexus. It is both a {{Seal|Seal}} effect and a {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}} effect. Generally speaking, it actually works like {{tk|Twinkle Seal}}, but this time it is the card that advents on top which owns such keyword. For details, please refer to the relevant section on the [[Seal Flag Contract Advent|Advent]] page. ------ === Seal Manifest === '''Seal Manifest''' ({{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}{{ruby|顕|けん}}{{ruby|現|げん}}; ''fuuin-kengen'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], possessed by part of the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remakes of the Twelve God-Kings. It is the combination of {{Seal|Seal}} and {{tk|Mani}}, and counted as a variant of both effects. The general form of the effect writes: '''Flash -''' {{Mani|Seal|[Condition|(Timing)}}
By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from the Field/Reserve to the Life, pay one cost from the target to summon this card from the Hand. For details, please refer to the [[Seal Manifest]] page. ------ === Imaginate Seal === '''Imaginate Seal''' ({{ruby|異|い}}{{ruby|奏|そう}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''isou fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The RatTwelveGodKing Mouchuu X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The RatTwelveGodKing Mouchuu]]. The effect is written as follows: * '''[LV1-2-3] {{Seal|Imaginate Seal}} (When Summoned)'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) You can send the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Field/Reserve to your Life. When you've done so, you can put a core from the Void to your Trash. The name comes from the archetype that [[The RatTwelveGodKing Mouchuu X]] supports, the "Imaginate (異奏)" deck that revolves around [[Imagine Brave]], which was what Mouchuu designed to work with back in its days as well. Effect-wise, the first part is very similar to the normal {{Seal|Seal}} on summon effect, but with the option of sending from anywhere on the Field instead of just the owner of the effect. The second part is the biggest difference, which allows the player to gain a core in Trash to compensate for the loss of one core (as the Soul Core is sent to the Life and can't be used unless that Life is reduced). This is very important for not letting the deck run out of the precious early resources (especially when "Imaginate" is a Yellow deck that is short of cores), and maximize the benefit of Mouchuu being the lowest cost card with {{Seal|Seal}}. It is also to note that the effect is a (Once per Turn: Same Name) effect unlike the ordinary {{Seal|Seal}} effects, as it comes with core boost. ------ === Sound Speed Seal === '''Sound Speed Seal''' ({{ruby|音|おん}}{{ruby|速|そく}}{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}}, ''onsoku fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS77]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The RabbitTwelveGodKing Mistral-Bit X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The RabbitTwelveGodKing Mistral-Bit]]. The effect is written as follows: * '''Flash -''' {{Seal|Sound Speed Seal}}
You can summon this card from the Hand by paying the summon cost from your Reserve, or paying it by sending cores from your Red/Green Grandwalker Nexuses to the Void. When you've done so, you can send the [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Reserve/Field to your Life. It is both a tribute to {{Seal|High Speed Seal}} that is originally possessed by [[The RabbitTwelveGodKing Mistral-Bit]], and a mix of {{Seal|Seal}}, the designated keyword for the God-Kings, and {{tk|Sound Speed}}, the designated keyword for [[Grandwalker Saraswati]]'s Spirits. Since Mistral-Bit X was made to fit in the deck of [[The MelodyContractor Saraswati|Contractor Saraswati]], the design has incorporated the concept of Sound Speed, which is essentially an upgrade version of {{tk|High Speed}}. It allows the summon cost of the card to be paid via cores from Grandwalker Nexuses instead of just the Reserve, and the core to be put onto the Spirit also does not need to come from the Reserve. This makes the overall effect a more powerful version of {{Seal|High Speed Seal}} as a result. Being the more powerful version of {{Seal|High Speed Seal}}, {{Seal|Sound Speed Seal}} inherits all the merit of the former, which allows the player to summon the card in Flash Timing for extra attacker/blocker while regaining a life. Since the effect is not once per turn, and the "sending [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] to life" part is not a prerequisite of the effect, one can summon all three copies of Mistral-Bit X in Flash during the same turn via {{Seal|Sound Speed Seal}}. Another thing to bear in mind is, while being a Flash effect, {{Seal|Sound Speed Seal}} could be used during the Main Step like other flash effects without timing restrictions. It is to note that, however, while {{Seal|Sound Speed Seal}} is a type of {{Seal|Seal}}, it is ''not'' a type of {{tk|Sound Speed}}. == Gallery == Rarubit.png|An example of High Speed Seal BS38-RV027.jpg|An example of Constellation Seal The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison.jpg|An example of Burst Seal Super exe.png|An example of Super Seal BS40-CP01.jpg|An example of Twinkle Seal BSSJ18-02.jpg|An example of Pyroxene Seal SD47-002.png|An example of Mystery Seal Horus' Sky Temple.png|An example of Sky Seal BS72-AX03.png|An example of Moonlight Seal BS76-X03.png|An example of Seal Flag Contract Advent BS76-X12.png|An example of Seal Manifest BS76-X10.png|An example of Imaginate Seal BS77-X06.png|An example of Sound Speed Seal == Also See == * [[:Category:Seal|List of cards with Seal]] * [[:Category:High Speed Seal|List of cards with High Speed Seal]] * [[:Category:Constellation Seal|List of cards with Constellation Seal]] * [[:Category:Burst Seal|List of cards with Burst Seal]] * [[:Category:Super Seal|List of cards with Super Seal]] * [[:Category:Twinkle Seal|List of cards with Twinkle Seal]] * [[:Category:Pyroxene Seal|List of cards with Pyroxene Seal]] * [[:Category:Mystery Seal|List of cards with Mystery Seal]] * [[:Category:Sky Seal|List of cards with Sky Seal]] * [[:Category:Moonlight Seal|List of cards with Moonlight Seal]] * [[:Category:Seal Flag Contract Advent|List of cards with Seal Flag Contract Advent]] * [[:Category:Seal Manifest|List of cards with Seal Manifest]] * [[:Category:Imaginate Seal|List of cards with Imaginate Seal]] * [[:Category:Sound Speed Seal|List of cards with Sound Speed Seal]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Accel.fullContent:
[[File:RU NING IN THE NINE TIES.png|thumb|319x319px]] '''Accel''' (アクセル, ''Akuseru'') is a keyword which debuted in [[BS37]] and is present on all colors. The default text on Accel cards is the following: * '''[Step Timing]''' {{Accel|Cost X (Reductions)}}
[Effect].After this effect resolves, put this card face-up onto the Removed Zone. After errata, starting from Block 11, the "face-up (オープンして)" text is removed from the common text, and it is implied that the card is placed face-up unless otherwise specified. The common text hence becomes: * '''[Step Timing]''' {{Accel|Cost X (Reductions)}}
[Effect].After this effect resolves, put this card onto the Removed Zone. The text on each card varies, but the common points are that they work like [[Magic]], with either Main or Flash effects, which can be used from the Hand. After the effect resolves, however, the card is placed face-up onto the '''Removed Zone''' (Removed From Game Zone). Hence, unlike Magic which enters Trash once used, like any other cards in Removed Zone, an Accel card may be summoned normally in Main Step from the Removed Zone, effectively allowing a single card to have two different uses. Like [[Burst]], it grows to become one of the core mechanics of the game. While '''Accel''' started out to be an ability primarily owned by Spirits, it slowly spread to other card types, including [[Brave]] and [[Ultimate]], over the years. Like [[Burst]] and [[Mirage]], an important thing to note about Accel is that it must be, and could only be used from the Hand unless otherwise specified on the card. Hence, once they are used, and placed on the Removed Zone, unless there are effects that directly use/activate them from the Removed Zone, you can't activate the Accel of the cards there. ==Official Q&A== Q1. What is [[Accel]]? A1. It is an effect where you can use cards at the specified timings, like (Flash) and (Main). After their effects activate, the used cards are revealed and kept in the [[Removed From Game Zone]] instead of being sent to the trash. Q2. Is Accel from a Spirit card a Spirit effect? A2. Yes, that is correct. They can be used even when magic cannot be. Q3. Does "revealed" mean the opponent can see the cards too? A3. Yes, please let your opponent see the cards as well. Q4. The cost of Accel has reduction, so can the symbols on your field be used to reduce the cost? A4. Yes, it can be reduced. Q5. Can spirit cards in the removed from game zone be summoned on your main step by paying the cost? A5. Yes, they can. Q6. Can the Accel effects of spirit cards in your removed from game zone be used? A6. No, it does not count as the hand, so they can't be used. Q7. Are cards in your removed from game zone affected by hand-discarding effects? A7. No, it does not count as the hand, so they can't be discarded. Q8. Can effects changing the cost of spirit cards in your hand also change the cost of Accel effects in your hand? A8. No, the cost of Accel cannot be changed. == Cards That Have Accel Effects == [[:Category:Accel|List of cards with Accel]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Advent.fullContent:
[[File:Type0.jpg|thumb|321x321px]] '''Advent''' (煌臨, ''Kōrin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS39]]. It then became the main mechanic and namesake of the next saga, being possessed by every color. On its introduction, the text was as follows: * '''Flash -''' '''Advent:''' [Conditions] (Either Attack Step) By sending [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]](Soul Core) to your Trash, this card in your Hand can be stacked onto your <[Conditions]> Spirit in the same position. But as of [[SD37]]/[[SD38]], the text was changed to: * '''Flash - Advent:''' [Conditions] (Either Attack Step) By sending your Soul Core to the Trash, stack this from your Hand onto your target Spirit. Advent can be activated in many different timings, the "flash" condition of the effect can only be "main", and the steps the cards can advent are either main step or attack step. There are more additional effects to allow the cards to advent outside of the usual conditions. Advent is an evolution of [[Tribute]], to the point cards which had Tribute were revived with Advent instead, and allows the player to change their Spirits for ones with a higher cost on a faster pace. It is important to note that the action of stacking is not the same as summoning, hence when adventing a Spirit/Ultimate, it cannot activate (When Summoned) effects, nor can it trigger any other effects that activate on summon. Because it is not a summon, players also cannot put additional cores to the adventing Spirit/Ultimate. Unless effects allow, Spirits/Ultimates cannot advent onto Braves in Spirit condition, [[Bunshin (Family)|Bunshin]] Spirits, or Nexuses treated as Spirits. [[The EvilGodKing Deathpeers-Zorc]] is the only exception where the Advent keyword it uses is simply "Advent", but the text of its Advent is different to the rest in the game (banishing the Soul Core instead of sending it the Trash). == Pre-advent Cards == As Advent is directly stacking a card onto another, it will cause a situation where there are face-up cards under a Spirit/Ultimate. Those cards are called pre-advent cards, and this state is called {{tk|During Advent}}. There are effects that can only activate when a Spirit/Ultimate is {{tk|During Advent}}. Even through effects, currently it is impossible to put face-up cards under Spirits/Ultimates without the Advent keyword. When the Spirit/Ultimate leaves the field, all pre-advent cards under it follow where it goes. For example, if the Spirit/Ultimate is returned to the deck, so are its pre-advent cards; if the Spirit/Ultimate is destroyed and sent to the trash, so are the pre-advent cards going to the trash. In the case of returning to the hand, pre-advent cards do not count towards the number of cards increased in the hand. There can be effects which add Spirits from the field into a pile of pre-advent cards. When this happens, the added Spirits do NOT enter [[Comprehensive Rules|standby state]], and "when Spirits leave field" effects do NOT activate. Same rules apply when other card types are being added as pre-advent cards. == See Also: == *[[:Category:Advent|List of cards with Advent]] == Grand Advent == [[File:Leonz.png|thumb]] '''Grand Advent ''' (神煌臨, ''Shinkōrin''), introduced in [[BS46]], is a subcategory of [[Advent]], which allows the player to advent by moving a core from a [[Grandwalker]] Nexus to a spirit as the cost instead of sending the Soul Core to trash. The text reads as follows: *'''Flash - ''Grand Advent: [Condition]''''' (Timing) By either sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, or putting a core from your Grandwalker Nexus to a Spirit you control, stack this from your Hand onto your target Spirit. Only [[Avatar|Avatars]] of supreme deities (and their respective [[Diva]] versions) have this effect, limiting it to a few Spirits and decks. In [[CB12]], [[Kamen Rider Kuuga Ultimate Form［2］]] was also released with Grand Advent, the only collaboration card to have that. Later in the future, [[［Diva Academy］Rei-Ohba]] was also released with Grand Advent, as a representation of Rei-Ohba being the most popular Diva among players' choices. Grand Advent allows the player to Advent a strong Spirit while still keeping the Soul Core stored, allowing for multiple Advents and still have Soul Core-exclusive effects available and it also doubles as a discreet [[Unleash]] effect. ===See Also:=== *[[:Category:Grand Advent|List of cards with Grand Advent]] == Dan Kuroto Deus Advent == [[File:Max genm.png|thumb]] '''Dan Kuroto Deus Advent''' (檀黎斗神煌臨, ''Dan Kuroto Shin kōrin''), introduced in [[CB08]], is a subcategory of [[Grand Advent]]. This effect also allows the player to advent by paying the alternate cost of moving a core from a [[Grandwalker]] Nexus to the Spirit instead of sending the Soul Core to trash. However, Dan Kuroto Deus Advent differs in that it specifies that the core must be moved from a "Dan Kuroto"-named Nexus. Currently, the only card to have this effect is [[Kamen Rider Genm God Maximum Gamer Level Billion]]. == Ultra Advent == [[File:BS51-10thX04.png|thumb]] '''Ultra Advent''' (超煌臨; ''Choukourin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS51]], exclusive to [[The SuperCentaurusDeity Grand-Sagitto-Nova]]. The effect is worded as follows: *'''Flash - ''Ultra Advent: During Advent''''' (Either Attack Step) By putting [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Reserve/Trash to a "[[Superstar]]"/"[[Galaxian]]" family Spirit you control, stack this from your hand onto your target Spirit. While Advent consists of sending Soul Core from anywhere to the Trash, Ultra Advent brings it from outside the Field onto a Galaxian/Superstar family Spirit. This way, while it cannot be used consecutively with itself, Ultra Advent can be used after regular Advent. == Ultra Thunder Advent == [[File:BS75-AX02.png|thumb]] '''Ultra Thunder Advent''' (超雷煌臨; ''Chourai-kourin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS75]], currently exclusive to [[The SuperThunderousDeity Grand-Sagitto-Nova]], the AX remake of [[The SuperCentaurusDeity Grand-Sagitto-Nova]]. The effect name is also modified from {{tk|Ultra Advent}} owned by the original Grand-Sagitto-Nova, adding in the element of "thunder" as represented by Indra. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Flash - ''' {{UTadvent|[[Thunderive]] & C8 or more|(Either Attack Step)}}
By sending the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Reserve/Trash to a "[[Thunderive]]" family Spirit, stack this from your Hand onto your target Spirit. The effect is almost identical to the normal {{tk|Ultra Advent}} owned by Grand-Sagitto-Nova, but with the condition changed to "[[Thunderive]]" family Spirits, the core family in [[The HeavenlyThunderContractor Indra|Indra]]'s deck, where [[The SuperThunderousDeity Grand-Sagitto-Nova]] belongs. == Contract Advent == [[File:BS60-X01.png|thumb]] '''Contract Advent''' (契約煌臨 ; ''keiyaku kourin''), introduced in [[BS60]], is a subcategory of Advent which has the exact same effect text as the original advent wording. The biggest difference is, however, that you can also advent cards with Contract Advent onto your Contract cards that are in Soul State via the effect written on the Contract cards. When adventing on cards in Soul State, you can put as many cores as you want from the Field/Reserve to the now advented spirit, instead of "keeping the same amount of cores" like in normal advent, as there are no cores on cards in Soul State to begin with. Such effect is worded as follows on the Contract cards: * While this card is in Soul State, you can Contract Advent onto it. When you do, you can put any number of cores from your Field/Reserve to the advent card. Apart from that, everything for Contract Advent is similar to that of the original Advent, with timing and conditions to follow. === See Also: === * [[List of Contract Cards]] * [[:Category:Contract Advent|List of cards with Contract Advent]] == Flag Contract Advent == [[File:BS76-X07.png|thumb]] '''Flag Contract Advent''' (F契約煌臨 ; ''furagu-keiyaku kourin''), introduced in [[BS76]], is a subcategory of Advent/Contract Advent which has almost the exact same effect text as the original Advent/Contract Advent wording. The biggest difference is, however, that you can also advent on '''Nexus cards''' when the condition is fulfilled. The "F" in "F契約煌臨" stands for "Flag" as stipulated by the furigana on the cards. And similar to Contract Advent, you can Flag Contract Advent onto your Contract Nexus cards (Flag Nexuses) that are in Soul State via the effect written on the Contract Nexus cards. When adventing on cards in Soul State, you can put as many cores as you want from the Field/Reserve to the now advented spirit, instead of "keeping the same amount of cores" like in normal advent, as there are no cores on cards in Soul State to begin with. The general form of the effect writes: '''Flash -''' {{Flag Contract Advent|[Condition]|(Timing)}}
By sending your [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, stack this from the Hand onto your target Spirit/Nexus. Different from normal advents or contract advents that mainly work on Spirits or Contract Spirits, however, it is worthy to note that if you are planning to {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}} a Spirit card onto a Flag Nexus that is ''not'' in Soul State, you need to ensure that there is one or more core placed on top of the Flag Nexus, as Flag Nexus doesn't require cores for their LV1 cost unlike Spirits/Contract Spirits in Spirit form. Another thing to note is, as the name tells, a holder of {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}} is also treated as a holder of {{tk|Advent}} and {{tk|Contract Advent}}. === See Also: === * [[Flag|Flag Nexuses]] * [[:Category:Flag Contract Advent|List of cards with Flag Contract Advent]] == Ultra Contract Advent == [[File:BS63-CP05.png|thumb]] '''Ultra Contract Advent''' (超契約煌臨; ''Chou keiyaku kourin''), introduced in [[BS63]], is a subcategory of Advent and Contract Advent. It's a combination of Contract Advent and Ultra Advent, possessed by the six new forms of Wanderer Dan's Contract Spirits. The biggest difference between Ultra Advent and Ultra Contract Advent is that you can also advent cards with Ultra Contract Advent onto your Contract cards that are in Soul State or Spirits with the designated Contract Spirits as their pre-advent cards. When adventing onto the Contract cards in Soul State directly, you can put as many cores as you want from the Field/Reserve to the now advented Spirit, instead of "keeping the same amount of cores" like in normal advent, as there are no cores on cards in Soul State to begin with. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Ultra Contract Advent: XXXX''' (Timing)
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By stacking this card from your Hand onto its target, including those that are in Soul State/pre-advent condition, send your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to this Spirit. While normal Contract Advent consisted of sending Soul Core from anywhere to the Trash, Ultra Contract Advent brings it from anywhere onto your targeted Contract Spirit/Spirit with the Contract Spirit as pre-advent card, including Trash. This enables player to Ultra Contract Advent after performing regular Advent/Contract Advent in the same turn, and save the Soul Core for another advent. Since it is a very powerful effect, all Ultra Contract Advents currently are limited to (Once per Turn: Same Name), and are name-limited. A key point to note is also that since Ultra Contract Advent is "by sending the Soul Core to the designated Spirit", you '''can't''' Ultra Contract Advent onto a Spirit with Soul Core on it, or carry out Ultra Contract Advent via "advent treating Soul Core as sent" effects like that of [[Cloudy Blow]]'s. === See Also: === * [[:Category:Ultra Contract Advent|List of cards with Ultra Contract Advent]] == Reverse Contract Advent == [[File:BS64-X01.png|thumb]] '''Reverse Contract Advent''' (裏契約煌臨; ''ura keiyaku kourin''), introduced in [[BS64]], is a subcategory of Advent and Contract Advent, possessed by the six partners of Contractor Kai. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Reverse Contract Advent: XXXX''' (Timing)
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] or the opposing [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, or by -1 opposing counter, stacking this card from your Hand onto its target, including those that are in Soul State/pre-advent condition. Different to any of the previous Advent variants, Reverse Contract Advent is the first variant which can use the opposing Soul Core directly, and is also the first variant which can manipulate counters as the cost. This provides a counter option for the player when facing against decks of the same structure (e.g. when both decks are Advent-based), giving themselves an advantage over the opponent. It also means the player can save the Soul Core for another chance of Advent. Reducing the opposing counter can also potentially disable some of the opposing effects which require a certain number of counters as conditions. Since Reverse Contract Advent is a very powerful effect, all its texts currently are limited to (Once per Turn: Same Name), and are name-limited. From the name to design, Reverse Contract Advent makes itself a parallel to Ultra Contract Advent owned by Dan's side Contract Spirits. Instead of returning Soul Core to use Advent again, it takes the opposing Soul Core and allows the player to advent again by not using their Soul Core at first. In a way, it also eats up the opposing Soul Core returned via their Ultra Contract Advent, if they didn't immediately use the Soul Core afterwards, making it an interesting counter against decks with Ultra Contract Advents. Unlike Ultra Contract Advents, however, since cards with Reverse Contract Advent can be normally advented by "sending Soul Core to the Trash", you '''can''' advent the cards with Reverse Contract Advent via "advent treating Soul Core as sent" effects like that of [[The OracleTwentyOnePillars II The High Priestess]]'s. === See Also: === * [[:Category:Reverse Contract Advent|List of cards with Reverse Contract Advent]] == Final Contract Advent == [[File:BS64-X06.png|thumb]] '''Final Contract Advent''' (最終契約煌臨; ''saishuu keiyaku kourin''), introduced in [[BS64]], is a subcategory of Advent and Contract Advent, currently possessed exclusively by [[The Ruler of FourDemonLords God-Javad]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Final Contract Advent: XXX''' (Timing)
By banishing the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Field/Reserve, stack this from the Hand onto your target Ultimate. While seems underwhelming on first sight, the harsh condition of Final Contract Advent can be understood with the rest of God-Javad's effects, which can be devastating when all conditions are met. This is also to make sure that God-Javad would not be abused at multiple copies, which had happened before with the domination of [[The Hellsoil FourDemonLord Magnamiser]]. Final Contract Advent serves as a reference to [[The EvilGodKing Deathpeers-Zorc]], which, before Final Contract Advent was introduced, had been the only card in the game which also banishes the Soul Core to Advent. Deathpeers-Zorc was also the first card with Advent revealed in the anime, as well as the first Ultimate with the ability to advent. == Tenma Advent == [[File:BSC48-XX01.png|thumb]] '''Tenma Advent''' (天魔煌臨, ''Tenma kourin'') is a sub-keyword of Advent introduced in [[BSC48]], possessed exclusively by [[The HeavenlyDemonKing God-Sechs X -Type The End-]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Flash -''' {{Advent2|Tenma Advent|[[Heavenly Demon King]] & Originally Cost 8/9/10|(Either Attack Step)}}
By either sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, or putting a core from your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Grandwalker Nexus to a Spirit you control, stack this from your Hand onto your target Spirit. As seen, Tenma Advent is simply another variant of Grand Advent, with the only difference being that Tenma Advent is limiting the Grandwalker Nexus target to only be one in the "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family. == Seal Flag Contract Advent == [[File:BS76-X03.png|thumb]] '''Seal Flag Contract Advent''' (封印F契約煌臨 ; ''fuuin-furagu-keiyaku kourin''), introduced in [[BS76]], is a subcategory of Advent/Contract Advent/Seal which merges those keywords together. The general form of the effect writes: '''Flash -''' {{SF Advent|[Condition]|(Timing)}}
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By sending your [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Life, stack this from the Hand onto your target Spirit/Nexus. It is in essence a form of {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}}, which allows you to Contract Advent onto Spirits/Nexuses that fit the condition from the Hand. Since it is a type of {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}}, you can advent onto the designated Flag Nexuses in Soul State as stipulated on the card text of the Flag Nexuses themselves. Cards with such effect are also treated as cards having {{tk|Advent}}, {{tk|Contract Advent}}, and {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}}. What makes it different from normal {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}}, however, is that the [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] isn't sent to the Trash, '''but your Life'''. The fact that it sends the [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] to your Life makes it essentially a {{Seal|Seal}} effect, as also reflected in the name. Hence, the effect is also treated as {{Seal|Seal}}, and any effect that are triggered by {{Seal|Seal}} would be triggered by the effect. (e.g. Burst with conditions: {{Burst|con|After you or the opponent {{Seal|Seal}} }}) It is worthy to note that since it isn't mentioned where the [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] is coming from, the [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] can '''come from your Trash''', like the reverse of normal Advents, and similar to {{tk|Ultra Contract Advent}}. The effect is hence locked to (Once per Turn: Same Name). Another thing to note is, since the effect doesn't specify sending [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash for {{tk|Advent}}, any effects that let you "Advent treating Soul Core as being sent to the Trash" do not apply to {{tk|Seal Flag Contract Advent}}. The effect is primarily owned by the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remakes of God-Kings introduced in Contract Saga: Proof, like [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou X]], as to merge the {{Seal|Seal}} elements of the [[God-King]]s and the Flag Contract Advent elements of the newly introduced [[Bannerace]] decks. === See Also: === * [[Flag|Flag Nexuses]] * [[:Category:Seal Flag Contract Advent|List of cards with Seal Flag Contract Advent]] ==See also== *[[Reload]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

'''Pyroxene Esoterica''' (輝石奥義, ''Kiseki Ougi'') is a pair of keywords related to the [[Birthgem Deity|Birthgem Deities]], a series of campaign X-Rares from the Advent Saga. Its Heaven counterpart debuted in [[BS40]] and Earth in [[BS41]]. The text of the keywords reads as:
* When your Field (Trash) is "[Color] symbols only & three symbols or more, [Effect] 
Said final effect is related to one of the color's gimmicks, occasionally an unusual variation of an effect, such as Juno's forbidding of setting a burst, or a rare effect, such as Julyre's summon limitation or August's banishing.
This effect punishes players who mix colors, an abrupt change in the game, as most recent sagas had a pair of families which existed in every color and supported each other ([[Galaxian]]s/[[Astral Soul]]s, [[Fencer]]s/[[Exalted Sword]]s, [[Lord]]s/[[Vassal]]s, [[God-King]]s/[[Ten Crown]]s), allowing for non-rush based mixed builds.

Twinkle Trace.fullContent:
[[File:BS42-CP08.jpg|thumb|250px]] '''Twinkle Trace''' (輝跡, Kō ato) is a keyword which debuted in [[BS42]]. The only Spirits to possess it are SixTwinkleGuards, the upgrade versions of the six searchers. The keyword's text reads: * {{twt|[Color]}} '''(Start of Your Attack Step)'''
If [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] on this Spirit, you can stack a [Color] card from your Hand onto this Spirit via {{tk|Advent}}. The effect name, while being a combination of "twinkle (輝)" + "trace (跡)" in a literal sense, is also a pun for "miracle (奇跡)" in terms of Japanese pronunciation. Effect-wise, it allows the player to {{tk|Advent}} at the Start of Attack Step, which comes before any Flash Timing during Attack Step. This means that the attacking player can {{tk|Advent}} safely without worrying that their base for {{tk|Advent}} is being removed by the opponent in Flash Timing, as the defense side takes the first flash. It also offers much more flexibility for the players to use the '''(When Attacks)''' effects that are immediately resolved (e.g. draw a card/destroy an opposing 5000 BP or less Spirit, etc.) of the {{tk|Advent}} cards, without the need to wait for a second chance of attacking with the Spirit, or to make an attack first, declare the {{tk|Advent}}, then deplete the attacker. The effect is particularly useful in Advent era where almost all the advent cards have their advent timing being Flash Timing of Attack Step. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Twinkle_Trace|List of cards with Twinkle Trace]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

'''Change ''' (チェンジ, ''Chenji'') is a keyword which debuted in [[CB04]] & [[SD42]].

The text on each card varies, but the common points are that they work like Magic, with either Main or Flash effects, which can be used from the hand, and, after they resolve, player can either discard the card or replace/swap one of your Spirits on field with this card in refreshed condition. If the Spirit that was used for the switching is currently battling, the new Spirit will continued the battle.

While this was originally introduced to cards that belongs to the "Kamen" family, as a representation of their transformation between different battle suits, some of the non-Kamen family cards introduced post-CB04 and SD42, such as [[Imperialdramon Dragon Mode]] and [[Imperialdramon Paladin Mode]], also has such ability as well, but has different card family requirements or no such requirement at all.

The default text on Change cards is the following:
* '''[Step Timing] - Change: Cost X''' (Reductions) (This effect can be used from your hand). [Effect]. After that effect resolves, either discard this card or replace one of your '''[condition]''' Spirit's with this card in refreshed condition. If the Spirit is currently battling, continue the battle.

Dark Esoterica.fullContent:

{{Nihongo|Dark Esoterica|闇奥義|Yamiougi}} is an effect which debuted in [[BS42]], and is exclusive to the 'DarkStones' spirits, serving as the dark counterpart to [[Pyroxene Esoterica]]. The Keyword is divided in two sub-keywords, Heaven and Hell. Dark Esoterica - Heaven counts cards of the designated color on the player's Field and [[Removed From Game Zone]], while Hell counts cards on the Field and Trash. It is also worth noting that the "Heaven" of Dark Esoterica is written as "Heaven's Prison." In a similar fashion, "Hell" is written as "Earth's Prison," thus also being connected to the Pyroxene Esoterica - Earth keyword.

While each Esoterica is different, their effects are deeply ingrained with their respective colors, and are generally control-oriented. While their conditions have varying degrees of ease to achieve and punish color-mixing like Pyroxene Esoterica, with [[The DarkStoneMaiden Alice]], Dark Esoterica can be activated freely.

It should be noted that while [[The DarkStones DarkfearSlashDeity Dinovenge]] lacks Dark Esoterica, the conditions of its [[Dark Unleash]] effect is similar to the other DarkStones' Dark Esoterica - Hell effects.

Minor Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:Daphned.png|thumb|318x318px]] '''Minor Unleash '''(小界放；''Shoukaihou'') is a keyword first appearing in LM18. It allows the activation of the [LV1][LV2] skill of a particular [[Grandwalker]] by paying one core from it to the Trash as the full cost. A card with this effect will usually have the following text: * {{Unleash|1|Minor}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3]''' (effect timing)
Once per turn, by sending one core from any of your exactly-named "Grandwalker xxxxxx" to the Trash, immediately activate that Grandwalker Nexus' '''[LV1][LV2]''' {{tk|Grand Skill}}/{{tk|Grand Field}}, treating core as having been sent to the Void. As the name implies, it is a variant of [[Unleash]]. Unlike [[Unleash]] that sends cores to the Field so that the cores can be immediately used within the same turn, Minor Unleash sends the core to Trash, so it can only be used next turn under most cases. On the other hand, while [[Unleash]] is an unique effect on the Spirit/Ultimate that owns the effect, Minor Unleash is in essence copying the effect from the Grandwalker Nexus that it references. And in that case, since only one core is needed, and the core is sent to the Trash, not Void, its cost effectiveness is usually much higher than using the {{tk|Grand Skill}}/{{tk|Grand Field}} directly, which usually sends the cores to the Void and requires a heavier cost. Considering that the owner of Minor Unleash is the {{tk|Core Charge}} target of that Grandwalker Nexus it references, {{tk|Minor Unleash}} is automatically fulfilled upon the summon of the owner, meaning that no preparation is needed beforehand other than having the corresponding Grandwalker Nexus deployed on field. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Minor Unleash|List of cards with Minor Unleash]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

As Celestial Unleash uses the "when you've done so" wording, it is possible to move cores from the Grandwalker Nexus even if the latter effect cannot be activated, and it is also possible to move fewer cores than the effect requires (only in case the Grandwalker Nexus doesn't have any. A player using Celestial Unleash: 2 can't deliberately only move a single core if their Grandwalker has more than two, but if it only has one core, they can move one), but the secondary effect does not activate in such cases.

Rebirth.fullContent:
[[File:Chronosides.png|right|382x382px|alt=]]
'''Rebirth''' (''{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}; Tensei'') is the main gimmick of the 11th saga of Battle Spirits, introduced in [[SD55]]. Cards which possess the keyword are printed on both sides, each side having their own effects, cost, and even differing card types. While some Rebirth cards do not possess the ability, the keyword serves mostly as a "remains on field" effect, as one of the general conditions for the flipping is for the opponent to remove the card from the field, through effects for Nexuses, via any means for Spirits.

The primary condition for Rebirth are counters, having less than a certain number allows the card to flip once they meet the condition, and when a card is Reborn, it adds a counter, making it so the more Rebirths are used, closer the player is to be unable to use them. However, since [[BSC47]], Rebirth conditions may also reference the life count, allowing the cards to flip more easily. 

Besides double-sided cards, Rebirth cards also first introduced the rarities "Rebirth Rare" and "Rebirth X-Rare". They also brought along checklist cards (more details below). A new area was also added to the board for these cards, the Counter Area (also more details below). 

Meanwhile, '''Zero Rebirth '''({{ruby|零|ぜろ}}{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}, ''Zero Tensei) ''requires the player to have zero counters to activate, and adds no counters upon flipping, conflicting directly with vanilla Rebirth, making it so the synergy with Rebirth and counter-based decks is nearly non-existing. This keyword only exists on collaboration cards.

Texts possible for Spirit Rebirths include:

*'''''(Zero) Rebirth'':''' '''X or less Counters''' (Only one Rebirth can be used at a time) When either (Condition A) or this Spirit leaves the field due to the opponent, put [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] on this Spirit and it is Reborn.

And for Nexus Rebirths, there is:

*When either (Condition A) or when opposing effects would remove this Nexus from the Field, you can put [[file: Soul Core.png|20px]] on this Nexus and it is Reborn.
*When (Condition A), this Nexus can be Reborn. When it is, you can put one core from your Field/Reserve to this now-Reborn Spirit.

In [[SD57]], '''Six Heaven Rebirth''' ({{ruby|六|ろく}}{{ruby|天|てん}}{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}, ''Rokuten Tensei'') was introduced, possessed exclusively by [[The HeavenlyDemonKing God-Sechs -Type Earth-]]. The effect is worded as follows:

*'''''Six Heaven Rebirth'':''' '''5 or less Counters''' (Only one Rebirth can be used at a time) When this Spirit attacks, You can flip it. If you have five or more symbol colors, instead, you can send an opposing Life to the Trash and flip it.

In [[CB18]], '''Absolute Rebirth''' ({{ruby|絶|ぜっ}}{{ruby|対|たい}}{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}, ''Zettai Tensei'') was introduced, possessed exclusively by [[Special Aircraft No. 4 Ultroid Zero]]. The effect is worded as follows:

* '''''Absolute Rebirth'': 0 or more Counters''' (Only one Rebirth can be used at a time) When the opponent reduces your Life, or this Spirit would leave the Field due to the opponent, immediately flip this Spirit.

In [[CB21]], '''Sortie Rebirth''' ({{ruby|出|しゅう}}{{ruby|撃|げき}}{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}, ''Shutsugeki Tensei'') was introduced, possessed exclusively by Nexuses in the "[[Pilot]]" family. The effect is worded as follows:

* '''''Sortie Rebirth: 5 or less Counters''''' (Only one Rebirth can be used at a time) When your "XXX"-named Spirit is summoned, you can flip this Nexus. When you do, this now-Reborn Brave either brave to your Spirit, or stay in Spirit condition.
In [[BS59]], '''Illusive Rebirth'''  ({{ruby|幻|げん}}{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}, ''Gen Tensei'') was introduced. The effect is worded as follows:

* ''[During Set] '''Illusive Rebirth: 5 or less Counters''''' (Only one Rebirth can be used at a time) ''[Effects and conditions]'', you can put any number of cores from your Reserve onto this [[Mirage]] and flip it onto your Field.

Once flipped by any "Rebirth"-named keyword, the Reborn side contains the following text:

*When you flip into this side, this card remains on the Field, and you gain a counter. (Put a core from the Void to your Counter Area.)

However, '''Zero Rebirth''' and '''Absolute Rebirth''' are the exceptions, as the Reborn side will contain the following text:

* When you flip into this side, this card remains on the field, and you gain no counters.

== Terms ==
During the game, while the Rebirth cards can be referred through normal means (such as if an effect targets a Spirit, a double-sided card with its Spirit side on the Field can be affected), there are also new terms to refer to them specifically, including "Rebirth cards", "Rebirth [card type]", "pre-Rebirth [card type]", and "Reborn [card type]".

"Pre-Rebirth XXX" refers to cards with their A sides face-up (can be recognised through having the cost at top left, and the set number writing "A"); while "Reborn XXX" refers to cards with their B sides face-up (recognised through having the cost at top right, and the set number writing "B"). In the meantime, "Rebirth XXX" will refer to the double-sided cards whichever sides they are at.

== Counter Area ==
Counter Area is situated outside of the field, and can be interacted with if rules or effects state "counter +X". If a card is reborn and does not leave the field, a specified number of counters is always needed to add to the Counter Area (unless the card itself possesses Zero Rebirth).

However, there is no official clarification where the Counter Area exactly is. On the play mat given out in [[PB09]], the Counter Area is situated on the left side of the deck; while on the play mat in the anime [[Battle Spirits: Gallet's Revolution]] and the official YouTube battles Extreme League, the Counter Area is situated above the deck.

As the gimmick is similar to the effects of [[:Category:"Seal"-named|"Seal"-named Magic cards]] and [[The First Ultraman]], be careful not to mix up with the cores in the Counter Area.

== How to Use Rebirth Cards in the Deck==
As the Rebirth cards are double-sided, unlike the normal cards, they do not have a side with the usual black surface with silver stripes and the BS logo. '''As such, it is a must to use colored sleeves.''' There are two methods to use these cards. While both methods can be used in the same game, the same copies of a card must be using the same method.

*Put the actual Rebirth cards inside the deck, and when needed to flip to the other side, pull them out from the sleeves, flip to the other side, and insert them back into the sleeves.
*Put the checklist cards inside the deck, and when played, put the actual Rebirth cards from outside of the game on top of the checklists.

===Checklist Cards===
[[file:Checklist.jpg|thumb|alt=|The checklist card from [[SD55]]]]
Checklist cards are provided to be put in the decks, and can be obtained along with the other products. Each checklist card displays multiple sections, with each section depicting the name, cost, reduction symbols, card type, families, and set number of a Rebirth card the checklist card can represent. Each checklist card in the deck must be ticked in one of the sections to specify which card each checklist card is representing.

* Checklist cards from booster boxes have their back sides printed with indexes. Their back sides do not look like normal cards (black surface with silver stripes and the BS logo).
* Otherwise, other checklist cards, like the ones printed in [[SD55]], have the back side the same as normal cards, so they can be played in a deck without sleeves or with transparent sleeves.
* Starting from [[CB16]], the sections of the checklist cards also display the effects that can be activated from hand (e.g. [[Exchange]], [[Armed Intervention]]).

When a checklist card is played, the player is required to take the actual card from their deck box and replace the checklist card with it. When the Rebirth card leaves the field, it switches places again with the checklist card, then the checklist card is placed to the designated area of where the actual card is actually sent to.

* The number of checklist cards in the deck and the number of actual Rebirth cards readied in the deck box must be the same.
* The contents of the Rebirth cards placed outside of the game cannot be checked by the opponent. It is also fine for you to intentionally hide the Rebirth cards until they are used.

==Rules==

===Rebirth Cards in Deck, Hand, and Trash===

* When building a deck, the name of a Rebirth card is the combination of the name on the A side and the name on the B side.
**For example, [[Aile Strike Gundam]] and [[Aile Strike Gundam (CB13-030 (A))|Aile Strike Gundam]]/[[Launcher Strike Gundam (CB13-030 (B))|Launcher Strike Gundam]] are treated as having different names, and so you can put three copies of each in the same deck.
*When a Rebirth card is on the field, only the side that is face-up to the players is referenced by the effects. When a Rebirth card is outside of the field, such as being in hand or trash or a pre-[[Advent]] card, when referencing or targeting it, only the A side can be referenced.
*During the game, you can always check the contents of your own Rebirth cards that are outside of the game. As for the opposing Rebirth cards, you can only ask to check them if those cards are placed in open areas, such as the field, trash, and the removed zone.

===Rebirth Cards on the Field===

* If a Rebirth card is a Nexus on the A side, and a Spirit on the B side. While it is in the pre-Rebirth state (on the A side), it cannot be targeted by effects that target Spirits.
* Rebirth Spirits and Rebirth Nexuses can still be targeted if the effect simply specifies "Spirit" or "Nexus". However, if the effect specifies "Rebirth Spirits" or "Rebirth Nexuses", normal Spirits and Nexuses are not affected.

=== When Rebirthing ===

* When a card is flipping into a Spirit via Rebirth, as it is not a summon, effects like "cannot summon Spirits", "cannot summon by effects" do not affect it. Of course, "when a Spirit is summoned" effects do not activate either.
* When flipping through Rebirth, there is no need to pay any costs, and cores cannot be moved unless effects state so. Unless specified, the card remains in the same state as before it flips.
** When the Rebirth effect also includes moving cores, you cannot move the cores without also flipping the card.
*** If the effect is "put [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] on this Nexus and flip it", the Soul Core can be from your field, reserve, trash, or life.
** When the Rebirth effect triggers upon "when leaving the field", as many cores as according to the effect stated are moved to the card and it flips. After flipping, if there are enough cores to maintain the card at the lowest level, then it remains on the field, and the player increases their counters.
*** However, if there are not enough cores to maintain the lowest level, the process of Rebirth is stopped, the Rebirth card does not remain on the field, counters do not increase, and '''it is treated as depletion through your own effect'''.
** In the case of "put [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] on this Nexus and flip it", the Soul Core must be put if possible. However, even if the Soul Core cannot be moved, the card can still be flipped. Again, if there is not enough cores to maintain the lowest level on the B side, the card is depleted.
** In the case of "you can put a core from your Field/Reserve to this now-Reborn Spirit" for a Rebirth Nexus with zero cores, if you choose not to put a core on it, and there are no other effects to put at least one core on it, and its lowest level on the B side cannot be maintained, it is depleted by your own effect. If such, the Rebirth process is stopped, no counters increased, and effects such as (When Reborn) effects cannot activate.
* "When you flip into this side, this card remains on the field, and you gain a counter. (Put a core from the Void to your Counter Area.)" '''is not an effect'''. As such, it cannot be nullified.
*The process of a "Flip a Rebirth card" effect is treated as rebirthing. As such, when flipped, counters increase according to the designated number, and effects such as (When Reborn) effects can activate.
**However, any effects stated on the Rebirth text of the card being flipped cannot activate, as the card is not flipped through its Rebirth but by other effects.
* Multiple Rebirth and "flip a Rebirth card" effects cannot activate together at the same timing. You can only choose one of them to activate. However, when the same timing fulfills the flipping conditions for both you and your opponent, each of you can activate one flipping effect, order decided by the turn player.
** Tip:  You have two Spirits with the Rebirth condition "when the opposing Life is reduced", the attack of your Spirit with the effect "when this attack reduces the opposing Life, send an opposing Life to the Reserve" reduces the opposing life, you can flip one of your Spirits with the stated condition, then activate the life burn and flip the second Spirit.
* When your Brave pre-Rebirth Spirit flips, it stays braved. However, it separates with the Brave if the B side does not meet the Brave condition.

=== Reborn Spirits ===

* The Reborn Spirits still carry the continuous effects which were affecting them prior to their Rebirth, such as "during this turn" effects. However, effects without a timing stated are lost after the card flips. Also, after flipping, if the cost, color etc. of the Reborn Spirit do not meet the conditions of the effects, those effects are also lost.
** A pre-Rebirth Spirit activates the effect "during this turn, give this Spirit +5000 BP" and applies it onto itself. It is then reborn, the effect is still applied on it.
** After the "once per turn" effects of Braves, such as that of [[The GroundDeityBlade Ootenta]] activates while the Brave Spirit is in pre-Rebirth state. After it flips, the Reborn Spirit cannot activate them again.
* When a battling Spirit is reborn, the Reborn Spirit continues the battle. However, if it is a Reborn Nexus, it does not continue the battle, but there is still Flash Timing for both players.
* When an attacking Spirit flips mid-way, the (When Attacks) effects of the Reborn Spirit can only activate depending on situations.
** Instantaneous effects such as drawing and destruction cannot activate.
** (When Attacks) effects with other timings, such as with the "Flash" timing stated, when comparing BP, when destroyed etc., and during battle effects that do not have the texts "during this battle" or "during this turn" stated, can activate.
* When you advent onto a Reborn Spirit, it is flipped back to the A side when it becomes a pre-Advent card. At this moment, the process of Advent is already complete, so it does not matter if the A side does not fulfill the Advent condition. However, when activating (When Advents) effects and is necessary to reference the Spirit that is being advented onto, the Reborn side is referenced. If part of the effects reference pre-Advent cards, then the pre-Rebirth side is referenced.

=== [[Burst]] Related ===

* If your Soul Core is in your life due to [[Seal]], then it is taken out due to your Rebirth effect, you can activate your set Burst with the condition "After your Life decreases".
* When your pre-Rebirth Spirit is depleted or destroyed, then you declare your set Burst with the condition "After your Spirit is depleted/destroyed by the opponent", but your Spirit activates Rebirth, flips, and remains on the field, as the card is not placed into the trash, your Burst cannot activate and it returns to its previous state.
* When your Reborn Spirit is depleted or destroyed, then you declare your set Burst with the condition "After your Spirit is depleted/destroyed by the opponent", even if the Reborn Spirit is a Nexus on the A side, you can still activate the Burst. This is because the card is placed into the trash '''before''' it flips back.
** However, in the example of [[Rampart Wall]], which has the effect "you can return a Spirit card in your Trash that was depleted/destroyed when this Burst activated to your Hand", if the depleted or destroyed Spirit has flipped back to a different card type, it cannot be returned to the hand. However, if the A side is also a Spirit card, then it can be returned.

=== Others ===

* For Rebirth effects which activate during Flash Timing, as they do not have the timing "Flash" written, '''they are not flash effects'''.
** For this reason, when [[The Duke Kingtaurus]] (Revival) activates its "during this battle, the opponent can't use flash effects", as long the Rebirth condition is fulfilled, it can activate during the Flash Timing of that battle.
* If a Rebirth Spirit has facedown cards under it due to [[Poison Blade]], those cards stay there if it becomes a Reborn Spirit/Ultimate. However, if it becomes a Reborn Nexus, the facedown cards are discarded.
* As Rebirth is not summon/advent/deploy, [[Core Charge]] cannot activate.

Return to Prime.fullContent:
[[File:BS52-TX01 b.png|thumb|320x320px]] '''Return to Prime''' (根幻回帰 ; ''kongengaiki'') in a keyword introduced in [[BS52]]. Only the Reborn side of Rebirth X-Rares have this keyword, which is worded as follows: * '''Return to Prime -''' When this card would leave the Field by opposing effects, you can flip and deploy it. Much like Rebirth works as a stay-on-field effect, so does Return to Prime, looping the card's presence on the field and enabling multiple uses of (When Deployed) and (When Reborn) effects, for as long as the player's counters allow it. == Noticeable Q&A == Q: What is a Reborn Spirit's "Return to Prime"?

A: When the Spirit is destroyed, depleted, returned to hand/deck, sent to Removed Zone or banished by an opposing effect, '''Return to Prime''' allows the player to pay the cost to deploy the Rebirth Nexus. When doing so, no counters are gained, and effects affecting the Reborn Spirit are interrupted. Also, while the player cannot use its own symbol to reduce the cost when deploying the Nexus, cores can be moved to it, and its (When Deployed)/Core Charge effects can activate, as well as any other effects which trigger upon a Nexus being deployed. Q: When you use the effect of your [[The HellDog Cerru-Berus]] to target the opposing [[The Red Divine Dragon Emperor]] and use it as your own Spirit, then during the Attack Step Emperor is destroyed, can its Return to Prime activate?

A: As you can't summon/deploy opposing cards on your Field, '''Return to Prime''', being a deploy effect, can't activate. However, when you target Emperor and move it to your Field, it's treated as leaving the opposing Field, so the opponent can activate its Return to Prime at that moment. Q: The Brave Reborn Spirit activates '''Return to Prime''', when does the braved Brave become Spirit condition?

A: The braved Brave becomes Spirit condition before you summon the Spirit card via '''Return to Prime''', so when paying the cost, you can use that Brave's symbol for reduction costs. Q: When you activates '''Return to Prime''' of a braved Spirit, and choose to have to braved Brave remains on field, when does the Brave becomes Spirit-form?

A: Before you deploy the Nexus card through '''Return to Prime'''. Hence, you can use the symbol of the brave to reduce the cost for deploying the Nexus card. == Related articles == * [[:Category:Return to Prime|Cards with Return to Prime]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Count Break.fullContent:
[[file:BS54-X03.png|thumb]]
'''Count Break''' (Cブレイク ; ''kaunto breiku'') is a keyword debuted in [[BS54]]. The effect is worded as follows: 

* '''Count Break: X''' (When Attacks) By -X counters (send X cores from your Counter Area to the Void), ''[additional effects]''. '''Count Break''' can only be used once per game. 

Count Break is a very powerful effect with a "once per game" restriction. Much like to the [[Soul Drive]] effect, all Count Break effects have the same kind of restriction, but can be attached with different kinds of additional effects. As the name suggests, the effect relies on decreasing a certain number of counts, meaning it is an effect that needs to go along with the [[Rebirth]] keyword. This also means Count Break is mostly forced to be used as a late game effect as it has to wait for the counters to build up. However, with the upcoming arrival of the next era based on the Contract Saga that would allow for the easy accumulation of counts and the potential to use these as finishers for Contract decks early on in the game, some cards that use the keyword are pre-emptively banned or limited to one per deck.
