Tenma-Kagemusha.fullContent:
[[File:SD57-X02.jpg|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Tenma-Kagemusha''' (天魔・影武者) is a keyword introduced in [[SD57]], exclusive to [[The HeavenlyDemonKing God-Sechs -Type Shadow-]]. This effect is read as follows:

* '''Tenma-Kagemusha -''' When your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) are targeted by an opposing effect, you can summon this card from the Hand. Then, choose to either change the target of that effect to this Spirit only, or change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your", and if it's the latter option, the opponent chooses the target.

While having a slightly different name and an additional effect to change targets, Tenma-Kagemusha functions basically the same way as [[Kagemusha]], so any Q&As about Kagemusha will also relate to Tenma-Kagemusha.

== Official Q&As ==
'''Q1''': What is "Tenma-Kagemusha"?

'''A1''': When your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) are targeted by an opposing effect, you can summon the card with "Tenma-Kagemusha" from your hand, and you can either change the target of that effect to this Spirit only, or change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your", and if it's the latter option, the opponent chooses the target. Although this keyword is different to "[[Kagemusha]]", the process of resolving "change the target of that effect to this Spirit only" effect is the same as "Kagemusha".


'''Q2''': When an opposing Spirit with "unaffected by effects" effects such as "[[Heavy Armor]]" targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), and you summon a Spirit through "Tenma-Kagemusha", can you choose the "change the 'opponent'/'opposing' text(s) of that effect to 'you'/'your'" option?

'''A2''': No, you cannot, as "Tenma-Kagemusha" is an effect that targets the original effect holder. However, you can choose the option to make the effect target only the Spirit with "Tenma-Kagemusha".


'''Q3''': When your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) are targeted by an opposing effect, then you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha". If the opposing effect has other timings such as "[[Rush]]", "then", or "after this effect resolves", can "Tenma-Kagemusha" also change the targets for those timings?

'''A3''': No, it cannot. Within one effect, different timings are treated as different effects. However, you can trigger a second "Tenma-Kagemusha" to counter those effects.


'''Q4''': When an opposing optional effect, such as with the wordings "can" and "may", targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), and your "Tenma-Kagemusha" changes the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your", can your opponent choose not to activate the effect?

'''A4''': No, they cannot. The effect has already activated.


'''Q5''': An opposing destruction effect targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), and you change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your" with "Tenma-Kagemusha", so opposing Spirits are destroyed instead. Can your opponent activate effects with the timing "when your Spirit is destroyed by the opponent"?

'''A5''': No, they cannot. They are destroying their own Spirits with their effect.


'''Q6''': When your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) are targeted by an opposing effect, can you activate two copies of cards with "Tenma-Kagemusha" at the same time?

'''A6''': No, you cannot. When the target is changed by the first copy, the new target will no longer be your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit (as it would either change to your "[[The HeavenlyDemonKing God-Sechs -Type Shadow-]]" which doesn't have the "Heavenly Demon King" family, or an opposing Spirit which does not matter whether it has the "Heavenly Demon King" family or not), the condition will become invalid for the second copy. In this case, the second copy will return to your Hand.


'''Q7''': When an opposing "target and attack" effect targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), and you change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your" with "Tenma-Kagemusha", can the opponent target their own Spirit(s) to block?

'''A7''': No, they cannot, as their own Spirits cannot block on their own Attack Step. The effect will be nullified and it will become a normal attack.


'''Q8''': When the "[[Triple Ultimate Trigger]]" of the opposing "[[The Hellsoil FourDemonLord Magnamiser]]" triple hits, then the "core removal" effect targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s). At this moment, you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha" and change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your", how does the "discard two cards from your opponent's hand, without looking at the contents" effect resolve?

'''A8''': The owner of "[[The Hellsoil FourDemonLord Magnamiser]]" puts the cards in their hand face-down, then ask the opponent to shuffle them, and discard two cards among them without looking at the content. If both sides agree, the owner can also just ask the opponent to discard two random cards from their hand.


'''Q9''': When the "[[Triple Ultimate Trigger]]" of the opposing "[[The Hellsoil FourDemonLord Magnamiser]]" gets triple hits, then the "core removal" effect targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s). At this moment, you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha" and change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your", then the opponent choose to have this effect deplete their own Magnamiser that is activating the effect. Does the rest of the "Triple Ultimate Trigger" effect resolves?

'''A9''': Yes, the "double hit" and "triple hit" effects continue to resolve, as they all activate at the same time.


'''Q10''': When your hand has six or more cards and the opponent activates the "[[Soul Burst]]" effect of their "[[The DarkStones MachineBeastDeity Fenrig]]", but they do not target your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) to remain on the field (meaning your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) will return to the deckbottom), can you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha"?

'''A10''': Yes, you can, as your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) will then become target(s) to return to the deckbottom. However, if your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s) are not affected by opposing effects due to effects like [[Heavy Armor]], or having already been targeted by effects like "this Spirit cannot be returned to Hand/deck due to opposing effects", then they will not targeted, and hence you will not be able to activate "Tenma-Kagemusha".


'''Q11''': When your hand has six or more cards and the opponent activates the "[[Soul Burst]]" effect of their "[[The DarkStones MachineBeastDeity Fenrig]]", then the effect targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), and you change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your" with "Tenma-Kagemusha"; but the opposing hand has less than six cards, does the "[[Soul Burst]]" effect just get nullified?

'''A11''': No, it does not. "Tenma-Kagemusha" simply reselects the target, but the "Soul Burst" effect has already fulfilled its condition, so the opponent will target their own cards.


'''Q12''': When the opposing "[[The ShiningHeavenDragonDeity Grand-Terasu]]" activates the "or" part of "[[Shining Heaven Unleash]]", and targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), can you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha"?

'''A12''': Yes, you can. At this moment, the effect still has not activated yet, so you can change the target. If the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect is changed to "you"/"your", the opponent will negate the effects of their own Spirits/Ultimates and return one of their Spirits/Ultimates to the deckbottom (both effects can activate as they activate at the same time). However, Grand-Terasu will not be able to refresh as its effect is already negated at that moment.


'''Q13''': When the opposing "[[The ShiningHeavenDragonDeity Grand-Terasu]]" activates the "or" part of "[[Shining Heaven Unleash]]", and targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), then you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha" and change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your", can the opponent choose to activate the destruction part of the effect instead?

'''A13''': No, they cannot. The effect has already activated.


'''Q14''': The (When Summoned) effect of the opposing "[[The DruidPrincess Fidelma]]" activates the "symbols become zero" part, and targets your "[[Heavenly Demon King]]" family Spirit(s), then you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha" and change the "opponent"/"opposing" text(s) of that effect to "you"/"your". Then, they summon a second copy of "The DruidPrincess Fidelma" during the game, can they activate the "symbols become zero" part of the effect, which can only be activated once per game, again?

'''A14''': No, they cannot.

== Official Q&As from Nabiden ==
'''Q:''' When an opposing Burst effect of a card still in the Burst Area targets your "Heavenly Demon King" family Spirits, then you activate "Tenma-Kagemusha", can you change the "opponent"/"opposing" texts of that effect to "you"/"your"?

'''A:''' No you cannot. Burst cards still in the Burst Area are only affected by effects that target "Burst" specifically.{{Keywords Nav}}

Manifest.fullContent:
[[File:What is Manifest.png|600px|thumb]] '''Manifest''' (顕現; kengen) is a keyword introduced in [[SD68]] that serves as the main gimmick of Contract Saga: True. The effect name matches with the divine nature of the Contract Grandwalkers (Contractors), which are often the targets of Manifest. The general effect is written as follows: '''Flash -''' {{Mani|(Condition)|(Timing)}}
By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, pay one cost from the target to summon this card from the Hand. As the name implies, the keyword is a special summoning effect that allows players to summon high cost Spirits, often the key Spirits, with a low cost when specific conditions are met. While in many ways it is similar to {{tk|Advent}}, including the use of Soul Core and bypassing the regular cost of summon, the nature of the effect is a '''Summon'''. Hence, any effects that restrict the summon of cards would be relevant. On the plus side, however, since it is a "one cost summon", it won't be stopped by effects like [[Zero Counter]]. As it is a "summon", [[Neo-Core Charge]] would also be able to react to '''Manifest'''. Since the general Manifest effect pays the cost from the Contractors, and you can +1 core to the Contractor after summoning the Devotee/Concluser cards via '''Manifest''', it is essentially a "free summon" at the cost of one Soul Core. Being a summon but not {{tk|Advent}} also means it won't be stopped by effects that restrict advent and the player doesn't need to prepare a separate Spirit to serve as the advent base. As a set to come with '''Manifest''', a new effect timing, '''(When Manifests)''' (『このスピリットの顕現時』), is also introduced. Effects with that timing could only proc when the card is summoned via Manifest, but not other summon methods. == Official Q&A == Click ''[[Manifest/Q&A|here]]''. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Manifest|List of cards with Manifest]] * [[Ultra Manifest]] * [[Seal Manifest]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

[[File:BS69-X01.png|thumb]] '''Primordial Unleash''' ({{ruby|原|げん}}{{ruby|初|しょ}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}} ; ''gensho kaihou'') is a derivative keyword of {{tk|Unleash}} introduced in [[BS69]] and owned by primarily by the [[Concluser]] Spirits of the [[Primordial|Primordial Deity]] faction. The general form of the effect is worded as below: *{{tk|Primordial Unleash}}
[Effect]. Then, you can send X cores from any of your "[[Primordial]]" family Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit. When you've done so, [Effect]. In terms of wordings, {{tk|Primordial Unleash}} is different to the original {{tk|Unleash}} in that while {{tk|Unleash}} uses the "by doing A, do B" wording, while {{tk|Primordial Unleash}} uses the "Do A. When you've done so, do B." wording. Another difference is that while {{tk|Unleash}} limits the core movements from Grandwalker Nexuses of specified colors, {{tk|Primordial Unleash}} limits the core movements from specifically "[[Primordial]]" family Grandwalker Nexuses, regardless of colors. Since all "[[Primordial]]" family Grandwalker Nexuses are Contract Grandwalker Nexuses so far, the only Unleash source would be the Contract Grandwalker Nexus put in the deck. On the other hand, unlike some other variants of Unleash like {{tk|Curse Unleash}}, where the Unleash target is tied to exact name, Primordial Unleash only requires the Grandwalker Nexus to be in "[[Primordial]]" family, meaning that the cards with {{tk|Primordial Unleash}} can be used interchangeably between different "[[Primordial]]" decks. ==Related Articles== *[[:Category:Primordial Unleash|List of cards with Primordial Unleash]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

(Once per Turn: Same Name) By putting your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] on top, +1 core to one of the targets, and summon this card from the Hand, treating all summon costs as paid. Same as Manifest, it requires both the Soul Core and a Contract Grandwalker Nexus (the "target"). While the effect text itself is a bit ambiguous due to the omission carried on from the original Japanese, it refers to: the summon of the card with {{tk|UMani}} from the Hand by putting your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Life/Field/Reserve/Trash onto '''that card with''' {{tk|UMani}}, and putting a core from the Void to the target Grandwalker Nexus listed in the effect. While you do, like normal Manifests, you need to satisfy the timing and conditions like counter conditions. And similarly, you can put any number of cores from your Field/Reserve to that card to establish the summon. For example, when using the {{tk|UMani}} of [[The JewelEmpress Bijour-Joyaux]], you declare the use of its {{tk|UMani}} from the Hand, put your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Reserve/Trash/Field to that card, and any other cores to establish the summon, while adding a core from the Void to one of your [[The MagicJewelContractor Morrigan]]. Unless via other effects, these can only be done during the Flash Timing of (Your Turn) and when you have 8 counters or more. In simple terms, it refunds the player the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] and have a core added to the Grandwalker Nexus, making the concept a reverse of {{tk|Mani}}, which requires sending the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to Trash + sending a core from the target Grandwalker Nexus to the Trash. In terms of design, as {{tk|UMani}} is counted as the evolution of Manifest, it is often owned by the evolution form of the key Spirits of the different Contract Grandwalker Nexus decks, and has a higher counter condition than what is required by the manifest of the original Spirit. {{tk|UMani}} is also treated as {{tk|Mani}}. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Ultra Manifest|List of cards with Ultra Manifest]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Draw a card. Then, you can send a core from any of your Contract Grandwalker Nexus to this Spirit.
Contract Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:PX25-06.png|200px|thumb]] '''Contract Unleash''' ({{ruby|契|けい}}{{ruby|約|やく}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}}；''keiyaku-kaihō'') is a keyword introduced by [[The DivineWorldSearcher Alex]], the {{tk|Mani}} remake of [[The ChosenSearcher Alex]]/[[The NewWorld's Alex]], and currently exclusive her. The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|1|Contract}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Manifests)'''
Draw a card. Then, you can send a core from any of your Contract Grandwalker Nexus to this Spirit. When you've done so, if it's the opposing Attack Step, during this battle, the effects of an opposing Spirit/Ultimate/Nexus can't activate, and when this battle ends, end the Attack Step. Following the recent trend of the new "Unleash"-named keywords, like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Curse Unleash]], this Unleash requires a special kind of Grandwalker Nexus to work. However, unlike the abovementioned ones, it only requires a "Contract Grandwalker Nexus" instead of Grandwalker Nexuses with a specific name, making it much more versatile than those Unleash variants. The effect is named "Contract Unleash" most probably because of such condition as well. Possessed exclusively by Alex, the actual effect is a polished version of Alex's signature Attack Step ending effect with extra resources. Since Unleash in itself is a "core boosting" effect, the effect is essentially draw + core boost, instead of having to choose one from the two for other variants of Alex. When compared to the OG and Revival versions of Alex, it has an extra part of effect lock inherited from [[The NewWorld's Alex]]. This maximizes the use of Alex's Attack Step ending effect, as it can shut down the increasingly common "the opponent can't end the Attack Step" effects on Field, making it a very solid defense effect. It is to note that, however, while the effect can lock the effects of an opposing Spirit/Ultimate/Nexus, it '''can't''' negate already resolved effects, like "During this turn, the opponent can't end the Attack Step via effects" activated before Alex's {{tk|Mani}}. ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Seal Manifest.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X02.png|200px|thumb]] '''Seal Manifest''' (封印顕現; fuuin-kengen) is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]] and exclusively owned by part of the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remakes of the [[TwelveGodKing]]s. The general effect is written as follows: '''Flash -''' {{Mani|Seal|[Condition|(Timing)}}
By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from the Field/Reserve to the Life, pay one cost from the target to summon this card from the Hand. In essence, it is a keyword combining {{Seal|Seal}} and {{tk|Mani}}. As such, '''it is treated as both''' {{Seal|Seal}} and {{tk|Mani}}, and can be referenced by any effects targeting the two. Effects that trigger upon the summoning of Spirit/{{tk|Mani}} of Spirit/carrying out {{Seal|Seal}} could all be activated via the effect. While it is undoubtedly a variant of {{Seal|Seal}}, the overall effect is based on {{tk|Mani}}, and changes from sending the Soul Core to Trash to sending it to the Life. Much like the original {{tk|Mani}}, it also requires paying cost from the "target", which is basically a type of Contract Grandwalker Nexus that matches the owner of Seal Manifest. For example, the target Contract Grandwalker for [[The TigerTwelveGodKing Revol-Tiger X]]'s Seal Manifest is [[The ThunderboltContractor Zeus]], which revolves around the [[Emperor Beast]] family that Revol-Tiger owns. As a merit, different from normal {{tk|Mani}}, since the Soul Core is sent to the Life instead of the Trash, it means that the user can carry out {{tk|Mani}} again in the same turn without the need to return Soul Core from the Trash. And the action of doing so can also trigger bursts that activate upon life decrease. On the other hand, doing so would mean the player is no longer {{Seal|During Seal}}, and relevant effects would not proc. It is to note that since the effect doesn't mention anything about "sending Soul Core to the Trash", you '''can't''' use any effect that states "{{tk|Mani}} the card treating Soul Core as being sent to the Trash" for Seal Manifest. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Seal Manifest|List of cards with Seal Manifest]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Terra Manifest.fullContent:
[[File:PX26-19.png|200px|thumb]] '''Terra Manifest''' (大地顕現; daichi-kengen) is a keyword introduced and owned exclusively by the promo card, [[The Converging Sealed Lands]], which was made to support the deck of [[The AstralMaterContractor Gaia]]. The effect is written as follows: '''Flash -''' {{Mani|terra|"Contractor Gaia" & C6 or more|(Either Attack Step)}}
By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, pay one cost from the target to deploy this card from the Hand. In essence, it is a modified version of the normal {{tk|Mani}} effect, where the owner of the effect is a Nexus that is being "deployed", instead of being "summoned". While the actual operation is similar to normal {{tk|Mani}}, there are a few things to note: By being "deploy" instead of "summon", it can bypass effects that lock "effect summons"; as the LV1 cost of [[The Converging Sealed Lands]] is 0, players also are not required to put cores onto it, making it different from the {{tk|Mani}} of Spirits or Ultimates, where at least one core has to be put onto the Spirit/Ultimate to maintain the LV1/LV3 cost under normal circumstances. As such, only one Soul Core and one core from [[The AstralMaterContractor Gaia]] is needed for the entire effect. Of course, similar to normal deploy of Nexus cards, it is up to the player to choose whether to put cores onto, and how many cores onto the Nexus when deploying using the effect. Regardless of all the differences, however, {{tk|Terra Manifest}} is still a {{tk|Mani}} effect, and a card with {{tk|Terra Manifest}} is treated as a card with {{tk|Mani}}. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Terra Manifest|List of cards with Terra Manifest]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Ultimate Trigger.fullContent:
[[File:SD19-X01.jpg|thumb]] '''Ultimate Trigger''' (Uトリガー, ''Arutimetto torigā'') or ''U-Trigger'' is a keyword introduced in [[SD19]] and [[SD20]]. This keyword occurs on all colors of Ultimates, and Ultimates only. Ultimates with this effect have the following effect: *'''''Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (''Timing'')
When Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''.
(Send a card from from the opposing deck to the Trash. If that card's cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it will hit.) While the process of activating Ultimate Trigger is the same for every Ultimate with this keyword, the effects after hit can vary between each card. The gambling element in this keyword is also to ensure that the Ultimates wouldn't be overpowered during its time of release, where there were little to no effects to counter them. As the chance of hitting relates to the Ultimate's card cost, most Braves which can brave to Ultimates have the effect to treat the Braves themselves as Cost 0 during brave, in order to avoid adding more costs to the Ultimates for a higher chance of hitting. The wording in which Ultimate Trigger uses to mill a card from the opposing deck is "send a card to the Trash" instead of "discard a card", meaning that any anti-deck destruction effects can't prevent Ultimate Trigger, nor can Ultimate Trigger be boosted by Blue [[Charge]] or similar effects. It's important to note that if [[Trigger Counter]] is used to stop the Ultimate Trigger, it has to be declared and activate before the targets for the Ultimate Trigger effect are chosen. As such, the Ultimate player is required to confirm with their opponent for any effect declarations right after the trigger is confirmed hit and before the rest of the Ultimate Trigger effect resolves. Some Ultimate Triggers also have an additional hit effect called [[Critical Hit]], which only activates when the condition for Critical Hit specifically is fulfilled. The keyword Ultimate Trigger also has several other keywords derived from it, which all are listed below. == Double Ultimate Trigger == [[File:Ultimate-Sagitto-Apollodragon.jpg|thumb]] '''Double Ultimate Trigger '''(ＷＵトリガー, ''Daburu arutimetto torigā'') or ''Ｗ-Trigger'' is a keyword introduced in [[SD25]]. It's a derivation of Ultimate Trigger, and the effect reads:  *'''''Double Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (''Timing'')
For each Ultimate Trigger hit, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Double Hit*:''''' Also, if the Ultimate Trigger hits twice, ''[additional effects]''.
(Double Ultimate Trigger: Send two cards from the opposing deck to the Trash. If each of those cards' cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it's a hit.) Each Double Ultimate Trigger effect will always have the [[Double Hit]] keyword. It's also important to note that as Double Hit uses the wording "also", its resolve timing is the same as Double Ultimate Trigger after both cards are confirmed as hit. When only one card is hit, it's considered as "one hit" instead of "guard". Therefore, any effects that activate upon guard don't activate. When the opposing deck only has one card to mill, Double Ultimate Trigger will still proceed, but with a definite maximum of one hit only. == Cross Ultimate Trigger == [[File:BS30-X04.png|thumb]] '''Cross Ultimate Trigger''' (ＸＵトリガー, ''Kurosu arutimetto torigā'') or XU-Trigger is a keyword introduced in [[SD28]]. It's part of Ultimate Trigger, and only exists within some of the Ultimate Trigger effects. The effect reads: *'''''Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (''Timing'')
When Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''.
After Ultimate Trigger, also, if your Life is at three or less, proceed to Cross Ultimate Trigger.
'''''Cross Ultimate Trigger:''''' When Cross Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''.
(Ultimate Trigger/Cross Ultimate Trigger: Send a card from the opposing deck to the Trash. If that card's cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it's a hit.) Cross Ultimate Trigger only activates after all effects triggered by Ultimate Trigger resolve first. However, any Burst declared via Ultimate Trigger will wait till Cross Ultimate Trigger resolves to activate. Even if Ultimate Trigger itself is guarded, Cross Ultimate Trigger can still proceed as long its condition is fulfilled. When Cross Ultimate Trigger activates, its procedure is the same as Ultimate Trigger, and can be countered by Trigger Counter, or trigger "when hit/guard" effects. == Triple Ultimate Trigger == [[File:The Hellsoil FourDemonLord Magnamizer.jpg|thumb]] '''Triple Ultimate Trigger''' (TUトリガー, ''Toripuru arutimetto torigā'' '') or TU-Trigger'' is a keyword and variant of Ultimate Trigger introduced in [[BS38]], possessed only by less than ten cards. The effect has two varying wordings: *'''''Triple Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (When Attacks)
For each Ultimate Trigger hit, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Double Hit*:''''' If the Ultimate Trigger hits twice, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Triple Hit*:''''' If the Ultimate Trigger hits thrice, ''[additional effects]''.
(Triple Ultimate Trigger: Send three cards from the opposing deck to the Trash. If each of those cards' cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it's a hit.) Or *'''''Triple Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (When Attacks)
When Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Double Hit*:''''' If the Ultimate Trigger hits twice, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Triple Hit*:''''' If the Ultimate Trigger hits thrice, ''[additional effects]''.
(Triple Ultimate Trigger: Send three cards from the opposing deck to the Trash. If each of those cards' cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it's a hit.) Each Triple Ultimate Trigger will always also have both the Double Hit and [[Triple Hit]] keywords. While there are no apparent wordings, all effects In Triple Ultimate Trigger are resolved at the same time. Take the effects of [[The Hellsoil FourDemonLord Magnamiser]] as an example, which deals a life burn and discards the opposing Hand at the same time, the opponent is required to discard [[Reactive Barrier]] first before both the life burn and hand discard happen, and Magnamizer won't be able to choose Reactive Barrier as a target for hand discard. Similarly, [[Arche Gundam]] can only be summoned after the whole Triple Ultimate Trigger effect resolves, meaning if it's discarded by Magnamizer's hand discard, despite having a life burn at the same time, it can't be summoned. Same as Double Ultimate Trigger, for example when only one card is hit, it's considered as "one hit" instead of "guard". Therefore, any effects that activate upon guard don't activate. When the opposing deck only has two or less cards to mill, Triple Ultimate Trigger will still proceed, but with a definite maximum of two hits only. == Octa Ultimate Trigger == [[File:SJ17-02.jpg|thumb]] '''Octa Ultimate Trigger''' (OUトリガー, ''Okuta arutimetto torigā'') is a keyword of [[Purple]], possessed only by [[The DragonEvilMarquis Overwhelm]]. The effect reads: *'''''Octa Ultimate Trigger''''' (When Summoned)
For each Trigger hit, send a core from any opposing Spirits/Ultimates to the Reserve.
(Octa Ultimate Trigger: Send eight cards from the opposing deck to the Trash. If each of those cards' cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it's a hit.) Octa Ultimate Trigger is by far the Ultimate Trigger with most cards sent to the Trash, and hence it can be easily abused if done right, causing a lot of restrictions to be put on Overwhelm itself. Same as Double Ultimate Trigger, for example when only one card is hit, it's considered as "one hit" instead of "guard". Therefore, any effects that activate upon guard don't activate. When the opposing deck only has seven or less cards to mill, Octa Ultimate Trigger will still proceed, but with a definite maximum of seven hits only. == Quadruple Ultimate Trigger == [[File:Is it more broken than Magnamiser?.png|thumb]] '''Quadruple Ultimate Trigger''' (QUトリガー, ''kuadorapuru arutimetto torigā'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS57]], possessed only by a few Ultimates. The effect reads: * '''''Quadruple Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (''Timing'')
When Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Double Hit*:''''' When it hits twice or more, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Triple hit*:''''' When it hits thrice or more, ''[additional effects]''.
'''''*Quadruple Hit*:''''' When it hits four times, ''[additional effects]''
(Quadruple Ultimate Trigger: Send four cards from the opposing deck to the Trash. If each of those cards' cost is lower than this Ultimate's, it's a hit.) Quadruple Ultimate Trigger may or may not come with Double Hit, Triple Hit, and Quadruple Hit keywords (It can skip any of the three). While there are no apparent wordings, all effects in Quadruple Ultimate Trigger are resolved at the same time, just like Triple Ultimate Trigger. Same as Double Ultimate Trigger, for example when only one card is hit, it's considered as "one hit" instead of "guard". Therefore, any effects that activate upon guard don't activate. When the opposing deck only has three or less cards to mill, Quadruple Ultimate Trigger will still proceed, but with a definite maximum of three hits only. == Count Ultimate Trigger == [[File:SD65-X02.png|thumb]] '''Count Ultimate Trigger''' (CUトリガー, ''Kaunto arutimetto torigā'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD65]], possessed only by a few Ultimates. The effect reads: * '''''Count Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (''Timing'')
When Count Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''.
(Count Ultimate Trigger: Send a card from the opposing decktop to the Trash. If that card's cost is lower than the number of your counters, it's a hit.) Unlike any of the previous Ultimate Triggers, Count Ultimate Trigger compares the user's number of counters with the opposing discarded card's cost, allowing the effect to have more flexibility against high cost decks, such as those which focus on [[Advent]]. It also means that when the player reaches a high enough number of counters, the chance of hitting with Count Ultimate Trigger is also higher, and when reaching more than ten counters, the effect is more or less guaranteed a hit whenever it activates. On the other Hand, it means that the Trigger effect can't get a hit at all if the player can't stack enough counters, especially at the beginning of the game. In a way, it is something that works right the opposite to how normal Ultimate Trigger functions, as the owner of the effect can make good preparation for it, and the effect relies on the preparation instead of the opponent and luck. == Double Count Ultimate Trigger == [[File:SD67-X01.png|thumb]] '''Double Count Ultimate Trigger''' (WCUトリガー, ''Daburu Kaunto arutimetto torigā'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD67]], possessed only by a few Ultimates. The effect reads: * '''''Double Count Ultimate Trigger''''' [LV] (''Timing'')
For each Count Ultimate Trigger hits, ''[additional effects]''. '''Double Hit:''' When it hits twice, ''[additional effects]''.
(Double Count Ultimate Trigger: Send two cards from the opposing decktop to the Trash. If the cards' cost is lower than the number of your counters, it's a hit.) It's basically a fusion of '''Double Ultimate Trigger''' and '''Count Ultimate Trigger''', having all the merits and demerits of the two keywords. ==Anime== Ultimate Trigger and some of its variants has been used in two anime series: [[Saikyo Ginga Ultimate Zero Battle Spirits]] and [[Battle Spirits Double Drive]]. Ultimate Zero was the first anime to introduce the [[Ultimate (Card Type)|Ultimate]] card type. As such, Ultimate Trigger was also a key element of the show, and was used by most of the main characters in the series. When they activated Ultimate Trigger, they'd shout "Ultimate Trigger, lock on!", and after a few gymnastic movements, they'd point their index fingers at the opposing deck and shoot out a laser beam, flipping up the top card of the opposing deck. In Double Drive, the only user was [[Kazuya Taiga]]. Interestingly, in [[Double Drive Episode 39|episode 39]], when the keyword was first shown in the series, Kazuya wrongly told his opponent to "reveal" the top card, when it should be "send to Trash". ==Related Articles== *[[:Category:Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Double Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Double Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Triple Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Triple Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Quadruple Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Quadruple Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Octa Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Octa Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Cross Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Cross Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Count Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Count Ultimate Trigger]] *[[:Category:Double Count Ultimate Trigger|List of cards with Double Count Ultimate Trigger]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Spirit Soul.fullContent:
[[File:BS24-001.jpg|thumb|300x300px]] '''Spirit Soul''' (スピリットソウル, ''Supiritto souru'') is a keyword which premiered in [[BS24]]. It is not restricted to any particular color. However, Spirit cards and Brave cards with this effect usually have a low cost to go along with the purpose of being cheap reductions for Ultimates' summon costs. The effect is read as follows: * {{SSoul|Symbol Name (+ Symbol Name)}}
When you're summoning an Ultimate card, this Spirit gains an extra (Any Color/Ultimate) symbol." It is worth noting that since Spirit Soul is not limited to any particular steps, the keyword also functions when summoning Ultimate cards outside of the Main Step, such as via [[High Speed]]. There also exists {{SSoul|∞}}, which allows the Spirit possessing the keyword to gain two extra symbols that match with any of the colors which the summoning Ultimate has. Though the limitation does not usually matter, since currently the only cards possessing {{SSoul|∞}} also have other effects treating all their symbols as any of the six colors. Since Spirit Soul is not a color-specific keyword, a Spirit can stack more than one Spirit Soul on itself. == See Also: == * [[:category:Spirit Soul|List of cards with Spirit Soul]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Ultimate Energy.title: Ultimate Energy
Ultimate Energy.contentSample:
[[File:BS28-X03.png|thumb]]

Soul Drive.fullContent:
[[File:BS33-X02.jpg|thumb|300x300px]]
{{Nihongo|'''Soul Drive'''|ソウルドライブ|Sōru Doraibu}} is an ability that debuted in [[BS33]] together the Sengoku Six Generals. Soul Drives can activate powerful effects, in exchange for removing a player's [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] (Soul Core) from the game. Rather than being restricted to a particular color, it is restricted to Ultimates. Different Soul Drive comes with different timings and conditions, but the most common one is (When Attacks).

The keyword text reads:
* (Timing) {{tk|Soul Drive}} - If you banish the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] (Soul Core) on this Ultimate from the game, (additional effect).
While the text indicates that you "banish the Soul Core from game", in tournaments, the banished Soul Core is put to the Void and the player can't take the Soul Core back from the Void during their core step. Another thing to note is, you can't activate {{tk|Soul Drive}} by depleting the Ultimate, meaning to send the only core on it, Soul Core in this case, to the Void. On the other hand, the LV of the Ultimate when activating {{tk|Soul Drive}} is accounted before actually sending the Soul Core to the Void. Therefore, an Ultimate at LV4 can activate its [LV4] {{tk|Soul Drive}} even if banishing the Soul Core would bring it down to [LV3].

{{tk|Reload}} is an effect that allows player to {{tk|Advent}} onto Spirit-form Braves, which is impossible under normal circumstances. When the Brave card becomes a pre-Advent card, you can immediately fuse the Brave to the Advent Spirit.

Players can decide to have the Brave card with {{tk|Reload}} remaining as a pre-Advent card. Players cannot activate the Brave's (When Summoned) effect if they choose to fuse the Brave to the Advent Spirit, as using the Reload effect does not treat as summoning it.

After the player advents on a Brave card with {{tk|Reload}}, they must first declare whether they will brave it with the Advent Spirit or keep it as a pre-Advent card. Once decided, both players will proceed to resolve (When Advents) and any other effects that trigger on advent.

When those are summoned/advent, the Grandwalker Nexus obtains one core from the Void. Apart from the normal route, Core Charge coul
Core Charge.fullContent:
[[File:Lologwn.jpg|thumb|321x321px]]
'''Core Charge''' ({{ruby|神託|コアチャージ}})<ref>Note: The characters "神託" is originally read as "shintaku (しんたく)" meaning "an oracle".</ref> is a keyword exclusive to Grandwalker Nexuses, debuting in [[SD43]]/[[SD44]]. This effect targets all kinds of card aspects, including families, card types, costs, card names, effects, and so on. When those are summoned/advent, the Grandwalker Nexus obtains one core from the Void. Apart from the normal route, Core Charge could also occur immediately as the Grandwalker Nexus is deployed by sending three cards from the owner's deck to the Trash. 

Their generic text is as follows:

{{tk|Core Charge:|(Condition)}}
* When you Summon/Advent(/Deploy/Use) a target Spirit(/Ultimate/Brave/Nexus/Magic), you can put one core from the Void onto this Nexus.
* When this Nexus is deployed, if you don't control a Grandwalker Nexus with the same card name, you can send three cards from your decktop to the Trash. For each target card among them, put one core from the Void onto this Nexus.

While most of the Grandwalker Nexuses could activate Core Charge via summon/advent/deploy/use of cards without restrictions other than following the conditions, there are individual Grandwalker Nexuses with extra restrictions added to their Core Charge effect. The most common type of such restriction is "core charge via summon/advent only once per turn", a restriction imposed usually when the Core Charge condition is too wide. (e.g. Cost 3 or more) Examples of this kind of Grandwalker Nexuses include [[Grandwalker Lolo]] and [[Producer Lili]]. Another type of restriction concerns the maximum cores that the Grandwalker Nexus can hold, and Core Charge doesn't occur if the number of cores on the Grandwalker Nexus is at a certain amount. Examples of this kind includes [[Grandwalker Antarc]] and [[Nonoin Nillon]]. This is usually applied to limit the number of times one can make use of the {{tk|Grand Skill}} of the Nexusin a single turn.    

Starting in [[BSC32]], Grandwalker Nexuses which charges upon deploying Nexuses have appeared; and starting in [[BS48]], Grandwalker Nexuses which charges upon using Magic cards. 

As also stated below, Core Charge started out to be mandatory besides the deploy charge, but turned into optional from block 6 onward. 

From block 9 (Contract Saga) onward, the core charge text of Grandwalker Nexuses is changed from "put one core from the Void to this Nexus" into "+1 core to this Nexus", such that it causes less confusion on whether effects that restrict increasing cores from the Void can apply to Core Charge or any effects that put cores to Grandwalker Nexuses. 

== Neo-Core Charge ==
[[File:SD68-CX01.png|thumb|321x321px]]
Starting from block 11 (Contract Saga: True), a new type of Core Charge, [[Neo-Core Charge]] appeared. 

'''Neo-Core Charge''' ({{ruby|真・神託|ネオコアチャージ}}), a new variant of the existing effect, [[Core Charge]], is introduced in [[SD68]], and serves as the main gimmick of Contract Grandwalker Nexuses.

Despite having a different name, '''Neo-Core Charge''' is a type of [[Core Charge]], and is affected by any effects that target [[Core Charge]]. The relationship between the two are much like {{tk|Advent}} and {{tk|Grand Advent}}.

The generic text is as follows: 

{{tk|Neo-Core Charge:|(Condition)}}
* When your target Spirit is summoned, you can +1 core to this Nexus.
* (Once per Turn: Same Name) When this Nexus is deployed, you can send three cards from your decktop to the Trash. For each target card among them, +1 core to this Nexus.

While it is still an effect to accumulate cores on Grandwalker Nexuses, there are quite a few differences between the original [[Core Charge]] and Neo-Core Charge.

The first major difference being how the "deploy charge", the part of Core Charge that you can carry out when deploying the Grandwalker Nexus, is now limited to (Once per Turn: Same Name) but doesn't care whether there are other copies of the same Grandwalker Nexus on your Field. While the deploy charge under the old [[Core Charge]] is often something similar to once per game unless the Grandwalker Nexus on your Field are destroyed, the deploy charge under Neo-Core Charge allow players to get an immediate boost for each copy of the same Grandwalker Nexus. This increases the flexibility of Core Charge against removal of cores on Grandwalker Nexuses. (In the past, if you have a copy of Grandwalker Nexus A deployed, and the cores on it get removed, even if you deploy a second copy of Grandwalker A, you can only charge slowly again via the regular summon/advent route. But with Neo-Core Charge, you can get an instant boost when you deploy a second copy Grandwalker A, just like the time when you deploy Grandwalker A for the first time.)

This feature also goes along with the new keyword, Revive, as you can re-deploy one copy of Contract Grandwalker Nexuses from Soul State per turn. A Core Charge that limits to (Once per Turn: Same Name) but doesn't concern whether a second copy is on the Field means that every time you revive a Contract Grandwalker Nexus, you can get an instant charge via the deploy charge route.

The second major difference is how {{tk|Advent}} is removed from the accumulation route of Core Charge in Neo-Core Charge. There can be multiple reasons behind the change. One of them is a balancing concern when the deploy charge of Neo-Core Charge is now (Once per Turn: Same Name) unlike the past. Another possible reason includes how {{tk|Advent}} is removed to separate the new era from the era before, which focused primarily on {{tk|Contract Advent}}. It also contrasts with the Grand Advent era and Ultra Advent era, the first two eras of Grandwalker Nexuses that partly revolves around advents. As the new keyword, Manifest, is essentially a type of summon, it is enough for Neo-Core Charge to react to summons only.

== Important rulings regarding Core Charge: ==

* Unless a card type is specified, all Core Charge conditions only target Spirits.
** e.g. A Core Charge condition with ([[Blade Beast]] & Cost 3 or more) can only target Spirits, and a Core Charge condition with ([[Blade Beast]] & Ultimate) can only target Ultimates.
* A comma in the condition indicates a separate condition of the same card type.
** e.g. In the Core Charge condition ([[Evil Shadow]] & Cost 3 or more, "Bladra"), the Core Charge targets Bladra of any cost. So when a player summons a Cost 0 Bladra, the Core Charge in the example can activate. Having "[[Evil Shadow]] & Cost 3 or more" and "Bladra" within the same bracket simply means both conditions need the same card type, which in this case, Spirit.
* The cards sent to the Trash when a Grandwalker Nexus is deployed are not affected by anti-deck destruction effects, as they are being "sent to the Trash," not "discarded from the deck," much like [[Ultimate Trigger]].
*Effects such as those of [[The DragonMaskOgre Biranba]] and [[Onmyou Child]] '''can't''' affect the cores obtained from Core Charge, but they can affect cores a Grandwalker Nexus's effect puts from the Void to other places (cards on the Field, Reserve and such).
* When multiple target Spirits are summoned at once (such as by the effects of [[The DarkSnakeGodKing Shenmadou]] or [[The GiantCannonMothership Mother-Phaia]]), only one core is added by Core Charge. Core Charge triggers upon timing instead of the number of Spirits summoned.
* Since the Ultra Advent saga, the activation of Core Charge became optional. Due to this, while the text of Core Charge on older Grandwalker Nexus cards does not state the option, their Core Charge is still optional to activate.

Grandphosis.fullContent:
[[File:Shiva.png|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Grandphosis''' ({{Ruby|転神|グランフォーゼ}}, ''Guranfōze, literally translated as "Transformation God" but read as Grandphosis'') is a mechanic introduced in [[SD48]], and a core mechanic in Ultra Advent era together with [[Saga Brave]]. This effect allows the Grandwalker Nexus to act as a Spirit, becoming an additional attacker or blocker that can't be easily removed.  

In the lore, it was first introduced as the signature ability of [[Hindida]] [[Grandwalker|Grandwalkers]], and represents their ability to separate themselves from their world and travel across the Divine World to other Grandwalkers' world without connecting worlds.

Grandphosis effects can trigger in different timings, such as Flash Timing of the player's Attack Step, the start of the player's Attack Step or Flash Timing of the opposing Attack Step, but their common text reads as follows:

*'''Grandphosis: X''' [LV1][LV2] (Send X cores from this Nexus to the Void) During this turn, this Nexus is also treated as Spirit with [LV1][LV2] xxxx BP, and can only be destroyed by Grandwalker Nexuses.

Like {{tk|Unleash}} and other similar effects, while the general text are common, various additional text can be attached to the actual effect depending on individual cards. 

Despite being treated as a Spirit, the Grandwalker in Grandphosis maintains its immunity to any effects which do not target Grandwalker Nexuses and will not be destroyed if blocked by a Spirit with higher BP. However, when two Grandwalkers in Grandphosis state battle, the one with lower BP will be destroyed like normal Spirit battles. 

While in a Grandphosed state, a Grandwalker Nexus can activate the spirit-specific effect of a [[Saga Brave|Saga]] family brave as well as the nexus-specific effect due to being treated as a spirit and a nexus at the same time. Concerning {{tk|During Spirit Brave}} effects, those with the clause "This Spirit XXX" can apply when a Grandwalker in Grandphosis state meet the timing and condition, e.g. (When Attacks). However, Grandwalker in Grandphosis state won't be affected by {{tk|During Spirit Brave}} effects that state "'''Your Spirits''' XXX", as the effect doesn't target the Grandwalker specifically. 

If the Saga Brave includes effect like {{tk|Unleash}}, you can send cores from your ''other Grandwalker Nexus''  (but not itself) to your Grandwalker Nexus in Grandphosis state.

Type: Flower.fullContent:
[[File:Primose.png|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Type: Flower''' (タイプ：華, ''Taipu: Hana'') is a type of Magic cards introduced in [[BS48]]. The effects of Type: Flower magics vary, but all of them have the effect to treat themselves as in the [[Fairy]] family, as well the ability to stay on the field. Unlike {{tk|Type: Song}} magic cards, the action of putting a {{tk|Type: Flower}} magic onto the Field is compulsory.

From [[BS48]] onwards, there are Fairy Spirits that have effects which rely on having these magics staying field. They are also a main source of Core Charge of [[Grandwalker Aphrodite]]. Each {{tk|Type: Flower}} magic card also has a name and illustration referencing a specific Fairy Spirit, such as [[Primrose Field]] is related to [[Godseeker GrandflowerFairy Primula]]. 

Unlike {{tk|Type: Song}} Magics which do not have effects while being placed on Field, all {{tk|Type: Flower}} Magic cards come with continuous effects that are active while being placed on the Field. And there are also {{tk|Type: Flower}} effects that upgrade itself when the number of {{tk|Type: Flower}} Magic cards on Field increases. Image-wise, it feels like planting various flowers on the Field, fitting the theme's nature.  

A card having {{tk|Type: Flower}} is counted as having a printed effect. However, if an effect leads to the card losing effects, or can't activate its effects, the {{tk|Type: Flower}} aspect it has won't be affected, and the card is still treated as having {{tk|Type: Flower}}.

'''Type: Field''' (タイプ：フィールド, ''taipu: fīrudo'') is a type of Magic cards introduced in [[BS49]], but their prototype concept was introduced in [[BS19]] with a cycle of Field-named cards, such as [[Flame Field]]. They're partially regular Magic cards, which at the end of their Main/Flash effect state they're placed on the Field upon resolving.

The On-Field effect is a passive effect which affects the player(s), and generally consists of anti-meta effects to counter specific decks or color mechanics, such as preventing deck discarding, unblockable attacks and anti-Grandwalker Nexus effects.

While usually unable to be affected by anything once on-field, effects such as [[The VenomKnight Blister]], [[The RedRockKing Boanefel]] and [[The UnderworldExecutioner Carno]] can discard on-field Magic cards.

Like every "Type:" card, even if its effects are negated, it still possesses its type and can be targeted/counted for effects which require it.

'''Release''' (解封, ''literally "kaifou", but read as "ririisu"'') is a keyword exclusive to [[Grandstone Nexus|Grandstone Nexuses]], debuting in [[BS54]]. This effect targets all kinds of card aspects, including families, card types, costs, card names, effects, and so on. When the Release condition is fulfilled, the Grandstone Nexus obtains one core from the Void. Release occurs immediately when the conditions is fulfilled, gaining one core from the Void. Afterwards, a Grandstone Nexus can flip itself through [[Rebirth]] when there are enough cores on it. The generic text is as follows: 

* '''''Release: ([condition])'''''   ◆When the Release condition is fulfilled, you can put one core from the Void to this Nexus.

Important ruling regarding Release:

* [[The DragonMaskOgre Biranba]] and [[Onmyou Child]] can't affect the cores obtained from Release, but they can affect cores a Grandstone Nexus puts to other places (cards on the field, Reserve and such).
* When multiple target Spirits are summoned at once (such as by the effects of [[The DarkSnakeGodKing Shenmadou]] or [[The GiantCannonMothership Mother-Phaia]]), only one core is added by Release.

For more Q&As on the Release keyword, check the Q&A section in [[Grandstone Nexus]].

█ ''[additional effect]''. While the keyword name is pronounced as "Brave Engage", the literal meaning of the keyword can be interpreted as "the contract with the Brave", tying into the lore of the Contract era, extending to Spirits owning their own dedicated Braves, similar to the concept of [[Saga Brave|Saga Braves]]. The Braves with {{tk|Brave Engage}} are called the "Engage Braves". Despite started out exclusive to normal Braves, the ability has extended to [[Saga Brave]] with [[BS70]]. And instead of requiring a Spirit with a certain Contract card as pre-advent card, the Brave Engage of [[Saga Brave]] required the player to brave it to a certain Grandwalker Nexus, and may come with a core requirement. With the "once per game" limitation, all current Brave Engage variants possess extremely powerful effects, ranging from drawing three cards with no cost to a potential five-core boost. Not to mention all these effects are given to decks in which the main colour does not usually own the abilities in which Brave Engage can give, such as core-boosting in a Red deck, or hand-filtering in a White deck. == Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |1 |What is "Brave Engage"? |It is an effect unique to the "[[Engage]]" family Braves, which can activate when braving with specific targets. |- |2 |Is '''Brave Engage''' a Brave effect, similar to a Brave's (When Summoned) effect? |No, '''Brave Engage''' is considered a Spirit effect activated from a Brave Spirit. As that is the case, when braving to a Spirit that is affected by a "Spirits can't activate effects" effect, '''Brave Engage''' cannot activate. |- |3 |While [[The AstralZeroSword Foranswer]] is braved to [[The Zero Partner, Wiz]], when you [[Contract Advent]] onto Wiz, can '''Brave Engage''' activate? |No, it cannot. In this case, you have to separate the Brave first, then brave it again to trigger '''Brave Engage'''. |- |4 |Can '''Brave Engage''' activate when a Brave is braved to the correct target during swapping of Braves? |Yes, it can. |- |5 |When summoning and direct-braving to the correct target, between '''Brave Engage''' and a "when a Brave is summoned" effect, which one activates first? |As both types of effects activate at the same time, the turn player decides the order. |} == See Also: == * [[:Category:Brave Engage|List of cards with Brave Engage]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

{{tk|Revive}} '''Main -''' (Once per Turn: Same Name) You can deploy this card from Soul State. As the name implies, it is an effect that allows you to "revive" the Grandwwalker Nexuses that have entered Soul State after being removed by the opponent. While Grandwalker removal has been
Revive.fullContent:
[[File:SD68-CX01.png|thumb|300px]] '''Revive''' ({{ruby|復活|ふっかつ}}) is a new keyword introduced in [[SD68]] that serves as the main gimmick of Contract Grandwalker Nexuses. The generic text is as follows:
{{tk|Revive}} '''Main -''' (Once per Turn: Same Name) You can deploy this card from Soul State. As the name implies, it is an effect that allows you to "revive" the Grandwwalker Nexuses that have entered Soul State after being removed by the opponent. While Grandwalker removal has been very rare in the past when Grandwalker Nexuses were first introduced, it is no longer a rare effect at this point of game. So when Grandwalker Nexus is going to become the focus of the game again with Contract Grandwalker Nexuses, how to revive the destroyed Grandwalker Nexuses becomes the major issue to tackle with. Unlike Contract Spirit and Contract Ultimate, Contract Grandwalker Nexuses don't come with {{tk|Contract Advent}} to return them to the field. While there can be other effects that allow player to re-deploy Grandwalker Nexuses from Soul State (e.g. [[The SunDragon Drago-Sole]]), it would be very inconveient to rely on those when it takes time for Grandwalker Nexuses to acumulate cores. Making use of the Soul State concept introduced by [[Contract Card]] and matching it with Grandwalker Nexuses' nature, '''Revive''' is established as a keyword to help the Contract Grandwalker Nexuses to come back over and over again on their own. Since '''Revive''' is a way of deploying the Grandwalker Nexuses, [[Neo-Core Charge]] can be triggered immediately upon the deploy as long as no Grandwalker Nexus of the same name has activated that in the same turn. While the effect is stiraghtforward enough, there are still a few points to note: 1) Unless otherwise specified, '''Revive''' requires the player to pay the cost of the card.

2) It is an (Once per Turn: Same Name) effect, so you can only re-deploy one even if you have multiple copies of the same Contract Grandwalker Nexus in Soul State. == Also See == * [[:Category:Revive|List of cards with Revive]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Contract Skill.fullContent:
[[File:SD68-CX01.png|thumb|200px]] '''Contract Skill''' ({{Ruby|契約技|コントラクトスキル}}), is a keyword introduced in [[SD68]], being one of the main gimmicks of Contract Grandwalker Nexuses. The general form is as follows: * {{cs|X}} [Level] (Timing)
(Send X cores from this Nexus to the void) ''Additional effects'' As the name and effect implies, '''Contract Skill''' is a remake of [[Grand Skill]], corresponding to the Contract Grandwalker Nexuses this time. While it is still triggered by sending the designated amount of cores from the Grandwalker Nexus to the Void, and the effect timing or effect contents differ between each Contract Skill, all of them come with a counter increase effect. Unlike [[Grand Skill]] which either shares equal importance with [[Grand Field]] or serves purely as a magic-alike effect, '''Contract Skill''' is a main source of counter gain in the decks using Contract Grandwalker Nexuses, and are crucial to build up the counters for [[Contract Field]]. While [[Grand Skill]] often conflicts with [[Grand Field]] that requires cores on Grandwalker Nexuses such that players are forced into a dilemma of choosing, using '''Contract Skill''' actively in turns contribute to a faster building of [[Contract Field]], making the two effect similar on the surface but very different in actual uses. Unlike the relationship between [[Neo-Core Charge]] and [[Core Charge]], '''Contract Skill''' is a brand-new effect that is '''NOT''' counted as a variant of [[Grand Skill]]. Hence, effects that target [[Grand Skill]] don't work on '''Contract Skill'''. == Also See == [[:Category:Contract Skill|List of cards with Contract Skill]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

(Additional Effects) As the name and effect implies, '''Contract Field''' is a remake of [[Grand Field]], corresponding to the Contract Grandwalker Nexuses this time. Much like [[Grand Field]], it is a lasting passive effect that
Contract Field.fullContent:
[[File:SD68-CX01.png|thumb|200px]] '''Contract Field''' ({{Ruby|契約域|コントラクトフィールド}}), is a keyword introduced in [[SD68]], being one of the main gimmicks of Contract Grandwalker Nexuses. The general form is as follows: * {{tk|Contract Field}} '''[LV2] (Timing)'''
(Additional Effects) As the name and effect implies, '''Contract Field''' is a remake of [[Grand Field]], corresponding to the Contract Grandwalker Nexuses this time. Much like [[Grand Field]], it is a lasting passive effect that works like normal nexuses as a support to the family the Grandwalker Nexus supports. However, unlike [[Grand Field]] which is often a LV2 effect that requires a specific number of cores on the Grandwalker Nexuses to unlock the effect, or a LV1 effect that requirees sending cores from the Grandwalker Nexus to the Void, '''Contract Field''', despite being a LV2 effect mostly, is unlocked by achieving a certain number of counters. When compared to effects that remove cores on Grandwalker Nexuses, there are very few effects that reduce opponents' counters. This means that as long as the player has reached a certain number of counters, '''Contract Field''' would be active regardless of whether the Contract Grandwalker Nexus is ''just'' deployed the same turn. As one may have already noticed by this point, it synergizes very well with another keyword, [[Revive]], which allows you to re-deploy destroyed Grandwalker Nexuses from Soul State. By having Contract Field tied to counters instead of cores on the Grandwalker Nexus, it makes '''Contract Field''' an immediately accessible effect once the Grandwalker Nexus is revived, and doesn't require further preparations ([[Grand Field]] that requires a number of cores on Grandwalker Nexuses doesn't work as cores on a Grandwalker Nexus will be sent to the Void once they are destroyed). With the new design, '''Contract Field''' is now more an outcome obtained by using the [[Contract Skill|Contract Skills]] frequently to add counters, and does not clash with the use of cores on Grandwalker Nexuses via [[Unleash]] or any other effect that sends cores from own Grandwalker Nexuses to the Void. Unlike the relationship between [[Neo-Core Charge]] and [[Core Charge]], it is to note that '''Contract Field''' is a brand-new effect, which is '''NOT''' counted as a variant of [[Grand Field]]. Hence, effects that target [[Grand Field]] don't work on '''Contract Field'''. == Also See == [[:Category:Contract Field|List of cards with Contract Field]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

'''Awaken''' (覚醒, ''Kakusei'') also known as ''Evolution'' in the English release, is a special ability of Red. Spirits with Awaken have this text: 
*'''Flash - '''{{tk|Awaken}} You can put any number of cores from Spirits you control to this Spirit.

{{tk|Awaken}} allows Red to compensate for not being a core generator, by moving around cores. It also allows a player to employ surprise tactics by leveling up their Spirits to surpass certain walls by either increasing their BP or gaining an useful effect of some sort. In the process of using Awaken, a player can also deplete its own spirits, which is used as a gimmick in the later development of the mechanic in Burning Soul era. The ability first appears on spirits only, then proceed to appear on braves as well. 

At the beginning of Constellation era, a new variant of Awaken, {{tk|Ultra Awaken}}, was introduced together with [[The PhantomStarDragon Gai-Asura]]. Entering the Ultimate era, another new variant of Awaken, {{tk|True-Awaken}}, appeared in game together with [[Ultimate-Siegfried]]. It centers around Ultimates instead. 

Examples of cards with the {{tk|Awaken}} ability include: [[Taurusknight]], [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried]], and [[The SengokuGoldDragon Ragou]].

Clash.fullContent:
[[File:SD01-008.jpg|200px|thumb]] == Introduction == '''Clash''' (激突, ''Gekitotsu'') is a keyword premiered in [[SD01]] and primarily owned by [[Red]] cards with a few exceptions. It is the second wave of major keyword for [[Red]], appearing after {{tk|Awaken}}. The name, 激突, means a "fierce clash" between two objects/persons, and is well-translated into the effect for being what forces the opponent to block if possible. It was once rendered into ''Rage'' by Bandai when English cards were still printed, which actually deviated from the original meaning of the keyword. Hence, the translation of the keyword is changed to {{tk|Clash}} for all cards with Japanese versions. == Renditions == As an old enough keyword, it experienced changes of wordings throughout the years. These changes, however, do not affect the actual effect of {{tk|Clash}}, but only changing it to make it clearer and easier to understand. The oldest version reads: * '''[Level]''' {{tk|Clash}} '''(When Attacks)'''
The opponent must block if possible. In Burning Soul era, the keyword is errata-ed to differentiate it better with {{tk|True-Clash}}: * '''[Level]''' {{tk|Clash}} '''(When Attacks)'''
The opponent must block with their Spirits if possible. However, Ultimates don't have to to block. In God-King era, the keyword is further reworded to avoid the confusion that it is a player-targeting effect, as it is actually targeting those Spirits on the Field, not the player: * '''[Level]''' {{tk|Clash}} '''(When Attacks)'''
Opposing Spirits must block if possible. And with the introduction of Standard Format, the newest wording in Standard with the new timing {{ST|During Attack}}, becomes: * '''[Level]''' {{tk|Clash}} {{ST|During Attack}}
Opposing Spirits must block if possible. == Merits & Demerits == As a keyword that forces opposing Spirits to block, it maximizes the BP-increasing effects that are prominent in Red, and works to remove opposing Spirits in a way different from effect removal. This prevents the opponent from activating effects related to Spirits being removed from the Field due to opposing effects, and bypasses effects that protect the Spirits from being destroyed by opposing effects. Another major merit of {{tk|Clash}} lies in how it prevents the opponent from taking life for the attack as long as they have Spirits available to block on Field. This allows the player to put the opponent into a dilemma when they are summoning new Spirits on their turn, as they shall fall prey to {{tk|Clash}} if they remain refreshed in the next turn. By using {{tk|Clash}}, players can avoid taking too many lives at an early stage, thus giving too many core resources to the opponent, while activating all effects related to attack declaration. This matches with [[Red]]'s style of effects like "'''(When Attacks)''' Draw a card" a lot, and contribute to a no-risk removal plan. An interesting way to use {{tk|Clash}} is also how, by forcing the opponent to block, it affects the opponent's planned order of blocking. By using Spirits with {{tk|Clash}} to bait high BP blockers to block means it is easier for your other Spirits with lower BP but possibly stronger effects to go through. Hence, it can also be used as a strategy to avoid the other Spirits being destroyed by the opposing blockers. Despite so, the weaknesses of {{tk|Clash}} are also obvious: (1) If the opponent controls no refreshed Spirits, they don't have to block; and (2) since it forces the opponent to block, it means it isn't taking a life. For (1), new effects like "opponent can block while exhausted" are introduced later to cover the loophole, and those [[White]] Spirits which can naturally block while exhausted would fall prey. However, it is worth noting that for Spirits that "can't block" due to rulings or effects, since "can't" is prioritized over "must", they won't be blocking your cards with {{tk|Clash}} regardless. For (2), the effect is often paired with "when only the opposing Spirit is destroyed by comparing BP, send an opposing Life to the Reserve" effects, or "refresh this Spirit when blocked" for the exact reason, so that you can still do the kill although your attack is blocked. While it was at times overshined by direct target-attack effects, {{tk|Clash}} has the merit of being a passive effect that lasts during the entire battle, and doesn't target a single Spirit, meaning that it won't trigger effects like {{tk|Yata-no-Kagami}}, and can come into effect immediately during an attack when the card suddenly gains {{tk|Clash}}. As a signature keyword and mechanic of [[Red]], the keyword has multiple variants created after it: * [[True-Clash]] * [[Twinkle Clash]] * [[Clash X]] * [[Ultra Clash]] * [[Supreme Clash]] == Also See == * [[:Category:Clash|List of cards with Clash]] * [[:Category:Clash support|List of cards supporting Clash]] == Trivia == * [[Dan Bashin]], the protagonist of [[Battle Spirits Shounen Gekiha Dan]], earned his name of "Clash King" for being famous of using Spirits with {{tk|Clash}}. == Navigation == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]
