Burst.fullContent:
[[File:BS14-X01.jpg|thumb|320x320px]]
''For rulings concerning the Mirage keyword, please check [[Mirage]].''

'''Burst''' (バースト, ''Bāsuto'') is a game mechanic which debuted along with the [[Battle Spirits Heroes]] anime. It is an effect that all types of cards may have. Cards with Burst are placed face down in the Burst Area, content unknown to the opponent, and activated under specific circumstances (such as when you lose a life). Each Burst effect varies on each card. For example, the Burst effect of [[The HeroDragon Lord-Dragon]] simply summons itself, while the Burst effect of [[The DragonHero Sieg-Yamato-Fried]] can also destroy an opposing Spirit. The Burst effects of Magic cards always have a part of the effect which allow them to also activate their main/flash effects. All cards with Burst can also be played as regular cards.

Burst is the most common keyword in the whole game, and became the third effect category after main and flash effects.

There are three separate keywords which derived from Burst, them being [[Burst Tribute]], [[Soul Burst]], and [[Burst Seal]] (more information can be seen below). When an effect targets a card with Burst, cards with the above three keywords can also be targeted.

Each card usually only has one Burst condition, but [[BS46]] introduced cards which carry two different Burst conditions each.

==Handling Burst==
Once per turn during your Main Step, you can set down a card with Burst from your hand facedown onto your Burst Area. You cannot set down a card with Burst from the Removed Zone. Furthermore, you can only have one set Burst at a time. You can also set a Burst with effects, such as the effect of [[The IceHero Mibrock-Baragan]], ignoring the number of times you've set down the Burst manually in the same turn. When there is already a set Burst, you can discard it and set down a new one. However, you cannot discard the set Burst without setting a new one.

When the Burst condition is fulfilled, you can declare its activation by flipping it up. However, the actual Burst effect only activates after the event that triggers it is resolved. For example, an opposing Spirit activates its (When Summoned) effect. You can then declare your Burst with the condition [After an opposing Spirit's (When Summoned) effect activates]. However, the Burst effect only activates after the summon effect is resolved. To further extend the example, say the summon effect destroys your Spirit, and your Spirit activates its (When Destroyed) effect. Your Burst effect also has to wait until the destroyed effect is resolved, as the trigger of the destroyed effect stems from the summon effect.

In the case of Burst with the condition [After your Spirit is destroyed by the opponent], the destroyed Spirit must be placed in the trash for the Burst to activate. If the destroyed Spirit remains on the field, or is sent to other places that is not the trash, the Burst condition is not fulfilled, and it is flipped back facedown, treating as no Burst activated.

When both players declare their Burst activations at the same time, same as the rules of flash timing, the defensive side is prioritised to activate their Burst effect. Therefore, it is important to ask your opponent if they have a Burst activation to declare before you declare yours.

The declaration of Burst activation and the activation of Burst effect are different timings. However, when declaring a Burst, the player must flip up the Burst. Burst placed facedown is referred as a "set Burst", while a face-up Burst activating its effect is referred as an "activated Burst". Until the Burst effect activates, the Burst is considered "set", even when it is face-up due to declaration. When an effect simply refers to a "set card", the set Burst is included.

All Spirit cards, Ultimate cards, Brave cards summoned, and Nexus cards deployed, through Burst effects do not require summon or deploy costs. However, this was not stated in the effect texts until block icon 2 (Burning Legend era).

All Burst effects can be prevented by immunity effects such as [[Armor]]. However, it is also important to note that the Burst Area is not considered within the field. So, when a Burst effect activates and the field of the same side does not have a symbol with the same color as the Burst, [[Heavy Armor]]: ∞ which references symbol colors on the opposing field, cannot prevent that Burst effect.

When activating a Magic Burst effect, the situation is considered "activating Burst" instead of "using Magic", and therefore cannot be countered by [[Ice Wall]] and similar effects, and is not limited by effects such as that of [[The Absorption Triumphal Arch]]. The main/flash effect activated through the Burst effect is also considered part of the Burst effect. For example, if you activate the Burst effect of [[Burst Draw]] to draw two cards, then activate its main effect through the Burst effect to draw two more cards, it is considered drawing four cards through one effect.

As long the Burst condition is met, the Burst can be activated even if the conditions ''within'' the Burst effect do not meet. In this case, the Burst is considered activated, but no effects are exerted. For example, when you declare the Burst activation of [[The DragonHero Sieg-Yamato-Fried]] (original version) at three lives, but before that the Lv2 effect of [[The Constellation Barrier]] increases your life to four, Yamato cannot destroy any Spirit nor can it be summoned, and is sent to the trash.

Ultimate cards can activate their Burst effects without meeting the summon conditions. When they cannot be summoned, they are sent to the trash after their Burst effects resolve.

== Unaffected Burst ==
Burst may receive protection with effects like "This set card is unaffected by any effects", or in the case of activating from hand, "Your hand is unaffected by opposing effects".

When the "unaffected" effect exists only on the Burst card itself (therefore unknown to the opponent), when opposing effects such as "Discard an opposing Burst", "Return an opposing Burst to the hand", or "Look at the opposing Burst" target your Burst, you are required to flip up the Burst to confirm with the opponent that your Burst is unaffected by the effect. Then you flip it back down, keeping it set. In this case, effects with the "When this effect can't discarded" clause can activate, but effects with the clause "Look at the Burst, if it is a Spirit card" etc cannot activate.

While being unaffected, Burst can be activated normally even if there's a "Burst cannot activate" effect active, as this kind of effects targets the cards themselves. In the game, there are effects with the clause "When a Burst activates, discard it", which are also useless towards unaffected Burst.

However, on the other hand, effects such as "The opponent cannot activate their Burst unless they pay the cost of that card" or "The opponent cannot activate Burst effects" are player-targeting effects, and hence unaffected Burst cannot prevent those, if the unaffected effects include the clause "when set".

==Burst Conditions==
*'''After your Life is reduced'''
**Burst with this condition can be activated after your life is reduced and all effects triggered by the life decrease are resolved. However, if there is another Burst activation before this one, you cannot declare this one.
*'''After an opposing Spirit's (When Summoned) effect resolves''' / '''After an opposing Spirit/Ultimate's (When Summoned) effect resolves'''  / '''After an opposing Spirit/Brave's (When Summoned) effect resolves'''  / '''After an opposing Spirit's (When Summoned/Advents) effect resolves''' / '''After an opposing Spirit's (When Summoned/Reborn) effect resolves'''
**Burst with this kind of condition can be activated after the (When Summoned), (When Advents) or (When Reborn) effect and all other effects triggered by it are resolved. However, if there is another Burst activation before this one, you cannot declare this one.
**If the (When Summoned), (When Advents) or (When Reborn) effect is optional, and the opponent chooses not to activate it, you cannot activate your Burst with this kind of condition.
*'''After your Spirit is destroyed by the opponent''' / '''After your Ultimate is destroyed by the opponent''' / '''After your Spirit/Ultimate is destroyed by the opponent''' / '''After your Spirit is depleted/destroyed by the opponent''' / '''After your Ultimate is depleted/destroyed by the opponent''' / '''After your "[[Diva]]" family Spirit is destroyed by the opponent'''
**You can declare the Burst activation of this kind of condition after the Spirit/Ultimate is depleted/destroyed and is confirmed by both players that it will be sent to the trash. Also, the Burst activation has to come in before effects of the next timing activate. However, if there is another Burst activation before this one, you cannot declare this one.
**If the depleted/destroyed Spirit/Ultimate remains on the field through effects, or it is placed into other places that are not the trash, Burst of this kind of condition cannot activate.
*'''After an opposing Spirit attacks''' / '''After an opposing Spirit/Ultimate attacks'''
**Burst of this kind of condition can be activated after all (When Attacks) effects and other effects triggered by those effects are resolved. However, if there is another Burst activation before this one, you cannot declare this one.
**If the attacking Spirit/Ultimate is removed from the Field before the Burst effect can activate, Burst of these conditions cannot activate.
*'''After the opposing Hand increases with an opposing effect'''
**Burst of this condition can be activated after the opposing effect which increase the hand and other effects triggered by that effect are resolved.
**Burst of this condition can activate upon effects such as "Draw two cards, then discard two cards from your hand".
**"Increase the amount of cards you draw by +1" effects during Draw Step are changing the number of cards drawn through game rules in Draw Step, but not directly increasing the hand, hence Burst of this condition cannot be activated upon these effects.
*'''After you or the opponent uses [[Seal]]'''
**If the Seal effect activates on attack, Burst of this condition waits until all (When Attacks) effects and other effects triggered by those effects are resolved, and is activated before flash timing. While for Seal effects activating on summon, Burst of this condition waits until all (When Summoned) effects and other effects triggered by those effects are resolved.
*'''After a Spirit/Brave is summoned by an opposing effect'''
**Burst of this condition is activated after the effect which summoned the Spirits/Braves and all other effects triggered by that effect are resolved.
**If the summoned Spirits/Braves are removed from the Field before the Burst effect activates, Burst of this kind of condition cannot activate.
*'''After an opposing [[Grand Skill]] resolves'''
**Burst of this condition is activated after the declared Grand Skill and all other effects triggered by the Grand Skill are resolved.

== Extra Rules ==

* When a player is found out they set down a card without Burst, they immediately lose the game.
* When the set card is returned to the hand or deck, the owner must reveal it to the opponent to confirm with each other that it has the Burst keyword. If the set card is found to not include the keyword, that player immediately loses the game.
* When the game ends, both players must reveal their set cards to confirm with each other that those set cards have the Burst keyword. If the set cards are found to not include the keyword, the player(s) immediately lose the game.

== Burst Tribute ==
[[File:BS18-X01.jpg|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Burst Tribute''' (バースト{{ruby|転|てん}}{{ruby|召|しょう}} ; ''Bāsuto tenshō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS18]], possessed exclusively by [[The SuperHero Lord-Dragon-Saviour]]. As the name suggests, the keyword is a combination of Burst and [[Tribute]], which means that when summoning the Spirit card via the Burst effect, another Spirit on the same Field must be depleted as a condition to enable the summon. It also means the card with Burst Tribute is simultaneously treated as a card with the Burst keyword, and a card with the Tribute keyword. Hence, the card with Burst Tribute is subjected to effects which target Burst or Tribute.

== Soul Burst ==
[[File:SD31-009.jpg|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Soul Burst''' (Sバースト) is a keyword introduced in [[SD31]]. All five card types in the game has this keyword. Cards with Soul Burst are treated as cards with Burst, and are subjected to effects which target Burst. The difference is that unlike regular Burst, set cards with Soul Burst can be activated at will with "[[Catalyze]]"-named effects.

== Burst Seal ==
[[File:The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison.jpg|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Burst Seal''' (バースト{{ruby|封|ふう}}{{ruby|印|いん}} ; ''Bāsuto fūin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS38]], possessed exclusively by [[The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison]]. As the name suggests, the keyword is a combination of Burst and [[Seal]]. As such, part of the Burst effect involves sending the Soul Core to Life. It also means the card with Burst Seal is simultaneously treated as a card with the Burst keyword, and a card with the Seal keyword. Hence, the card with Burst Seal is subjected to effects which target Burst or Seal.

'''Type: Song''' (タイプ：{{Ruby|歌|ソング}}, ''Taipu: Songu'') is a special type of magic card that premiered in [[BSC18]]. The effect of Type: Song magics vary, but most have the ability to be put onto the Field after they are used. Numerous [[Diva]] family cards could activate various effects depending on whether there is a '''Type: Song''' Magic card on the Field, or the number of such Magic cards. All '''Type: Song''' Magic cards have the illustrations of Divas on them. As the name tells, these magic cards are mainly representing songs sung by the Divas, and the names of quite a number of them are based on actual songs and melodies.  

A card having '''Type: Song''' is counted as having a printed effect. However, if an effect leads to the card losing effects, or can't activate its effects, the Type: Song aspect it has won't be affected, and the card is still treated as having Type: Song.

'''Consecutive Blade''' (連刃, ''Renjin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS31]], acting as a modified version of [[Clash]]. It requires the use of [[Soul Core]], while battling two Spirits/Ultimates at once. It's a keyword exclusive to Red Spirits, and [[Souldragon]]s in particular. 

It has the following effect: 

* '''Consecutive Blade''' (When Attacks) By sending [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]](Soul Core) from this Spirit to your Trash, your opponent must block with two of their Spirits or Ultimates if possible, and simultaneously battle this Spirit.

Since Consecutive Blade doesn't have a specific duration for the effect, if the LV is brought down to lower than what the effect requires in the process of sending the Soul Core to Trash, the effect would be invalidated. Also, while Consecutive Blade forces the opponent to block with two Spirits/Ultimates, the effect also works if the opponent controls only one Spirit/Ultimate.

Infinite Blade.fullContent:
[[File:BS33-X01.jpg|thumb|200px]]
'''Infinite Blade''' (無限刃, ''Mugenjin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS33]].

Spirits with the keyword have the following effect:
*'''(Your Attack Step)'''  While there is [[File: Soul Core.png|20px]] (Soul Core) on this Spirit, this Spirit can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. When you do, this Spirit doesn't exhaust. 

This means that unless you choose to attack the life, the owner of the effect is capable of making unlimited attacks, so long as it doesn't get destroyed in the process. Attacking without exhausting also implies that it won't trigger any effects that happens when "opposing Spirit exhausts", which typically includes Purple's draw nexuses and Green's reactive effects. Do note that, however, the owner of the effect still need to "be able to attack" in the first place. Hence, if it is exhausted to begin with, you can't activate {{tk|Infinite Blade}} to attack under normal circumstances. 

Currently, the only card with this effect is [[The MasterSwordsmanDragon Samurai-Dragon-Amatsu]].

In [[BS73]], the keyword is upgraded into [[Infinite Unleash]], and possessed by Amatsu's remake, [[The MasterSwordsmanDragon Samurai-Dragon-Amatsu X]].

Infinite Flame.fullContent:
[[File:Souldragon.jpg|thumb|320x320px]] '''Infinite Flame''' (無限焔, ''Mugen Homura'') is a keyword which will debut in [[SD40]]. The only Spirit to possess it is [[The NinjaHead Souldragon-Hokage]]. The keyword's text reads: * '''(When Attacks)''' You may target and attack an opposing Spirit. When the battling Spirit is depleted/destroyed during this battle, for every Symbol on this Spirit, send one core from the opposing Life to the Reserve, and refresh this Spirit.
1. What is Infinite Flame?
It is an effect where you target attack an opposing spirit. When the blocked spirit is depleted/destroyed, for each symbol of this spirit, send 1 core from your opponent's life to the reserve and this spirit will refresh itself. 2. If I did not specify a target spirit to attack when activating Infinite Flame, can I send cores from my opponent's life to reserve and refresh itself, after spirit that blocked this spirit were depleted/destroyed?
No, you cannot. If you did not specify a targeted spirit the attack with [Infinite Flame], the effect will not be activated. 3. If the opponent targeted spirit is depleted/destroyed before the blocking occurs, can I send cores from my opponent's life to reserve and refresh itself?
No, you cannot. [Infinite Flame] will not activate unless it is blocked by the specified/targeted spirit. 4. When this spirit activated [Infinite flame], during BP comparison, it has the same BP as the specified/targeted spirit. As both spirits are destroyed, can I send cores from my opponent's life to reserve?

Zero Counter.fullContent:
[[File:BS44-RV009.png|thumb|223x223px]] [[File:BS44-096.png|thumb|left|222x222px]] '''Zero Counter''' (ゼロカウンター, Zero kauntā) is a keyword which debuted in [[BS44]]. The keyword's text reads: * '''Zero Counter''' - When the opponent summons a Spirit/Brave without paying the cost, other than by a Burst effect. this card in your hand can be used without paying the cost and immediately activate the following effect.
█ '''''Effect'''''. After this effect resolves, by paying ''X'' cost, return this card to your hand. Later, in [[BS51]], another set of '''Zero Counter''' cards appeared with six Revival cards. Unlike previous '''Zero Counter''' that destroys or ends the step, the new set of '''Zero Counter''' bounces the target to bottom of deck. And the text for returning the '''Zero Counter''' cards back to hand is altered from "After this effect resolves" to "Then". So far there are four different effects released: # '''Destroy one opposing Spirit'''. After this effect resolves, by paying '''one''' cost, return this card to your hand. # '''Immediately end this Step'''. After this effect resolves, by paying '''two''' cost, return this card to your hand. # '''Destroy opposing Spirits up to a total of 10000 BP.''' After this effect resolves, by paying '''one''' cost, return this card to your hand. # '''Return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom.''' '''Then''', by paying '''one''' cost, return this card to your hand. == Q&A == Q1. What is '''Zero Counter'''?
A1. It is an effect that can be used without paying the cost when opponent summons Spirit/Brave without paying the cost, other than by a Burst effect. '''Zero Counter''' activates before (When Summoned) effects. Q2. Between '''Zero Counter''' effect and (When Summoned) effect of opponents Spirit/Brave that was summoned without paying the cost, other than by a Burst effect, which will be resolved first?
A2. '''Zero Counter''' will be resolved first. However, when facing removal effects, the summoned Spirit's "[[Armor]]"-named effects or "unaffected" effects are in activation before '''Zero Counter'''. Q3. When the Summoned Spirit/Brave is destroyed by '''Zero Counter''', even when it has a (When Summoned) effect, it isn't activated and is sent to trash?
A3. Yes, that is correct. Other effects that trigger when a Spirit is summoned, such as the [[Core Charge]] of Grandwalker Nexuses, also cannot activate before '''Zero Counter'''. Q4. When using '''Zero Counter''' effect that immediately end the step, does the step ends without activating the summoned Spirit's/Brave's (When Summoned) effect?
A4. Yes. When '''Zero Counter''' effect that immediately end the step is activated, only the effects of '''Zero Counter''' and any other effect derived from/against '''Zero Counter''' will be resolved. At that time, any other effects that is not related to '''Zero Counter''' aren't resolved, such as (When Summoned) effect or any other effect derived from the summon of a Spirit / Brave (e.g. [[The Rose Blooming in the Lake]] - add core from void to the nexus when a cost 4 or higher green spirit is summoned). Q5. When opponent uses '''Zero Counter''' effect that immediately end the step, then pays two cost to return the Magic card to hand (e.g. Revival [[Thorn Prison]]), can you activate "After your opponent increases their hand due to their effects" effects?
A5. Yes, you can, because it is derived against opponent's '''Zero Counter'''. Q6. When opponent uses '''Zero Counter''' effect that immediately end the step, then pays two cost to return the Magic card to hand (i.e, Revival [[Thorn Prison]]), can you activate Burst that triggers with the condition [After your opponent increases their hand due to their effects]?
A6. Yes, you can, because it is derived against opponent's '''Zero Counter'''. Q7. When the opponent is using '''Zero Counter''' effect that immediately end the step, can they activate his Burst that trigger with the condition [After a Spirit/Brave is summoned by opposing effects] (i.e. [[The Valkyrie Schwertlaute]])?
A7. As the [[Burst]] is derived from the summon of your Spirit/Brave, the Burst can't be activated and the step will end. Q8. When using '''Zero Counter''' effect that immediately end the step, can effects that activate at the end of the step activate?
A8. Yes, it can be activated. Q9. During opponent's Main Step, if I used 2 copies of '''Zero Counter''' with effect that immediately end the step, does the Opponent's Main Step and Attack Step be ended?
A9. No, it doesn't end the opposing Main Step and Attack Step. When resolving the 1st copy, the step will end and no other effect can be resolved, unless derived from or against the 1st copy's '''Zero Counter''' effect. The 2nd copy will be unusable and will be returned back to your hand. Q10. When the opponent summons one Spirit/Brave without paying the cost, other than by a Burst effect, and you use two copies of '''Zero Counter '''effects, both with the effect "Destroy an opposing Spirit", can you destroy two opposing Spirits simultaneously?
A10. Yes, you can. However, if the 1st copy of '''Zero Counter''' destroys the summoned Spirit, the 2nd copy will be unusable and will be returned back to your hand. Q11. When a Spirit is summoned with no costs due to the change of cost or full reductions, can '''Zero Counter''' be used?
A11. No, you can't. In these cases, the Spirit is summoned "in 0 costs" instead of "without paying the cost". '''Zero Counter''' specifically deals with Spirits/Braves summoned "without paying the cost". Q12. When the effect summons a Spirit without paying the cost while having other effects activating right after the summon (e.g. [[The DragonMaskOgre Biranba]]), can '''Zero Counter''' be used and intercept the effect?
A12. No, it can't. Unless the effect has the wording "after this effect resolves" in between, Zero Counter can only be used after the summoning effect has fully activated. For example, in Biranba's case, the player has to wait until Biranba also sends the cores to the Void before they're able to use Zero Counter. Q13: When two '''Zero Counter''' are activating at the same time, which one resolves first?
A13: All '''Zero Counter''' effects are declared first, then the turn player decides which effect resolves first. After the 1st '''Zero Counter''' effect resolves and cancels the condition fulfilment for the 2nd '''Zero Counter''' effect, the 2nd copy will be unusable and will be returned back to the hand. == Cards with Zero Counter Effects == [[:Category:Zero Counter|List of Magics with Zero Counter]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

'''Mirage''' (ミラージュ) is a game mechanic debuted in [[SD59]] and [[BS56]]. It is an effect which all card types may have. Cards with Mirage are placed face-up on the Burst Area by paying the cost depicted in the Mirage effect, and they then activate their varying "During Set" effects. Any cards with Mirage can also be played normally.

"Mirage" is the fourth effect category after main, flash, and Burst effects. When an effect simply refers to a "set card", Mirage is included.

== Handling Mirage==
Once per turn during your Main Step, you can set down a card with Mirage face-up onto your Burst Area. This "once per turn" limit does not concern with the Burst, so you can set down both Burst and Mirage once each in the same turn.  You cannot manually set down a card with Mirage from the Removed Zone. Furthermore, only one Mirage can be set at a time. You can also set a Mirage with effects, such as via [[Mirage Boost]], ignoring the number of times You have set down a Mirage manually in the same turn.

While there is already a set Mirage, when you try to set a new Mirage, you switch places between the one that is already set and the new one after paying the cost for the new Mirage. You cannot simply return the set Mirage to hand without setting a new one. As swapping does not equate to increasing hand, any effects which trigger upon "increasing hand size" do not trigger when swapping Mirage.

The Burst Area can contain both a set Burst and a set Mirage at the same time. In this case, the Mirage and the Burst stack together, with the Mirage always above the Burst. When swapping the Mirage, the set Burst cannot be swapped together (the same applies if the Mirage is discarded). Vice versa, when discarding the set Burst, the set Mirage cannot be discarded together.

As the Burst Area is a separate zone to the field, any effects which reference or target the cards on the field cannot affect the Mirage. By the same logic, the Mirage itself also cannot activate its effects that does not have the "During Set" timing. You also cannot summon/deploy/use the set Mirage from the Burst Area. Also, Mirage cannot be affected unless the effect specifies "Mirage".

Like any other kind of effects, Mirage effects can be prevented by immunities.

The main difference is that Phantom Return re-summons a Spirit while Return to Prime re-deploys a Nexus. While Phantom Return only triggers when the Spirit is destroyed, it is enough to balance the potential of Gai-Asura X.
== Selected Official Q&A == {| class="article-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |4 |What is this Reborn Spirit's Phantom Return? |It is an effect that when this Reborn Spirit is destroyed by the opponent either through effects or BP comparison, you can pay the cost to summon the pre-Rebirth side of the Spirit. When you flip back and summon it, you do not increase counters, nor do the effects applied on the Reborn Spirit continue. Also, when you summon it, you cannot use its own symbols for cost reductions, and you can add more cores to the re-summoned Spirit, plus you can also activate effects which trigger upon summon, such as [[Core Charge]]. |- |5 |When you activate Phantom Return to flip back the Spirit and summon, do the cores stay on it as they are? |No, when you are resolving Phantom Return, the Reborn Spirit is treated as a Spirit card that you declared to summon. The cores on it are moved to the reserve first, then you pay the cost to summon the Spirit via Phantom Return. |- |6 |When you activate Phantom Return to flip back the card to summon, is the Reborn Spirit before the flip still considered in destroyed state? |No, it is not. When Phantom Return is resolved, the Reborn Spirit is treated as a Spirit card that you declared to summon, so any effect related to “being destroyed"/“leaving the field” cannot resolve, and it is not treated as a Spirit leaving the field anymore. |- |7 |The Reborn Spirit has facedown cards under it due to [[Poison Blade]]. When Phantom Return activates, do the facedown cards stay with the pre-Rebirth Spirit after summon? |No, they do not. When Phantom Return is resolving, the Reborn Spirit technically does not exist anymore, so the facedown cards are sent to the trash. |- |10 |The Brave Reborn Spirit activates Phantom Return, when does the braved Brave become Spirit condition? |The braved Brave becomes Spirit condition before you summon the Spirit card via Phantom Return, so when paying the cost, you can use that Brave's symbol for reduction costs. |} {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Once per turn, this Spirit can battle up to four times in a row. (Before the end of battle, you can carry out another battle from the before-block Flash Timing (Max. 3 times).) A unique effect for the game, Emperor Ro
Emperor Road.fullContent:
[[File:The Emperor.png|thumb]] '''Emperor Road''' (皇帝連激 ; ''literally meaning "continuous attacks of the emperor"'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS57]], exclusive to [[The OracleTwentyOnePillars IV The Emperor]]. The wording is as follows: *'''Emperor Road''' (When Attacks)
Once per turn, this Spirit can battle up to four times in a row. (Before the end of battle, you can carry out another battle from the before-block Flash Timing (Max. 3 times).) A unique effect for the game, Emperor Road allows the Spirit to bypass quite a few defensive mechanics, mainly the "end Attack Step" effects, which always happen at the end of the battle. It drives the players to rely more on other kinds of defences than just ending the Attack Step. With the addition of [[Oracle IV Over Emperor]], which allows the Spirit to ignore White Magic effects, it further encourages players to use more than White cards for defence. A point to note is that Emperor Road isn't allowing the player to ''declare'' attacks for four consecutive times, but more of repeating the same battle for three more times, with all four battles counted as one attack. As such, instantaneous (When Attacks) effects such as "draw a card" or "destroy a Spirit" don't activate again when the battle repeats. However, "during this battle" effects and those without a specified timing will last throughout all four battles. As such, one may use Braves to utilize advantage, such as [[The ThunderSacredArtillery Cannon-Arms]] or [[The AbyssGiantSword Abyss-Apocalypse X]] to lock the opposing hand. == Official Q&A == {| class="article-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |1 |What is Emperor Road? |It's an effect which allows up to four consecutive battles in one attack. When resolving a battle, after Spirits/Ultimates are destroyed via BP comparison, or the attack reduces the opposing Life, and effects triggered by either of those timings are resolved, plus the Spirit with Emperor Road hasn't left the Field, instead of ending the battle, it continues the battle by going back to the before-block Flash Timing. The battle can be continued for up to three times, amounting to a total of up to four battles in one attack. |- |2 |Do you have to declare the number of times you're repeating the battles when you first declare the attack? |No, you only choose if you want to repeat once after each battle, before reaching the "end of battle" timing. As such, if you [[Advent]] onto the Spirit with Emperor Road, or replaced it during a battle, or the Spirit with Emperor Road is brought down to LV1, it won't be able to repeat more battles after that. |- |3 |When the Spirit with Emperor Road battles for the second time or more, can either player's "when a Spirit attacks" effects or the (When Attacks) effects of the Brave braved to the Spirit with Emperor Road activate? |As you don't declare an attack again when battling for the second time or more, attack effects which happen instantaneously, such as drawing and destroying don't activate again. However, those which can be activated during other timings in the attack, such as during Flash Timing or when comparing BP, like "this Spirit gains +5000 BP" or "the opponent can't activate [[Burst]] effects", can activate. |- |4 |When the attacking Spirit activates Emperor Road, do the "during this battle" effects that activated from the first battle continue into the second battle and so on? |Yes, they continue to activate, as the attack hasn't reached the "end of battle" timing yet. |- |5 |While the Spirit with Emperor Road is attacking, the opponent uses cards such as [[Burst Wall]] (SD56-RV009) to end the Attack Step at the end of battle. Does the Attack Step end with no battles continued? |No, except for the fourth battle, you can continue for more battles before the Attack Step ends, as Emperor Road allows the battle to jump from right before the end of battle to before-block Flash Timing. The Attack Step only ends when the end of battle comes after Emperor Road finishes activating. |- |6 |While the Spirit with Emperor Road is attacking, the opponent uses cards such as [[Tousenbo Wall]] (BS50-RV013) to prevent Spirits from attacking. Does the attack ends with no battles continued? |No, when proceeding towards the second battle and so on, another attack declaration isn't needed. So while the Spirit is affected by the "can't attack" effect, the battles can continue. |- |7 |While the Spirit with Emperor Road is attacking, the opponent uses cards such as [[Closed Gemini]] (BS47-101) to end the battle immediately. Does the attack ends with no battles continued? |Yes, the battle has been forcefully proceeded to the "end of battle" timing, so battles can't continue. |- |8 |The Spirit with Emperor Road reduces the opposing Life via its attack, and the opponent declares a Burst with the condition "After your Life is reduced". Does the Burst resolve before the battle continues? |Yes, it does. All effects triggered when the Life is reduced are resolved first, then the Burst triggered by the Life reduction is resolved, then the battle continues. |- |9 |After adventing onto the Spirit with Emperor Road or replacing it with another Spirit, can the extra battles continue? |No, they can't. |- |10 |The Spirit with Emperor Road is refreshed during its attack. Does it exhaust when the second battle and so on continue? |No, it doesn't. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Emperor Road|Cards with Emperor Road]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Dragon Awaken.fullContent:
[[File:BS64-XV01.png|thumb]] '''Dragon Awaken''' ({{ruby|龍|りゅう}}{{ruby|皇|おう}}{{ruby|覚|かく}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}；''ryuuou kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS64]], exclusive to [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried XV]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] Flash -''' {{tk|Dragon Awaken}}
Once per turn, you can send two cores from your Counter Area/Spirits to this Spirit. When you've done so, this Spirit can refresh, and you can destroy an opposing Spirit/Ultimate with the highest BP and an opposing Nexus. The name echoes with [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried|Siegfried]]'s title, and ties with Siegfried's identity of being an X-Rare with {{tk|Awaken}}. Effect-wise, it is a modified version of {{tk|Awaken}} with a restriction on the number of cores you can move to the Spirit, but with additional benefits like how it can take cores from the Count Area and is followed by a refresh + Spirit/Ultimate removal + Nexus destruction. The refresh and Spirit/Ultimate destruction effects draw high resemblance to the {{tk|Twinkle Awaken}} of [[The TwinkleDragonEmperor New-Siegfried]], another remake of [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried|Siegfried]]. The ability of being able to take cores from Count Area instead of own Spirits makes the effect an actual core boost, which is precious in Red, and makes it the third card that can return Soul Core from your Count Area. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Type: Vision.fullContent:
[[File:BS65-084.png|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Type: Vision''' (タイプ：{{ruby|幻魂|ヴィジョン}}, ''Taipu: Bijion'') is a type of Magic cards introduced in [[BS65]]. While the kanji reads as "phantom soul (幻魂)" in a literal sense, the furigana reads "Vision (ヴィジョン)".  

The effects of '''Type: Vision''' magics may vary, but all of them have the effect to remain on the Field after being used. While a part of them has effects that are active while on the Field, unlike [[Type: Flower]] magic cards that focus on keeping the Magic on Field for continuous effects, Type: Vision Magic cards encourage players to actively discard them from the Field at different instances to activate various effects. 

'''Type: Vision''' magics are themed after past [[Yellow]] Spirits from different eras. Most of their effects are also modified from, or are at least related to their Spirit counterparts. In the lore, '''Vision (ヴィジョン)''' are illusions of Spirits from other dimensions summoned by summoners who live in [[Summoners' Hidden Village, Gil-Ghibarue]]. [[The Phantom Partner, Palm]] is one of such summoners, and all the Type: Vision magics are currently Visions summoned by Palm. It is also reflected in the card effects that all of them require players to control Palm to use their Main/Flash effects. It is hence also the theme of the [[Phantom Contract]] deck. Having effects that activate when discarded from Field instead of staying on the Field also reflect the nature of them being illusions that do not last.

Contract Awaken.fullContent:
[[File:P24-06.png|thumb]] '''Contract Awaken''' ({{ruby|契|けい}}{{ruby|約|やく}}{{ruby|覚|かく}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}；''keiyaku kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[Battle Spirits Twin Wafers ~Return of the Phantom Star~]], exclusive to [[The PhantomStarDragon Gai-Asura XV]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3][LV4] Flash - {{tk|Contract Awaken}} (Either Attack Step)'''
You can put as many cores from your Spirits/Contract Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit. When you've done so, this Spirit refreshes. A modified version of [[Ultra Awaken]] and created after [[Phantom Awaken]], it takes cores from Contract Grandwalker Nexuses, the theme of the year, this time instead of only the Spirits. In essence, it works as an {{tk|Unleash}} effect that limits to Contract Grandwalker Nexuses but without an upper limit for cores to be put from the Grandwalker Nexuses at a time. Since it is a "when you've done so" effect but not a "by A do B" effect, you can move cores from Contract Grandwalker Nexuses to Gai-Asura XV even if it is already in refreshed state. Since Gai-Asura XV comes with {{tk|Mani}} which allows it to be summoned with one Soul Core as long as the conditions of 8 counters and a Contract Grandwalker Nexus are fulfilled, it is much easier to bring out the card than previous Gai-Asura variants with [[Ultra Awaken]] or similar effects. Providing cores and refreshing, the keyword, when combined with Gai-Asura's [[Concluser]] family, allows Gai-Asura XV to be a versatile card with potentials in different decks with Contract Grandwalker Nexuses. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Infinite Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BS73-X01.png|thumb|200px]] '''Infinite Unleash''' (無限界放, ''Mugen-kaihou'') is a new keyword introduced in [[BS73]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The MasterSwordsmanDragon Samurai-Dragon-Amatsu X]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV2][LV3] {{In Unleash|2}} (Your Attack Step)'''
This Spirit can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. When you do, this Spirit doesn't exhaust. By sending two cores from any of your "Rekka Yukimura" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit, instead, this Spirit attacks without exhausting. As the name implies, it is an upgraded version of {{tk|Infinite Blade}}, taking in the power of Unleash. Hence, the base part of the effect, "attacking without exhausting by performing target attack" is exactly the same as {{tk|Infinite Blade}}, with the only difference being that it doesn't require Soul Core to be placed on Amatsu anymore. The effect is powerful in the regard that it doesn't trigger any effect related to the Spirit being exhausted, which for prey to a lot of the Rebirth conditions of Green cards. The second/extended part of the effect, however, is the real upgrade part where the owner of Amatsu X can attack without exhausting even if there is nothing to target attack, as long as there are cores on the designated Grandwalkers for "Unleash". Such an upgrade is powerful is multiple aspect. To begin with, this means that the consecutive attack made is no longer dependent on opponent's board state, and pseudo "infinite" attack can be made as long as there are enough cores. Second, while {{tk|Infinite Blade}} is focusing on clearing opponent's board, {{tk|Infinite Unleash}} can directly go for opponent's life, making it a winning pattern of the deck. Third, as Unleash in itself is a type of "core boost", it doesn't only level up Amatsu X in the process, but also provide resistance to core removal, and generates more cores for the player to use every attack, which is particularly precious in Red. On the other hand, there are also limitations which keep the effect in check. Much like many recent variants of {{tk|Unleash}}, it requires the cores to be sent from Grandwalkers with specific card names, "Rekka Yukimura"-named in this context, limiting the use of the card outside the designated deck which charges "Rekka Yukimura"-named Grandwalker Nexuses. This is particularly restrictive when one of the "Rekka Yukimura"-named Grandwalker Nexuses is a Contract Grandwalker Nexuses, which couldn't co-exist with other Contract cards in a deck. Hence, while Infinite Unleash is a powerful effect, especially when combined with Amatsu X, which summons itself lightly and comes with draw power, it can't be used everywhere. == Related Cards == * [[The BurningContractor Rekka Yukimura]] * [[Rekka Yukimura]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

War Catalyze.fullContent:
[[File:BS74-033.png|thumb|320x320px]] '''War Catalyze''' ({{ruby|戦|せん}}{{ruby|起|き}}{{ruby|導|どう}}, ''ikusa-ki-dou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS74]], possessed only by "[[Catalyst]]" family Spirit cards of specific colors at the moment. It is an alternate version of [[Catalyze]]. The effect reads as follows: * '''[Level] {{W Catl|All Color}} (When Attacks)'''
By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]], or a core from your Grandwalker Nexus to the Trash, immediately activate one of your Soul Bursts. OR * '''[Level] {{W Catl|(Color)}} (When Attacks)'''
By sending your [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]], or a core from your Grandwalker Nexus to the Trash, immediately activate one of your (Color) Soul Bursts. Same as other variants of Catalyze, '''War Catalyze''' is meant to pair with cards with [[Soul Burst]], allowing the player to forcefully activate their set Soul Burst, ignoring the Burst condition. But in addition to sending [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash, '''War Catalyze''' offers the option of sending cores from Grandwalker Nexuses to the Trash. This allows players to activate multiple Soul Bursts in the same turn (as long as you can set another one) like [[True Catalyze]]. When compared to [[True Catalyze]], while both come with the merit of not needing to send the actual Soul Core to Trash, War Catalyze requires sending core from Grandwalker to the Trash. This implies that a compatible Grandwalker must be deployed and charged with cores for it to be available. It also means that the number of times one can use War Catalyze is limited to the number of cores on their Grandwalker Nexuses, unlike True Catalze, which allows the Spirit to activate Soul Bursts as long as it can fit the timing. On the other hand, sending core from Grandwalker Nexus to the Trash is essentially a sort of delayed core boost, which provides future resources. '''War Catalyze''' also doesn't require the Soul Core to be placed on the Spirit, meaning that you can activate War Catalyze from multiple copies of cards with the keyword in the same turn without the need to throw the Soul Core around. The keyword is introduced in [[BS74]] together with the renewal of the [[Ninja Gale]] deck revolving around Soul Bursts as demonstrated in the anime, [[Battle Spirits Burning Soul]], primarily used by [[Kanetsugu Houryokuin]]. Hence, the first batch of cards with the effect is all Green. == See Also == * [[:Category:War Catalyze|List of cards with War Catalyze]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Once per turn, you can send a core from your Spirit/Life to this Spirit. When yo
Crimson Awaken.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X01.png|thumb|200px]] '''Crimson Awaken''' ({{ruby|紅|ぐ}}{{ruby|蓮|れん}}{{ruby|覚|かく}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}；''guren-kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently exclusive to [[The CrimsonStarDragonDeity Sieg-Meteorwurm]], the Crimson remake of [[The StarDragonDeity Sieg-Meteorwurm]]. The wording is as follows: * {{tk|During Advent}} '''[LV1-2] Flash - {{tk|Crimson Awaken}} (Either Attack Step)'''
Once per turn, you can send a core from your Spirit/Life to this Spirit. When you've done so, send up to three cores, besides [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]], from your Trash to your "Crimson". As the name implies, it is a modified version of {{tk|Awaken}} and makes a contrasting pair with {{tk|Silver Awaken}} which came by around the same time (despite being one set earlier). The "crimson" name comes from the supporting target of the effect, and acts as a tribute to the name of the starter deck that [[The ThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]], the base of the Contract Spirit which [[The CrimsonStarDragonDeity Sieg-Meteorwurm]] supports, was in. Effect-wise, while it is also about moving cores from own Spirits to the owner of the effect like the original {{tk|Awaken}}, there are quite a lot of limitations, including how it is a once-per-turn effect, it works only during Flash Timing of Either Attack Step instead of any Flash Timing, and it can only move exactly "one" core instead of "any number of cores". Despite so, much like many other variants of {{tk|Awaken}}, it comes with an extra benefit of being able to ''retrieve cores from Trash'', and redistribute to "Crimson"-named Spirits on the Field. This in essence make the second part of the effect a "reverse Awaken", which, instead of taking cores from other Spirits to place onto it, put cores back to the other Spirits. If you choose to send all those cores to the owner of {{tk|Crimson Awaken}}, it will also mean that the Spirit would gain a maximum of 1 + 3 = 4 cores. This amount is more or less the amount you will expect to get while using normal {{tk|Awaken}} effectively. As the core comes from the Trash, it also provides what normal {{tk|Awaken}} cannot accomplish, as the number of cores available for use on the Field ''actually increases'' after using {{tk|Crimson Awaken}}, while it is not the case for normal {{tk|Awaken}}. As the effect also works on the opposing turn, it means that the player can advent [[The CrimsonStarDragonDeity Sieg-Meteorwurm]] defensively during first Flash Timing, then activate {{tk|Crimson Awaken}} to retrieve cores from the Trash to pay for the cost of defense cards or the summon of [[The StarMedium Kushina]], which is otherwise quite heavy in cost. Apart from sending cores from other Spirits to the owner like the normal {{tk|Awaken}}, the effect comes with one more triggering option: "sending one of your Lives to it". While this sounds like a demerit alone, it is an effect that matches the playstyle of the Crimson deck led by [[The CrimsonThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]] a lot. Other than letting the player to gain an extra core from the Life instead of moving existing cores on the Field, it triggers various effects that proc upon life reduction in the deck, such as the Mirage effect of [[The CrimsonDragonStar Ankillersaurus]], and life reduction bursts like [[The CrimsonDragonStar Balmung]]. The extra life reduction is particularly important as Crimson is a deck that works stronger in offense the lower the player's life count is. For example, [[The CrimsonSupernovaDragon Siegwurm-Nova]], the finisher of the deck, burns one more life when the player's life is one fewer, and [[The CrimsonDragonStar Balmung]] only refreshes a Spirit when the player has 3 lives or below. By choosing to reduce own life via {{tk|Crimson Awaken}}, it is easier and one step faster to achieve these conditions and activate more additional effects. On the other hand, the demerit of the effect is also very obvious. By being a Flash effect in Either Attack Step, it means that one need to survive the first flash timing from the defense side. Luckily, [[The CrimsonThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]], which should act as the advent base for [[The CrimsonStarDragonDeity Sieg-Meteorwurm]], the owner of {{tk|Crimson Awaken}}, is unaffected by opposing effects during (Own Turn) unless it is blocked. This means that a player can safely activate {{tk|Crimson Awaken}} without needing to worry about the newly advented Sieg-Meteorwurm being removed. All in all, while {{tk|Crimson Awaken}} is in fact a very straightforward and simple effect, it enables a lot of new interactions and expands the combo potential for the Crimson deck by being able to reduce own life further in Flash Timing and taking back cores for various uses. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31686. |What kind of effect is {{tk|Crimson Awaken}}? |It is an effect where: once per turn, you can send a core from your Spirit/Life to the Spirit, and when core is sent, send up to three cores, besides [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]], from your Trash to your "Crimson". {{tk|Crimson Awaken}} is not treated as {{tk|Awaken}}. |- == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Curse.fullContent:
[[File:SD01-011.jpg|thumb]] '''Curse''' (呪撃, ''Jugeki'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD01]], exclusive to Purple Spirits. The effect is worded as follows: *'''Curse''' (When Attacks)
Destroy an opposing Spirit that blocked when the battle resolves at the end of battle. A keyword which can destroy the blocking Spirit, regardless of the end result from resolving battles, ignoring the major factors of battles such as BP comparison. Even if the Spirit with Curse is destroyed via comparing BP, Curse can still activate at the end of battle, when the Spirit itself is supposedly no longer present. If the Spirit with Curse is removed from the Field before resolving the battle, Curse won't activate. Being one of the oldest keywords in the game, the way Curse functions clashes with a lot of current rulings. In the past, the keyword uses the trigger timing "when a block has declared", indicating that Curse would begin checking for conditions when the opposing Spirit blocks. However, later on with a rule change which persists till this day, the timing is changed to "when resolving the battle", meaning the trigger timing is pushed back, and hence, as mentioned above, if the Spirit with Curse is removed from the Field before resolving the battle, Curse won't activate. This also means that if the Spirit gains Curse mid-battle, for example, by levelling up, the effect can still activate at the end of battle. The rulebook also has to specify that Curse can activate even if the Spirit is no longer on the field after resolving the battle, as normally, any effects with the "end of battle" can only activate if the effect holder is still on the field by then. As Curse is a Spirit-targeting effect, once Ultimates were introduced to the game, the keyword has died down. There are other keywords derived from Curse, including [[Spell Blight]] and [[True-Curse]]. ==Anime Users== *[[Mai Viole]] == See Also == * [[:Category:Curse|List of cards with Curse]] * [[:Category:Curse support|List of cards supporting Curse]] * [[:Category:Curse counter|List of cards countering Curse]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The wording of the effect alone is as follows: * {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} '''(When Attacks)'''
You can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. This effect can't be prevented by oppo
Vermillion Furious Charge.fullContent:
[[File:BS77-X02.png|200px|thumb]] '''Vermillion Furious Charge''' ({{ruby|赫|かく}}{{ruby|走|そう}}{{ruby|破|は}}；''kaku-sou-ha'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS77]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The HorseTwelveGodKing Execeed X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The HorseTwelveGodKing Execeed]]. The wording of the effect alone is as follows: * {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} '''(When Attacks)'''
You can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. This effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. Also, at the end of the battle, for each symbol this Spirit has, send an opposing Life to the Reserve. As the name implies, it is a remake of the {{tk|Furious Charge}} keyword owned by the original Execeed. The first part of the name comes from [[Vermillion Contract]], the name of the new Contract family owned by [[The FlameBladeFlagbearer Seiba]], whom Execeed X is designed to work with. Same as the original {{tk|Furious Charge}}, it is a rather special keyword that is not directly written on the card itself, but granted to specific Spirits, including Exceed X itself, via another effect: * '''[LV1-2-3-4]'''
Give all your "[[Bannerace]]"/"[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" family Spirits: "{{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} '''(When Attacks)''' You can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. This effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. Also, at the end of the battle, for each symbol this Spirit has, send an opposing Life to the Reserve." When compared to the original {{tk|Furious Charge}}, it is basically a direct upgrade version. While the general effect is very similar to its original, powerful upgrades have been added to the two parts of the effect. First, the target attack part now becomes a "can't be prevented" effect, making it a good tool to pierce through Spirits/Ultimates unaffected by opposing effects like [[The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison X]], overcoming one of the major weakness of the original {{tk|Furious Charge}}. With the high BP of Execeed X itself, it is almost guaranteed that it would win the BP battle and destroy the opposing battling Spirit/Ultimate. Since it is a destroy-by-battle, it would not be counted as "destroyed by opposing effects"/"leaving the Field due to opposing effects", and would not trigger any "remaining on Field" effects which react upon effect removal. Usually, when such "remain on Field when leaving the field due to opposing effects" effect goes together with "unaffected by opposing effects", the situation would become very hard to deal with. However, the piercing target attack provided by {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} can perfectly deal with the situation. Another upgrade is of course the second part, where the life burn no longer requires a "blocked battle". While everything else, including the timing and symbol referencing remain the same, the removal of the "blocked battle" requirement is a drastic change in a way that the effect can work perfectly fine even when the opponent has an empty board, be it intentional or unintentional. While the life burn of the original {{tk|Furious Charge}} could be avoided by self-depleting every Spirit/Ultimate on board and leaving no target for target attack, such strategy no longer works for {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}}. This alone has increased the game-setting power of the effect by a ton. It is also important to remember that {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} is an effect granted to ''every'' "[[Bannerace]]"/"[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" family Spirit. While the opponent might not have more than three Spirits on Field for you to perform target attack, with the condition of "blocked battle" now removed, the life burn can hit for as many times your designated Spirits can attack in the turn. In essence, when combined with the piercing target attack, it means that having an unaffected-by-effect board, a board with only one Spirit, or even an empty board, could not save you and prevent the life burn of {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}}. The only other effective way, apart from casting defense magics, would be to remove the attacking Spirit, or Execeed X itself, who grants them the effect. That, however, does not seem too easy when Execeed X now possess an effect that grants himself full immunity. While the actual line of text did not double itself in length after 10 years, the deadliness of the effect has certainly increased by tenfold. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31914 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}}? |It is an effect where: You can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate, and such effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. Also, at the end of that battle, for each symbol the Spirit who activated {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} has, you can send an opposing Life to the Reserve. {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} is not treated as {{tk|Furious Charge}}. |- |31915 |Even if my Spirit with {{tk|Vermillion Furious Charge}} was not blocked, I can send a number of opposing Life to the Reserve per its number of symbols at the end of battle? |Yes. |- |} == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Showdown.fullContent:
[[File:CQJQxHbUkAEn03p2-0.jpg|thumb|320x320px]] '''Showdown''' (一騎打) is a special ability of Red that was introduced in [[BS33]]. Cards with this effect have the same text: * '''(Opposing Start Step)''' The opponent chooses a Spirit they control and compares BP with this Spirit. Destroy the Spirit(s) with equal or lower BP. When only the opposing Spirit is destroyed, activate the following effect: XXXXXXX The effect name means a one-to-one direct battle between two sides without interference, and the effect closely resembles the origin. A rare effect in Red that activates at the start of opposing turn. Since it is a direct BP comparison effect without flash timings or actual battles, it can destroy opposing spirits ignoring other effects in place. It is also not counted as "effect destroy", which can bypass remain on field effects that work solely on "leaving the field due to opposing effects", or effects like "cannot be destroyed by opposing effects". Since it is not "attack & block", [[Showdown]] can also target opposing spirits that "cannot block", or [[Imagine Brave]]. The effect hence provide a strong control tool for the player to shutdown the opposing board. The extra benefit provided with winning the Showdown, like drawing cards, is also allowing the player to obtain extra value without using further cards or even attacking. On the downside, since the effect is compulsory and the opponent chooses what they compare BP with, the spirit with [[Showdown]] can easily be destroyed if the opposing Spirits' BP is high. In addition, although it is not a destroy effect, you still cannot target an opposing Spirit that is unaffected by Spirit effects. At some point of the game, since it doesn't matter if the opposing Spirit is exhausted or not, and can be used to destroy your own spirits (the one with [[Showdown]]) at the opposing start step without the opponent reacting to it, a loop is formed by using any low BP Showdown cards, [[The PreserverGod Vishten]], effects that changes the burst condition to (When Destroyed by the opponent), effects that set [[Soul Burst]] cards from the Trash during (Your End Step), and retrieval cards. By keep destroying the spirit with Showdown, Vishten continues to force the opposing turn to end on spot, and allow the player to keep stalling. In [[CB16]], the second Gundam collaboration booster, [[Bushido]], a new ability that is similar to [[Showdown]] but essentially an upgrade for it allows the player to choose which opposing spirit to compare BP with instead, is introduced . In [[BS73]], a new variant of the keyword, [[Rekka Showdown]], is introduced. ==Showdown== Q1. What is [[Showdown]]?
A1. Showdown is an effect that has your Showdown spirit and a spirit of your opponent's choice compare BP during the opponent's start step. After comparing BP, the one with less BP is destroyed, and if the BP is the same, both spirits are destroyed. When only the opposing spirit is destroyed by comparing BP through Showdown, spirits can activate their own effects. Q2. Is the spirit with Showdown exhausted?
A2. No, it is not exhausted. Q3. Do "When Attacks" and "When Blocks" activate during Showdown?
A3. No, they do not. Showdown does not count as a battle. Q4. When the opponent's spirit is destroyed through Showdown, does that count as being destroyed by opposing effects? Or does it count as being destroyed by BP comparison?
A4. It counts as being destroyed by BP comparison. Effects that activate when destroyed by effects do not activate. Q5. When an opposing spirit with a "cannot be destroyed by opposing effects" effect is selected, is that spirit still destroyed if its BP is lower?
A5. Yes, it is destroyed. Q6. When a spirit with Showdown is destroyed through Showdown, can a burst with the condition "when your spirit is destroyed by the opponent" be activated?
A6. Yes, it can activate. Q7. When Showdown is activated, can the opponent select a spirit with {{ha|Red}} or one that is unaffected by opposing effects?
A7. No, they cannot. Q8. Is there flash timing while Showdown is active?
A8. No, there is not. Q9. Must Showdown be activated even if the opponent has a spirit with higher BP?
A8. Yes, it must. Q10. Does Showdown activate even if the spirit with Showdown is exhausted?
A8. Yes, it does. Q11. When your opponent activates Showdown, can you choose your own exhausted spirit?
A8. Yes, you can. Q11. When two opposing spirits activate Showdown, which comes first?
A8. As the turn player, you can choose the order of the Showdown effects. == Also See == * [[:Category: Showdown|List of Cards with Showdown]] * [[:Category: Showdown support|List of Showdown support cards]] == Navigation == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

God Strike.fullContent:
[[File:tiamadou.png|thumb]] '''God Strike '''(神撃, ''Shingeki'') is a [[Purple]] keyword, possessed exclusively by [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou]]. It is worded as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|God Strike}} (Your Attack Step)'''
While your "[[God-King]]" family Spirit is attacking, the opponent can't block unless they send a core from their Life to the Void. A powerful restricting effect, God Strike offers strong block-restricting powers to the already powerful God-King Spirits. As it targets the opponent directly, it applies regardless of opposing Spirits/Ultimates being unaffected by your effects or not. This means as long as the attackers stays on the Field, the opponent will have to choose losing a life due to their attack without blocking, or blocking them while losing a life. While the end result seems to be the same, sending the core to the Void means it can't increase your resources the same way when life is taken normally, making it an even worse situation for a player to declare block even if their blockers might destroy the attacker. As the name, "God Strike", tells, it applies to all "[[God-King]]" family Spirits, and works very well with Tiamadou's "[[God-King]]" summoning effect, {{tk|God-Army}}. Since there is no mention of "can't stack", if two Tiamdaou are aligned on the Field, it will mean the opponent has to send TWO lives to Void for each block, which is not exactly impossible with {{tk|God-Army}}. The keyword was later modified to become {{tk|Banner God Strike}} in Tiamadou's remake, [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou X]]. ==Anime Users== * [[Tatsumi]] ==See also== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

God-Army.fullContent:
[[File:tiamadou.png|200px|thumb]] '''God-Army '''(神軍, ''Shingun'') is a Purple keyword, possessed exclusively by [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou]]. It has the following text: * {{Seal|When Sealed}} {{tk|God-Army}} '''[LV2][LV3] {{tk|God-Army}} (When Attacks)'''
You can summon "[[God-King]]" family Spirit cards from your Hand and Trash, one from each, without paying the cost. As the name implies, the effect allows players to summon [[God-King]] family Spirit cards at no cost, and twice at once, to spam the field and form an army of [[God-King]]. This particular associates with the motif of Tiamdaou, Tiamat, which is said to have led the 11 monsters she gave birth to to a fight against the deities to revenge her son in the myth. It is also mentioned in the flavor text that Tiamadou is leading the Twelve God-Kings as a commander in the frontline, matching the ability of {{tk|God-Army}} to call upon the various God-Kings. Since there is no limit on the cost or color of the [[God-King]] family Spirit to be summoned, the combo potential of the effect itself is very high. By summoning "[[God-King]]" family Spirits from other colors which usually are of finisher level and have their unique strength make it very hard for the opponent to predict what is coming and react. As it also doesn't stop you from summoning another Tiamadou, and the card can be summoned from the Trash, the effect itself can form a close loop. The effect is later remade into {{tk|Banner God-Army}}, owned by [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou X]]. == Anime User == * [[Tatsumi]] ==See also== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

* {During Seal} '''Pyro Drive''' - (When Attacks) Destroy any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates with a BP equal or inferior to this Spirit's up to the number of "[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" family Spirits you control, and you
Pyro Drive.fullContent:
[[File:Super_exe.png|thumb|300x300px]]
'''Pyro Drive''' (''炎走破'', ''Ensouha'') is a keyword which was introduced in [[BS39]] as the powered-up version of [[Furious Charge]] and is possessed exclusively by [[The Super-TwelveGodKing Execeed Formula]]. The keyword reads:
* {During Seal} '''Pyro Drive''' - (When Attacks) Destroy any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates with a BP equal or inferior to this Spirit's up to the number of "[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" family Spirits you control, and you can target attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. When you've done so, at the end of a blocked battle, for each Spirit/Ultimate destroyed in this battle, send one opposing Life to the Reserve.

An extremely powerful destructive effect, Pyro Drive already takes the Life-crushing target attack ability from the original Furious Charge and further adds it with a destruction effect that destroys a number of the opponent's weaker Spirits and/or Ultimates equal to the number of [[God-King]] and [[Ten Crown]] Spirits the player has on the Field.

Adding to that, with a possibly large amount of Spirits and/or Ultimates that are destroyed in one battle while Pyro Drive is in use, a vast number, if not all of the opponent's Lives can be taken away. If used properly, the player can easily win the game.

However, as opposed to the original {{tk|Furious Charge}} effect, the number of lives reduced depend on the number of available destroy targets on either field, and the target for target attack must not be the target of BP destroy, it is less stable an effect as attacking with a braved spirit with {{tk|Furious Charge}}, which only looks at its own number of symbols for the life reduction.

Twinkle Clash.contentSample:
[[File:The ThunderEmperorDragon SiegwurmRev-A.jpg|thumb|200px]] '''Twinkle Clash ''' ({{ruby|煌|こう}}{{ruby|激|げき}}{{ruby|突|とつ}}; ''Kō gekitotsu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS41]], together with the Revival Version of [[The ThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]]. The effect reads as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Twinkle Clash}} (When Attacks)'''
Opposing Spirits/Ultimates must block if possible. When blocked, you can stack a card from your Hand onto this Spirit via {{tk|Advent}}, without se
Twinkle Clash.fullContent:
[[File:The ThunderEmperorDragon SiegwurmRev-A.jpg|thumb|200px]] '''Twinkle Clash ''' ({{ruby|煌|こう}}{{ruby|激|げき}}{{ruby|突|とつ}}; ''Kō gekitotsu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS41]], together with the Revival Version of [[The ThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]]. The effect reads as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Twinkle Clash}} (When Attacks)'''
Opposing Spirits/Ultimates must block if possible. When blocked, you can stack a card from your Hand onto this Spirit via {{tk|Advent}}, without sending the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash. After errata in block 6, it reads: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Twinkle Clash}} (When Attacks)'''
Opposing Spirits/Ultimates must block if possible. When blocked, you can {{tk|Advent}} a card from your Hand onto this Spirit, without sending the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash. As the name implies, it is a new variant of {{tk|Clash}} that is deeply associated with the {{tk|Advent}} mechanic newly introduced to the game in the era. When compared to older variants of {{tk|Clash}}, it is obviously modeled after {{tk|True-Clash}}, which forces opposing Ultimates to block if possible as well, instead of only Spirits. Since it comes with the second part of effect, it is in essence a stronger version of {{tk|True-Clash}}. As for the said "second part of effect", it allows the player to {{tk|Advent}} onto the card owning such effect when it is blocked, which is highly likely going to happen due to the first part of the effect, without sending the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash. While it still requires the owner of such effect to survive the pre-block Flash Timing, the benefit of {{tk|adventing}} without sending Soul Core to the Trash is still great. Similar to other effects that allow one to {{tk|Advent}} "without sending Soul Core to the Trash", it is worthy to note that such effect '''can't''' be used if your Soul Core is already in Trash, with the rationable being: if you are to take the option of "without sending Soul Core to the Trash", you must be "able" to send that Soul Core to Trash first. Another interesting point is, as the two parts of effects are separated and do not depend on each other, even if you performed a "target attack" by an effect from a Brave or granted by your other Spirits, as long as the Spirit with {{tk|Twinkle Clash}} is blocked, you can {{tk|Advent}} a card from your Hand onto the Spirit, without sending the [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] to the Trash. The keyword was originally possessed exclusively by the Revival version of [[The ThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]], whose original version has been one of the most iconic Spirits with {{tk|Clash}}. It was later printed on [[The SuperstarDragonBlade Siegwurm Sword]], which is in fact another remake of [[The ThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm]]. Since the brave condition of Siegwurm Sword is just "cost 4 or more", and there is no family nor color restrictions for {{tk|Twinkle Clash}}, it essentially grants every Cost 4 or more Spirit the ability to {{tk|Advent}} without sending Soul Core to Trash as long as the Brave can be summoned and braved. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |6670 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Twinkle Clash}}? |It is an effect where when the Spirit with this effect attacks, the opponent must block whenever there is a Spirit/Ultimate that can block. And when blocked, the player can {{tk|Advent}} a card from the Hand onto the Spirit with this effect without sending their Soul Core to the Trash. |- |6671 |If my Soul Core is in the Trash, can I {{tk|Advent}} via {{tk|Twinkle Clash}}? |No, you can't. |- |} == Also See == * [[:Category:Twinkle Clash|List of Cards with Twinkle Clash]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Opposing Spirits/Ultimates must block if possible. This effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. Ultra Clash is an upgrade of [[True-Clash]], which itself was an upgrade of [[Clash]]. The significance of Ultra Clash is that it can't be prevented by opposing effects, covering the main weakness which the other two older keywords have. While introduced as one of the main gimmicks of the new generation Red-Green [[Rush]] deck during True-Rebirth era, cards with the keyword aren't really used at the end as it turns out to be more straightforward to use the cards that gain resources and directly remove opposing Spirits/Ultimates on attack. The relatively low BP of the cards with Ultra Clash also contributed to the issue. On the collaboration side, however, Ultra Clash becomes the main gimmick of [[Henshin!! Kamen Rider Drive|Kamen Rider Drive]]'s deck introduced in the Contract Era. Different from the Red-Green deck in True-Rebirth era, the keyword becomes the literal core of the deck, and comes with more supports that generates value and synergizes well with the keyword, including Bursts that immediately opens when Spirits are blocked, cards with life burn effects when own Spirits with Ultra Clash are blocked, draws and increase of BP, Grand Skill that refreshes the opposing Spirit in Flash to make the best use of the ability etc. While first introduced as a main set keyword, it becomes a complete deck via collaboration. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Ultra Clash|List of cards with Ultra Clash]] * [[:Category:Ultra Clash support|List of cards supporting Ultra Clash]] * [[Clash]] * [[True-Clash]] * [[Clash X]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

You can put any number of cores from your Reserve/Field to a "[[Scarlet Flame]]" family Spirit/Nexus you control. (Once per Turn: Same Name) When cores are put via this effect, your counter +1. Also
Toppa Awaken.fullContent:
[[file:SD66-CX01.png|thumb]] '''Toppa Awaken''' (突破覚醒 ; '' Toppa Kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD66]], currently exclusive to [[Top Buddy, Aibou]]. The keyword is worded as follows: * {{tk|Soul State}} {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}}/{{tk|Spirit}} '''[LV1][LV2] Flash -''' {{tk|Toppa Awaken}}
You can put any number of cores from your Reserve/Field to a "[[Scarlet Flame]]" family Spirit/Nexus you control. (Once per Turn: Same Name) When cores are put via this effect, your counter +1. Also, if it's your Attack Step, your counter +1. While the name's literal meaning is closer to "breakthrough awaken", considering that it is exactly the same as [[Toppa Bashin]]'s name (馬神'''突破'''), and a keyword that exclusively belongs to Toppa's partner, Aibou, which comes in a dream deck themed around Toppa, Toppa's name is used instead of the literal meaning. The keyword itself is a remake of the original [[Awaken]] keyword, but with multiple breakthroughs like what the effect name implies. Unlike the original keyword which can only moves cores from the Field, Toppa Awaken allows player to move cores from their Reserve as well. Apart from Spirit, the effect also now covers Nexuses. This allow more interactive uses with LV2 effects of Nexuses when cores are short. Another strong point is also how unlike previous awaken effects that are printed on the cards themselves, Toppa Awaken is printed on the Contract card and it's an effect that works while Aibou is in {{tk|Soul State}}. This means that instead of relying on the spirits you summoned to have awaken for you to move cores to them, you can move cores to Spirits/Nexuses that fulfill the condition even if the cards themselves do not possess such keyword. Being an effect that can be activated in Soul State and without step or turn limitations, it also means a player can freely move cores between their Reserve and Spirits/Nexuses of the designated family, opening up more ways to make use of cores outside Main Step. Apart from the breakthroughs on the core-moving aspect, being a new keyword introduced in Contract era, the effect also comes with counter-generating ability. The flexibility of adding one counter in flash that can be done during Main Step and opposing Attack Step, or two counters during own Attack Step, even when Aibou is in Soul State, provides a stable counter-generating method for [[Top Buddy, Aibou]]'s deck. While there are turn limitations for the counter gain, it is well-covered by the stability and flexibility of the effect. For its downside, the effect limits its targets to [[Scarlet Flame]] family Spirits/Nexuses, balancing out the fact that it enables the player to move cores around all their Spirits, Nexuses and Reserve. Like previous awaken effects, the effect also only move cores to one Spirit or Nexus at a time, instead of multiple Spirits/Nexuses, meaning that it can't be used to save multiple Spirits that are going to become depletion targets on the next Flash. Despite so, the merits basically outshine everything, and allow the keyword to act as a core mechanic of Aibou's deck. == Related Articles == * [[Awaken]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Grudging Curse.fullContent:
[[file:BSC45-XV02.png|250px|thumb]] '''Grudging Curse''' (怨呪撃; ''on-jugeki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC45]], possessed exclusively by [[The SevenShogun Beelzebeat XV]]. The effect reads as follows: * {{tk|Grudging Curse}} (Your Turn)
When your Spirits would leave the Field due to the opponent, you can draw a card. Then, (Once per Turn: Same Name) you can send an opposing Life to the Trash. '''Grudging Curse''' serves as a modified version of the [[Curse]] keyword, and is in a way closer to [[Spell Blight]] considering that it involves reducing opposing Life directly but not removing opposing Spirits/Ultimates on the Field like what [[Curse]] and [[True-Curse]] did. Much like some other new keywords introduced in the same set, it serves as a keyword that supports the entire Field instead of only itself. While it might vary for other Spirits with the keyword in the future (if any), the effect timing is (Your Turn), while the LV requirement is LV1 only. This makes it a very potent Field supporting effect, and combines very well with the resurrecting Burst effect of [[The SevenShogun Beelzebeat XV]]. Unlike normal [[Curse]] or [[True-Curse]] that focuses on removals, Grudging Curse provides resources via the draw and a deterring life burn effect, making it a very good support to aggro decks. The only major weakness of the keyword, much like all the keywords derived from [[Curse]], is that it relies on the opponent's action to work. This, however, can be resolved by giving enough pressure to the opponent with numbers and powerful Spirits summoned via the other effect. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Grudging Curse|List of cards with Grudging Curse]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]
