You can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. When you've done so, at the end of battle, send two opposing Lives to the Reserve. '''Supreme Clash''' serves as an upgrade of the [[Clash]] keywo
Supreme Clash.fullContent:
[[file:BSC45-XV01.png|250px|thumb]] '''Supreme Clash''' ({{ruby|覇|は}}・{{ruby|激|げき}}{{ruby|突|とつ}}; ''ha gekitotsu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC45]], possessed exclusively by [[The StarEmperorDragon Meteorwurm XV]]. The effect reads as follows: *{{tk|Supreme Clash}} '''(When Attacks)'''
You can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. When you've done so, at the end of battle, send two opposing Lives to the Reserve. '''Supreme Clash''' serves as an upgrade of the [[Clash]] keyword, changing from only forcing the opponent to block to directly targeting an opposing Spirit or Ultimate of the user's choice. The extra life burn also ensures the extra disruption done to the opponent. The keyword allows Meteorwurm XV to become a standalone finisher, a fine addition to the multiple options which the [[Astral Dragon]] family already has. It allows Meteorwurm XV to disrupt the opposing board while progressing through the game. With the abundance of other life burn effects existing in the family, such as the [[Grand Field]] of [[Grandwalker Apollon]], one may even be able to finish the opponent with simply one attack from Meteorwurm XV. The weakness of this keyword lies in the fact that the life burn only happens at the end of battle, which gives the opponent enough chances to remove Meteorwurm XV before that can happen, though that can usually be covered by "remain on field" effects. Supreme Clash in general also requires an opposing Spirit or Ultimate to be targeted, so if that doesn't exist, either due to the opposing field being empty, or their Spirits and Ultimates are unaffected by Supreme Clash, then the keyword would become useless as well. ==See Also:== *[[:Category:Supreme Clash|List of cards with Supreme Clash]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Curse Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BS70-X02.png|200px|thumb]] '''Curse Unleash''' ( 呪界放；''Jukaihō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS70]], exclusive to [[The MakaiCelestialNymph Diesdoll]], the [[Concluser]] Spirit of [[The CurseConsortContractor Hera]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|1|Curse}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Summoned/Attacks)'''
You can destroy an opposing Spirit/Ultimate with two cores or more on it. Then, you can send a core from any of your "Hera" Grandwalker Nexus to this Spirit or the Trash. When you've done so, send two cores from the opposing Reserve to the Trash. Like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Shining Heaven Unleash]], this Unleash requires a specific Grandwalker to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. When compared to the average Unleash effects, it is closer to [[Nether Unleash]] in a way that it has the option for the player to send the core from the Grandwalker Nexus to the '''Trash''' instead of the Spirit itself. The major reason for that is probably how as an effect of a Spirit that goes along with [[Grandwalker Hera]] and [[The CurseConsortContractor Hera]], {{tk|Curse Unleash}} as a (When Summoned) effect might be activated via the {{tk|Grand Skill}} and {{tk|Contract Skill}} of the aforementioned Grandwalker Nexuses. And in that case, since Diesdoll would not be on the Field, "this Spirit" can't be used as a reference to send the core from Grandwalker Nexus to, and the effect can't be used if it only allows the player to send core to the Spirit. Hence, the keyword also provides the option of sending core to the Trash so that it can be completed even when it is being avtivated from a card being discarded from Hand or banished from Trash. ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

True Genesis.fullContent:
[[File:SD69-RVX01.png|thumb|250x250px]] '''True Genesis''' (真創聖 ; ''Shin Sōsei'') is a keyword introduced in [[SD69]], currently exclusive to the Revival version of [[The CreatorDragonDeity Generator Dragon-Zero]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{Tk|True Genesis}} (When Manifests/Attacks)'''
Once per turn, you can send out up to one "Rig Avatar Dragon" Token for every three counters you have, putting one core from your Field/"Brahama" Grandwalker Nexuses to each of them. (Max. 3 Tokens) As the name implies, it is the remake/upgrade version of {{tk|Genesis}}, which was owned by the original version of [[The CreatorDragonDeity Generator Dragon-Zero]]. The name also matches the era title of Contract Saga: True. With the introduction of [[Token Cards|Token Spirits]], instead of revealing and summoning Avatar Dragons from the deck like what {{tk|Genesis}} did, {{Tk|True Genesis}} directly sends out Token Spirits from outside the game. While the number of Tokens to be sent out depends on the number of counters, the effect itself is changed from a '''(When Attacks)''' effect on a Cost 7 Spirit to a '''(When Manifests/Attacks)''' effect on a Spirit that can summon itself via {{tk|Mani}} at a condition of 4 counters, which can pretty much be the second turn going first. Being changed to a '''(When Manifests)''' effect that it tied to a card that can {{tk|Mani}} during Either Attack Step makes {{Tk|True Genesis}} a powerful tool in both offense and defense, with the flexibility to send out Tokens during either turn, and doesn't require one to manually summon then attack with Generator Dragon-Zero. While the target is fixed, it is less likely affected by effects that lock summons (as sending out Tokens is not counted as "Summon"), and effects that alter the deck (mill effects, etc.). == Related == * [[Rig Avatar Dragon]] * [[:Category:"Brahma"-named|List of "Brahma"-named cards]] == Other Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Rekka Showdown.title: Rekka Showdown
Rekka Showdown.contentSample:
[[File:BS73-008.png|thumb|200px]] '''Rekka Showdown''' (一騎打・烈火, ''ikiuchi-rekka'') is a new keyword introduced in [[BS73]], currently possessed exclusively by [[Rekka]] family Spirits. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Rekka Showdown}} (When Attacks)'''
You can compare the BP of this Spirit with an opposing Spirit. Destroy the targets with the same or lower BP, and when only the opposing target is destroyed, activate the following effect.
█ [Additional effect]
Rekka Showdown.fullContent:
[[File:BS73-008.png|thumb|200px]] '''Rekka Showdown''' (一騎打・烈火, ''ikiuchi-rekka'') is a new keyword introduced in [[BS73]], currently possessed exclusively by [[Rekka]] family Spirits. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Rekka Showdown}} (When Attacks)'''
You can compare the BP of this Spirit with an opposing Spirit. Destroy the targets with the same or lower BP, and when only the opposing target is destroyed, activate the following effect.
█ [Additional effect] As the name implies, it is a remake of {{tk|Showdown}}, and in general an improved version of such, despite having different pros and cons under specific conditions. Similar to {{tk|Showdown}}, since it is a "BP comparison" effect, it isn't counted as a "Destruction effect", and can bypass cards that protect themselves from being destroyed by opposing effects (e.g. [[The FlameShieldGuardian Corona-Dragon]]). Since it is merely comparing BP, you can also target opposing targets that cannot block by effect or by rule, like various [[Imagine]] Braves, or [[Pilot]] Braves. When compared to {{tk|Showdown}}, there are three major changes. First, the player controlling the Spirit with {{tk|Rekka Showdown}} chooses which Spirit to battle instead of the opponent. This gives much bigger freedom to the player who activates the effect, and the result is much more controllable to produce a desirable outcome. Second, the effect is now optional. That means, you won't be forced to compare BP with opposing Spirits if opposing Spirits have higher BP or come with specific reactions when destroyed by you. Third, the effect timing is no longer '''(Opposing Start Step)''' but '''(When Attacks)''', which changed the use of such effect entirely. On the plus side, it is a helping effect for offense, and provide extra way of removals other than "effect destroys" amid an attack. Since the effect is activated in your own turn, it is also more controllable and could be used immediately after summoning the card, instead of having to wait for the next turn. On the minus side, since the timing is changed to own turn, it could no longer be used to interfere the opponent's board on their turn, or trigger self-destroy related effects on opposing turn by deliberately losing the BP match. Despite so, the change is in general an upgrade under normal circumstances. == Related Cards == * [[:Category:Rekka Showdown|List of Cards with "Rekka Showdown"]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

You can target any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates and battle them simultaneously. When you've done
Rekka Consecutive Blade.fullContent:
[[File:BS73-TX01b.png|thumb|200px]] '''Rekka Consecutive Blade''' (連刃・烈火, ''renjin-rekka'') is a new keyword introduced in [[BS73]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The SengokuDragonEmperor Burning-Souldragon X]], the remake of [[The SengokuDragonEmperor Burning-Souldragon]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3][LV4] {{tk|Rekka Consecutive Blade}} (When Attacks)'''
You can target any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates and battle them simultaneously. When you've done so, during this battle, the cores on the targets targeted by this effect can't be moved. As the name implies, it is a remake of {{tk|True-Consecutive Blade}}, and in general an improved version of its original. In terms of how the life burn effect was removed and included in a separate effect instead, it was closer to the original {{tk|Consecutive Blade}}'s design, but the target attack part makes it a direct upgrade of {{tk|True-Consecutive Blade}}. When compared to {{tk|True-Consecutive Blade}}, user of the effect no longer needs to pay the Soul Core as a cost, making the effect much more flexible in an era where Soul Core is a key to many other effects like {{tk|Mani}}. Another big difference is how the "double target attack" has finally evolved to "targeting any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates on the Field," essentially turning the effect from double kill to literal board swipe as long as Souldragon wins the battle. Adding on to the pressure it brings to the opponent, it comes with a new element of locking cores which usually appears in Green. This allows the player to maximise the benefit of target attacking the whole bard, as it basically prevents the opponent from using Magics or other sorts of defense that requires paying costs as long as there aren't enough cores in their Reserve. This combines well with the end-of-battle life burn of [[The SengokuDragonEmperor Burning-Souldragon X]] as this prevents the opponent from using cards in Flash Timing. == Related Cards == * [[:Category:Rekka Consecutive Blade|List of Cards with "Rekka Consecutive Blade"]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Soul Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BS74-X13.png|thumb|320x320px]] '''Soul Unleash''' ({{ruby|魂|たましい}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}}, ''Tamashii kaihou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS74]], possessed by [[The EndgameSharkEmperor Aztlan]] and [[The RedLavaSeaDragon Blezion]], both [[Concluser]] of [[The Light-DarkContractor Ometeotl]]. It is a derivative keyword of [[Unleash]], yet it functions in a quite different way when compared to the original, or even the other variants. The effect is worded as follows for Aztlan: * {{tk|S Un}} '''Flash - (Either Attack Step)'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By putting your [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] from your "Contractor Ometeotl" Grandwalker Nexus to this card, summon this card from the Hand, treating all summon costs as being paid. As the effect wording suggests, unlike most Unleash effects which serve as powerful effects unlocked by moving cores from Grandwalker Nexuses to cards '''on the Field''', Soul Unleash itself is an effect that allows players to summon the effect owner from the Hand. In essence, the effect is closer to {{tk|Mani}}, but in a reverse way as the Soul Core is made free instead of being sent to the Trash. And this unique effect is made possible because of the unique feature of [[The Light-DarkContractor Ometeotl]]'s deck, which includes Aztlan, the owner of the Soul Unleash keyword, obviously. The effect is still considered an "Unleash" effect, despite being completely different from other variants, most probably because it does come with the action of "moving cores from Grandwalker Nexus to Spirit/Ultimate". Despite not having any specific effects tied to it, the mere summon in Flash enables players to have an extra body on the Field during either Attack Step for both offense and defense. It also links to the (When Summoned/Attacks) effect of Aztlan, which provides very powerful removal. In [[BS75]], another card with the effect is released, with a slightly different structure: {{Unleash|1+[[file:Soul Core.png|20px]]|Soul}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Summoned/Attacks)'''
Once per turn, you can destroy an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. Then, you can send the [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] and one core from your "Contractor Ometeotl" Grandwalker Nexus to this Spirit. When you've done so, negate an opposing active White Magic effect, besides any on-field effects. Instead of being part of an effect that activates from outside the Field, it becomes an effect closer to normal Unleash. As such, it can be concluded that Soul Unleash is in essence an effect that "Moves cores from Grandwalker Nexuses but with a special requirement of Soul Core". == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Soul Unleash|List of cards with Soul Unleash]] * [[The Light-DarkContractor Ometeotl]] {{Keywords Nav}}

The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|2|Solar}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Manifests/Attacks)'''
Destroy any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates up to a total of 30000 BP. Then, by sending two cores from any of your "Bashin Dan" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit, discard up to six cards from your decktop. If this effect discards any "[[Devotee]]"/"[[Astral Deity]]" family card, refresh this Spirit. Following the recent trend of the new "Unleash"-named keywords, like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Curse Unleash]], this Unleash requires a Grandwalker of specific name to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. In this case, it is any Grandwalker Nexus with "Bashin Dan" in name. The name takes the Sun as motif, and makes the effect a contrasting pair with the {{tk|Moon Unleash}} of [[The MoonlightDragonGod Strikewurm-Leo-Hawk]]. It is made consistent with the Sun motif in [[The SunContractor Bashin Dan]], the actual motif behind the name tag, "Apollo", used by the series of key cards Bashin Dan used in the show, and the "sun" motif carries by [[The ShineCentaurusDeity Sagitto-Apollodragon]], as it is the reborn form of [[The SunDragonDeity Rising-Apollodragon]] in lore. As mentioned, the design of the owner of the effect, [[The SunDragonGod ShineTres-Sagitto-Apollodragon]], is resembling [[The ShineCentaurusDeity Sagitto-Apollodragon]] when braved to both [[Tres-Beluga]] and [[The ShineDragon Shine-Blazer]] in the anime, [[Battle Spirits Brave]], as a final form of the former. Hence, what Sagitto-Apollodragon holds while double braved was upgraded and separated into two effects on ShineTres-Sagitto-Apollodragon. {{tk|Solar Unleash}} takes the "mill six to refresh" from [[Tres-Beluga]], and the BP destruction effect from Sagitto-Apollodragon itself. Unlike the original design, however, since {{tk|Solar Unleash}} is a '''(When Manifest/Attacks)''' effect, and [[The SunDragonGod ShineTres-Sagitto-Apollodragon]] can manifest during Either Attack Step, on top of being a strong offensive effect like its originals, it can also be a powerful defensive effect. The refresh condition is also much looser when it isn't tied to card type, and allow "[[Devotee]]" family cards. Much like some other Spirits with "Unleash" effects, since ShineTres-Sagitto-Apollodragon's LV2 core requirement is 3, by activating {{tk|Solar Unleash}}, it automatically levels up to LV2, making the second effect active. == Also See == * [[:Category:"Bashin Dan"-named|List of "Bashin Dan"-named cards]] ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|2|Devil}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] Flash -'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By sending two cores from any of your "Viole Mai" Grandwalker Nexuses to t
Devil Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BSC50-XV03.png|200px|thumb]] '''Devil Unleash''' (魔界放；''Makaihō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC50]], exclusive to [[The StarSlayerDragon Darkwurm-Nova XV]], the XV remake of [[The StarSlayerDragon Darkwurm-Nova]], and one of the designated finishers of [[The StarSlayerContractor Shinomiya Mai]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|2|Devil}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] Flash -'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) By sending two cores from any of your "Viole Mai" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit, send up to two cores from the opposing Field to the Trash. When you've done so, during this turn, you can attack with two "Nova" with different colors you control simultaneously. The opponent can block one of them, but the other can't be blocked (Both battles conclude at the same time) Like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Shining Heaven Unleash]], this Unleash requires Grandwalkers of a specific name to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. Such target is "Viole Mai" for that [[The StarSlayerDragon Darkwurm-Nova XV]] was designed as a key card to the revamped double nova deck which was originally used by Mai in the show, [[Battle Spirits Brave]]. When compared to {{tk|Slayer Unleash}} of [[The StarSlayerDragon Darkwurm-Nova X]], the previous remake of [[The StarSlayerDragon Darkwurm-Nova]] a few years ago which was eventually limited to one copy thanks to its unconditional core boost ability via the Unleash and a "once per game" restriction that can be ignored when the card can be resummoned and reusing the effect, the design of {{tk|Devil Unleash}} tells that the dev team has reflected on the event in a way that being (Once per Turn: Same Name), it can't be used multiple times within the same turn. On the other hand, the effect is by no means a weaker effect. Instead of destroying Braves or exhausted Spirits, Devil Unleash proceeds to deplete opponent's available cores for defense on the Field, including those on Nexuses, and allow a legitimate double attack of "Nova"s. On top of being able to achieve the romance which couldn't be done in the show, that is, attacking with both Siegwurm-Nova and Darkwurm-Nova at the same time, it also increases the pressure the attacks have on the opponent, as the double symbol x2 + 2 life burn = an attack that takes six lives at once. The unblockable part of the double attack means one of the double symbol attacks would certainly go through if the opponent fails to remove any of the attackers. This makes it harder to defense by ending the attack step. {{tk|Devil Unleash}} is essentially a portmanteau between the archetype "[[Makai]]" and the base keyword {{tk|Unleash}} (read as ''kaihou'' in Japanese). Besides being the main card archetype which [[Mai Viole]] uses, "Makai" also translates to the "demon realm", hosting a group of people which Mai temporarily sided with in the [[Battle Spirits Brave]] series, and the motif of the [[Superstar]] family. == Also See == * [[:Category:"Viole Mai"-named|List of "Viole Mai"-named cards]] * [[:Category:"Nova"-named|List of "Nova"-named cards]] ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

True Infinite Flame.fullContent:
[[File:BS75-RV001.png|thumb|250px]] '''True Infinite Flame''' (真・無限焔, ''Shin Mugen Homura'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS75]], and currently possessed exclusively by the Revival version of [[The NinjaHead Souldragon-Hokage]]. The effects reads: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|True Infinite Flame}} (Your Attack Step)'''
When your Red/Green Spirit attacks, you can target and attack an opposing Spirit/Ultimate, and during this battle, the opponent can't activate Burst effects. When the specified target is depleted/destroyed, either refresh the attacking Spirit, or, for each symbol the attacking Spirit has, send an opposing Life to the Reserve. As the name implies, it is a modified version of the original {{tk|Infinite Flame}} effect owned by the original Hokage. While the parts concerning target attack, life burn, and refresh are retained, there are quite a lot of changes when compared to the original {{tk|Infinite Flame}}. First of all, the effect now applies to '''ALL''' Red/Green Spirits you control instead of just Hokage himself. This makes the effect an actual supporting effect that applies to the other finishers or just any supporting Spirits in the deck. By turning it into a field-supporting effect, and having such a loose condition (only requiring Red/Green in color, and not even Red-only or Green-only), this has created immeasurable flexibility for the finishing plan, and made Revival Hokage an ultra versatile card when it is now a Burst card as well. Second part is how the burst sealing effect from the LV2-3 effect, a separate effect on OG Hokage, is now upgraded to Burst effect lock, and added to {{tk|True Infinite Flame}}. As it is a field-supporting effect, it essentially gives all Red/Green decks using Hokage automatic burst effect lock. The duration is also changed from a "Lasting effect as long as the Spirit is on Field" to "During this battle", contributing to even stronger locking regardless of opponent's removal. As for the third part, the life burn & refresh from the original is changed to "life burn OR refresh" in the new version. This is probably to balance out the overly versatile factors mentioned above. Nonetheless, the effect is solid enough that this downside is minimal. {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Thunder God Bombardment.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X02.png|200px|thumb]] '''Thunder God Bombardment''' ({{ruby|雷|らい}}{{ruby|神|しん}}{{ruby|砲|ほう}}{{ruby|撃|げき}}；''raishin-hougeki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The TigerTwelveGodKing Revol-Tiger X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The TigerTwelveGodKing Revol-Tiger]]. The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1-2-3] {{tk|Thunder God Bombardment}} (When Attacks)'''
You can reveal two cards from your decktop. Among them, for each "Zeus"/"Z"/"GodKing", send an opposing Life to the Reserve. Add the revealed cards to the Hand. As the name implies, it is a new variant of the {{tk|Bombardment}} keyword owned by the original Revol-Tiger, and a modified version of {{tk|Grand Bombardment}}. The first two word, "Thunder God", also fits the title of Zeus, its ideal support target, very well. Similar to [[The RedThunderGodKing Revol-Tiger-Z]], the owner of {{tk|Grand Bombardment}}, which was designed to serve the deck led by [[Grandwalker Zeus|Zeus]], which revolves around the [[Emperor Beast]] family that Revol-Tiger is in, [[The TigerTwelveGodKing Revol-Tiger X]] was designed to serve the contract Grandalker version of Zeus, [[The ThunderboltContractor Zeus]]. Hence, the "hitting targets" of {{tk|Thunder God Bombardment}} are changed to "Zeus"/"Z"/"GodKing"-named cards, which are essentially "all" cards that one would put into Contractor Zeus' deck, not counting tech cards or generic defense cards. As the keyword is also "Bombardment"-named, it can be supported by cards that specified "Bombardment"-named keywords (note: but not those which supports {{tk|Bombardment}} only), like [[Mogami Shunta]]. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

[[File:BS76-X03.png|200px|thumb]] '''Banner God Strike''' ({{ruby|旗|き}}{{ruby|神|しん}}{{ruby|撃|げき}}；''ki-shin-geki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou]]. Since it now supports the [[Flag]] decks, and the "[[Bannerace]]" family, the name has incorporated the flag/banner element. Being a powerful effect to begin with, the effect is almost exactly the same as the original one. However, the supporting target is changed from "[[God-King]]" family Spirits only to all "[[Bannerace]]"/"[[God-King]]" family Spirits. Considering the fact that almost every card in the deck that Tiamdou X is supporting would have the "[[Bannerace]]" family, this means that the new "God Strike" isn't only limited to the "[[God-King]]" Spirits, but also minions and every other member of the deck. The pseudo unbloackable ability is hence upgraded by just extending its target to far beyond a few high cost cards in the deck. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

You can draw two cards. Then, you can summon a Purple "[[Bannerace]]"/"[[God-King]]" family card fr
Banner God-Army.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X03.png|200px|thumb]] '''Banner God-Army''' ({{ruby|旗|き}}{{ruby|神|しん}}{{ruby|軍|ぐん}}；''ki-shin-geki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The SnakeTwelveGodKing Tiamadou]]. The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1-2-3] {{tk|Banner God-Army}} (When Advents)'''
You can draw two cards. Then, you can summon a Purple "[[Bannerace]]"/"[[God-King]]" family card from your Hand/Trash, without paying the cost. As the name implies, it is a remake of the {{tk|God-Army}} keyword owned by the original Tiamadou. Since it now supports the [[Flag]] decks, and the "[[Bannerace]]" family, the name has incorporated the flag/banner element. When compared with the original {{tk|God-Army}}, the number of cards to be summoned is limited to one from either the Hand or Trash, instead of one from each. The color of the card to be summoned is also restricted to Purple, so the combo potential across colors and the ceiling of the effect is reduced by a considerable level. Meanwhile, the effect can now summon any "card" of the designated family and color. This means that it can also summon ''Brave cards'' like [[Absolute Wind Demon-God]], or ''Ultimate cards'' like [[The UltimateGodKing Mugenchocoian-Dragon]], from the Hand/Trash. As the "[[Bannerace]]" family is the core family of the new era which covers basically every card in the deck, from low costs to high costs, the effect in itself becomes something that can free summon almost any card in the deck instead of just the finishers, as that's what usually the Spirits with [[God-King]] family are. This enables player to summon other cards that provide resources or removal abilities instead of only big cost finishers. As such, while it was mentioned that the combo potential is reduced, there are actually new rooms to explore as well. Another big change to the effect is that it now comes with card draw. With the "draw two cards" effect, it not only helps to provide the card(s) you want to summon, but also provide further hand resources that can be used both offensively or defensively. As the advent timing of Tiamadou X is (Your Turn), and the effect timing of {{tk|Banner God-Army}} is '''(When Advents)''', this means that one can now draw two cards + summon the card in Main Step before even launching an attack. As a weakness of {{tk|God-Army}}, since it was a (When Attacks) effect, you can't immediately use the (When Attacks) effect of a card you summoned via {{tk|God-Army}} until the next attack (as Tiamadou is attacking), and the opponent would have the Flash Timing to remove your summoned Spirit. However, with {{tk|Banner God-Army}}, since everything can be done in Main Step, you can attack with the summoned Spirit directly without needing to worry that it got removed before it can attack. This changes the nature of the effect fundamentally. While it also means that it can only be used once unless you advent-ed another Tiamadou X, unlike the original which can activate as many times as long as it can refresh, the flexibility of the effect is increased by a lot. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Dark Assault.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-AX01.png|200px|thumb]] '''Dark Assault''' ({{ruby|暗|あん}}・{{ruby|強|きょう}}{{ruby|襲|しゅう}}；''an-kyou-shiyuu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The DinoEvilDeity Diablo-Gundinos]], the AX remake of [[The DinoDeity Gundinos]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV1-2-3] {{D Assault|2}} (When Attacks)'''
Up to twice per turn, you can send a total of three cards from your Hand and decktop to the Trash. When you've done so, this Spirit can refresh, and during this battle, you can increase the LV cost of an opposing Spirit/Nexus by +3. The general form is as follows: * '''[Level] {{D Assault|X}} (When Attacks)'''
Up to [X times] per turn, you can send a total of three cards from your Hand and decktop to the Trash. When you've done so, this Spirit can refresh, and during this battle, you can increase the LV cost of an opposing Spirit/Nexus by +3. As the name implies, it is a twisted version of the {{tk|Assault}} keyword, which is also owned by the original [[The DinoDeity Gundinos|Gundinos]] despite being a Red card (as Gundinos is a part of the keyword-exchange series). The "dark" part of the name most probably comes from the fact that the AX remake of Gudinos is now a [[Purple]] card. While the keyword is named after {{tk|Assault}}, the common condition of exhausting own nexuses to refresh the owner of the effect, which existed in all previous remakes of {{tk|Assault}}, is removed and changed to something entirely unrelated to Nexuses. To match the decktype and core mechanic of [[The DemonArmyFlagbearer Amon|Amon]], which Diablo-Gundinos is designed to serve, the triggering condition becomes "sending cards from Hand and Decktop to the Trash." Instead of relying on the number of Nexuses on Field, the condition for refreshing is much looser when there is no need for preparation (i.e. deploying Nexus on the Field). This is in fact rather ironic when Amon is actually a Flag "Nexus". Regarding the condition, it is worthy to note that, one can choose to send all three cards from the decktop to the Trash, while sending 0 cards from the Hand. Also, as the action is "Sending cards to the Trash", instead of "discarding cards", effects that prevent cards from being discarded from either player's deck '''cannot''' stop the effect. And the refresh part is not the end of {{tk|Dark Assault}}. Most probably incorporated from the effect of the original and revival version of Gundinos, {{tk|Dark Assault}} also comes with a removal effect for its second part. By increasing the LV cost of opposing Spirit/Nexus, it stops even [[Rebirth]] and is one of the most effective format of removal in [[Purple]]. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

High Speed.fullContent:
[[File:Leavwolf1.jpg|thumb]]
'''High Speed''' (神速, ''Shinsoku''), is a keyword exclusive to Green cards. The effect is worded as follows: 
* '''Flash - High Speed -''' This card in Hand can be summoned by paying the cost with cores in the Reserve. In this case, cores to be put on this Spirit must also be from the Reserve. 
High Speed allows the player to avoid summoning everything in their Main Step, reducing the chances of their cards getting removed before attack/block. This effect also allows players to reuse cores, especially since cores on a card go to the Reserve after it's removed from the Field. If used correctly, an aggressive play can be made.

Armor (Keyword).fullContent:
[[File:BS02-040.jpg|thumb|320x320px]] '''Armor''' (装甲; ''Soukou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS02]], possessed exclusively by White Spirits, and given exclusively by White cards. It was one of the very first keywords received by the White color. The keyword is worded as follows: * {{Armor|Color(/Color)}}
This Spirit is unaffected by Spirit/Nexus/Magic effects of the specified color(s). == Overview == It is worth noting that the keyword only applies to effects which directly affect the Spirit possessing it, for example if the effect attempts to remove cores from it, or exhausting it. The effect does not shut out effects which affect other elements of the game, such as force ending the Attack Step or changing the battle rules. While the wording is formatted simply, in specific details, "unaffected" means the following two points: # The Spirit with {{tk|Armor}} cannot receive opposing effects of the specified color. ## '''Example:''' While an opposing Red Spirit is attacking with {{tk|Clash}}, as the Spirit with {{Armor|Red}} cannot receive opposing Red effects, it cannot be forced to block by {{tk|Clash}}. # The Spirit with {{tk|Armor}} cannot be selected by opposing effects of the specified color. ## '''Example:''' When the opponent uses [[Binding Thorn]] (BS01-134), a Green Magic card, they cannot select your Spirit with {{Armor|Green}}. ## As long as the effect is by the opponent, the same rule also applies even if the effect requires you, the affected player, to select your own Spirits. ### '''Example:''' When the opponent uses [[Thorn Prison]] (BS06-100), a Green Magic card, even if you are the one selecting your own Spirits, since it is an opposing effect, you cannot select your own Spirits with {{Armor|Green}}. As immunity effects are prioritised over other effects except by "cannot be prevented" effects, {{tk|Armor}} can negate any applied effects on a Spirit. * '''Example:''' While your Spirit is attacking, during the opponent's Flash timing, the opponent uses [[Euthanasia]] to disallow your Spirits' "When Destroyed" effects from activating. Then, when it is your chance to activate a Flash effect, you use [[Invincible Shield]] on your attacking Spirit. Since your attacking Spirit now gains {{Armor|Purple}}, it will be able to activate its "When Destroyed" effects. * For more details, check out [[Comprehensive Rules/Effect Texts#"Unaffected by Effects" Effects (効果を受けない)]]. Also, when a Brave Spirit activates its {{tk|During Brave}} effect received from the Brave, as the effect is treated as a Spirit effect, {{tk|Armor}} can block off the effect. However, any "When Summoned" effects, [[Burst]] effects, or {{tk|Accel}} effects, or as a rule of thumb, any effects listed above the Brave condition bar on a Brave card, are treated as Brave effects, and {{tk|Armor}} cannot block them off. For [[The ArmoredSacred Walhalance]] (BS06-X24), instead of stating the colors specifically, the {{tk|Armor}} keyword has the infinity symbol (∞). This means that the protection range of the keyword is changeable, depending on which symbol color the opposing field has. == Trivia == {{tk|Armor}} was introduced during the time when the game still had official English release. The official English translation of the keyword was called "Immunity" instead, and the specifications of the keyword were as follows: * '''''Immunity: Color(/Color)'''''
(Permanent)
This spirit is unaffected by the effects of cards your opponent controls with the listed color(s). == Derivative Keywords == As the game develops, more and more different "Armor"-named keywords are introduced to the game. These derivative keywords are not treated as the same as {{tk|Armor}} (nor are the derivative keywords treated as the same to each other), hence if any effect were to target a Spirit with {{tk|Armor}}, Spirits with the following "Armor"-named keywords listed are not affected. If an effect wants to target all "Armor"-named keywords, it will use the wording "'Armor'-named effects" instead. === [[Heavy Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS12]]. * Different to {{tk|Armor}}, {{tk|Heavy Armor}} also protects the possessing card from Brave effects, in addition to Spirit, Nexus, and Magic effects. * {{tk|Heavy Armor}} does not protect the possessing card from Ultimate effects, as the keyword was introduced before the Ultimate card type was introduced. * Completely replaced {{tk|Armor}} since its introduction, and was the main reason why {{tk|Armor}} never showed up in the game anymore. === [[Ultra Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS25]]. * Different to {{tk|Armor}}, {{tk|Ultra Armor}} also protects the possessing card from Ultimate effects, in addition to Spirit, Nexus, and Magic effects. * {{tk|Ultra Armor}} does not protect the possessing card from Brave effects. === [[Ultra Heavy Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS36]]. * Unlike any of its predecessors, Ultra Heavy Armor does not specify any card type, and instead block off all effects of the specified colors. === [[PS Armor]] === * Introduced in [[SD52]] as a keyword exclusive to the Gundam collaboration series. * Unlike any of its predecessors, {{tk|PS Armor}} references the cost of a card instead of the color. * Full name of the keyword is "Phase Shift Armor", a technology introduced in the anime Mobile Suit Gundam SEED. * In [[Battle Spirits CrossOver]], the video game, as collaboration cards cannot be added to the game, game-exclusive cards with effects almost exactly the same as the collaboration cards were introduced instead. Among them, some cards with {{tk|PS Armor}} were referenced, and the keyword was named {{tk|MD Armor}} instead. ** It is never explained what "MD" means. === [[TP Armor]] === * Introduced in [[CB13]] as a keyword exclusive to the Gundam collaboration series. * Unlike any of its predecessors, {{tk|TP Armor}} references the level of a card instead of the color or cost. * Full name of the keyword is "Trans-Phase Armor", a technology introduced in the anime Mobile Suit Gundam SEED. === [[VPS Armor]] === * Introduced in [[CB16]] as a keyword exclusive to the Gundam collaboration series. * An upgrade version of {{tk|PS Armor}}, {{tk|VPS Armor}} references the original cost of a card, meaning even if, for example, a Cost 5 card increases its cost, such as by braving, its effect still would not get past {{VPSa|Cost 5 or less}}. * Full name of the keyword is "Variable Phase Shift Armor", a technology introduced in the anime Mobile Suit Gundam SEED Destiny. === [[Illusive Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS57]]. * Its protection range is the same as {{tk|Heavy Armor}}, with the additional effect of having the possessing card being unblockable. === [[Contract Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS62]], possessed exclusively by the Revival version of [[The MoonlightDragon Strike-Siegwurm]]. * Its protection range is the same as {{tk|Heavy Armor}}, but additional specified color protection can be unlocked if it is possessed by a "Strike-Siegwurm"-named Spirit that is during [[Contract Advent]]. === [[Aurora Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS63]], possessed exclusively by [[The UltraAuroraMachineDeity Great-Stark]]. * Its protection range is the same as {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, with the additional effect of receiving all effects from a "Super-Stark"-named pre-advent card underneath the possessing card. === [[Count Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BS64]], possessed exclusively by [[The AstralZeroSword Foranswer]]. * Its protection range is the same as {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, with the additional effect of giving the possessing Spirit an extra White symbol while the player has six counters or more. === [[Illusive Ultra Heavy Armor]] === * Introduced in [[BSC50]], possessed exclusively by [[The MoonlightDragonGod Strikewurm-Leo-Hawk]]. * It is basically a combination of {{tk|Illusive Armor}} and {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}. ==Related Articles== * Spell Blight.fullContent:
[[File:BS14-X02.jpg|thumb]] '''Spell Blight''' (呪滅撃, ''Jumetsu geki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS14]], exclusive to Purple Spirits, a modified version of [[Curse]]. The effect's text reads: *'''Spell Blight''' (When Destroyed by the Opponent)
By sending an opposing Life to the Trash, this Spirit remains on the Field, refreshed. Although the keyword spawns from Curse, the effect works completely different to Curse. Curse works offensively, and the theme is all about bringing the opponent down together. On the other hand, Spell Blight is more effective defensively, as remaining on the field, refreshed, means providing an unrestricted blocker for the rest of the turn, as well as giving detriments to the opponent. Unfortunately, Spell Blight is still weak to all other kinds of removals that aren't destruction, since the effect only activates upon destruction by the opponent. The effect is also using the "By doing A, do B" wording, meaning that if the Spirit with Spell Blight either can't reduce the opposing Life (e.g. the opponent has used [[Delta Barrier]] for the turn), then Spell Blight can't activate at all. Despite being related to Curse in terms of mechanics, Spell Blight '''isn't''' treated as a "Curse"-named keyword due to different spellings. == Also See== *[[:Category:Spell Blight|List of cards with Spell Blight]] *[[:Category:Spell Blight support|List of Spell Blight support cards]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Bunshin.fullContent:
[[File:BS22-X03.PNG|thumb]] '''Bunshin '''(分身) is a Green keyword premiered in [[BS22]], along with its respective family with the same name. Cards with this effect have the following text: Place up to X cards from your decktop face down onto your Field, and by adding one or more cores from your Reserve to them, during the game, those cards become "Cost 0/Family: Bunshin/<1>LV1 BP 3000/''[Green symbol]''" Green Bunshin Spirit. (Bunshin Spirits can't be braved/advented onto/switched place, and are discarded if sent to the Hand/Removed Zone/Deck.) ''(X= the number indicated by the effect.)'' In other words, this keyword can create weaker copies of the Spirit you summon. The timing of this effect also varies. For example, it activates when  [[The LightFangPhoenix Rekkuumaru]] is summoned, and it activates when [[Jounin-Tonbi]] is destroyed. With the assistance of [[The Twisting Dangaro Mountains]], Bunshin can easily fill up the board and swarm the opponent. When '''Bunshin''' was first out, face-down cards were undisclosed info to both players that not even the owner can know about its content. Hence, supporting cards like [[Summoning Technique]] involved quite some luck factor. However, following the change of rules concerning face-down cards from Ultra Advent Era that the owner of the face-down cards can now check the content of the card, the use of [[Bunshin]] and [[Summoning Technique]], combining with [[Ninja Gale]] support, brought upon a new change to the play-style of decks using such effect. == Trivia == * The name "Bunshin" is the pronunciation of the Japanese word "分身", which exactly means a copy of something. The word is usually used on humans, like ninja skills. == Noticeable Q&As == Q5: Are Bunshin Spirits treated as Spirits with no printed effects?
A5: Yes, they are. Q8: While you control "[[The Inverse Tower of Frozen Icicle]]", when a Bunshin Spirit is out, can you put a core from the Void onto a White Spirit you control?
A8: No, you can't. Bunshin Spirits are put out, not summoned. Q9: Can you flip it up and check the content of your face-down Bunshin Spirits on field?
A9: Yes, you can. Be careful not to let the opponent see the content when you check them. == Also see == * [[:Category:Bunshin|List of cards with "Bunshin"]] * [[:Category:Bunshin support|List of "Bunshin"/"Bunshin Spirit" related support]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

At the start of each opposing step, you can send a core from the opposing Reserve/any opposing Spirit to their Trash. As the name implies
Spellbind.fullContent:
[[File:Ouro.png|thumb|319x319px]] '''Spellbind''' (呪縛, ''Jubaku'') is a Purple keyword which had its debut in [[BS36]]. Currently, the only Spirit to possess it is [[The DragonTwelveGodKing Ourovorius]]. Spirits which possess this ability have the following text on their cards: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Spellbind}} (Opposing Turn)'''
At the start of each opposing step, you can send a core from the opposing Reserve/any opposing Spirit to their Trash. As the name implies, it is a "binding" effect that works like a curse applied on the opponent, which makes them start with one less core every step. While Refresh Step would bring back the cores, just by ending the turn after summoning Ourovorius would mean the opponent losing a total of five cores from their Spirits before they can make any changes to their core arrangements in their Main Step (going through Start/Core/Draw/Refresh/Main Steps). Apart from removing cores from Spirits on the Field, {{tk|Spellbind}} also allows the player to remove cores from the Reserve, which include those cores reserved for using defense magics or Accels. Sending core from Reserve to the Trash also reduces the possibility of Green's special summons like {{tk|High Speed}} or {{Seal|High Speed Seal}}, which generally require cores from the Reserve. In general, the effect is a great addition to the core control ability of the [[Death Dragon]] deck. While it could not provide one-time swipe of cores, its lasting impact is not to be underestimated. The keyword was later remade as {{tk|True Spellbind}} by the 10th anniversary of [[Battle Spirits Double Drive]] with [[The DragonTwelveGodKing Ourovorius X]]. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

* '''Whirlwind: X - '''(When Attacks) Heavy exhaust X opposing Spirits/Ultimates. (Heavily exhausted cards are turned upside down and become exhausted after refreshing once.)

* '''Whirlwind: X - '''(When Advents/Attacks) Heavy exhaust X opposing Spirits/Ultimates. (Heavily exhausted cards are turned upside down a
Whirlwind.fullContent:
[[File:The BladeKingBeast Byak-GaroRev-A.jpg|thumb]]
'''Whirlwind '''(旋風, ''Senpū'') is a special ability of green spirits. Spirits or Magics with this effect have the following text: 
* '''Whirlwind: X - '''(When Attacks) Heavy exhaust X opposing Spirits/Ultimates. (Heavily exhausted cards are turned upside down and become exhausted after refreshing once.)

* '''Whirlwind: X - '''(When Advents/Attacks) Heavy exhaust X opposing Spirits/Ultimates. (Heavily exhausted cards are turned upside down and become exhausted after refreshing once.)

* '''Flash''' - '''Whirlwind: X - ''' Heavy exhaust X opposing Spirits/Ultimates. (Heavily exhausted cards are turned upside down and become exhausted after refreshing once.)

This ability allows Green to heavy exhaust opposing Spirits/Ultimates accoording to the number highlighted in the keyword.

Examples of cards with this ability include [[The WhirlwindKingBeast Blast-Saber]] and [[The BladeKingBeast Byak-Garo]].

== Rulings ==
0. The amount of Spirits/Ultimates to be heavy exhausted by '''Whirlwind '''cannot be increased by Green [[Charge]].  

1. Spirits/Ultimates in Heavy Exhausted condition cannot attack or block just like S/U in Exhausted condition.

2. In order for the S/U in Heavy Exhausted condition to be in Refresh condition, it needs to be refreshed twice. *S/U in Heavy Exhausted condition turns to Exhausted condition when refreshed (from refresh step or any refresh effects) and any effects triggered [When Spirit is refresh] can be activated at this situation.

3. Any effects that target S/U in Exhausted condition can target S/U in Heavy Exhausted condition as well. Therefore, effects that can destroys exhausted S/U can target them as well. In addition, any S/U that can block while exhausted can activate their effect while Heavy Exhausted.

4. Any S/U in Heavy Exhausted condition that were destroyed or removed from the field, it it trigger an effect that allows them to remains on the field in a specific condition, will changed to the specified conditon and not considered refreshed if remained on the field in exhausted condition or in refreshed condition. 

5. Heavy Exhaust is treated as Exhaust.

6. Heavy Exhaust can target S/U in Refresh condition and in Exhausted condition.

7. When S/U is Heavy Exhausted, any effects triggered [When Spirit is exhausted] can be activated at this situation.

8. Any effect that cannot be exhausted cannot be heavy exhausted. In addition, Imagine Brave cannot be heavy exhausted.

9. If you fuse a Brave to a Heavy Exhausted condition S/U, the Brave will be in Heavy Exhausted condition as well.

10. If you fuse an Imagine Brave to a Heavy Exhausted condition S/U, the Imagine Brave in refresh condition, but the S/U is in Heavy Exhausted condition.

At the start of each opposing step, you can send a core from the opposing Field/Reserve to th
True Spellbind.fullContent:
[[File:BS77-X04.png|200px|thumb]] '''True Spellbind''' ({{ruby|真|しん}}・{{ruby|呪|じゅ}}{{ruby|縛|ばく}}；''shin-jubaku'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS77]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The DragonTwelveGodKing Ourovorius X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The DragonTwelveGodKing Ourovorius]]. The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1-2-3] {{tk|True Spellbind}} (Opposing Turn)'''
At the start of each opposing step, you can send a core from the opposing Field/Reserve to the Trash. Then, you can send a core from any opposing Grandwalker Nexus to the Void. As the name implies, it is a remake of the {{tk|Spellbind}} keyword owned by the original Ourovorius. When compared to the original {{tk|Spellbind}}, it is basically a direct upgrade version, making the "true" prefix a very fitting description. While the general structure of the effect is the same as its original, the core removal target is upgraded from "Spirit/Reserve" to "Field/Reserve", making it much more flexible in dealing with Nexuses on field or Ultimates, which its original version could not handle. Since "Reserve + Field" has basically covered all regions to put cores normally, in essence it means "nowhere is safe" for the opponent to put their cores to escape from Ourovorius. While it is not specified that you directly remove the opponent's Soul Core, as long as the Spirit/Reserve you targeted as only Soul Core on it, {{Tk|True Spellbind}} could remove even the Soul Core, which is having even greater importance these days than before. As Ourovorius X can {{tk|Mani}} at a very early stage, bearing no other complicated {{tk|Mani}} conditions, {{tk|True Spellbind}} can hit the field at early game, where every core matters a lot. The combination of the increased coverage and fast appearance have made the effect more powerful than what it might feel reading the effect. On top of the upgrade of the field control part, another big change is that {{tk|True Spellbind}} now covers cores from Grandwalker Nexuses. True to Ourovorius X's flavor text, "its Spellbind could reach even the gods". While one core at the start of each step might not be as big impact after Refresh Step, one core to void per step from Grandwalker Nexuses is certainly posing continuous threat to Grandwalker-centric decks. Just by summoning Ourovorius X and ending the turn, opposing Grandwalker Nexuses would automatically lose five cores until the opponent reaches their Main Step. The nuke at the Attack Step that follows would also disrupt the game calculation for cores for {{tk|Mani}} or {{tk|Grand Skill}}/{{tk|Contract Skill}}/{{tk|Grandphosis}}. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31917 |What kind of effect is {{tk|True Spellbind}}? |It is an effect where: at the start of each opposing step, you can send a core from the opposing Field/Reserve to the Trash. Then, you can send a core from any opposing Grandwalker Nexus to the Void. {{tk|True Spellbind}} is not treated as {{tk|Spellbind}}. |- |31918 |When sending core to Trash via {{tk|True Spellbind}} at Core Step, do you send the core before the opponent adds a core from the Void to the Reserve? |Yes. |- |31919 |When sending core to Trash via {{tk|True Spellbind}} at Refresh Step, do you send the core before the opponent moves their core from the Trash to the Reserve? |Yes. |- |31920 |During the opposing Start Step, if you activated the {{tk|Contract Field}} of [[The DestructionContractor Shiva]] and discarded a card from the Removed Zone to make {{tk|True Spellbind}} "can't be prevented", would {{tk|True Spellbind}} become a "can't be prevented" effect for the Core Step that comes right after? |No. In this case, only the {{tk|True Spellbind}} that takes place at the Start Step would become "can't be prevented". Also, since the part after "then" in {{tk|True Spellbind}} has a different effect timing, it won't become "can't be prevented" as well. |- |} == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

This Spirit is unaffected by opposing (Color) effects. Also, this Spirit gains every effect of a "Super-Stark" pre-advent card beneath this Spirit, ignoring levels. The effect consists of two parts: (1) Unaffected by opposing effects of the listed colors + (2) Inherit all effects from [[The AuroraMobile Super-Stark|Super-Stark]]. Part (1) is essentially the same as {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, making Aurora Armor an upgraded version of the effect. As a demerit, however, since the effect is not treated as {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, effects that can only be prevented by {{tk|Heavy Armor}}/{{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}} could pierce {{tk|Aurora Armor}} despite the fact that {{tk|Aurora Armor}} is the stronger version. Part (2) is the common feature across all Ultra Contract Advent forms of [[Wanderer Dan]]'s six Contract Spirits, an effect that shows how the Ultra Contract Advent forms are the upgrade forms of their X-rare Contract Advent counterparts. While the name reads like "Extreme Armor" in a literal sense, considering the context of Stark and the ability of inheriting the effects from [[The AuroraMobile Super-Stark|Super-Stark]], it is supposedly based on the aurora (極光) motif of Stark instead. The double meaning and the ability to grant Stark the long-waited immunity make it a fitting keyword for the final form of Stark. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Barrier.fullContent:
[[file:BS64-087.png|thumb]]

'''Barrier''' (バリア; ''Baria'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS64]] that isn't actually owned by any card but a name given to the cards put onto the Removed Zone by [[Bravery Barrier]]. The effect is worded as below:

*“{{tk|Barrier}} When your Life would be reduced, by adding this card to the Hand, you reduce one less Life.” (You can only put up to three {{tk|Barrier}}. Besides {{tk|Barrier}}, those cards are unaffected by any other effects, and can't be used.) 

As the name implies, Barrier cards work like extra barriers to protect their owner's life. They also serve as potential extra hand resources that can be added to the hand when the owner cancels out life damage with it. The effect in general is built on prior White's life protection effects like [[The OracleTwentyOnePillars XVII The Star]]'s, with an extra layer of protection for it being placed on the Removed Zone and unaffected by other effects. To avoid it being abused with other facedown card synergy, Barrier cards can't be used while they serve as Barrier, and are unaffected by own effects as well. Since they are facedown, their contents also can't be referenced. However, as they are still cards in the Removed Zone, they can be ''counted''.  

For rulings concerning Barrier cards, check the extra information on [[Bravery Barrier]]'s page.

When this Spirit would leave the Field due to the opponent, destroy an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. True-Curse serves as a direct upgrade of [[Curse]], being able to activate whenever the Spirit possessing it would leave the Field by any
True-Curse.fullContent:
[[file:BS67-008.png|thumb]] '''True-Curse''' (真・呪撃 ; ''shin-jugeki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS67]], possessed only by Purple Spirits, and currently also only in the "[[Blood Crystal]]" family. The effect reads as follows: *{{tk|True-Curse}} (Your Turn)
When this Spirit would leave the Field due to the opponent, destroy an opposing Spirit/Ultimate. True-Curse serves as a direct upgrade of [[Curse]], being able to activate whenever the Spirit possessing it would leave the Field by any methods, as long it is by the opponent, comparing to Curse which can only activate if the Spirit remains until BP comparison, largely increasing the range of activation timing. True-Curse also allows the player to freely choose whichever opposing Spirit/Ultimate to destroy, comparing to Curse which can only destroy the blocking Spirit (and cannot even target Ultimates). The effect serves as a great menace to the opponent, as with every attack, the opponent always has to make the decision of either trading a block with their own Spirit/Ultimate, or taking a life. It allows the True-Curse to become an effective tempo deck, keeping the number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates low. With the nature of being in the Purple color, it also means that there are always ways to replenish the hand by drawing more, so to summon more Spirits with True-Curse, or retrieving said cards from the Trash to repeat the procedure. Obviously, the weakness of True-Curse would mainly be Purple [[Armor]] (or any variations of "Armor"-named effects), as the immunity prevents the opposing Spirits/Ultimates from getting destroyed. The keyword may also be weak to removal effects which disallow the activation of effects upon leaving the Field. == See Also: == * [[:Category:True-Curse|List of cards with True-Curse]] * [[:Category:True-Curse support|List of cards supporting True-Curse]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Fierce Windstorm.fullContent:
[[file:BSC45-XV03.png|250px|thumb]] '''Fierce Windstorm''' ({{ruby|激|げき}}{{ruby|暴|ぼう}}{{ruby|風|ふう}}; ''geki boufuu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC45]], possessed exclusively by [[The BladeKingBeast Byak-Garo XV]]. The effect reads as follows: *{{F Wind|2}} '''(Your Attack Step)'''
Unless the opponent exhausts two non-blocking Spirits they control, they can't block. '''Fierce Windstorm''' is an upgraded version of the [[Windstorm]] keyword. Instead of limiting to only when a certain Spirit is attacking, Fierce Windstorm activates throughout the whole Attack Step, and can activate regardless of whichever card type is attacking, since the keyword simply adds conditions to the opponent's block declaration. This is also different to the original Windstorm keyword, which only makes the opponent exhaust Spirits when they block, instead of putting the exhaustion effect as a requirement to block. While currently only Byak-Garo XV is given the keyword, with the effect given a specific number ("2" in this case), it's suggested that the number can be changed if any future cards were to be released with the same keyword, allowing even further potential upgrades of the effect. ==See Also:== [[:Category:Fierce Windstorm|List of cards with Fierce Windstorm]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Nether Immortality.fullContent:
[[file:BS75-016.png|thumb|200px]] '''Nether Immortality''' (冥不死 ; ''meifushi'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS75]], currently exclusive to "Nether"-named cards in the [[The NetherContractor Dionysus|Dionysus]] archetype. The wording is as follows: * {{N Im|(Condition)}} '''(Either Attack Step)'''
(Can't Stack: {{tk|Nether Immortality}}) When your (Condition) "Nether" is destroyed, you can summon (deploy) this card from the Trash. With the effect, you can summon/deploy the card with {{tk|Nether Immortality}} from your Trash by paying the summon/deploy cost when your "Nether"-named cards on Field of XXX condition (e.g. those with Cost 8 or more/those with [[Devotee]]/[[Concluser]] family, etc.) is destroyed during Either Attack Step. It is a new variant of {{tk|Immortality}}, and the general concept is still the resurrection of cards with such keyword when the condition is fulfilled (aka when XXX is destroyed). However, there are certain unique features making it a different effect. 1) The target is more specific and limited to the destruction of "Nether"-named cards, fitting Dionysus' theme and essentially giving the keyword the name, "Nether Immortality". 2) While the target is more limited in card name, it isn't limited to the Spirit card type like normal {{tk|Immortality}}, meaning that it works even when your "Nether"-named '''Ultimates or Nexuses''' are destroyed. 3) On top of (2), unlike {{tk|Immortality}}, the card to be resurrected from the Trash is also not limited to Spirit/Brave, as the owner of {{tk|Nether Immortality}} includes Nexus cards like [[The Nether Mausoleum]]. Hence, while the effect target is more limited when comparing to {{tk|Immortality}}, the actual effect range is wider in the right deck. Since the {{tk|Contract Skill}} of [[The NetherContractor Dionysus]] allows you to destroy own Spirits/Ultimates, {{tk|Nether Immortality}} is actullly a semi-active effect instead of a passive one reliant on opponent's actions. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Nether Immortality|List of cards with Nether Immortality]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

By paying two costs, refresh this Spirit. When you've done so, dur
Grand Twinkle Soar.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X06.png|200px|thumb]] '''Grand Twinkle Soar''' ({{ruby|神|しん}}{{ruby|煌|こう}}{{ruby|飛|ひ}}{{ruby|翔|しょう}}；''Shinkou-hishou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The RoosterTwelveGodKing Gale-Phoenix X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The RoosterTwelveGodKing Gale-Phoenix]]. The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1-2-3] {{tk|Grand Twinkle Soar}} (When Attacks)'''
By paying two costs, refresh this Spirit. When you've done so, during this battle, all your Spirits gain +5000 BP, and the opponent can't move any cores, besides [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]], from their Field/Grandwalker Nexuses/Trash. As the name implies, it is a new variant of {{tk|Soar}}, the original keyword held by [[The RoosterTwelveGodKing Gale-Phoenix]]. While the name also reads like a combination of {{tk|Grand Soar}} and {{tk|Twinkle Soar}}, effect-wise, it is closer to {{tk|Twinkle Soar}}, the keyword owned by [[The SwiftnessGodKing Gale-Phoenix-Voltech]], the advent remake of [[The RoosterTwelveGodKing Gale-Phoenix]]. On top of the signature "pay cost to refresh" effect, {{tk|Grand Twinkle Soar}} comes with (1) a Field BP increase effect, and (2) a core locking effect. For (1), considering how the amount is 5000, it can be perceived as being a reference and upgrade to the original Gale-Phoenix's second effect, which adds only to Gale-Phoenix itself. Actual gaming-wise, the BP increase maximize the strong points of God-Kings: a very high BP that surpasses the normal standard of a card with the same cost. With Gale-Phoenix X's LV3 BP being 18000, the actual BP after paying two costs would become 22000, surpassing the range of most BP destroy effects and BP decrease effects. As it adds the BP of other Spirits as well, it also protects those Spirits from BP destroys. As Gale-Phoenix X is designed to work with [[The AdventureFlagbearer Liber]], which runs Imagine Braves, the actual BP when Gale-Phoenix X attacks would be even higher than 22000, making it extremely hard to remove by BP, or lose BP battles. The addition of (2), however, is what actually makes the keyword so much more deadly than any previous versions/remakes of {{tk|Soar}}. By locking all cores from Field/Grandwalker/Trash, it prevents the opponent from reacting with most cards or effects, which might remove Gale-Phoenix or protect their lives from the consecutive attacks of Gale-Phoenix X that are paired with pseudo unbloackable effect (Gale-Phoenix X's Lv2-3 effect). As cores on Grandwalkers can't be moved, on top of {{tk|Grand Skill}} or {{tk|Contract Skill}} from Grandwalkers, {{tk|Mani}}, the main gimmick in the era prior to Contract Saga: Proof, also couldn't be used as well, as cost can't be paid from the Grandwalkers. For the Trash locking part, it means that the opponent also cannot use the effect of [[Blizzard Wall LT]], the most common defense card at the time when Gale-Phoenix X was released. This greatly limits the options the opponent has when dealing with Gale-Phoenix X, making it a very solid finisher. As the effect lasts throughout the battle, even if another card is advented on top of Gale-Phoenix X, the effect lasts. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Holy Life.fullContent:
[[File:Isfiel.jpg|thumb]] '''Holy Life''' (聖命, ''Seimei'') is a special ability of [[Yellow]], the second batch after [[Brilliance]]. Cards with this effect in general have the following text: * {{tk|Holy Life}} '''(When Attacks)'''
When this Spirit's attack reduces the opposing Life, put one core from the Void to your Life. Together with [[Brilliance]] that showcases the magic-related aspect of Yellow, Holy Life demonstrates a different strength of Yellow: longevity and stalling ability via life recovery. Examples of cards with this effect are [[The ArcAngelia Isfiel]] and [[The Angelia of Olimpics Phaleg]].　In terms of the ability itself, since it increases your Life when opposing Life is reduced, it added on to the differences between two players' lives every time the ability activates (opponent minus one while you plus one = a difference of two). This also means the owner of the Spirits with Holy Life could attack more aggressively as the attack brings them extra life that can guard opposing attacks next turn in place of blockers. While it is first added to the life, it is also essentially a core-boosting ability for [[Yellow]], which isn't good at adding cores normally. The obvious weakness, however, is that the ability only activates when the attack hits opposing Life. This means if the attack is blocked, or opponent used cards that limit life reduction for the turn, the ability would be rendered useless. Hence, cards that support Holy Life come with unblockable or doubling the amount recovered each time, such that the hit rate and effectiveness of effect could increase. The keyword has inspired many keywords that derived from it, including [[Divine Holy Life]], [[Chaotic Holy Life]], and [[Ultra Holy Life]]. While the keyword itself is an ancient one, it is a practical ability that it has been picked up from time to time in the past. And in [[BS68]], when [[The ToolcraftContractor Kinich-Ahau]] is introduced with the new keyword, [[Ultra Holy Life]], the original keyword, Holy Life, also got picked up and quite a lot of new Spirits in the deck possess the keyword. This time, in addition to unblocakble, they may also come with unaffected and draw abilities. == Also See == * [[:Category:Holy Life|List of cards with Holy Life]] * [[Divine Holy Life]] * [[Chaotic Holy Life]] * [[Ultra Holy Life]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

When the opponent uses the effect of a Color A (/Color B) Magic, by exhausting this Spirit, negate that effect. After errata, the effect is later written as: * {{iw|Color A(/Color B)}} '''(Opposings Turn)'''
When the
Ice Wall.fullContent:
[[File:Woden.jpg|thumb]] '''Ice Wall''' (氷壁; ''hyouheki'') is a special keyword of [[White]], the second generation shared keyword introduced in Gekiha Dan era. First rendition of Ice Wall was written in the following form: * {{iw|Color A(/Color B)}} '''(Opposings Turn)'''
When the opponent uses the effect of a Color A (/Color B) Magic, by exhausting this Spirit, negate that effect. After errata, the effect is later written as: * {{iw|Color A(/Color B)}} '''(Opposings Turn)'''
When the opponent uses a Color A (/Color B) Magic card, before that effect resolves, by exhausting this Spirit, immediately negate that effect. Straightforward as what it lets on, the keyword allows players to negate effects of Magic cards used by the opponent on their turn. While this doesn't stop the opponent from using defense magics on your attacking turn, it can be used to stop the opponent using Magic to gain advantage and set up their board, which notably includes the use of draw magic cards. As a White ability, it also adds on the defense power as the opponent can't use designated Magic cards to aid their advance. More importantly, when the Magic is negated, the cost paid won't return. On the other hand, the downside is also fairly obvious. Since it requires the player to exhaust the Spirit to negate the effect, the Spirit must be kept refreshed until the opposing turn, meaning that it can't participate in attacking unless it comes with refreshing ability. By exhausting the Spirit to negate Magic, it also means that the Spirit can't participate in blocking battle that turn unless it comes with exhaust block abilities. As mentioned, despite the fact that {{tk|Ice Wall}} as an effect isn't tied to a particular timing, the only timing of {{tk|Ice Wall}} so far has been (Opposing Turn). Hence, it can't be used to break through opponent's defence. It is also worthwhile to note that, similar to {{tk|Armor}}, {{tk|Ice Wall}} is tied to specific colors. If the color doesn't match in the match-up, the ability might just become useless. Therefore, ultimately, the actual usefulness and effectiveness of the keyword depends greatly on whether "negating set-up magics of particular colors" is important in a certain meta/point of time in game. There are also a few more points to note: # As the target of {{tk|Ice Wall}} is the "use (使用)" of Magic, it can't be used to negate the "activation (発揮)" of Magic cards, which includes Burst effect of Magic cards and the Flash/Main effect activated via the Burst effect.

# As the Magic was still "used", the opponent can return the negated card to Hand via {{tk|Brilliance}}. The keyword was later remade into {{tk|Grand Ice Wall}} in Ultra Advent Era. == Also See == * [[:Category:Ice Wall|List of cards with Ice Wall]] == Magic cards that have the same effect as/ related to Ice Wall == * [[Iceberg]] * [[Moonbow Cloak]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Divine Holy Life.fullContent:
[[File:BS26-X02.jpg|thumb|320x320px]] '''Divine Holy Life''' ({{ruby|神|しん}}{{ruby|聖|せい}}{{ruby|命|めい}}, ''Shinseimei'') is an effect introduced in [[BS26]]. It is a modified version of [[Holy Life]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{tk|Divine Holy Life}} '''(When Attacks)'''
Put a core from the Void to your Life. Then, if your Life is three or less, once per turn, refresh this Spirit. Unlike [[Holy Life]] that takes place when the Spirit/Ultimate reduces the opposing Life, Divine Holy Life occurs directly upon attack, making the life recovery much more stable than its original. The additional refresh also comes in handy for both pressuring the opponent via consecutive attacks, and recovering more lives when life amount is low. A thing to note, however, is that if your Life is at three before the effect, and your Life becomes four after the first part, you can't refresh with the second part of the same effect. In general, the effect solves the major limitation and downside of [[Holy Life]]. == See Also == * [[:Category:Divine Holy Life|List of cards with Divine Holy Life]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Dispersion.fullContent:
[[File:The ArcAngelia Saint d'Arc.png|thumb]]
'''Dispersion''' (分散, ''Bunsan'') is a keyword exclusive to Yellow Spirits introduced in [[BS29]]. Spirits with this effect have the following text: 
*'''Dispersion: X''' (When Battles) When you use a Magic card that targets one opposing Spirit/Ultimate, change the number of targets to X.

''(X = the number indicated by the effect.)''

This effect allows for Magic cards to have a much heavier impact on the opposing Spirits and Ultimates. Without having to pay the cost or using the Magic multiple times, you can easily cut down the opposing forces. Important things to note include the fact that the effect requires the Magic to be a solo-target effect, and it only applies to "use" of Magic cards, but not "activation". For effect with multiple parts that target more than one Spirit in total, if the parts are connected by "also (さらに)", [[Dispersion]] can't apply, as the effect targets more than one Spirit/Ultimate at the same time; If the parts are connected by "then (その後)", or "after this effect resolves (この効果を発揮後)", and each part only targets one Spirit/Ultimate, [[Dispersion]] can apply, as the timing of the different parts of the effect are different.

|What does {{tk|Dispersion}} do? 
|When you use a Magic card that targets a single opposing Spirit/Ultimate, it allows you to increase the number of targets of that effect to the number stated in the effect. (e.g. Increase to 3 for {{Disp|3}})
|-
|2
|When you activate the Burst of a Magic card that targets a single opposing Spirit/Ultimate, can you activate {{tk|Dispersion}}? 
|No, you can't. The activation of Burst, or the activation of the Main/Flash effect of a Burst aren't treated as "using a Magic card". 
|-
|3
|When you change the target of a Magic card that targets a single opposing Spirit/Ultimate to two via {{Disp|2}}, can you target one Spirit and one Ultimate respectively?  
|Yes, you can. 
|-
|4
|When activating the {{tk|Rush}} effect of a Magic card, can you activate {{tk|Dispersion}}?  
|No, you can't. 
|-
|5
|When using Magics with effects that don't specify "one Spirit" like [[Deadly Balance]] or [[Core Drain]], can you activate {{tk|Dispersion}}?  
|No, you can't. 
|-
|6 
|When using [[Danse Macabre]] with {{Disp|2}}, if you discard one card from Hand, can you send one core each from two opposing Spirits to the Trash?  
|No, you can't. With {{Disp|2}}, you can choose two targets, but the amount of cores to be removed still depends on the number of cards you discarded, which is one in this case. 
|-
|7 
|When using [[Crystal Crack]] with {{Disp|2}}, how do you resolve the effect?   
|Send cores from two opposing Spirits to their Trash so that each of them has one core left on it.  
|-
|8 
|When using [[Diva Medley]] with {{Disp|2}}, you can choose to "return two opposing Spirits to the deckbottom", or "by sending a core from your Trash to the Void, return two opposing LV3 Ulimates to the deckbottom"?    
|Yes. However, when choosing the second option, since it is a "by A do B" effect, if you can't return two opposing LV3 Ulimates, you can't activate the effect.   
|-
|9 
|For effects like [[Fireball Attack]]'s, if the effect target becomes multi-target, can {{tk|Dispersion}} be activated?     
|No, you can't. 
|-
|10 
|When using [[Binding Creeper]] while you control any Ultimate, or paying Soul Core to use [[Wind-Thunder Break]], so that apart from the original target of the Magic, an extra Spirit is targeted by the effect, can you activate {{tk|Dispersion}}? 
|No, you can't. With an additional target, the effect becomes an effect that target two or more Spirits/Ultiamtes at once. 
|-
|11 
|When using [[Crescent Howling]] or [[Dream Ribbon]] (Revival), where different Spirits/Ultimates are targeted at different instances as connected by the effect clause "then" or "after this effect resolves", can {{tk|Dispersion}} be applied to the corresponding instances? 
|Yes, you can. If you use [[Crescent Howling]] with {{Disp|2}}, you can return two opposing Spirits to the Hand with the first part, and another two opposing Spirits to the Hand for the part after "then".  
|-
|12
|When using effects like [[Lightning Poison]]'s Flash effect, where one Spirit is targeted for the destroy and the other is targeted for moving the cards, such that the effects are independent but resolved at the same time, can {{tk|Dispersion}} be applied? 
|No, it can't, as two or more opposing Spirits are targeted at the same time.    
|-
|}
