Brilliance.fullContent:
[[File:BS03-X11.jpg|thumb]] '''Brilliance''' ({{ruby|光|こう}}{{ruby|芒|ぼう}}, ''Kōbō'') is a keyword debuted in [[BS03]], exclusive possessed by Yellow cards. Cards with Brilliance have the following effect: * {{tk|Brilliance}} '''(When Attacks)'''
At the end of the battle, return every Magic card you used during this battle to your Hand. Starting from BS34, the wording has changed to the following: * {{tk|Brilliance}} '''(When Attacks)'''
At the end of the battle, every Magic card you used during this battle returns '''from your Trash''' to your Hand. Brilliance is a keyword which allows a player to recycle used Magic cards from the trash, so to preserve resources. Most Spirits and Ultimates possessing Brilliance have relatively low BPs. As such, if there are no external supports, it is a frequent occurrence where a Spirit or Ultimate cannot remain on the field at the end of battle to activate Brilliance. However, the Brilliance keyword allows the players to make use of Magic cards outside of the Yellow color, especially with effects which allow the free use of Magic cards, such as with [[The ArcAngelia Mikafar]]. As one of the first Yellow keywords, Brilliance also has a few derivative keywords spawned from it, including [[Evil Light]] and [[Heavenly Light]]. == Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |1 |What is Brilliance? |It is an effect which, at the end of an attack of a Spirit possessing Brilliance, returns all Magic cards used during that battle to hand. |- |2 |Can I not return the used Magic cards? |No, you must return as many Magic cards as possible to hand. |- |3 |Can I also return any Magic card that is used during the Attack Step? |No, you can only return Magic cards that are used during "the battle where a Spirit with Brilliance is attacking". |- |4 |What happens if the Spirit with Brilliance is destroyed during battle? |If at the end of the battle, the Spirit with Brilliance which attacked is not on the field anymore, Brilliance does not activate. |- |5 |If a Spirit which possesses Brilliance only at LV2 and LV3 attacks at LV2, and then during the battle, cores on the Spirit are used to pay for the use of Magic, and it becomes LV1, is the used Magic card returned to hand? |No, it is not. If the attacking Spirit does not possess Brilliance by the end of the battle, the used Magic card is not returned to hand. |- |6 |If a Spirit which possesses Brilliance only at LV2 and LV3 attacks at LV1, and during the battle, it gets levelled up, such as via the effect of [[Build Up]], are Magic cards used during that battle be returned to hand? |Yes, they are. Even if the Spirit does not possess Brilliance at attack declaration, as long as it does possess the keyword by the end of battle, all Magic cards used during that battle are returned to hand, including the Magic card that is used to level up the Spirit. |- |7 |If a Spirit with Brilliance is switched into battle via the effect of [[Teleport Change]], can Magic cards used during that battle be returned to hand via Brilliance? |Yes, they can be, including the copy of [[Teleport Change]] that is used to switch the Spirit with Brilliance into battle. |- |8 |During the attack of a Spirit with Brilliance, can used Magic cards which place themselves in other areas besides the trash, such as [[Healing Melody]], be returned to hand via Brilliance at the end of the battle? |No, they cannot be. After use, Magic cards which are not placed into the trash are not valid targets of Brilliance. |} ==See Also:== * [[:Category:Brilliance|Cards with Brilliance]] * [[:Category: Brilliance support|Cards which support Brilliance]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Kagemusha.fullContent:
[[File:BS32-033.png|thumb]] '''Kagamusha''' (影武者, ''Kagemusha'') is a keyword debuted in [[BS32]], possessed only by White Spirits. Spirits with this keyword have the following text:  * '''Kagemusha''' - When your Spirit with Soul Core on it becomes the target of an opponent's effect, you can summon this Spirit card in your hand. Then, change the target of that effect to this Spirit only. There are also two other keywords derived from Kagemusha, which are [[True-Kagemusha]] and [[Tenma-Kagemusha]]. ==List of cards with Kagemusha== * [[:Category:Kagemusha|List of cards with Kagemusha]] == Assisting Cards == [[The CleverMachineCommander Tycoon]] (BS32-X04) == Trivia == * The word "kagemusha" is the pronunciation of the Japanese word "影武者", which is a pronoun for people who substitute famous generals or emperors in Japan's Warring State era. Those people would have similar faces as the generals and emperors, and they wore the same clothes. So they could distract the enemies, while the victims escaped. This is exactly what the effect here is reflecting. == Official Q&As == Q1: What is "Kagemusha"?
A1: When your Spirit with Soul Core is targeted by an opposing effect, before that effect activates, you summon the Spirit card with "Kagemusha" by paying the cost, and change the target of the opposing effect to the summoned Spirit only. Q2: Can the target of the effect "destroy all opposing BP 3000 or less Spirits" be changed to a BP 4000 Spirit with "Kagemusha" only?
A2: Yes, it can be. You can also change the target of effects that do not normally target Spirits to Spirits with "Kagemusha". Q3: When the target of the effect "destroy all opposing BP 3000 or less Spirits" is changed to a BP 4000 Spirit with "Kagemusha", is that Spirit with "Kagemusha" not destroyed?
A3: That is correct. Q4: Can "Kagemusha" change the target of the Lv2/3 effect of "[[The GiantArmCleverMachineMusha Rakan]]"?
A4: No it cannot. The Lv2/3 effect of "[[The GiantArmCleverMachineMusha Rakan]]" is a permanent effect between steps, so the target(s) cannot be changed. Q5: When your Spirit with Soul Core is targeted by an opposing effect, can you summon multiple copies of Spirit cards with "Kagemusha"?
A5: Yes, you can. However, in this case, after you declare the multiple copies of Spirit cards with "Kagemusha", then the turn player chooses the effect order, if the Spirit summoned by "Kagemusha" does not have Soul Core put on it, the condition for the next "Kagemusha" effect is not fulfilled, and so their effects cannot activate, and the cards are returned to the Hand. Q6: After you summon a Spirit through "Kagemusha", and put the Soul Core onto it, since that Spirit will become a new target of the effect, can you summon another Spirit card with "Kagemusha" from the Hand?
A6: No, you cannot. Q7: When you activate "Kagemusha", the opposing effect is also targeting cards in the hand and trash, can the Spirit with "Kagemusha" change those targets?
A7: No, it cannot. the targets that can be changed are the Spirits, Ultimates, Braves, and Nexuses on the field. The targets towards hand, deck, trash, or the Burst zone cannot be changed. Q8: The opposing "[[Homuracheetah]]" with Soul Core attacks, and targets both your Spirit with Soul Core and your Nexus with the same effect at the same time. In this case, when "Kagemusha" activates, is the Nexus destroyed?
A8: No, it is not. When "Kagemusha" activates, targets at the same time towards Ultimates and Nexuses by the same effect are also changed to only the Spirit with "Kagemusha". Q9: When your Spirit with Soul Core is targeted by an opposing effect, you activate "Kagemusha". If the opposing effect has other timings such as "[[Rush]]", "then", or "after this effect resolves", can "Kagemusha" also change the targets for those timings?
A9: No, it cannot. Within one effect, different timings are treated as different effects. However, you can trigger a second "Kagemusha" to counter those effects. Q10: When your Spirit with Soul Core is targeted by an opposing "[[Showdown]]" effect, can you activate "Kagemusha", and compare BP with the Spirit summoned by "Kagemusha"?
A10: Yes, you can. However, in the case of "[[The CleverMachineTactician Shimokaze]]", as it is unaffected by opposing Spirit effects, after the target changes, it is unaffected by the "Showdown" effect, and BP will not be compared. Q11: When your Spirit with Soul Core is affected by opposing in-activation effects, such as "during this turn, give all opposing Spirits/Ultimates -1000 BP", can you activate "Kagemusha"?
A11: No, "Kagemusha" cannot activate against effects that are already in activation. Q12: With effects that last throughout the steps and turns, such as "give all opposing Spirits/Ultimates get -1000 BP" from "[[Small Phynx]]", which does not specify activation timings such as "during this battle" or "during this turn", when they affect your Spirit with Soul Core, can you activate "Kagemusha"?
A12: No, you cannot. ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Mealtiply.fullContent:
[[File:Strawberry.png|thumb]]
'''Mealtiply '''(増食, ''Soushoku''), also known as ''Fruitiply'' in English, is a special ability of Yellow spirits. It debuted in [[BS35]]. Spirits with this effect have the following text: 
*"'''Mealtiply: Cost X or less''' - (When Summoned) You can reveal two cards from your decktop. Among them, you can summon one Cost X or less "[[Drifting Spirit]]" family Spirit card, without paying the cost. Discard any unsummoned or remaining cards."


Examples of cards with this ability include [[The Fruitsel Straw-Berry]] and [[Kuurin]]. The ability allows the player to summon multiple spirits during Main Step through a chain reaction of multiple Mealtiply from Spirits summoned. It became the core tactic of the God-King era [[Drifting Spirit]] deck, and the core theme of the Fruitsels (果物人).

The major weakness of the effect is that it relies on reveals from deck and the cost limit of the cards to be summoned. Stronger Mealtiply effects have a higher cost limit but also a higher raw cost in geneal, making the balance and ratio of different costs of cards in deck become an important thing that the players need to take note of. Another weakness is that while the player can chain summons via Mealtiply, the number of cores one can spend on maintaining the level of spirits don't increase in the process, so a new summon doesn't necessarily increase the total number of spirits on the Field.  

The introduction of [[The FruitQueen Mangosteena]] later, however, greatly changed the structure of the deck by providing core boost every summon. This enables the chain summon of Mealtiply to build up a board with unimaginable numbers and provide a great number of cores in the process for later use. The number of cores it generates and the speed of digging up one's deck soon proves to be problematic when it both makes the deck extremely fast and unwanted loops possible. Mangosteena was hence limited to change the situation.

Ultra Heavy Armor.fullContent:
[[File:Mammo.png|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Ultra Heavy Armor''' (超重装甲, ''Chō Jūsōkō'') is an effect possessed by White Spirits, debuting in [[BS36]]. 
It is an modified version of the white effect [[Ultra Armor]] and [[Heavy Armor]], and gives coverage against every effect of the designated color. 

Spirits with this effect have the following text on their cards:
* '''Ultra Heavy Armor - Color(/Color):''' This Spirit is unnaffected by opposing (Color) effects.

Being a powerful effect, its occurrence is rather rare when compared to [[Heavy Armor]] and [[Ultra Armor]]. It is generally only on high rarity cards, and limited to one to two colors. And partly because of the low utility rate, and partly because of how the effect is effectively full immunity against the designated colors, when piercing effects becomes rampant in Ultra Advent era to deal with the increasingly common complete immunity/card type immunity owned by cards in decks like [[Grandwalker Thoth]], the text are worded as "this effect can only be prevented by {{tk|Heavy Armor}}/{{tk|Ultra Armor}}, making {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, the supposedly stronger variant of armor, the "weaker" effect ironically against these piercing effects. 

After the increase of utility rate of the keyword in decks like [[Grandwalker Tezcatlipoca]]'s [[Armored Beast]], and probably the realization that {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}} should be the stronger variant of armor when compared to {{tk|Heavy Armor}} and {{tk|Ultra Armor}}, piercing effects from Contract Era onwards have changed to "this effect can only be prevented by {{tk|Heavy Armor}}/{{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}."

Twinkle Equip.fullContent:
[[File:SD39-X01.jpg|thumb|320x320px]] '''Twinkle Equip''' (煌転装, ''Kō tensō'') is a keyword which debuted in [[SD39]]. The only Spirit to possess it is [[The NobleDragoon Nu-Siegfried]]. The effect in itself is very unique in the game where direct search (not counting GX cards) doesn't really exist. The keyword's text reads: * {{tk|Twinkle Equip}} '''(When Advents)'''
Target a family, and you can discard cards from your decktop until a Brave card with the targeted family is discarded. When you've done so, summon that card without paying the cost. Rulings: # You must continue to discard cards from the top of your deck and stop once you discard a Brave card with the targeted family. # First, you must discard until you've discarded a Brave card with the targeted family. Second, you will summon the Brave card from your trash. # You may summon any spirit/brave cards from your trash that can be summoned if it was discarded from the deck (i.e. [[The NobleOrder Soldier-Azure]], [[The GloryWarrior O-Superia]], [[Glorious-Flugel]], etc). While it comes with the risk of emptying own deck, the effect proves to be a very effective one to accelerate the game plan of the user of Nu-Sieg as the effect is essentially both a search and free summon effect. By calling Braves with symbols, Nu-Sieg would instantly become a double symbol attacker than is unaffected by opposing effects and can refresh once per turn. This is particularly lethal during early turns when the opponent doesn't have much cores reserved for defense. Due to the advent nature of Nu-Sieg, it can come down at very early stage as long as advent base is ready (via special summons or Bursts etc.) and pose lethal threats to the opponent. Since it is a deck-discarding effect, its arch enemy would be cards that prevent deck destruction like [[God Break]]. The user must also know clearly how many Braves are left when they advent Nu-Sieg and activate the effect, as a wrong declaration would result in milling the entire deck and losing the game next turn. There are also rare cases that the Brave the player calls is exactly the bottom card of the deck, which would again be forcing the user into a life-and-death situation during that turn if there are no means prepared to return cards back to own deck. However, all things considered, the tempo advantage brought by the effect is still too huge that the weakness can be covered. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Load.fullContent:
[[File:BS63-CX01.png|thumb]]
'''Load''' (装弾) is a keyword introduced in [[BS63]], possessed only by [[Silver Zero]] family cards to work with [[The PartnerBurai Vrick]]'s Steel Contract deck. 

The simplest form of the effect is written as follows:

* Load: X - (''Timing'') You can put X cards from your decktop facedown under your "The PartnerBurai Vrick", including those that are in Soul State/pre-advent condition.

The literal meaning of the name, {{ruby|装|そう}}{{ruby|弾|だん}}, is "loading bullets", and refers to a part of Vrick's battle style and design in the lore of being a gunslinger. Game-wise, it allows you to put cards from decktop facedown under Vrick for various uses, just like how one loads a gun with bullets. The effect works in pair with {{tk|Fast Draw}}, which uses the "bullets" you stack under your Vrick via {{tk|Load}}. Apart from the basic function of putting facedown cards under Vrick, the effect usually comes with other benefits like adding counters. It also isn't limited to a particular timing, and can be a part of Burst effects.  

The effect as a whole works like a reversed [[Poison Blade]] that the owner of Vrick put facedown cards under the different Vrick they control, instead of the opposing Spirits. When Vrick leaves the Field, the "bullets" (facedown cards) under it would also be discarded. However, unlike other similar effects, since Vrick is by nature a Contract Spirit, the owner can choose to let him enter Soul State when being removed, and in such case, the bullets would stay underneath Vrick as he has never left the Field.

Being a card-digging deck, the "[[Zero Contract]]" family has a l
Excite.fullContent:
[[File:BS64-033.png|thumb]]
'''Excite''' (励起; ''reiki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS64]], possessed only by White "[[Silver Zero]]" family cards which work with the "[[Zero Contract]]" family. The effect is worded as follows:

* {{Excite|X}} (Can't Stack: {{Excite|X}} ) When the opposing Life is reduced by your "Zero Contract" family Spirit, if you have X counters or more, you can return this card from your Trash to the Hand.

Being a card-digging deck, the "[[Zero Contract]]" family has a lot of effects which reveal cards from the top of the deck and discard them, which may cause a lot of useful cards to be lost in the process. Despite being a White deck, the play style of the deck is also taking into some traits of the Blue color, as seen by the {{tk|Brave Engage}} effect of [[The AstralZeroSword Foranswer]] (the card itself is half-Blue as well), further reinforcing the idea of filtering which is normally unique to the Blue color. As such, the {{tk|Excite}} keyword proves to be a useful mechanic to replenish the hand with the discarded cards.

Unlike most of the other keywords, the interchangeable part of {{tk|Excite}} (represented by "X" in the example above) isn't separated from the keyword name itself with a colon, meaning that the "X" is integrated into the keyword's name. As such, {{tk|Excite}} with different numbers are treated as different effects. For example, {{Excite|3}} is treated as a different effect to {{Excite|5}}.

Excite also has a derivative keyword called [[Ultra Excite]].

In addition, in a case where X is a different number between two different {{tk|Excite}} effects, they are treated as different effects.

The effect is written as follows: * {{tk|During OC}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|Steel Load}} (When Advents)'''
You can put cards from your decktop facedown under one of your "The PartnerBurai Vrick", including those that are in Soul State/pre-advent condition, until there are five cards under it. As the name implies, this is an alternate version of {{tk|Load}}, allowing players to load up to five bullets immediately under one of their [[The PartnerBurai Vrick|Vrick]], serving as a super boost to enable more flexible plays using {{tk|Fast Draw}}, the key gimmick of Vrick's [[Steel Contract]] deck. Unlike other {{tk|Load}} effects that are limited to one or two cards at a time, the boost of five cards with the timing of '''(When Advents)''' on a card that can {{tk|Contract Advent}} during (Your Turn) allows players of the deck to charge enough bullets for finisher-type effects like Mavrick-Menace's {{Fast Draw|X}} and [[The GunEmperorMachineDeity Guns-Mavrick]]'s {{Fast Draw|2}} before entering Attack Step. When using such powerful effect, it is however necessary to note that {{tk|Steel Load}} loads all the bullets under one [[The PartnerBurai Vrick|Vrick]], and loads '''up to five''', instead of '''load five'''. Hence, the player must decide which Vrick they are loading the cards to before they check the contents of the facedown cards, and consider which Vrick they should load in order to get the greatest number of bullets. While being a variant of {{tk|Load}}, {{tk|Steel Load}} is '''NOT''' treated as {{tk|Load}}, and can't be supported by effects that support {{tk|Load}}. == See Also: == * [[Load]] * [[Steel Contract]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Ultra Excite.fullContent:
[[file:BS67-CP04.png|thumb]]
'''Ultra Excite''' (超励起 ; ''chou-reiki'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS67]], possessed exclusively by [[The SilverZeroDragonDeity Wiz-the-Answer]]. The effect reads as follows:
* {{tk|Ultra Excite}} (Once per Turn: Same Name) At the end of the battle of your "[[Zero Contract]]" family Spirit, you can return this card from your Trash to the Hand.

As the name implies, Ultra Excite is an alternative version of [[Excite]], and in general an evolved version of the effect. While [[Excite]] requires the player to reduce the opposing Life on attack and reaching a certain amount of counters to retrieve the card, Ultra Excite doesn't have such restrictions, and can work even if the attack is blocked, or the player doesn't have any counters. In actual battle, when cards like [[Diamond Wall]] that restricts the reduction of life, or effects that swipe the symbol of the attacking "[[Zero Contract]]" family Spirit is applied, normal Excite won't be able to proc. However, with Ultra Excite, it can work as long as the Spirit survives the battle. Since it is a different keyword, a card with Ultra Excite can act as an extra constant discard fodder every turn, as it can be retrieved together along with cards with {{Excite|3}} and {{Excite|5}}. Apart from that, another benefit of the keyword is how it works on the opposing turn as well, which synchronizes nicely with [[Zero Fencer, Wiz]]'s exhaust-block effect and [[The AstralZeroSword Foranswer]]'s refresh effect.   

On the downside, as mentioned above, Ultra Excite requires the Spirit to remain on the Field until the end of battle. Hence, it takes the risks of the opponent having any responses upon losing lives or having their Spirits/Ultimates destroyed via battle.

Heavenly Light.fullContent:
[[file:BS67-XV04.png|thumb]] '''Heavenly Light''' (天光芒 ; ''tenkoubou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS67]], possessed exclusively by [[The ArcAngelia Valiero XV]]. The effect reads as follows: *{{tk|Heavenly Light}} (Either Attack Step)
(Can't Stack) At the end of the battle which you used any Magic card, return a "[[Golden Cloud]]" family Spirit card/Magic card from your Trash to the Hand. Heavenly Light is an upgrade of [[Brilliance]], minus the potential versatility which Brilliance can give, as Heavenly Light limits itself from only retrieving "Golden Cloud" family cards. Heavenly Light also does not require the possessor of the effect to attack, nor does it have to retrieve the Magic cards specifically used in that battle, giving more flexibility in terms of choosing which Spirit to attack for the use of Magic. Being a separate keyword also means that Heavenly Light can be used together with Brilliance and [[Evil Light]], allowing the player to recycle through even more Magic cards. Also unlike Brilliance, which the player's used Magic card is required to be placed into the Trash, Heavenly Light allows the player to also use Magic cards that can stay on the Field, and still recycle other cards from the Trash. It is worth noting that it is possible to create a pseudo-infinite combo in order for the player to recycle all "Golden Cloud" family Spirit cards and Magic cards from the Trash in the same turn. However, a few conditions are required. The player needs to have enough Spirits to attack, either by just having the sheer amount, or using other methods to create infinite attacks. Then, during each attack, the player uses [[Diamond Storm]], and targets an opposing Spirit that doesn't reach 0 BP after the effect, so that Diamond Storm can return itself to hand. In other words, as long the player can create enough attacks, as well the opponent having enough high BP Spirits that don't reach 0 BP easily, one can simply use Diamond Storm and Valiero XV to take back all their "Golden Cloud" family Spirit cards and Magic cards from the Trash. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

[[file:BSC45-XV05.png|250px|thumb]] '''Heaven Holy Life''' (天聖命; ''ten seimei'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC45]], possessed exclusively by [[The ArcAngelia Isfiel XV]]. The effect reads as follows: * {{tk|Heaven Holy Life}} '''(Your Attack Step)'''
(Can't Stack) When your Spirit's attack reduces the opposing Life, you can put a core from the Void to your Life. '''Heaven Holy Life''' serves as an upgraded and modified version of the [[Holy Life]] keyword which [[The ArcAngelia Isfiel]] originally possesses, and this time supporting every Spirit on the Field instead of only applying to the Spirit with the keyword. Unlike [[Holy Life]] which requires the Spirit itself to attack, and is limited to the Spirit that owns the keyword, {{tk|Heaven Holy Life}} can provide support without the need of attacking with the Spirit. This enables much more combo potential. For instance, the {{tk|Contract Field}} of [[The ToolcraftContractor Kinich-Ahau]], a Contractor Nexus that supports "Holy Life"-named keywords in general. While the {{tk|Contract Field}} requires the attacking Spirit to be in the "[[Puppet Beast]]" family, it doesn't require the "Holy Life"-named keyword to be activated to come from the attacking Spirit. This allows players to deal extra damage per attack by activating {{tk|Heaven Holy Life}} every attack. The only major weakness of the keyword, much like the original [[Holy Life]], is that it is limited to normal attacks and not effects. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Heaven Holy Life|List of cards with Heaven Holy Life]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

You can exhaust this [Card Type]. When you've done so, [Extra Effect]. Being a keyword introduced together with [[The SilverWheelContractor Brigit]], a Celtica Grandwalker Nexus that is based on Celtic/Irish/Norse mythology, the
Silver Wheel.fullContent:
[[File:BS70-036.png|thumb|200px]] '''Silver Wheel''' (銀輪; ''ginrin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS70]], possessed exclusively by White Spirits, and primarily those with the [[Frostling]] family. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Flash -''' {{tk|Silver Wheel}}
You can exhaust this [Card Type]. When you've done so, [Extra Effect]. Being a keyword introduced together with [[The SilverWheelContractor Brigit]], a Celtica Grandwalker Nexus that is based on Celtic/Irish/Norse mythology, the effect of exhausting own Spirits for extra benefits has a strong resemblance of White cards like [[The ArmoredSacred Walhalance]], cards that are also based on Norse mythology. As the name implies, the keyword involves turning own Spirits sideway for resources and extra effects, much like the spinning of wheel in terms of both the action and the result of generating momentum. Unlike some other effects that exhaust own Spirits, however, the effect is not a "by" effect. Hence, players can exhaust the cards with {{tk|Silver Wheel}} to "activate" the effect even if they can't obtain the extra benefit due to other effects (e.g. can't add cores from the Void). This facilitates cards that are based on the the activation of the keyword, like the {{tk|Contract Field}} of [[The SilverWheelContractor Brigit]], to run without worrying that it is stopped by opposing locking effects. Since the effect is a Flash Timing effect without timing restrictions, it allows the player to activate the effect during Main Step and Attack Step on both turn flexibly according to the actual situation. In addition, while self-exhausting is the controlling factor, if you can manage to refresh the card, you can activate {{tk|Silver Wheel}} of the same card more than once per turn. On the downside, since it involves exhausting own Spirits/Nexuses to activate the effect, a natural demerit would be how the exhausted targets can't be used to attack/block without other supporting effects. It is also naturally weak against opposing effects that heavily exhaust your cards. While it is flexible to use in Main Step, a Flash Timing tied effect means it is hard to use outside Main Step as it is vulnerable to opposing removals either on their flash timing as the defense side, or their attack effects on their turn. All in all, despite being a "new" effect, it has elements dated back to ancient [[White]], and is rather technical due to the nature of being a Flash effect and the need to disable own attackers/blockers. == Also See == * [[:Category:Silver Wheel|List of cards with Silver Wheel]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Contract Reload.fullContent:
[[File:PB39-RVX05.png|right|thumb]] '''Contract Reload''' ({{ruby|契|けい}}{{ruby|約|やく}}{{Ruby|装填|リロード}}, ''Keiyaku-Rirōdo'') is a keyword introduced in [[PB39]], currently possessed exclusively by the revival version of [[The SongBirdGun Pentan Blaster]]. The keyword's text reads as: * '''[LV1]''' {{C Rel|"The Partner Pentan"}}
You can {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto this Spirit-condition Brave. When {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto this Brave, you can Brave this pre-Advent card to that Spirit. When you've done so, you can add one of your "The Partner Pentan" , including those that are in Soul State, to underneath this Spirit as a pre-advent card. As the name implies, it is a modified version of {{tk|Reload}}, adapted to fit the gimmick of Contract Card and {{tk|Contract Advent}}. While it shares the same effect as {{tk|Reload}} for enabling target cards to be advented onto a Brave, and braving to the advented card instead of serving as a pre-advent card, it added the part which allow players to add their corresponding Contract Card to beneath the advented Spirit, regardless of whether this Brave will be used as a Brave or pre-advent card. This solved the dilemma of not being able to revive the Contract Card and use its {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}} effects when you {{tk|Contract Advent}} the designated cards onto the Brave with {{tk|Contract Reload}}, and also provided an upgrade version for directly {{tk|Contract Advent}} on the Contract Card in Soul State, as it gives the advented Spirit a Brave in one action. It perfectly synergizes with the design of {{tk|Contract Advent}} while provides the flexibility of {{tk|Reload}}. Interestingly, such an ability appeared in a Premium Bandai item instead of BSC boosters or main set boosters. An important thing to note is, being the same as {{tk|Reload}} on this regard, after the player advents on a Brave card with {{tk|Contract Reload}}, they must first declare whether they will brave it with the advented Spirit or keep it as a pre-Advent card. If it is decided to be braved, it must be performed before other effects that come at that point resolve. Once settled, both players will proceed to resolve (When Advents) and any other effects that trigger on advent. Contract Reload does '''NOT''' treat itself as {{tk|Reload}}. == See Also: == * [[:Category:Contract Reload|List of cards with Contract Reload]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

[[file:BS73-TX03b.png|thumb|320x320px]] '''Cycle Force Unleash''' ({{ruby|氣|き}}{{ruby|廻|かい}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}} ; ''kikai-kaihou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS73]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The BirdBeastBushinMachine Yamato-Orgunar -Bombardment Form-]], the [[Concluser]] Spirit of [[The CycleForceContractor Yamato Takeru]]. The effect is written as follows: * {{CF Unleash|2}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Reborn/Attacks)'''
You can send two cores from any of your "Yamato Ta
Cycle Force Unleash.fullContent:
[[file:BS73-TX03b.png|thumb|320x320px]] '''Cycle Force Unleash''' ({{ruby|氣|き}}{{ruby|廻|かい}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}} ; ''kikai-kaihou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS73]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The BirdBeastBushinMachine Yamato-Orgunar -Bombardment Form-]], the [[Concluser]] Spirit of [[The CycleForceContractor Yamato Takeru]]. The effect is written as follows: * {{CF Unleash|2}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Reborn/Attacks)'''
You can send two cores from any of your "Yamato Takeru" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit. When you've done so, return every card from the opposing Removed Zone to the Hand. Then, leaving three cards in the opposing Hand, reveal and return all others to the deckbottom. After this effect resolves, if the opposing Hand + Removed Zone have a total of five cards or more, you can send two opposing Lives to the Trash. Just like the original {{tk|Unleash}}, {{tk|Cycle Force Unleash}} is all about activating effects by moving cores from Grandwalker Nexuses. The difference is that since {{tk|Cycle Force Unleash}} requires specifically "Contractor Yamato Takeru"-named Grandwalker Nexuses, there is a need to give it an exclusive name. As Yamato Takeru is a Contract Grandwalker Nexus (which can't be used together with other Contract cards), it is a way to prevent other contract decks from borrowing the powerful effect. While it should be obvious enough, the name of the effect comes from the title given to [[The CycleForceContractor Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru]] (氣廻). The word itself is a pun to "machine (機械)", which is essentially the theme of the [[Machine]] family Spirits and [[Force Fighter]] family Spirits led by Yamato Takeru, particularly the [[Machine]] family ones. At the same time, the effect itself is a "cycling effect" for the opponent, which returns opposing cards in the Hand/Removed Zone back to the opposing deck, adding on an extra favor to the name. Game-wise, Cycle Force Unleash is a powerful effect that conjures up the image of the banned [[The DarkStones MachineBeastDeity Fenrig]]. While it doesn't touch the Field, it removes the most important source of defense and counter force of the opponent: their Hand. Before returning cards from Hand to the deckbottom, it first returns cards from the Removed Zone to the Hand, making sure that the opponent can't escape by putting the important resources in their Removed Zone. It also acts as a counter to Removed Zone centered decks like Athena or Gekiha. As {{tk|Cycle Force Unleash}} is an effect that targets the opposing Hand, it will be render useless if the opposing Hand is unaffected by the activating player's effect, which is common in Blue and White. To cover such weakness, the second part of the effect deals direct life damage when the opposing Hand + Removed Zone is five or more after the effect, which is basically the case where their hand/removed zone is unaffected by Yamato-Orgunar's effect. As such, the deploy of nexuses that give immunity to hand/removed zone to prevent the fist part of effect becomes an option that one must consider carefully when they are facing Yamato-Orgunar, and in essence, Yamato-Takeru's deck. == Related Articles == * [[The CycleForceContractor Yamato Takeru]] * [[:Category:Cycle Force Unleash|List of cards with Cycle Force Unleash]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

When any Spirit/Ultimate exhausts, by sending two cores from any of your "Barone" Gr
Moon Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BSC50-X02.png|200px|thumb]] '''Moon Unleash''' ({{ruby|月|つき}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}}；''Tsukikaihō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC50]], exclusive to [[The MoonlightDragonGod Strikewurm-Leo-Hawk]], the remake of [[The MachineLionDeity Strikewurm-Leo]] that is braved to [[Hawk-Breaker]] in the anime. The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|2|Moon}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (Either Attack Step)'''
When any Spirit/Ultimate exhausts, by sending two cores from any of your "Barone" Grandwalker Nexuses to any Spirit, during this turn, the opponent can't end the Turn/Attack Step via effects. Then, if it's not this Spirit which exhausts, you can refresh this Spirit. Following the recent trend of the new "Unleash"-named keywords, like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Curse Unleash]], this Unleash requires a Grandwalker of specific name to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. In this case, it is any Grandwalker Nexus with "Barone" in name. The name takes the Moon as motif, and makes the effect a contrasting pair with the {{tk|Solar Unleash}} of [[The SunDragonGod ShineTres-Sagitto-Apollodragon]]. It is made consistent with the moon motif in [[The MoonlightContractor Barone]], and the "moon" motif carries by [[The MachineLionDeity Strikewurm-Leo]], as it is the reborn form of [[The MoonlightDragonDeity Lunatech-Strikewurm]] in lore. While the idea of Strikewurm-Leo-Hawk comes from Strikewurm-Leo braved to Hawk-Breaker, the main part of {{tk|Moon Unleash}} is derived from Leo's own effect. In addition to being able to refresh when the others exhaust, it gain the ability of negating the step-ending/turn-ending effects. One thing to note is, while "any other Spirit/Ultimate exhausts" is the condition for the entire effect, the "sending core from Grandwalker Nexuses" part is unrelated to resolving the part after "Then". As such, as long as any other Spirit/Ultimate exhausts, even if you control no "Barone" Grandwalker Nexuses, or there aren't enough cores on them, you can refresh Strikewurm-Leo-Hawk. == Also See == * [[:Category:"Barone"-named|List of "Barone"-named cards]] ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

(Once per Turn: Same Name) Put a core from the Void and any number of cores from your Spirits to this Spirit, and when cor
Silver Awaken.fullContent:
[[File:BS75-AX01.png|thumb]] '''Silver Awaken''' ({{ruby|銀|ぎん}}{{ruby|覚|かく}}{{ruby|醒|せい}}；''gin-kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS75]], currently exclusive to [[The ArgentHolyPlanetDeityDragon Gai-Asura]], the AX remake of [[The PhantomStarDragon Gai-Asura]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3][LV4] Flash {{tk|Silver Awaken}} (Either Attack Step)'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) Put a core from the Void and any number of cores from your Spirits to this Spirit, and when cores are put, you can return an opposing Spirit/Ultimate to the deckbottom. While the effect is owned by a new variant of Gai-Asura, instead of resembling its signature {{tk|Ultra Awaken}}, it is actually closer to the original {{tk|Awaken}} effect. On top of being able to move cores from own Spirits, {{tk|Silver Awaken}} now allows players to add core from the Void as well, making it an actual core gain effect instead of merely a core-rearranging effect. Unlike {{tk|Ultra Awaken}} and its other variants that come with refresh, {{tk|Silver Awaken}} comes with removal as an additional bonus. Without any restriction on the target for removal, it constitutes one of the strongest kind of direct removal in Flash. A key point to note is, you '''don't have to move cores from Spirits''' for the "when you've done so" to proc. As long as you added a core from the Void to Gai-Asura, the "when you've done so" part works. Considering all the extra benefits, it is in general an upgrade version of {{tk|Awaken}}. Yet, most probably beecause of its core-boosting nature, the effect comes with the limitation of being a (Once per Turn: Same Name) effect. This means that players can't activate the effect multiple times across different copies unlike normal {{tk|Awaken}}. However, taking into account the other benefits it provided, the downside is negligible. Another weakness of the effect is how the effect timing is (Either Attack Step) instead of just "'''Flash -'''", which could be used in Main Step. However, as [[The ArgentHolyPlanetDeityDragon Gai-Asura|Gai-Asura]] is unaffected by opposing effects during Either Attack Step, the risk of itself being removed before activating the effect is also negligible. While the effect in itself doesn't contribute to winning directly unlike {{tk|Ultra Awaken}}, it offers resources and removal that bridges the next attack or contributes to defense. It is hence a great supporting effect in both Argent [[The ArgentIronKnight Yggdrasil|Yggdrasil]] deck and Crimson [[The CrimsonThunderEmperorDragon Siegwurm|Siegwurm]] deck. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2]''' {{Armor|Red/White/Yellow|Knight}}
All your "Argent" Spirits are unaffected by opposing Red/White/Yellow effects, and can block while exhausted. As the name implies, it is a new variant of "Armor" type ef
Knight Armor.fullContent:
[[file:BS75-CX02.png|thumb]] '''Knight Armor''' (騎装甲; ''ki-soukou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS75]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The ArgentIronKnight Yggdrasil]], the Contract Spirit remake of [[The IronKnight Yggdrasill]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2]''' {{Armor|Red/White/Yellow|Knight}}
All your "Argent" Spirits are unaffected by opposing Red/White/Yellow effects, and can block while exhausted. As the name implies, it is a new variant of "Armor" type effect. Although the defining part of the name, 騎, means "ride" on its own, it is considered to be referring to "Knight" in this context of Yggdrasil, especially when considering how the family of Contract Yggdrasil is [[Knight Contract]]. Effect-wise, it is essentially a modified {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, which offers complete immunity against effects of certain colors, regardless of card types. On top of that, however, what makes {{tk|Knight Armor}} different from most of the existing armor variants, is that it is granting such immunity to ''ALL'' "Argent"-named Spirits, instead of just the holder of {{tk|Knight Armor}}, Yggdrasil himself. While there has been countless case of granting "XX Armor" to other Spirits via another effect, it is very rare for the "XX Armor" itself to be covering all target Spirits on its own. Thematic-wise, it probably is a way to reference original Yggdrasil's effect of granting Armor to every White Spirit. Game-wise, it is made that way most probably because it is printed as an unique effect of a Contract Spirit, which is made to be the center of the deck, and "Argent" deck's style is all about linkage and connections, instead of solo attack. Apart from the immunity, it also grants "exhaust block" to the "Argent" Spirits. This further increases the resilience of the deck, and combines very well with Contract Yggdrasil's second effect of exhausting own Spirits. This makes the deck a natural enemy to Green decks, which mains exhaust, on top of having armor against Red, Yellow, and White. All in all, providing both immunity that increases the survival rate of all "Argent" Spirits against removal and exhaust-block effect that cancels out the demerit of exhausting own Spirits, {{tk|Knight Armor}} serves as the core effect that supports the deck led by [[The ArgentIronKnight Yggdrasil]]. Like some of the other armor effects, it is to note that while some parts read similar, {{tk|Knight Armor}} is NOT counted as {{tk|Armor}} or {{tk|Ultra Heavy Armor}}, etc. == Related Articles == * [[The ArgentIronKnight Yggdrasil]] * [[:Category:"Argent"-named|List of "Argent (白銀)"-named cards]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The wording is as follows: * '''[LV2-3]''' {{tk|True Fortress}}
This refreshed Spirit is unaffected by opposing effects. As the name implies, it is a modified version of {{tk|Fortress}} owned by
True Fortress.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X08.png|200px|thumb]] '''True Fortress''' ({{ruby|真|しん}}・{{ruby|要|よう}}{{ruby|塞|さい}}；''baku-toshin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The OxTwelveGodKing Avalanche-Bison]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV2-3]''' {{tk|True Fortress}}
This refreshed Spirit is unaffected by opposing effects. As the name implies, it is a modified version of {{tk|Fortress}} owned by the original Avalanche-Bison, which reads: * {{Seal|When Sealed}} '''[LV2][LV3] {{tk|Fortress}} (Opposing turn)'''
All your "[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" family Spirits in refreshed state are unaffected by opposing effects. While both are powerful protection effects that guard effects from all card types and colors, and both required the protection target to be refreshed, the effect range of {{tk|True Fortress}} was shrinked from protecting all "[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" family Spirits to protecting only Bison X itself when compared to the original {{tk|Fortress}}. Despite so, the effect now (1) does not require {{Seal|During Seal}} anymore, and (2) can work in '''any timing''', including own turn. For (1), as Bison X was designed to support the deck led by [[The GlowInsectFlagbearer Fala]], which revolves around {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}}, the removal of {{Seal|During Seal}} condition allows Bison X to stay unaffected even when the Soul Core is used for another round of advent, offering much more freedom and flexibility. As Bison X is a Burst card on top of a {{tk|Flag Contract Advent}} card, when the player would like to summon the card via Burst directly instead of doing advent via {{tk|Seal Flag Contract Advent}}, Bison X won't be rid of its immunity by choosing not to seal. When used outside Fala deck, which the option of {{Seal|Seal}} may not exist, one can still fully utilize Bison X's immunity. For (2), even more importantly, the change of effect timing to "any timing" leads to a drastic change of use of Bison. By having immunity on own turn now means that it can be used as an unaffected attacker instead of just a passive defender or protector on opposing turn. It also prevents the opponent from removing Bison X on its player's turn during Flash Timing. When combined with the refresh effect of Bison X, it can now attack while refreshed and unaffected for at least once per turn every single turn. The absolute protection {{tk|True Fortress}} provides also make it easier for [[The GlowInsectFlagbearer Fala]] to gather [[Platinum Bug]] under it as pre-advent cards during own turn. While the refresh effect of Bison X is tied to {{tk|During Advent}}, White is unironically a color famous for being able to refresh own Spirits, with popular examples like [[The SkyLightSword Crown-Solar]] (Revival). This means that even if Bison X is not during advent (e.g. not used in Fala's deck), you still have plenty of ways to make it an unaffected attacker (with potentially three symbols). Or it can also mean it can attack twice while refreshed if during advent. In general, while the effect range is reduced, the effect itself is getting more powerful with the removal of all the restraints. While {{tk|Fortress}} might remain to be a stronger effect in a dedicated "[[God-King]]"/"[[Ten Crown]]" deck, {{tk|True Fortress}} has turned Bison X into a versatile attacker on its own. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Great Crush.fullContent:
[[File:BS15-X06.jpg|250px|thumb]]
'''Great Crush''' (大粉砕, ''Dai funsai'') is a modified version of [[Crush|Crush]]. It is a special ability of Blue spirits. Spirits with Great Crush have the following effect: 
*'''Great Crush''' (When Attacks) For each LV this Spirit has, discard five cards from the opposing decktop. If any card with Burst effects is discarded by this effect, destroy an opposing Spirit. 

While it still looks at the attacking Spirit's LV for the amount of cards to be discarded, the basic amount jumps from one card to five cards, making a much greater impact. Just at LV2, a Spirit with Great Crush can discard 10 cards on attack. Since the keyword was created in an era where Burst was first introduced and roamed around, the keyword also offers a bonus destroy when a Burst card is milled, touching even the opponent's board besides their deck. With Burst being a recurring mechanic and almost exist in every deck, while it relies on luck, it can be said that the extra destroy is very solid even after the first era of Burst ended. As a balancing factor, there are only a few cards with Great Crush, and those cards are usually of a fairly high cost, with high level costs.

Summon Bolt.fullContent:
[[File:BS25-045.jpg|thumb]] '''Summon Bolt''' (招雷, ''Shōrai'') is an effect introduced in [[BS25]] that is currently exclusive to [[Blue]] Spirits. The effect name is probably a play on the word, '''招来 (the pronunciation is also ''Shōrai'')''', which means "calling someone/something". In the lore, it is being referred to as a tactic called "Calling Thunder", a transliteration of the keyword's name, and is a key part in sending the investigators to the Reverse Continent, and later bringing them back from the past. Spirits with this effect have the following text: * {{sb|Cost X}} '''(When Battles)'''
At the end of the battle, by destroying this Spirit, summon a Cost X Spirit card in the same family as this Spirit from your Hand, without paying it's cost. In essence, the keyword allows the player to summon a different Spirit at the end of battle by paying the price of sacrificing the Spirit that has finished the battle. This means that the player can summon a new attacker/blocker after a battle is finished, and use the effect to summon big Spirits with high costs at ease. Limitation of the effect, however, includes how the Spirit must survive until the end of battle for the effect to proc, and it requires the correct summon target (of the designated cost) to be in the player's Hand. While it makes good use of Blue's hand-filter ability, destroying own Spirits is also a significant loss to Blue which doesn't usually have lots of Spirits on board due to a limitation of hand size. Hence, supporting cards of Summon Bolt revolves around helping the Spirits with such effects to survive until the end of battle, activating the effect without destroying the Spirit, and returning cards from Trash to Hand to compensate the loss. While introduced in the Ultimate era, it received a powerful upgrade in Burning Soul era with [[The Peafowl WisdomKing]] which targets Cost 2~8 instead of the usual one or two specific costs. Additionally, being a Burst that comes with draws with net gain, it allows the player to construct their deck using the keyword more effectively. Since the keyword is said to be a technology owned by the Pirates in the Ultimate era, it has long been a keyword exclusive to the [[Fighting Spirit]] family, with additional families like [[Fencer]] or [[Astral Guardian]]. Since family is referenced for the summon target, the family owned by the Spirits with Summon Bolt determines the range of summon targets, and the combo range of cards. The addition of [[Vassal]], a major family in Burning Soul era, with [[The Peafowl WisdomKing]], adds a big card pool for combo to the deck, or deck that uses Summon Bolt as part of its engine. Since color is not restricted, players can summon Red [[Vassal]] family Spirits without paying the cost via [[The Peafowl WisdomKing]]'s Summon Bolt. Later, in Ultra Advent Era, with the introduction of [[The GrandseaPirateCaptain Narwilliam]], [[Worldswalker]] and [[Fusion Beast]], one being the major era family of the time, the other being another big staple family in [[Blue]] besides [[Fighting Spirit]], are added to the pool, and have expanded the possibility further. However, since Narvilliam himself is not [[Fighting Spirit]], it can't be linked to the previous Summon Bolt Spirits. == Also See == * [[:Category:Summon_Bolt|List of cards with Summon Bolt]] * [[:Category:Summon_Bolt support|List of Summon Bolt's supporting cards]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Once per turn, you can look at the entire opposing Hand, and discard a card among them. This effect
True Plunder.fullContent:
[[File:BS77-X14.png|200px|thumb]] '''True Plunder''' ({{ruby|真|しん}}・{{ruby|強|ごう}}{{ruby|奪|だつ}}；''shin-goudatsu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS77]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The DogTwelveGodKing Greedog X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The DogTwelveGodKing Greedog]]. The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV1-2-3] {{tk|True Plunder}} (When Advents/Attacks)'''
Once per turn, you can look at the entire opposing Hand, and discard a card among them. This effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. If that's a Magic card/card with {{tk|Accel}}, you can immediately activate one of its Main/Flash effects as your effect. However, that card doesn't move from the Trash. As the name implies, it is a remake of the {{tk|Plunder}} keyword owned by the original Greedog. When compared to the original {{tk|Plunder}}, in spite of the turn restriction, it is basically a direct upgrade version of the original effect, making the "true" prefix a very fitting description. That being said, the essence of the effect remain unchanged, by being an effect that checks the contents of every card in the opposing Hand, reducing opposing resources, while turning it into own benefit. The upgrading points, however, come in multiple aspects. First, the effect now discards ''any'' card after looking at the opposing Hand, instead of just Magic cards. While {{tk|Plunder}} could also discard Spirit card when used with [[No. 41 Support Celebration]], {{tk|True Plunder}} alone could choose to discard any type of card from the opposing Hand. While most of the direct hand discard effect only discards a random card, {{tk|True Plunder}} allows the player to choose and discard what is of the biggest loss to the opponent at that point of game. On top of that, it is now a "can't be prevented" effect, having obtained the strongest buff the effect ever wanted by piercing through all types of hand immunity, be it on the cards themselves in Hand or on the Field. This is particularly critical when there has been much more "unaffected by opposing effects in Hand" Magics in the current meta. A third point of change is the effect timing. Instead of a '''(When Attacks/Blocks)''' effect, it becomes a '''(When Advents/Attacks)''' effect. As Greedog X's advent timing is (Your Turn), this means that {{tk|True Plunder}} can activate during the Main Step without entering Attack Step. And with that, the owner of Greedog X can check the contents of cards in the opposing Hand, discarding a card key card from it, while further setting up their Field before launching an attack. This change alone has brought great difference to the actual usage of the effect. Apart from the strength of the effect itself, since it is designed to be used together with [[The SeaShellFlagbearer Lije]], whose deck revolves around hand-discarding, a "can't be prevented" hand-discard effect on advents/attack itself already synergizes with tons of other effects in the same deck. With all the above merits, there is also added restriction for the effect when compared to the original {{tk|Plunder}}, which is the "once per turn" restriction. As Greedog X can refresh itself up to three times, and the effect is a '''(When Advents/Attacks)''' effect, the restriction is added to balance out the maximum hand-discard amount. Yet even with such restriction, it doesn't really affect the power and impact of the effect itself. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31929 |What kind of effect is {{tk|True Plunder}}? |It is an effect where: Once per turn, you can look at the entire opposing Hand, and discard a card among them. This effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. Also, if that's a Magic card/card with {{tk|Accel}}, you can immediately activate one of its Main/Flash effects as your effect. However, that card doesn't move from the Trash. {{tk|True Plunder}} is not treated as {{tk|Plunder}}. |- |} == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Stampede.fullContent:
[[File:Boar.png|thumb|320x320px]]
'''Stampede ''' (突進, ''Tosshin'') is a Blue keyword which had its debut in [[BS36]]. Currently, the only Spirit to possess it is [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar]]. The effect is worded as follows:
* {During Seal} '''''Stampede''''' (When Attacks) Target and attack the opposing Spirit with the lowest cost. When the blocking Spirit is destroyed, target the next opposing Spirit with lowest cost and make it block.
Stampede is a rare effect that allows a Spirit to continuously attack opposing Spirits. The advantage is that since everything is considered one battle, effects such as ending the Attack Step don't activate before Stampede has finished its activation, making it easy to clear the opposing board. Being a target attack effect, it also skips any flash-timings before block.

== Rules ==
# As Stampede specifies that the attack can only continues if the blocking Spirit is destroyed, if the blocking Spirit is removed from the Field in any other ways (e.g. depleted, returned to hand), or simply can't be destroyed, then Stampede's activation ends after the battle with that Spirit.
# When Stampede targets the second Spirit or more, all these battles are considered within one single battle. So if Calamity-Boar gains another (When Attacks) effect (e.g. through braving), that effect only activates when Boar target attacks the first Spirit, and doesn't activate when Stampede targets other Spirits afterwards.
# As all these attacks are considered within one single battle, any effects with the timing "at the end of battle" only activate after the last battle made by Stampede has ended.
# During Stampede, if a Spirit is removed, but has a "remain on Field" effect, or a braved Spirit is removed and it's needed to decide whether the brave is staying, all these effects/actions are paused by being on standby state, and are only resolved after Stampede has ended.
# During Stampede, when the targeted Spirit is destroyed, and the opponent declares a Burst with the timing "When your Spirit is destroyed by the opponent", that Burst activates before Stampede targets the next blocking Spirit.
# When Calamity-Boar attacks and Stampede doesn't target a Spirit, Stampede's "When the blocking Spirit is destroyed" effect doesn't activate.

When your Yellow Spirit is blocked, you can refresh five of your Yellow "[[Bannerace]]" family Spirits. When not blocked, you can return an
Violent Windstorm.fullContent:
[[File:BS77-AX02.png|200px|thumb]] '''Violent Windstorm''' ({{ruby|烈|れつ}}{{ruby|暴|ぼう}}{{ruby|風|ふう}}；''retsu-boufuu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS77]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The ImperialDeity Galoud]], the AX remake of [[The RaptorDeity Galoud]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV1-2-3] {{tk|Violent Windstorm}} (Your Attack Step)'''
When your Yellow Spirit is blocked, you can refresh five of your Yellow "[[Bannerace]]" family Spirits. When not blocked, you can return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom. As the name implies, it is a remake of the {{tk|Windstorm}} effect owned by [[The RaptorDeity Galoud]], a Blue Spirit granted with a Green keyword. The "violent (烈)" part of the name comes from Galoud's Japanese title, 鳥獣'''烈'''神. While {{tk|Windstorm}} was an effect that changes its number of targets as per the number prescribed on the effect (e.g. {{ws|1}}, {{ws|5}}, etc.), {{tk|Violent Windstorm}} is an effect with a fixed number of targets. Being a Yellow keyword this time, the effect is constructed in a reverse way that instead of exhausting opposing Spirits, it now refreshes own Spirits, with the fixed number being 5 as a tribute to original Galoud's signature {{ws|5}}. In addition to the part that activates "when your Spirit is blocked" like regular {{tk|Windstorm}}, {{tk|Violent Windstorm}} also comes with a second part which activates when your Spirit is "not blocked". This is probably a reference to the second effect of original Galoud, which activates when it is not blocked and has reduced the opposing Life; but instead of discarding cards from the opposing deck, it returns an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom, creating pressure for the opponent even if they choose not to block in order not to let Galoud refresh the other Spirits. In the context of Yellow, the effect is actually quite similar to that of [[The FantasyHeavenBlade Twilight-Fantasia]]. Another obvious but strong point of the effect resides on that it applies to ''all'' Yellow Spirits instead of just Galoud himself, unlike the original effects of [[The RaptorDeity Galoud]]. While the refreshing target is locked the "[[Bannerace]]" family Spirits, the Spirit who would trigger the refresh of those Spirits or the removal of opposing Spirit do not have to be "[[Bannerace]]" family Spirits, making {{tk|Violent Windstorm}} a rather generic effect. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31934 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Violent Windstorm}}? |It is an effect where: when your Yellow Spirit is blocked, you can refresh five of your Yellow "[[Bannerace]]" family Spirits, and when it is not blocked, you can return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom. {{tk|Violent Windstorm}} is not treated as {{tk|Windstorm}}. |- |} == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Friend.fullContent:
[[File:uniform noah.jpg|thumb|322x322px]]
'''Friend''' (''フレンド'', ''Furendo'') is a Yellow keyword, premiered in [[BSC28]]. All Spirits with this keyword are part of the "[[Diva]]", "[[School Style]]", and "[[Stage Style]]" families. The keyword has multiple readings with varying activation timings and designated costs, the most common being:
* '''Friend: X/X/X(/X)''' (When Attacks) You can reveal the top card of your deck. If it's a Cost X/X/X(/X) Spirit in family "Song Princess", you can summon it in exhausted state without paying the cost. Remaining cards are discarded.
Other designated conditions include: '''Friend: X or less''', '''Friend: X or more''', and '''Friend: Pretty Animals'''.

Other activation timings include: (When Attacks/Blocks) and (When Blocks).

This effect offers Divas another option of bringing out more Divas at no cost beyond [[On Stage]], trading off guaranteed summons for versatility.

Friend also faces the same problem as [[On Stage]], being vulnerable to Zero Counter and anti-free-summon effects. Furthermore, since Friend summons Spirits in exhausted state, this side effect slows down the pace of the game, and also leaving the Spirits unprotected, easily got rid by the opponent. But there are cards that protect exhausted Divas, and there are also effects that allow the player to summon Divas in refreshed state instead.

Another problem Friend faces is that when it misses, the revealed card always goes to trash. However, this is fixed by effects that allow you to add the revealed card to hand.

Grand Stage can also be seen as an effect more fit than On Stage to the current era, as it requires the player to pay cost to summon a card, avoiding the anti-free-summon effects. On the other hand, On Stage can only summon cards for free.

Mirage Trance.fullContent:
[[File:BS56-X08.png|thumb]] '''Mirage Trance''' (ミラージュトランス) is a keyword introduced in [[BS56]]. The wording is as follows: *'''[LV1][LV2][LV3]''' '''Mirage Trance: Color(/Color)'''
Besides '''(When Deployed)''' effects, your Color(/Color) Mirage also activates its [LV1]/[LV2] Nexus effects. Since cards that are set as Mirage can only activate their Mirage effects, Mirage Trance basically allows the player to set a Nexus as a Mirage while not losing its Nexus effects. It is particularly important to the control-based Nexuses and decks that are more reliant on Nexuses, like the Space Pirate deck. Another use of the effect is to enable the player to activate high level cost LV2 effects of a Nexus. Cards like [[Abyssal Mirage]] can activate their LV2 effects with high core requirement when set in the Mirage Zone via this effect without the need to spend any cores on it. The major downside of the effect is that the player needs to choose between which Nexus card to set as a Mirage. And while the Mirage can activate its Nexus effects, it is still NOT treated as a symbol on Field. A thing to note is that for the Nexus effects activated via Mirage Trance, they are NOT counted as "Mirage effects", as that only covers any {{tk|During Set}} effects (including "when set"). So Spirits that are unaffected by Mirage effects like [[The PartnerBurai Vrick]] would still be affected by the "nexus effects" the Nexus card activated being a Mirage via Mirage Trance. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Mirage Trance|List of cards with Mirage Trance]] {{Keywords Nav}}

AFO.fullContent:
[[File:BS62-060.png|thumb]]
'''AFO''', short for "All For One (オールフォーワン)", is a keyword introduced in [[BS62]], possessed only by [[Azure Wave]] Spirit cards, with the purpose of solely to support [[The PartnerLion Raon]]. The effect is written as follows:

* Give this Spirit and every "The PartnerLion Raon" you control, including those that are in pre-advent condition, the effect: "Contract Pre-Advent/Spirit (Timing) ''[Additional effects].''"

As the name implies, AFO's theme is to have Raon gathering all the effects from the other Spirits, like how a king is supported by his followers. Each follower is also responsible for a different role, reflected by how each AFO gives a different effect. As such, in order to gather many effects, it's necessary to fill the board with Spirits. Since the Spirits with AFO rarely have immunity, it becomes very easy for the opponent to clear them out. However, luckily [[The PartnerLion Raon]] has an effect to retrieve Spirit cards from Trash and re-summoning them, which helps to revive the removed AFO Spirits. The Contract Advent form of Raon, [[The MightyKing King-Raon]], also has an effect to allow AFO Spirits to remain on the field upon being removed, protecting his followers like what a King does.

The opponent chooses one among the following: Core Step/Draw Step/Main Step/Attack Step. On the next turn, the chosen step doesn't occur for the opponent. Each step of your {{tk|Enchain}} can only be chosen once per game. The symbolic effect of [[The Or
Enchain.fullContent:
[[File:BS63-X08.png|thumb]] '''Enchain''' ({{ruby|縛|ばく}}{{ruby|鎖|さ}}) is a keyword introduced in [[BS63]], exclusive to [[The OracleTwentyOnePillars XII The Hanged Man]]. The wording is as follows: * {{tk|Enchain}} '''(When Attacks)'''
The opponent chooses one among the following: Core Step/Draw Step/Main Step/Attack Step. On the next turn, the chosen step doesn't occur for the opponent. Each step of your {{tk|Enchain}} can only be chosen once per game. The symbolic effect of [[The OracleTwentyOnePillars XII The Hanged Man|The Hanged Man]]. While each step could only be chosen once per game, meaning that it could at most be used four times in game, each choice limits the next choice, and ultimately the opponent would have to choose to skip their Main Step/Attack Step via this effect, which almost equals to giving an extra turn to the owner of Hanged Man, as they can't arrange a proper counterattack next turn if Main Step or Attack Step is skipped. The diminishing freedom to choose and locking of steps work like how you slowly strangle the opponent with a loop of strings, fitting the image of Hanged Man. The effect is particularly useful in sealing off opponent's chance of counterattack when you want to finish them, as even if they survive this turn, they can't do anything on their next turn to counterattack, or even to touch your board. While the effect is very strong, it has two major weaknesses. One of them is how it is the opponent choosing which step to skip, and the second one is how they only need to choose one step each time. For the first weakness, it means the opponent can choose to skip their Attack Step, or even Main Step when they are still preparing for attack or setting up if you attacked and activated {{tk|Enchain}} very early in game. This makes the timing of using the effect hard to measure in game. And it is also linked to the second weakness, which refers to how the effect needs 3-4 attack to achieve the most desirable outcome (skipping Main Step/Attack Step). In order to achieve this, you would need to keep Hanged Man alive for more than one turn or refresh it to make multiple attacks. However, with the second effect of Hanged Man, and its own [[Oracle XII Over Hanged Man|Oracle Mirage magic]], those two weaknesses can be dealt with easily. [[Oracle XII Over Hanged Man]] allows you to choose which steps to lock instead, giving you the complete control of when to skip the opponent's important steps, and completely solved the problem of timings. Being able to directly choose the important steps also means you don't need to do extra attacks beforehand to limit the opponent's choices, and can use Hanged Man only at the time you want to finish the game. In fact, Hanged Man's second effect also allows you to activate {{tk|Enchain}} when your Blue-only "[[Astroblazer]]"/"[[Azure Contract]]"/"[[King Contract]]" family Spirit attacks, meaning that you can still activate {{tk|Enchain}} when attacking with your actual finisher in the three designated families. Another use of this effect is how when you attack with Hanged Man at Lv2 or above, you can activate the effect twice and the amount of attacks you needed to achived the desirable outcome will be halved. == Navigation == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Draw Lock.title: Draw Lock
Draw Lock.contentSample:
[[file:BS64-X04.png|thumb]] '''Draw Lock''' (ドローロック ; ''dorou roku'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS64]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The GreatJudge Gefan-Gnis]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2] {{tk|Draw Lock}} (When Advents)'''
You can reveal three cards from each player's decktop. Both players return those cards to their decktop, face-up. While there are face-up cards in deck, when drawing via an effect, only one card can be drawn. (Effects that target decktop s
Draw Lock.fullContent:
[[file:BS64-X04.png|thumb]] '''Draw Lock''' (ドローロック ; ''dorou roku'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS64]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The GreatJudge Gefan-Gnis]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2] {{tk|Draw Lock}} (When Advents)'''
You can reveal three cards from each player's decktop. Both players return those cards to their decktop, face-up. While there are face-up cards in deck, when drawing via an effect, only one card can be drawn. (Effects that target decktop start below the face-up cards, and cards that return to the decktop return to the deck below the face-up cards.) As the name implies, the effect locks drawing effects and restricting normal decktop draws in a way that the content is known to the opponent. While not the first effect that flips card face-up in deck, it's the first effect that makes the face-up cards in deck a separate entity that can only be removed by regular draws in Draw Step (Cards that are returned to the decktop are returned to below the face-up cards, and any drawing effects or decktop-targeting effect don't affect the face-up cards). Unlike some other similar control effects, Draw Lock also doesn't require Gefan-Gnis to remain on the Field, but purely depends on whether there are face-up cards remaining in deck, making it much harder to deal with. Apart from knowing the content of the next few draws the opponent is getting, the greatest use of Draw Lock is to block large amount of draws via a single effect, or even multiple effects. Despite being a Blue card itself, Draw Lock hits Blue the hardest, as most of Blue's drawing effects involves discarding after drawing. For example, while Draw Lock lasts, the effect of [[Stream Draw]] will become "drawing one card from the deck, then discard two cards from the Hand", which chips away the user's resources instead. Another big victim of Draw Lock is Green, with half of its draw needing the player to discard the entire Hand and draw from deck until they have the same amount of cards in the opposing Hand. While Draw Lock lasts, however, the user of such effects can only draw one card after discarding their entire Hand, making the effects almost pointless. Another thing to note is, while Draw Locks last, since only one card can be drawn, "by A do B" effects that includes drawing two cards or more as its part A or part B can't be activated at all. (e.g. [[The ArmoredWarOgre Rashou]]'s (When Summoned) effect) As a balancing factor, Draw Lock also applies to the player who activated the effect. It also doesn't affect any "reveal-and-add" effect like the typical godseeker cycle of grandwalker nexus decks, or any similar searching effects. As a remedy or countering measure, effects that increase the number of cards a player draws during Draw Step (e.g. The LV1-2 effect of [[The Burning Canyon]]) will be very effective against Draw Lock, as this adds to the amount of cards one draws regularly during Draw Step, and it can hence remove two or more face-up cards from the deck. Another thing worthwhile to note is that while only face-up cards are left in deck, since effects that target decktop '''can't''' target the cards, Blue's traditional effect of milling, which involves discarding cards from '''opposing decktop''' stops functioning. Despite being a rather desperate attempt, it ensures the player who used Draw Lock that its deck won't be milled to zero by opposing milling effects. Interestingly, in the same set where Gefan-Gnis debuted, each of the three new Contract decks introduced possesses at least one way of drawing two or more cards at once (e.g. [[The Cyclo Canyon]]/[[The EmeraldFlowerLance Bloom-Stem]]/[[The AstralZeroSword Foranswer]]). And in both the anime CM and card lore, [[The Zero Partner, Wiz]] is fighting against Gefan-Gnis holding [[The AstralZeroSword Foranswer|Foranswer]], which has the ability of drawing 4 cards and discarding 2 cards from Hand via its {{tk|Brave Engage}}. In the lore, Gefan-Ganis cancelled out the effect of Brave Engage, and it can be done exactly in game via Draw Lock. ==See Also== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]
