(Once per Turn: Same Name) You can discard ten cards from the opposing decktop. Then, if there is any opposing cards being banished, destroy any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates up to a total cost of 15. As the name im
XV Crush.fullContent:
[[File:BS66-XV05.png|thumb]] '''XV Crush''' ({{ruby|XV|エックスブイ}}{{ruby|粉|ふん}}{{ruby|砕|さい}}；''ekkusu-vi funsai'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS66]], exclusive to [[The GiantHero Titus XV]]. The wording is as follows: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|XV Crush}} (When Summoned)'''
(Once per Turn: Same Name) You can discard ten cards from the opposing decktop. Then, if there is any opposing cards being banished, destroy any number of opposing Spirits/Ultimates up to a total cost of 15. As the name implies, it is a new variant of {{tk|Crush}}, the first-ever Blue keyword that focuses on deck destruction. The "XV" in the name fits the 15th anniversary theme of the XV-Rares and is essence a showcase of how new-generation deck-discarding effect works after 15 years. Being the first X-Rare in [[Blue]], and hence the first X-Rare with deck-discarding abilities, there are no better choices than the XV remake of Titus to get such an ability. Despite the fact that it is named after {{tk|Crush}}, however, the effect works entirely different from {{tk|Crush}}. Instead of looking at levels of the effect owner, it is a fixed amount mill. Considering the amount and timing, it is in fact the remake of [[The GiantHero Titus]]'s (When Summoned) effect, rather than a remake of {{tk|Crush}}. It is also to be noted that while it can be supported by effects stating "Crush"-named effects, it '''can't''' be supported by effects that state {{tk|Crush}} directly (e.g. [[Tsundog-Golem]]). As a XV-Rare that shares the same color as the new Contract Spirit coming in the same set like a lot of the other XV-Rares, it is designed to work with [[Petit Shack]]. By using [[Petit Shack]]'s {{tk|Wave Crush}} ability, the condition of having opposing cards banished is easily fulfilled, and the effect will then come with extra cost destruction that destroys up to a total cost of 15, sticking to the "XV (15th anniversary)" theme. While [[Petit Shack]]'s [[Wave Contract]] deck revolves around a bit-by-bit milling/banishing scheme, {{tk|XV Crush}} serves as a finishing move with a high mill number and cost destruction that removes opponent's blocker and reduction symbols on Field, which matches well with [[The GrandseaPirateEmperor Tri-Shack]]'s LV2 effect. As a limitation, unlike other deck-discarding effects, the effect is limited to (once per turn: same name), most probably a precaution to loops, especially when players can easily return Titus XV from Trash to Hand via [[The GrandseaContractAnchor Abyssal Anchor]]'s {{tk|Brave Engage}}. The card cost of Titus XV, who owns the keyword, is also relatively high regardless of the reduction symbols. This can be solved, however, by [[The GrandseaPirateEmperor Tri-Shack]]'s (When Attacks) effect. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Wave Crush.title: Wave Crush
Wave Crush.contentSample:
[[File:BS66-CX03.png|thumb]] '''Wave Crush''' ({{ruby|波|なみ}}{{ruby|粉|ふん}}{{ruby|砕|さい}}；''nami-funsai'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS66]], exclusive to [[Petit Shack]]. The wording is as follows: * {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}}/{{tk|Spirit}} '''[LV1][LV2] {{tk|Wave Crush}} (When Attacks)'''
Banish a card from the opposing decktop. For each 4 cost this Spirit has, this effect banishes +1 card. Also, this Spirit's symbol is fixed as zero. As the name implies, it is a new variant of {{tk|Crush
Wave Crush.fullContent:
[[File:BS66-CX03.png|thumb]] '''Wave Crush''' ({{ruby|波|なみ}}{{ruby|粉|ふん}}{{ruby|砕|さい}}；''nami-funsai'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS66]], exclusive to [[Petit Shack]]. The wording is as follows: * {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}}/{{tk|Spirit}} '''[LV1][LV2] {{tk|Wave Crush}} (When Attacks)'''
Banish a card from the opposing decktop. For each 4 cost this Spirit has, this effect banishes +1 card. Also, this Spirit's symbol is fixed as zero. As the name implies, it is a new variant of {{tk|Crush}}, with some similarities and also some major changes. Like {{tk|Charge}}, it looks at the spec of the card with the keyword; But instead of level, it looks at the cost. And while it is named after "Crush", it isn't actually a deck-discarding effect, but a ''deck-banishing'' effect. On top of that, the effect also removes the symbol of the attacking Spirit, allowing the user to focus purely on attacking the opponent's deck, not giving the opponent extra resources in the process. Being a banish effect, the merit includes bypassing all existing anti-mill effects (e.g. [[Gardenia Field]]), and removing opponent's cards without needing to worry about how sending cards to Trash might help the opponent instead when they are using decks with strong trash retrieval and reanimation power. Fixing own symbol as zero, as mentioned, allows the player to attack without reducing the opposing Life, which stops the opponent from gaining core resources through taking lives, or using any cards with effects that activate when their Life is reduced/activate Bursts that reacts to Life reduction (e.g. [[Magibullet]], [[Burst Wall]] (Revival), [[The Phanto-Magia Hermit-Ritter Badgerdulles]] etc.) As a new keyword, the demerit includes how it can't be supported by effects that support {{tk|Crush}} alone in the past. Effects that increase the amount of cards to be banished are also very rare when compared to normal mill. When effectiveness are to be considered, with the initial amount being "one", the increase per four cost is relatively tame. However, being the center of the [[Wave Contract]] deck, new cards introduced in the same set have more or less covered the weakness. And as a keyword that is printed on a [[Contract Spirit]] which revolves around Brave, it also means that it can be activated consistently with {{tk|Contract Advent}} bringing back the card, and Braves raising the cost to a considerable amount (e.g. Cost 8 Advent + Cost 4 Brave = Banish 5 cards at once). == Also see == * [[The GrandseaPirateEmperor Tri-Shack]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

[[file:BS68-X06.png|thumb]] '''Ultra Holy Life''' (超・聖命；''chou-seimei'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS68]], exclusive to Yellow Spirit cards. The effect is worded as follows: *{{tk|Ultra Holy Life}} '''(When Attacks)'''
When blocked, draw a card from the deckbottom; when not blocked, put a core from the Void to your Life. As an upgraded version of [[Holy Life]], Ultra Holy Life applies more pressure to the opponent by also gaining value when being blocked. The Yellow color has always been lacking draws from all front, so Ultra Holy Life has provided a great power jump by giving conditional draws to more Spirits, allowing the deck to avoid fully relying on only certain cards to extend the game. Chaos Stage.fullContent:
[[file:BSC40-X02.png|thumb]] '''Chaos Stage''' (呪滅劇) is a keyword introduced in [[BSC40]], possessed exclusively by [[［Monochrome Fantasia's Idol Three Giants］Queenstel Merduk]]. The effect is read as follows: *{{tk|Chaos Stage}} '''(When Destroyed by the Opponent)'''
By sending an opposing Life to the Reserve, this Spirit remains on the Field, refreshed. Since Queenstel Merduk is based off [[The NetherThreeGiants Queen-Merduk]], similarly, {{tk|Chaos Stage}} is based off Queen-Merduk's possessing keyword, {{tk|Spell Blight}}. The only difference is that {{tk|Spell Blight}} sends the life to the trash, while {{tk|Chaos Stage}} sends the life to the reserve. Thanks to the different aspects of Queenstel Merduk, one may find more uses with {{tk|Chaos Stage}} than expected. Being in the "[[Stage Style]]" family allows Queenstel Merduk to be summoned by [[［Off Shot］Queenstel Merduk]] at a low cost, as early as turn two going first. At minimum BP being 5000, ［Monochrome Fantasia's Idol Three Giants］Queenstel Merduk proves to be an effective blocker early on. Later in the game, one can also summon [[［10th Diva's Idol Three Giants］Queenstel Merduk]] for anti-bounce effects, limiting Merduk's weakness to only depletion effects. While the effect is read as "kaosu sutēji" in furigana, literally the keyword would've been read as "jumetsu geki", the same pronunciation as {{Tk|Spell Blight}}. The only difference between the two keywords is the last kanji. == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}}

[[File:BSC43-RV007.png|thumb]] '''CoZ12 Part''' (CoZ12パート) is a new effect introduced in [[BSC43]], a derivative version of [[Solo Part]], possessed exclusively by the Revival version of [[［All Out Diva］Candy-Cerd]]. The effect is worded as follows: *{{tk|CoZ12 Part}}
While [[file:Soul Core.png|20px]] is on this Spirit, all your {{tk|CoZ12}} Spirits can't be destroyed by opposing effects. Unlike Solo Part, CoZ12 Part is an immunity effect which covers all cards in the CoZ12 team, giving a wider range of destruction protection, and it also means that [[Diva]] family cards which treat themselves as in all teams also benefit from this keyword. [[file:BSC45-XV06.png|250px|thumb]] '''Grand Assault''' ({{ruby|神|しん}}・{{ruby|強|きょう}}{{ruby|襲|しゅう}}; ''shin kiyou-shiyuu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC45]], possessed exclusively by [[The GiantEmperor Alexander XV]]. The effect reads as follows: * {{G Assault|2}} '''(When Attacks)'''
Up to twice per turn, you can exhaust a Nexus/Grandwalker Nexus you control. When you've done so, this Spirit refreshes twice, and during this battle, the cost of every card in the opposing Hand/Removed Z
Grand Assault.fullContent:
[[file:BSC45-XV06.png|250px|thumb]] '''Grand Assault''' ({{ruby|神|しん}}・{{ruby|強|きょう}}{{ruby|襲|しゅう}}; ''shin kiyou-shiyuu'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC45]], possessed exclusively by [[The GiantEmperor Alexander XV]]. The effect reads as follows: * {{G Assault|2}} '''(When Attacks)'''
Up to twice per turn, you can exhaust a Nexus/Grandwalker Nexus you control. When you've done so, this Spirit refreshes twice, and during this battle, the cost of every card in the opposing Hand/Removed Zone increases by +2. '''Grand Assault''' serves as a new upgrade version/variant of the original [[Assault]] keyword, changing from exhausting only Nexuses to Nexuses/Grandwalker Nexuses, refreshing once to refreshing twice at once, and having embedded with a opposing-card-cost-increasing effect. The change of exhausting only Nexuses to Nexuses/Grandwalker Nexuses has probably referenced the {{tk|Grand Field}} of [[Suzuri Hideto]], the user of [[The GiantEmperor Alexander]] in [[Battle Spirits Shounen Gekiha Dan]], and allows Alexander XV or any future Spirit with the keyword to work better with Grandwalker decks and Grandwalker Nexuses in general. With Grandwalker's nature of being Nexuses that are harder to remove and in general lower in cost, this change allows the Spirit with the keyword to refresh more consistently. Another interesting change of the effect is that it allows the Spirit to be refreshed twice in a roll. While it is unclear it is tied to the number X stated on the {{G Assault|X}} keyword or not, it allows a Spirit to become refreshed from being heavily exhausted. Despite so, since {{tk|Grand Assault}} is currently limited to being a '''(When Attacks)''' effect, the Spirit would still need to be able to declare an attack first. Such effect is most probably designed to work with/overcome the {{tk|Contract Field}} effect of [[The RagingGaleContractor Huracan]], the closest Blue Contractor Nexus deck released when Alexander XV was released, so that players can use Alexander XV in the deck without rendering the refresh from "Assault" type of effects useless. As a new element, instead of deck destruction, this time the keyword comes with imposing restrictions on the use of cards from the opposing Hand/Removed Zone, making the consecutive attack move of the Spirit with {{tk|Grand Assault}} more stable without the fear of getting easily stopped by opponent's flash reactions from Hand/Removed Zone. Since the cost increase lasts throughout the battle, it is worth noticing that the effect persists during the battle even if one {{tk|advent}} on the attacking Spirit. On the technical side, {{tk|Grand Assault}} uses the wording "You can exhaust....When you've done so, ....", making it different from original [[Assault]]'s "by A do B" clause. While the actual usefulness is in question, this allows a player to exhaust their Nexuses/Grandwalker Nexuses via the effect even when their Spirits with {{tk|Grand Assault}} can't refresh. ==See Also:== *[[:Category:Grand Assault|List of cards with Grand Assault]] ==Related Articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The effect is worded as follows: * {{SA Unleash|3}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (Your Attack Step)'''
When your "[[Scalostle]]" family Brave Spirit attacks, you can send three cores from any of your "Nuadha" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit. When you've done so
Silver Arm Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BS71-X09.png|200px|thumb]] '''Silver Arm Unleash''' ( 銀腕界放；''Gin-wan-kai-hō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS71]], exclusive to [[The SilverArmDivineEmperor Agateram]], the [[Concluser]] Spirit of [[The SilverArmContractor Nuadha]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{SA Unleash|3}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (Your Attack Step)'''
When your "[[Scalostle]]" family Brave Spirit attacks, you can send three cores from any of your "Nuadha" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit. When you've done so, unless the opponent discards a Magic card from their Hand, for each differently named "[[Scalostle]]" family Brave you control, send an opposing Life to the Trash. The name comes from the most well-known feature of Nuadha, his prosthetic silver arm. Like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], [[Shining Heaven Unleash]], and [[Curse Unleash]], this Unleash requires a specific Grandwalker to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. When compared to the average Unleash effects, it is a rare case that the effect doesn't require the owner, [[The SilverArmDivineEmperor Agateram]], to attack or do any specific action. Instead, it can be triggered as long as [[The SilverArmDivineEmperor Agateram]] is on the Field and any "[[Scalostle]]" family Brave Spirit attacks. Hence, even without refresh effects, this effect can be activated multiple times as long as there are cores on Nuadha, and there are Brave Spirits to attack. When it comes to the nature of the effect, while it can be avoided by discarding defense Magic cards to prevent the life burn, protective text like "this card is unaffected by opposing effects in hand" have become more and more common among the defense magics (e.g. [[Burst Wall]] Revival, [[Burst Flame]] Revival), which makes the owner unable to discard those Magic cards, and is forced to take the life burn. It is also rare that the life burn doesn't have an actual upper limit. While most life burn effects are capped at two lives, like [[Super Unleash]], Silver Arm Unleash doesn't have any limitations. Despite being such a powerful effect on paper, the number of "[[Scalostle]]" family Brave that one can put in a deck and gather at a time act as the physical limitation for the effect. With that in mind, most probably serving as a balancing measure, there were only two "[[Scalostle]]" family Braves on the set Agateram was released, and the upper limit of Silver Arm Unleash was hence capped at two. ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Contract Duet Part.fullContent:
[[File:BSC46-RV008.png|thumb]] '''Contract Duet Part''' (契約デュエットパート) is a keyword introduced in [[BSC46]], currently exclusive to the Revival version of [[［Star Fest］Jeanne Doraniece]]. The effect is worded as follows: * '''[LV2][LV3]''' {{tk|Contract Duet Part}}
While you control a "Rei-Ohba" with {{tk|Contract Advent}}, your "Rei-Ohba"/"Jeanne Doraniece" can't be destroyed by opposing effects. As the name implies, it is a modified version of {{tk|Duet Part}}. When compared to {{tk|Duet Part}}, it doesn't require putting Soul Core onto the Spirit, which has been a significant downside of {{tk|Duet Part}} considering that Soul Core might be the requirement of other effects, among which is {{tk|Contract Advent}}, the core mechanic introduced together with [[Contract Card|Contract Spirits]] that came to [[Diva]] since [[BSC40]]. Removing the Soul Core condition makes the effect much more compatible with Contract Spirit decks, and the intended support target of [[［Star Fest］Jeanne Doraniece]], the deck led by [[［Together Forever］Rei-Ohba]], is exactly a Contract Spirit deck. Instead of Soul Core, however, it requires another designated Spirit on Field this time which [[［Star Fest］Jeanne Doraniece]] on her own can't fulfill, making it a keyword that can't function on itself unlike {{tk|Duet Part}}. Note that {{tk|Contract Duet Part}} is '''NOT''' counted as {{tk|Duet Part}} in game, and can't be supporter by effects that support {{tk|Duet Part}}. == Related articles == * [[:Category:Contract Duet Part|List of cards with Contract Duet Part]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Time Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BSC47-X04.png|200px|thumb]] '''Time Unleash''' ({{ruby|時|じ}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}}；''Jikaihō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC47]], exclusive to [[Shin-Chronos-Returnal]], the [[Concluser]] Spirit of [[The SpacetimeContractor Chronos]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{T Unleash|2}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Manifests/Attacks)'''
You can destroy an opposing Spirit with the highest cost. Then, you can send two cores from any of your "Chronos" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit. When you've done so, your counter or the opposing counter gets -2. Following the recent trend of the new "Unleash"-named keywords, like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Curse Unleash]], this Unleash requires a Grandwalker of specific name to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. In this case, it is any Grandwalker Nexus with "Chronos" in name. As the name implies, and reflected by the nature of its owner, [[Shin-Chronos-Returnal]], the effect manipulates ownself or the opponent's counters, and effectively "rewinding" the time. Since the effect is not limited to once per turn, it can potentially bring the number of opposing counters to zero with consecutive attacks supported by [[The SpacetimeContractor Chronos]]'s effect. When used to reduce own counters, it allows players to activate more rebirth with counter limits. Much like [[Celestial Unleash]], the effect is a "You can do A. When you've done so, do B" effect. Hence, even if there is only one core on your "Chronos"-named Grandwalker Nexuses, you can send the core to [[Shin-Chronos-Returnal]], just that the part after "when you've done so" won't proc. ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

By sending two cores from your "Contractor Indra" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit, during this turn, all your "Can
Thunder Unleash.fullContent:
[[File:BS75-X10.png|200px|thumb]] '''Thunder Unleash''' ({{ruby|雷|らい}}{{ruby|界|かい}}{{ruby|放|ほう}}；''raikaihō'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS75]], exclusive to [[The ThunderGodDragonEmperor Vajrawurm]], the [[Concluser]] Spirit of [[The HeavenlyThunderContractor Indra]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{Unleash|2|Thunder}} '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] (When Manifests/Attacks)'''
By sending two cores from your "Contractor Indra" Grandwalker Nexuses to this Spirit, during this turn, all your "Can't Attack/Block" effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. When you've done so, during this game, two opposing Spirits/Ultimates can't attack/block. Following the recent trend of the new "Unleash"-named keywords, like [[Creator Unleash]], [[Absolute Unleash]], and [[Curse Unleash]], this Unleash requires a Grandwalker of specific name to activate an effect much more powerful than an average Unleash effect. In this case, it is any Grandwalker Nexus with "Contractor Indra" in name. Like what the name implies, and following one of the main gimmick of Indra's deck, the effect allows players to turn two opposing Spirits/Ultimates immobile for the rest of the game, effectively "stunning them with thunder". What the effect provides on top of the other stunning effects in Indra is a "piercing" effect, which makes all the following "can't attack/block" effects that turn, including the second part of {{tk|Thunder Unleash}}, effects that can't be prevented by opposing effects like {{tk|Heavy Armor}}. While it is easy to misjudge, once the piercing effect is granted, all your "can't attack/block" effects activated in the same turn can't be prevented by opposing Spirits/Ultimates for the duration of such effects even if they gain immunity or armor afterwards. For example, if you targeted an opposing Spirit with {{ha|Yellow}} via the second part of {{tk|Thunder Unleash}}, even after your turn ended, where the "during this turn, all your "Can't Attack/Block" effect can't be prevented by opposing effects" part of {{tk|Thunder Unleash}} ended, since the "can't attack/block" effect lasts for the entire game, and can't be prevented when it was established, the effect lingers on, and the Spirit with {{ha|Yellow}} under the influence of such effect still can't attack/block for the rest of the game even when the "piercing effect" has apparently ended. In Indra's deck, the effect takes a core position as it provides multiple benefits: 1) Piercing effect that helps the stunning effects, the main gimmick of Indra, overcome decks with overwhelming immunities like [[The ArgentIronKnight Yggdrasil]]'s [[Knight Contract]] deck, and [[The MoonlightContractor Barone]]'s White [[Astral Deity]] deck. 2) Defense option. In Vajrawurm's case, as it can manifest during opposing attack step, it provides defense option with pierce that maximizes the stunning ability to prevent opponent's follow-up attacks. As Indra's deck is rather aggressive in nature, it provides the minimal defense to survive the turn and bridging the win next turn. 3) Cores to fund the card-summoning effect of [[The ThunderGodDragonEmperor Vajrawurm|Vajrawurm]]'s LV3 effect. Same as most of the other "Unleash"-named effects, regardless of what the additional effect is, the Unleash effect gives the players cores, which is particularly useful in [[Yellow]] decks like Indra that is short in cores. In Vajrawurm's case, as it is a (When Manifest/Attacks) effect with no "once per turn" restriction, the effect alone can provide 4 cores without refreshing Vajrawurm. This provides the resources needed for further summons or the use of magic, which is particularly important in Indra deck, which is aggressive in nature and aiming to finish the opponent in fewest number of turns if possible (hence it is unlikely to stack cores through stalling or taking lives). == Also See == * [[The HeavenlyThunderContractor Indra]] ==Related articles== {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]] [[Category:2nd tier effects]]

Fleur Part.fullContent:
[[File:PB48-CP01.png|thumb]] '''Fleur Part''' (フルールパート) is a keyword introduced in [[PB48]], currently exclusive to the Revival version of [[［Sengoku Goddess］Diana Fleur]]. The effect is worded as follows: * {{tk|During OC}} '''[LV1][LV2]''' {{tk|Fleur Part}}
All your {{tk|During Advent}} "Fleur" can't be destroyed. As the name implies, it is a modified version of {{tk|Duet Part}}. When compared to {{tk|Duet Part}}, it doesn't require putting Soul Core onto the Spirit, which has been a significant downside of {{tk|Duet Part}} considering that Soul Core might be the requirement of other effects, among which is {{tk|Contract Advent}}, the core mechanic introduced together with [[Contract Card|Contract Spirits]] that came to [[Diva]] since [[BSC40]]. Removing the Soul Core condition makes the effect much more compatible with Contract Spirit decks, and the intended support target of [[［Sengoku Goddess］Diana Fleur]], is the Contract Spirit edition of the "Fleur" deck introduced by the new cards in [[PB48]]. Instead of Soul Core, however, it requires the Spirits to be {{tk|During Advent}}, making the target rather limited. On the other hand, as per the concept of Contract Spirit, the Contact Spirit that is during advent is usually the main attacker. Hence, it can be more than enough for the effect to protect the main attacker in a game. Another special feature about {{tk|Fleur Part}} is, the "can't be destroyed" isn't limited to "effect destroy" like {{tk|Duet Part}} or other similar variants, but also covers "BP comparison", making it an even stronger effect despite having rather limited target as per the {{tk|During Advent}} condition. That being said, it isn't an invincible effect, as the target is still vulnerable to bounce or depletion. But with effects like those from [[［Monochrome Fantasia］Noa Fleur]], which provide bounce immunity, the protection is rather complete. == Related articles == * [[:Category:"Fleur"-named|List of "Fleur"-named cards]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Roaring Stampede.contentSample:

The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV2-3] {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} (When Attacks)'''
Target and attack the opposing Spirit with the lowest cost. Also, when the blocking Spirit is depleted/
Roaring Stampede.fullContent:
[[File:BS76-X12.png|200px|thumb]] '''Roaring Stampede''' ({{ruby|爆|ばく}}{{ruby|突|とっ}}{{ruby|進|しん}}；''baku-toshin'') is a keyword introduced in [[BS76]], currently exclusive to [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar X]], the {{ruby|X|Ten}} remake of [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar]]. The wording is as follows: * {{Seal|During Seal}} '''[LV2-3] {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} (When Attacks)'''
Target and attack the opposing Spirit with the lowest cost. Also, when the blocking Spirit is depleted/destroyed, discard six cards from the opposing decktop, and target the next opposing target with lowest cost to make it block. This "target attack/block" effect can't be prevented by opposing effects. In general, the core part of the effect is no difference from {{tk|Stampede}}, the signature keyword owned by the original [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar]], but with various details upgraded and fine-tuned to fit the newest era. The new name comes from adding the "bakuon" element from [[The RagingGaleContractor Huracan|Huracan]] and "[[Roaring Azure]] (爆蒼)" element from Calamity-Boar's own family in front of the original keyword name. When compared to {{tk|Stampede}}, the effect now absorbs the deck discarding effect that was originally printed on a separate effect on Calamity-Boar that requires 4 cores to proc. While the maximum number of cards discarded is reduced to six, and is limited to this Spirit's own attack, the fact that {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} is an effect that works needing only two cores cover the aforementioned loss. Another significant improvement is on how the deck discarding effect now applies even when the opposing blocking Spirit is depleted. Much like the improvements observed from similar Red effects, covering depletion means the opponent can't just deplete their own Spirits after blocking by another effect or simply paying costs for Magics to avoid the deck discarding effect. Lastly, turning the effect into a piercing effect (i.e. "can't be prevented by opposing effects") perfectly deals with the concern of the entire effect being rendered useless when opposing Spirits are unaffected by effects, which is in fact increasingly common. Being an effect modified from {{tk|Stampede}}, its strength and weakness are more or less the same as the original effect. While the above improvements have covered most of its weakness, the new effect still doesn't cover Ultimates for effect target, making it useless against Ultimate-main decks like the [[Evil God]] deck. It also remained to be a mandatory effect, meaning that if there's any opposing Spirit for you to target attack, you have to do so and cannot go for the opposing Life for the attack. Since you can target attack even exhausted Spirit and the effect can't be prevented, it means that you are forced to do so even when the opponent controls only exhausted Spirits and even when those exhausted Spirits are unaffected by opposing effects. On the other hand, the forcing-block effect works very well with the supporting cards of [[The RagingGaleContractor Huracan|Huracan]], which Calamity-Boar X is designed to work with, as it basically forces the opposing Spirit to get heavily exhausted before Flash Timing by being targeted to block. And by heavily exhausting opposing Spirits, effects that trigger upon either player's Spirits being heavily exhausted can proc immediately. == How the effect actually works == From the effect text alone, it might be slightly hard to visualize, but in general, the effect works in a way that: 1) You attack with Calamity-Boar X, and target attack an opposing Spirit with the lowest cost.

2) Resolve all other effects from both players that take place upon attack declaration, including any Burst with the condition: {{Burst|con|After an opposing Spirit attacks}}.

3) The targeted Spirit, if not already exhausted, exhausts and blocks Calamity-Boar X.

4) Resolve all effects related to the block declaration of that Spirit.

5) After-block Flash Timing occurs, if the blocking opposing Spirit is not depleted/destroyed, proceed to the resolution of battle when both players declared no Flash. (On the other hand, if the Spirit that blocked is depleted/destroyed during Flash Timing, discard six cards from the opposing decktop, and target the next Spirit to attack, then jump to (8).) 6) Compare the BP of both Spirits, and destroy the one(s) with lower (same) BP.

7) If the opposing blocking Spirit is destroyed, discard six cards from the opposing decktop; If Calamity-Boar X also survives, target the next Spirit to attack at the same time as any effect related to the opposing blocking Spirit that was just destroyed resolve.

8) The next battle commence without starting a "new attack" (i.e. without making a new attack declaration), and Calamity-Boar X would remain exhausted unless it is refreshed in Flash Timing or through other effects.

9) When no Spirits are available for target attack, the entire attack ends, and proceed to the "end of battle" timing. == Official Q&As == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31698 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}? |It is an effect where: you target and attack an opposing Spirit with the lowest cost, and if the Spirit that blocked is depleted/destroyed, discard six cards from the opposing decktop, and target an opposing Spirit with the next lowest cost. After resolving all effects that take place at that timing, returns to the timing of block declaration for the new Spirit, and the new Spirit is forced to block. This "target attack/block" effect can target even exhausted Spirits. As it "can't be prevented by opposing effects", opposing Spirits that are unaffected by your effects must block as well. However, if they are Spirit-condition Braves like Imagine Braves which cannot block due to rules, or Grandwalker in {{tk|Grandphosis}} state which cannot be targeted by this effect in the first place, you can't target attack them. {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} is not treated as {{tk|Stampede}}. |- |31699 |When [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar X]] attacks and activates {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, if you activated any "during this battle" effects, would those effects last while the second and third Spirit block your Calamity-Boar X? |Yes, as it is still within the same battle when blocked by the second or the third Spirit, such effects will last. |- |31700 |When a second block induced by {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} is successfully established, can I activate effects like "when your Spirit attacks", or '''(When Attacks)''' effect of the Brave braved to [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar X]]? |No, you can't. For the second or subsequent block, you are returning to the block declaration timing, but not the attack declaration timing. Hence, immediate effects that resolve at attack declaration, like draw a card or destroy a Spirit, cannot be activated again. However, if the ''(When Attacks)''' effect is something that takes place during Flash Timing, or when a battle resolves, or when Spirits are destroyed, etc., which take place during or after block declaration, it can be activated again. Continuous effects that are always active during an attack, like "this Spirit gains +5000 BP", or "the opponent can't activate Burst effects", would also remain active in the second or subsequent block. |- |31701 |When [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar X]] attacks and activates {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, if the opponent uses any effects that "end the Attack Step when this battle ends" like [[Burst Wall]]'s, would the Attack Step end before proceeding with the following battles? |No, as long as there are Spirits to target attack next, the same battle continues, and the Attack Step won't end. Hence, the attack will continue while {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} lasts, and the Attack Step will end when the entire battle actually ends. |- |31702 |When [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar X]] attacks and activates {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, if the opponent uses any effects that makes "opposing Spirits can't attack", like [[Tousenbo Wall]] (Revival), would the battle end before proceeding with the following battles? |No, the second or subsequent block initiated is not an action of making a new attack, so the battles will continue even if Calamity-Boar X is under "can't attack" effects. |- |31703 |When [[The BoarTwelveGodKing Calamity-Boar X]] attacks and activates {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, if the opponent uses any effects that "end the battle immediately" like [[Closed Gemini]]'s, would the battle end before proceeding with the following battles? |Yes, as it will skip to the "end of battle" timing directly, the remaining battles can't continue. |- |31704 |After activating {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, if the Spirit is being {{tk|advented}} on, or switched with another Spirit, as long as the opposing blocking Spirit is depleted/destroyed, I can make a new Spirit block? |No, you can't. The current battle will continue, but the {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} effect is gone, and you can't make a new Spirit block. |- |31705 |When I made a target attack and refreshed the attacking Spirit in the process, then I make a new Spirit block via {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, would Calamity-Boar X get exhausted? |No, it won't. Meanwhile, if the opposing Spirit that is going to block is refreshed, that Spirit will be exhausted. |- |31706 |When I destroyed the opposing Spirit via BP comparison after using {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, but there aren't any opposing Spirit for me to target attack next, what will happen? |Since there aren't any other Spirits for you to make them block, it will proceed to the "end of battle" timing like normal battles. |- |31707 |If the Spirit targeted by {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} to block can't be destroyed by BP comparison, what will happen? |Since the "when XXX destroyed" part of effect can't activate, it will proceed to the "end of battle" timing like normal battles. |- |31708 |If the Spirit targeted by {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} to block is destroyed by a Magic effect during the post-block Flash Timing, and I targeted the next opposing Spirit to block, what will happen? |After the Flash Timing is over, the battle-resolve timing is skipped, and it goes back to the block declaration timing. |- |31709 |If you target attacked an opposing Cost 3 Spirit via {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, that Spirit blocked, and entered depletion/destruction standby, can you target that Spirit in standby state to make it block with {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}? |No, you can't. You need to target the Spirit with the next lowest cost, and can't target the same Spirit. |- |31710 |If you made an opposing Cost 4 Spirit that is braved to a Cost 3 Brave block via {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} and destroyed it, and it is confirmed that the Brave would remain, can you target and attack the Brave that would remain next? |No, you can't. When you are targeting the next Spirit to attack via {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, the braved Brave isn't separated yet, so you can't target it. If a Brave has remained on the Field in Spirit-condition, and it is in fact the lowest cost Spirit on the Field after you battled with another Spirit via {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, you can target it and make it block, provided that there isn't any blocking restriction on the Brave like that of an Imagine Brave. |- |31711 |If a Spirit that is forced to block due {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} get destroyed, and the opponent would activate a Burst with the condition: {{Burst|con|After your Spirit is destroyed by the Opponent}}, when would that Burst resolve? |It would resolve after all (When Destroyed) effects, and any other effects related to that Spirit being destroyed are resolved, but before returning to the block declaration timing. |- |31712 |After an opposing Spirit is destroyed, if the opponent move all cores from the Spirit being targeted to block next by {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} to a Spirit summoned by Burst following the destroy, how will {{tk|Roaring Stampede}} proceed? |Since the Spirit targeted to block next is removed from the Field, it will proceed to the "end of battle" timing. |- |31713 |If the opponent controls no Spirits, and you attacked normally without attacking via Calamity-Boar X's {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}, but Calamity-Boar X is blocked by an opposing Spirit summoned afterwards, and that blocking Spirit get destroyed, can you activate {{tk|Roaring Stampede}}'s effect to force the Spirit with the next lowest cost to block? |Yes, when the blocking Spirit is depleted/destroyed, if there's any other opposing Spirit that can block, you must target them to make them block. |- |} == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

On Stage is a very convenient effect as it
On Stage.fullContent:
[[File:Noa1.png|thumb]]
'''On Stage''' (オンステージ, ''Onsutēji'') is an effect introduced in [[BSC16]]. This effect is made only for the "[[Diva]]" family Spirit cards.

The effect reads: 
* '''On Stage''' (Your Attack Step) Instead of attacking with this Spirit, by returning this Spirit to the deckbottom, summon one "[[Stage Style]]" family "XX" from your Hand/Removed Zone, without paying the cost, and draw a card.

XX = Name of a certain Spirit/Ultimate.

On Stage is a very convenient effect as it allows the player to summon a high-cost Spirit very quickly, pushing the game in a quick progress. Furthermore, since it also summons Spirits from the opened zone, the player can still put out cards for other effects.

However, since the Grand Advent era, anti-free-summon effects were promoted, leading to On Stage become a much weaker effect.

== Trivia ==
* Only Divas in teams Shiny Hearts and Absolutes have this effect.
* Before [[BSC31]], Divas with the [[Stage Style]] family don't have this effect.

A Spirit having Team is counted as having a printed effect. Spellsong.fullContent:
[[File:Rias Urovorun.png|thumb|322x322px]]
'''Spellsong''' (''呪歌'', ''Juuka'') is a Yellow keyword, possessed only by[[［Fleeting Dark Princess］Rias Urovorun]]. The keyword is based on [[Spellbind]], the keyword of Rias-Urovorun's motif, [[The DragonTwelveGodKing Ourovorius]]. It reads:
* '''Spellsong''' - (Opponent's Turn) While you have a {{tk|Song}} Magic card on your Field, at the start of each Step of your opponent's turn, return one opposing Spirit with equal or less BP than this Spirit to the bottom of the deck.
While Spellsong offers deck bouncing instead of Spellbind's core removal, both effects share the characteristic of activation at the start of each of the opponent's steps.

Although somewhat hindered by Rias-Urovorun's mediocre BP, Spellsong is a very powerful effect capable of both clearing the opponent's Field of many Spirits and limiting the opponent's resources.

When used correctly, Spellsong can perform a complete lockdown to the opponent, especially with the help of Nexus, [[The Nocturne Twilight Gothic Stage]]. When at Lv2, the Nexus can add 2000 BP more to Rias-Urovorun for each Song magic on field.

However, a weakness of Spellsong is that it can only target Spirits. Ultimates are still completely unaffected. Furthermore, a Song magic is required to be on the user's field. Although it is rare for a Song magic to be removed from field, it still posts a small threat to Spellsong.

Although not a significant ability, Solo Part can prove to be useful in many parts, especially when facing Red,
Solo Part.fullContent:
[[File:BSC23-X03_500.jpg|thumb|322x322px]]
'''Solo Part''' (''ソロパート'', ''Soro Paato'') is a Yellow keyword, appearing exclusively in [[BSC23]]. It is possessed only by "[[Diva]]" and "[[Stage Style]]" family Spirits. The keyword reads:
* '''Solo Part -''' While [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]](Soul Core) is on this spirit, all your "[Name]" Spirits cannot be destroyed by opposing effects. 
Although not a significant ability, Solo Part can prove to be useful in many parts, especially when facing Red, Blue, or even Yellow itself. Solo Part is also especially important as there is almost no effects that protect Stage Style Spirits among the Diva cards.

However, a big disadvantage of Solo Part is that it only prevents destruction, meaning depletion from Purple, or returning to hand/deck by White are still effective to the Divas. Furthermore, Solo Part requires Soul Core to be on a specific Spirit, limiting the user from Soul Core usage. Luckily, there are still a few cards that support Solo Part.

Solo Part can also be an indirect way to promote decks with a single Diva character, as the ability only targets Divas with the same name.

Derived from Solo Part, there are also [[Duet Part]] and [[CoZ12 Part]].

Appeal.fullContent:
[[File:Akari.png|thumb|321x321px]]
'''Appeal''' (アピール) is a keyword introduced in [[SD50]] and [[BSC35]], exclusive to Coord-named Spirits, as an Appeal consists of bringing forth the full radiance of the Coord they wear and entrancing the audience. The keyword's text can be found in the following format:
# '''Appeal -''' (When Attacks) By sending [[Soul Core]] from this Spirit to the Trash, [effect].
# '''Appeal -''' (When Attacks) [condition], you can send Soul Core from this Spirit to the Trash, When you've done so, [effect].
# Flash '''Appeal -''' (When Attacks) [condition], you can send Soul Core from this Spirit to the Trash, When you've done so, [effect].
In-universe, Appeals are techniques which an idol can use multiple times, which is represented in-game by needing Soul Core to be sent to the Trash for them to activate it and, as the Appeal depends on the Coord, as each Coord is different, so are the effects of the Appeals.

As Soul Core is frequently sent to Trash, a deck focused on Appeal can also uses additional cards that can retrieve Soul Core from Trash, such as [[The GroundDeityBlade Ootenta]] and [[［Star Fest］Sandy-Z-Leonora]].  [[［Star Fest］Rize Chromwell]] also enables the deck greatly by changing the activation condition to paying one cost. The downside of Soul Core reliance is, as it was when the gimmick was introduced in Burning Legend, the limited use of effects and the inability to make use of defensive magic such as [[Diamond Wall]].

Bushido.fullContent:
[[File:CB16-045.png|thumb]] '''Bushido''' (武士道) is a keyword introduced in [[CB16]]. Literally meaning "they way of warrior", it is a moral code concerning samurai attitudes, behavior and lifestyle. It is an ideology upheld by [[Graham Aker]], the main antagonist in the Gundam 00 series. The keyword is worded as below: * '''Bushido''' (Start of Your Attack Step) You can compare the BP of this Spirit and an opposing Spirit. Destroy the Spirit(s) with the same or lower BP, and when only the opposing Spirit is destroyed, activate the following effect:
█ ''[additional effect]'' While having the exact same procedure as [[Showdown]], Bushido also allows the user to choose their own target. Activating at the start of the Attack Step means that no attacks are needed to clear off some of the opposing Spirits, allowing a better set up or more stalling chances. The keyword also fully reflects on Graham Aker's personality, who is constantly seeking for challenges. == Q&A == {| class="article-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |3 |When comparing BP through '''Bushido''', do (When Attacks) or (When Blocks) effect activate? |No, they do not. Activating '''Bushido''' does not start a battle. |- |4 |When a Spirit is destroyed through '''Bushido''', is it counted as destroyed by effects or through BP comparison? |It is destroyed through BP comparison, so effects that trigger upon destroyed by effects do not activate. |- |5 |'''Bushido''' targets an opposing Spirit with the effect "cannot be destroyed by opposing effects", does that Spirit get destroyed if it has the same or lower BP as the comparing Spirit? |Yes, it is destroyed. |} == Also See: == * [[:Category:Bushido|List of cards with Bushido]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

'''Top Gun''' (トップガン) is a keyword introduced in [[CB16]]. Assemble.fullContent:
[[File:CB19-002.png|thumb]] '''Assemble''' ({{ruby|集|しゅう}}{{ruby|結|けつ}}；''shuugetsu'') is a keyword introduced in [[CB19]], possessed exclusively by "[[Showa]]" family Spirits of the Kamen Rider franchise. The effect is worded as follows: *'''Assemble: X''' - (When Summoned)
You can reveal X cards from your decktop. Among them, summon any number of "Showa" family cards without paying the cost. Return any remaining cards to the deckbottom. '''Assemble''' can only be used once per turn. Later, as a promo card for the Battle Spirits Kamen Rider Perfect Guide Book 2, a [[Kamen Rider Ichigou & New Cyclone|X-Rare Kamen Rider Ichigou]] is introduced with a new variant of Assemble. The effect is worded as follows: * '''Assemble: X (Kamen) ''' - (When Summoned/Attacks)
(Once per Turn: Assemble) You can reveal two cards from your decktop. Summon any number of "Kamen" family cards among them, without paying the cost. Return the remaining cards to the deckbottom. The scope of the cards can be summoned via the effect is extended to any "[[Kamen]]" family cards, and it is also the first time the timing of the effect covers (When Attacks). Similar to many keywords in the past, Assemble is another one that can summon cards from the top of the deck. However, with the lesson learnt from the meta dominated by [[Mealtiply]], Assemble is designed to be only once per turn, regardless of the number of copies of the card. Furthermore, the Spirit with Assemble with the lowest cost is four, avoiding the player to build up a board in the first turn, even when starting second. The name "Assemble" most likely references a trend in the Kamen Rider series back in the Showa era, where each Kamen Rider would often be gaining assistance from older or newer Kamen Riders in their own series, acting like a kind of collaboration among each other. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Assemble|Cards with Assemble]] * [[:Category:Assemble support|Cards supporting Assemble]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

A.T. Field.fullContent:
[[file:SD62-TX01.png|thumb]] '''A.T. Field''' (A.T.フィールド) is a keyword introduced in [[SD62]] and [[CB21]], basing on an ability unique to the Evangelion series. The effect is worded as follows: *'''A.T. Field''' - ''(Timing)''
This [[Spirit]] (or [[Nexus]]) is unaffected by opposing effects except those of the opposing Spirit with [[Soul Core]] on it. Currently, the timing for this effect usually activates at (When Attacks/Blocks). In some cases, it activates during (Your Turn). Unique to other kinds of immunity effects, A.T. Field is especially strong against [[Magic]] and [[Mirage]] effects, as these effects cannot have Soul Core on them. Some [[Burst]] effects may also struggle facing A.T. Field, since some Burst effects proceed before the cards can be summoned/deployed, ridding of the chances to put the Soul Core onto the card. In order to support this keyword further, SD62 and CB21 also introduce a large amount of effects which can treat the Spirits as having Soul Core on them, so that the players can still use the Soul Core effectively while keeping up the A.T. Field. "A.T. Field" is the abbreviation of Absolute Terror Field. In-universe, it is a barrier which both [[Angel|Angels]] and Evangelions can generate to protect themselves. It is also revealed that every living being that has a soul possesses an A.T. Field (just that the Angels and Evangelions are powerful enough to make the force apparent), explaining the representation of Soul Core in the game. == See Also: == * [[:Category:A.T. Show Up.fullContent:
[[file:BSC39-X02.png|thumb]] '''Show Up''' (ショーアップ) is a keyword introduced in [[BSC39]], exclusive to the "[[Diva]]" family cards. As the name applies, it represents the Divas turning up to an event as idols. The effect is worded as follows: *{{tk|Show Up}} {[[Stage Style]] & "''[name]''"}'''
By not attacking with this Spirit and returning it to the Hand, summon a target card from your Hand, without paying the cost.''' While there is already [[On Stage]], Show Up has the difference of returning the activating Spirit to the Hand, giving the player another chance to use Show Up again by summoning the same card. This allows the deck to be perfectly functioning with high cost cards while relying on only a few low cost cards. Any Divas that have both cards with On Stage and cards with Show Up also benefit from having more easy ways to summon the higher cost cards. Unlike [[Digivolution]], Show Up can be activated anytime outside of battle during the Attack Step; and unlike [[Super Digivolution]], an attack declaration isn't needed to activate Show Up, hence avoiding battles. A rule to note is that if the Spirit with Show Up is unable to attack, such as being exhausted, or under the effect of [[King's Command]], it can't activate Show Up. A tip to know is that since the effect doesn't specify a card type, Ultimates can also be summoned via Show Up. == Trivia == * Show Up is the first effect to use the () bracket in the original Japanese text. == See Also == * [[:Category:Show Up|List of cards with Show Up]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

In the show, "funnels" are essentially funnel-shaped drone units t
Funnel.fullContent:
[[file:CB25-X01.png|thumb]] '''Funnel''' (ファンネル) is a keyword introduced in [[CB25]]. The keyword is worded as follows: *Flash - '''Funnel: X''' (Either Attack Step)
Once per turn, destroy any number of opposing Spirits up to a total of X BP. Also, by paying one cost, (extra effect) The effect is currently exclusive to the [[NZ]] family cards (and hence [[Red]] cards), representing the Funnel technology used in the units. In the show, "funnels" are essentially funnel-shaped drone units that are designed to be remotely controlled by a Newtype pilot with great precision, allowing them to remotely attack an enemy from all directions. This is represented by the freedom of destroying any number of opposing Spirits up to a maximum amount of BP, and how that the effect can be used during Either Attack Step at ease, for both attack and defense. Since the funnels have to be recharged after use, the effect is also limited to "once per turn". While the technology is applied on different units, the actual design and function vary, as represented by the different additional effects player can obtain via paying one cost with the effect. Game-wise, it is a rare keyword that allows [[Red]] cards to defend on the opposing turn. While this requires the Spirit to remain on Field until Flash Timing, it is still a very powerful defense mechanic as it doesn't require any cost (only if you pay one for the additional effect), and can interrupt the opponent's plan of advancing. Since the "once per turn" is not shared among the Spirits with Funnel, one can activate multiple Funnel effects in one turn, making the offensive/defensive power even stronger. To overcome the weakness of a limited BP amount of destroy and flash timing limited use, there are also supporting cards like [[Nanai Miguel]]. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Funnel|List of cards with Funnel]] * [[:Category:Funnel support|List of cards supporting Funnel]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Yata-no-Kagami.title: Yata-no-Kagami
Yata-no-Kagami.contentSample:
[[file:CB25-033.png|thumb]] '''Yata-no-Kagami''' (ヤタノカガミ) is a keyword introduced in [[CB25]]. The keyword is worded as follows: * '''Yata-no-Kagami'''
When this Spirit would become the target of an opposing Spirit/Nexus effect, this Spirit is unaffected by that effect. After that effect resolves, you can return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom. The effect is currently exclusive to [[Akatsuki［Oowashi Equipped］]] and [[Akatsuki［Shiranui Equipped］]], representing the Anti-beam Defensive R
Yata-no-Kagami.fullContent:
[[file:CB25-033.png|thumb]] '''Yata-no-Kagami''' (ヤタノカガミ) is a keyword introduced in [[CB25]]. The keyword is worded as follows: * '''Yata-no-Kagami'''
When this Spirit would become the target of an opposing Spirit/Nexus effect, this Spirit is unaffected by that effect. After that effect resolves, you can return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom. The effect is currently exclusive to [[Akatsuki［Oowashi Equipped］]] and [[Akatsuki［Shiranui Equipped］]], representing the Anti-beam Defensive Reflection System with the same name used by the units in the show, MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM: SEED DESTINY. The name, Yata-no-Kagami (ヤタノカガミ), comes from '''八咫鏡''', a sacred bronze mirror that is part of the Imperial Regalia of Japan, and one of the "three sacred treasures" of the royal family said to be inherited from the heavens. In the show, the system, essentially the golden armor covering the unit and all its armaments, can protects against incoming beams by deflecting the beam fire, while tracking the enemies and automatically redirecting those beams back at them. It is represented by how a Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' would become unaffected by an effect that targets it, and can counter by returning the Spirit (unit) that launched such an attack (effect) to the deckbottom. As for its weakness, the armor doesn't provide protection for melee attacks, which is also reflected in the effect that it doesn't provide any protection against BP comparison under normal battle. Game-wise, it works like [[The SteelPaladin Stefanos]]'s effect, and turns unaffected once being targeted. Together with its counter attack of returning spirits to deckbottom, it helps the Spirit remain on field easily, and makes the opponent think twice about effects that target every opposing Spirit, or removals that target the owner of Yata-no-Kagami. While being able to reflect even turn-lasting effects, the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' must be on field when such an effect is applied. It can't react to an already resolved effect and would hence be affected by such an effect if it is summoned after that effect applies. Since this is *not* changing targets, the "unaffected" part would still be vulnerable to "can't be prevented" effects, like [[Sazabi]]'s effect when braved to "Char". And in that case, you can't return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom as the Spirit itself is removed before proceeding to the "after this effect resolves" part of Yata-no-Kagami. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |1 |What is '''Yata-no-Kagami'''? |It is an effect where when a Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' becomes a target of an opposing Spirit/Nexus effect, the Spirit becomes unaffected to that effect, and after that effect resolves, subsequently returning an opposing Spirit to the bottom of the deck. |- |2 |When the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' is being targeted twice by an opposing Spirit/Nexus effect with two separate targeting timings, such as '''[[Rush]]''', or those with the wordings "then" or "after this effect resolves", can two opposing Spirits be returned to the bottom of the deck with '''Yata-no-Kagami'''? |No, only one Spirit can be returned to the bottom of the deck, as the "return to deck" effect only activates after all other effects resolve (due to the "after that effect resolves" wording). However, the "unaffected" part of the effect can activate twice. |- |3 |When the opponent activates a Spirit/Nexus effect that has a turn duration, such as "during this turn, give all opposing Spirits -1000 BP", can '''Yata-no-Kagami''' activate? |Yes, it can. The duration of the "unaffected" effect depends on the duration of the effect which targets the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''', meaning the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' will remain unaffected to the opposing effect for the turn. |- |4 |The opponent has already activated a Spirit/Nexus effect with turn duration, such as "during this turn, give all opposing Spirits -1000 BP". While that effect is already active, can '''Yata-no-Kagami''' activate? |No, '''Yata-no-Kagami''' cannot react against an effect that is already active. |- |5 |When the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' is targeted by the '''[[Dragonshot]]''' of the opposing [[The ShootingStardragonArcher Lykeios]], and then '''Yata-no-Kagami''' activates, does the Spirit not get destroyed? |No, the Spirit will be destroyed. While it can become unaffected against opposing effects, "unaffected" effects by rule can't defend against opposing "opposing effects cannot prevent" effects. Also, since the Spirit is destroyed, the "after this effect resolves" part of '''Yata-no-Kagami''' will not activate. |- |6 |When the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' is targeted by the "When Summoned/Advents" effect of the opposing [[Freedom Gundam]], can '''Yata-no-Kagami''' activate? |Yes, it can, as '''Yata-no-Kagami''' activates before Freedom Gundam's effect does. The Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' will become unaffected, and its effects unable to be negated. |- |7 |When an opposing Spirit/Nexus effect activates, originally the effect targets the Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''', but then the target is changed, for example via the effect of [[Forbidden Gundam]]. In this case, can '''Yata-no-Kagami''' activate? |No, it cannot, as the target has moved onto another Spirit, and hence the condition of "when this Spirit would become the target" is never fulfilled. |- |8 |While an opposing Spirit braved to [[Suletta Mercury ［GUND-ARM, Inc.］]]is attacking, and the effect of "unless the opponent returns a LV1 Spirit they control to the Hand, they can't block" is active, can you return your LV1 Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''' to hand and then choose another Spirit to block? |Yes, you can do that. '''Yata-no-Kagami''' does not react against attacking effects which do not have activation duration specified. Effects with the wordings "during this battle" or "during this turn" are examples of effects with activation duration. |- |9 |When an opposing effects with two parts connected by "After this effect resolves" targeted your Spirit with '''Yata-no-Kagami''', which part would go first, the "After this effect resolves" part of the opposing effect, or the "After that effect resolves, you can return an opposing Spirit to the deckbottom" of '''Yata-no-Kagami'''? |The "after this effect resolves" part of the '''opposing effect'''. And the "after this effect resolves" part of '''Yata-no-Kagami''' only resolve after '''all''' effects derived from the "after this effect resolves" part of the '''opposing effect'''. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Yata-no-Kagami|List of cards with Yata-no-Kagami]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Quantum Burst.fullContent:
[[file:CB29-X07-SCR.png|thumb]] '''Quantum Burst''' (クアンタムバースト) is a keyword introduced in [[CB29]]. The keyword is worded as follows: * {{tk|During OC & During Advent}} '''[LV1][LV2] {{tk|Quantum Burst}} (When Attacks)'''
You can discard 25 cards from your decktop. When you've done so, return both players' Hand to the deckbottom. The effect is currently exclusive to [[00 Qan［T］]]. It refers to the maximum output mode of the Quantum System installed in [[00 Qan［T］]] in the original show, ''Mobile Suit Gundam 00 The Movie: Awakening of the Trailblazer''. It deploys a high-density GN Particles field that exceeds the one produced by the [[Trans-Am]] system. The major purpose of such system is to connect the thoughts of everyone within the field by unifying their consciousness through the Innovator’s Quantum Brainwaves. It helps Celestial Being, and in essence humans, to successfully establish a bridge of communication with the alien lifeform, [[ELS]], in the show. The form of [[00 Qan［T］]] when activating Quantum Burst is depicted in its parallel art. Game-wise, it is an ability that surpasses that of [[Trans-Am Raiser]] and [[00 Raiser]]'s effect, sending both players' Hand to the deckbottom instead of the Removed Zone, representing the superior spec of the mode in the show. While the "25 card" condition is slightly harsh, the sending-hand-to-bottom effect seals off any defense and removal from the opponent that can't be seen (Hand being undisclosed info), and minimizes the possibility of any counter attack even if the opponent somehow survives the turn. Just like how Tieria supports [[00 Qan［T］]] in achieving the Quantum Burst mode in the show, the 25 cards requirement can be relieved by [[Tieria Erde ［Veda］]]'s effect. When using the effect, it is important to note that since it is a "when you've done so" effect, you '''must''' be able to discard 25 cards from your deck for the "send Hand to deckbottom" effect to proc. If your deck can't be discarded from, or there are only 24 cards in your deck, the second part won't work. On the other hand, even if you can't send the entire opposing Hand to the deckbottom since their Hand are unaffected by your effects, you can still activate the own deck destruction part of the effect. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Quantum Burst|List of cards with Quantum Burst]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

RioRia Blast.fullContent:
[[file:BSC46-RV009.png|thumb]] '''RioRia Blast''' (リオリア砲；''rioriahou'') is a keyword introduced in [[BSC46]], currently only possessed by the Revival version of [[［School Band］Riolu Tida (Vo/Gt)]]. The wording is as below: * '''[LV1][LV2][LV3] {{tk|RioRia Blast}} (When Attacks)'''
You can reveal two cards from your decktop. Among them, you can summon a "[[Diva]]" family "Riolu"/"Rias" without paying the cost. Add any remaining cards to the Hand. From the name and design, {{tk|RioRia Blast}} is a modified version of {{tk|Resonance Blast}}, the ability owned by the original version of [[［School Band］Riolu Tida (Vo/Gt)]]. The summon targets are changed from the [[SD58|School Band]] members with designated instrument parts to "[[Diva]]" family "Rio" and "Rias", which primarily refer to "Riolu Tida" and "Rias Urovorun", representing the bond of the two. When compared to {{tk|Resonance Blast}}, which discards the remaining card when not summoned, {{tk|RioRia Blast}} adds the cards to the Hand regardless of what the cards are, making it closer to [[Bombardment]], the ability exclusively owned by [[The TigerTwelveGodKing Revol-Tiger]], the motif of Riolu-Tida, meaning that it is at the very least a draw-two. In terms of actual use, the ability fits the Riolu-Rias deck introduced from before, and further solidified since [[BSC40]] with [[［Together Forever］Rias Urovorun]]. While it loses the synergy with the other School Band members, it goes along better with the Riolu-Rias deck (considering the summon targets/revealing deck part) and offered the deck a new option. [[file:BSC40-CX02.png|200px]] On School Band side, while it is now summoning only Riolu herself and potentially [[［School Band］Rias Urovorun (Ba)]], the attack effect in general becomes a draw-two instead of "summon or nothing". Despite so, while unrelated to the keyword itself, losing the life burn on LV2 makes it an inferior option to the original one in the School Band deck. == See Also: == * [[:Category:RioRia Blast|List of cards with RioRia Blast]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

You can send a core from this Spirit to the Trash. When you've done so, '''[Effect]'''. Most {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} also has an additional ef
Starlight Appeal.fullContent:
[[File:PB44-X02.png|thumb]] '''Starlight Appeal''' (スターライトアピール) is a keyword introduced in [[PB44]], which is a collaboration premium box with the Aikatsu series, and currently exist exclusively in that set. The effect can be worded in several patterns, but generally the common structure includes the following: * {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} '''(Timing)'''
You can send a core from this Spirit to the Trash. When you've done so, '''[Effect]'''. Most {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} also has an additional effect before sending the core to the Trash. While most of them can activate the "send core to Trash" effect and its subsequent effects without conditions, some do follow a specific timing, such as that of the Revival version of [[［King Leo Coord］Shibuki Ran]], in which the "send core to Trash" effect activates as an interruptive effect. With the effect being worded as "sending a core" instead of "paying one cost", it allows the effect to bypass effects which disallow the player from paying costs, and is only subject to core lock. However, the bigger reason is probably just because that the keyword's predecessor, {{tk|Appeal}}, is worded the same way, but instead of sending any core, it sends the Soul Core specifically. {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} has changed to sending any core to adapt to the play style changing to relying on the Soul Core for {{tk|Contract Advent}}. It is worth noting that {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} is '''not''' treated as {{tk|Appeal}} or other "Appeal"-named effects. {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} does not exist as a term in the Aikatsu series. The term is mostly introduced to differentiate itself from the other "Appeal"-named effects in the Battle Spirits card game. However, as a fun fact, all characters possessing {{tk|Starlight Appeal}} is currently studying in, or graduated from, the [[Starlight Academy|'''Starlight''' Academy]], a main location in the Aikatsu series. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Starlight Appeal|Cards with Starlight Appeal]] {{Keywords Nav}}

Ringing Charge.fullContent:
[[File:26RDB01-043.png|thumb|200px]] '''Ringing Charge''' (響走; ''kyou-sou'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RDB01]], the first Diva booster set of the Standard Format, and is exclusive to [[［Horse Origin］Formulia Execeeda]] and [[［Rooster Origin］Gail Fenique]], the two core members of {{tk|Double Vivid}}. Its general wording reads as follows: * '''[LVX]''' {{RC|"[Name]"}} {{ST|During Attack}}
At the end of battle, you can target one of your "[Name]". Refresh it. You can only use {{tk|Ringing Charge}} once per turn. An actual example from [[［Rooster Origin］Gail Fenique]] would be: * '''[LV2]''' {{ST|True Release}} {{RC|"Formulia Execeeda"}} {{ST|During Attack}}
At the end of battle, you can target one of your "Formulia Execeeda". Refresh it. You can only use {{tk|Ringing Charge}} once per turn. The name itself is most probably a tweak on "競走", which has the same pronunciation and means "race" in itself. It is also a reference to {{tk|Furious Charge}} ("走破"), the signature keyword giving to [[Ten Crown]] and [[God-King]] Spirits by [[The HorseTwelveGodKing Execeed]], half the motif of Formulia Execeeda. The effect content, however, concerns "refreshing another Spirit", and is based on the in-lore relationship between two Spirits, which, in this case, refers to Formulia and Gail. While the effect reads simple and the name restriction is strict, considering how refreshing a Spirit means it can be used to launch a new attack, or saved for blocker next turn, it is indeed a powerful effect, particularly in Standard Format, where removal is not as fierce and the setting up of blocker for defense is important. Regarding the benefit of making an extra attack, it also means any {{ST|When Attacks}} effect that has no turn restriction can be triggered multiple times, like [[［Rooster Origin］Gail Fenique|Gail]]'s LV1-2 effect. It is to note that since one can only use {{tk|Ringing Charge}} once per turn, even if you control both Formulia and Gail, only one of them can activate {{tk|Ringing Charge}} to refresh the other one. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Level Up|List of cards with Ringing Charge]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{tk|Soul Awaken}} {{ST|When Attacks}}
You can send the [[File:Stan Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Field/Trash to this Spirit. If you've done so, refresh this Spirit. You can only use {{tk|Soul Awa
Soul Awaken.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS03-X03.png|thumb|200px]] '''Soul Awaken''' (ソウル覚醒; ''souru-kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS03]], currently exclusive to [[The PurgatoryPhoenix Zekuga]], the key Spirit of [[Ku Bashin]] in the anime [[Battle Spirits (Re): Zekkai no Ku]]. The effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{tk|Soul Awaken}} {{ST|When Attacks}}
You can send the [[File:Stan Soul Core.png|20px]] from your Field/Trash to this Spirit. If you've done so, refresh this Spirit. You can only use {{tk|Soul Awaken}} once per turn. As the name implied, it was a modified version of {{tk|Awaken}}, which focused on moving own cores around, but concerning "Soul Core" in particular this time. While the normal {{tk|Awaken}} concerned only moving cores from the Field, {{tk|Soul Awaken}} could also move the Soul Core from the Trash. In addition, it was not a Flash effect. The two differences made the outcome very different from how one would make use of {{tk|Awaken}}. Being a (When Attacks) effect, players can activate it without needing to worry that it would get interrupted by the opponent during their Flash Timing, unlike {{tk|Awaken}}, if it was to be used during Attack Step. As for the main part of the effect, it allowed players to take back their used Soul Core from the Trash, which had multiple uses in Standard Format, including paying for the cost of Magic cards via [[Soul Magic]], or placing on Spirits to unlock their True Release status. [[The PurgatoryPhoenix Zekuga]] itself, for example, had True Release. By sending the Soul Core to him, it would automatically become LV2, with 11000 BP, and its LV2 effect unlocked, even if you attacked with only one core on Zekuga. Besides, the deck with Zekuga as ace, the [[Purgatory Wings]] deck, came with a lot of effects that went with extra benefits if Soul Core was used to pay the cost, or if Soul Core was in Trash when using the effect. Being an effect that could retrieve the Soul Core from Trash, {{tk|Soul Awaken}} effectively covered the weakness of not having the Soul Core ready for counter measures after using such other effects in the deck which required Soul Core, while also providing another chance for you to pay cost with Soul Core again for those effects. On top of all the benefits about returning the Soul Core, the effect was in fact also a self-refreshing effect. It was simple yet very effective by making Zekuga capable of attacking for another time, or stay refreshed for defence. When combined with Zekuga's level 2 effect, this essentially meant Zekuga could deal three life damages alone. It was to note that, however, with all merits mentioned above, the effect was restricted to once per turn per entire effect. Hence, even if you control multiple copies of Zekuga, you can only activate one of their {{tk|Soul Awaken}}. Interestingly, the effect in itself was a lot similar to {{tk|Twinkle Awaken}} from Eternal. The major difference, however, was that {{tk|Twinkle Awaken}} was a Flash effect. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31869 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Soul Awaken}}? |It is an effect that allows you to send the Soul Core from your Field/Trash to the Spirit owning the effect. If you did so, you can refresh that Spirit. And regardless of the card names of the Spirits owning such effect, {{tk|Soul Awaken}} could only be used once per turn even if you control multiple Spirits with {{tk|Soul Awaken}}. {{tk|Soul Awaken}} is also not treated as {{tk|Awaken}}. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Soul Awaken|List of cards with Soul Awaken]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

You can send out on
Fish Troop.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS03-X07.png|thumb|200px]] '''Fish Troop''' (魚軍; ''gyo-gun'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS03]], currently possessed exclusively by [[The AberrantWhale DeepCaesar]]. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * '''[Level]''' {{FT|X}}{{ST|Timing}}
You can send out X of your "Swordish" Tokens. You can only use this effect of the same card name once per turn. An actual example from DeepCaesar reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{FT|1}}{{ST|When Summoned}}
You can send out one of your "Swordish" Tokens. You can only use this effect of the same card name once per turn. As the name implied, the effect was about calling out an army of fishes, which in this context, referring to sending out various [[Swordish]] Tokens. While the effect itself was simple, it was undoubtedly powerful in Standard Format where the number of hit points one could create in a single turn was directly proportional to the killing power of the deck, as non-battle removal was rather limited. It was even more so when the extra hit point did not requiring using other resources like cards from the Hand to fuel it. In this case, generating Token Spirits out of nowhere was definitely a good example. In fact, when compared to other Token-generating method in the [[Abyssen]] deck, where [[Swordish]] and DeepCeasar was designed to work with, "card from Hand" was the common trigger for calling out extra [[Swordish]]. As of the time when the deck was released, {{tk|Fish Troop}} of DeepCaesar was the only other way to send out Tokens which did not require burning cards from Hand, apart from [[Swordish Comes]]. This further confirmed its significance in the relevant deck. While it is the general rule of [[Token Cards]], it is noteworthy that "sending out Tokens" did not equal to "summoning Spirits". Hence, any effect reacting to the summon of Spirits, or in turn, restricting the summon of Spirits, do not affect {{Tk|Fish Troop}}. Another point to note is, as {{tk|Fish Troop}} is once per turn per card name, you can activate {{tk|Fish Troop}} of a different card with a different card name in the same turn after using the first {{tk|Fish Troop}}. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31749 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Fish Troop}}? |It is an effect that allows you to send out X "[[Swordish]]" Tokens at a timing specified after {{FT|X}}. Even if you control multiple copies of a Spirit with the same card name that owns this effect, you can only use this effect once per turn. For other details, please refer to [[Token Cards]]. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Fish Troop|List of cards with Fish Troop]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

'''Clock Up''' (クロックアップ, ''Kurokku appu'') is a keyword introduced in [[CB09]], exclusive to the [[Kamen]] family. This effect is based on the actual ability own by the Riders from the Kabuto series, who could use such ability to speed up to light speed to battle their enemies, the Worms. Within the universe, one can only match the speed if they also activate clock up, or own special abilities like the Worms, which is well-reflected in the effect. All cards with the '''Clock Up''' ability have the following text:

* '''Clock Up -''' (When Attacks) By sending [[File:Soul Core.png|20px]] from this Spirit to the Reserve, this Spirit can only be blocked by opposing Spirits with "Clock Up"-named effects.


This ability is not limited to a color and made exclusively for the [[Kamen]] family Spirits from the Kabuto series. Examples of cards with this ability include [[Kamen Rider Sasword Rider Form]], [[Kamen Rider Kabuto Rider Form]], [[Kamen Rider Drake Rider Form]], and so on. With the way it is worded, Spirits that activated '''Clock Up''' can't be blocked by Ultimates at all. 


An upgrade version of the ability in the show, allowing the user to travel even through time, [[Hyper Clock Up]], is also an upgraded version of the effect in game, adding limitations to the opponent's use of Flash effect on top of the unblockable effect.
