Hyper Clock Up.fullContent:
[[File:HyperKabuto.png|thumb|318x318px]]
'''Hyper Clock Up''' (ハイパークロックアップ) is a keyword introduced in [[CB09]], and is an upgraded version of [[Clock Up]]. The keyword's text reads:

* '''Hyper Clock Up -''' (When Attacks/Blocks) This Spirit can't be blocked. Also, if the opponent would use a Flash effect, they can't use it unless they pay three extra costs.

As an upgrade version of [[Clock Up]] in the show, Kamen Rider Kabuto, Hyper Clock Up enables the user to accelerate to a speed that alters even time. The user can move at a speed that is n times faster than that obtained by [[Clock Up]], and travel to the past or the future as he wants. 

While Spirits with [[Clock Up]] could still be blocked by opposing Spirits with [[Clock Up]], Hyper Clock Up not only is completely unblockable, but also limits the opponent's Flash responses. Be it Magic, Advent, Change, Accel or a '''Burst's Flash effect''', an additional three core must be paid before it can be used, forcing the opponent to use resources they'd rather spare, or completely locking them out of using Flash. Different from similar effects that target the "use" of cards or effects, Hyper Clock Up adopts the 使う wording, which targets both the "use" and "activate" actions in the game. Hence, even if it is "activating" a Flash effect, the owner would have to pay three extra costs. Additionally, since Hyper Clock Up '''targets the player''', so it isn't stopped by "Your Hand is unaffected" effects. 

== Q&A ==
{| class="fandom-table"
|+
!No.
!'''Question'''
!'''Answer'''
|-
|1
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, when the opponent uses a Flash effect, when do they actually pay the extra cost?
|They pay when they declare the use of Flash effect.
|-
|2
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, the opponent paid the three extra costs to use a Flash effect. Within the Flash effect, there is a cost-paying effect like "pay one cost to summon". Do they also have to pay three extra costs for that?
|No, they do not.
|-
|3
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, the opponent attempts to activate a Flash effect from a Spirit unaffected by {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}}, or a Grandwalker Nexus. Do they have to pay three extra costs?
|Yes, they do. {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} targets the player instead of the cards.
|-
|4
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, the opponent attempts to activate a Flash effect from hand while their Hand is unaffected by effects. Do they have to pay three extra costs?
|Yes, they do. {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} targets the player instead of the cards.
|-
|5
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, the opponent activates a Magic card Burst, and after activating the Burst effect, they attempt to pay the cost to activate the Flash effect as well. Do they have to pay three extra costs?
|Yes, they do. {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} targets the player instead of the cards.
|-
|6
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, the opponent attempts to activate a Flash effect of {{gs|2}} of a Grandwalker Nexus. Including the three extra costs, do they send a total of five cores to the Void?
|No, they send two cores from the Grandwalker Nexus to the Void, and send three cores from their Field/Reserve to the Trash.
|-
|7
|While {{tk|Hyper Clock Up}} is active, the opponent attempts to activate a LV2 Flash effect of a LV2 Spirit. After they pay the three extra costs, the Spirit would be reduced to LV1 or depleted. In this case, does the Flash effect activate?
|No, it does not. If the three extra costs cannot be paid while maintaining the Spirit at LV2, then the Flash effect itself cannot be declared. If cores are already moved, return them to their original placements.
|}

Target one of your Spirits. Put any number of cores from it to this Spirit. If core is put during Your Attack Step, during this turn
Re Awaken.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS03-X02.png|thumb|200px]] '''Re Awaken''' (Re覚醒; ''aru-i-kakusei'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS03]], currently exclusive to [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried (26RBS03-X02)]], the standard format version of first X-Rare in the game. The effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{tk|Re Awaken}}{{ST|Either Attack Step}} {{Invoke|Flash}} {{ST|Once Per Turn}}
Target one of your Spirits. Put any number of cores from it to this Spirit. If core is put during Your Attack Step, during this turn, give all your "[[Red Cloud]]" family Spirits +1000 BP. As the name implied, it was a modified version of {{tk|Awaken}}, an effect owned by the original [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried]] in Eternal. The name, "Re", fits the name of the new anime to be released for the game in the same year, [[Battle Spirits (Re): Zekkai no Ku]], and the overall "reboot" theme of Standard format. Unlike {{tk|Awaken}} which allows players to gather cores from various Spirits onto a single Spirit, {{tk|Re Awaken}} only allows player to send cores from one Spirit to the owner of {{tk|Re Awaken}}. The effect is also limited to once per turn. However, it is no less powerful in Standard when True Release is an important thing of the game plan. {{tk|Re Awaken}} allows players to reallocate their Soul Core to Siegfried, which essentially creates a situation where player can own "two" Spirits in True Release state during Attack Step. For Siegfried in particular, just by sending a Soul Core to him would make him a 10000 BP Spirit with a when destroyed effect that increases life. Regardless of the restrictions imposed, all the original merits of {{tk|Awaken}} are also retained. This includes the flexibility to avoid destruction of own Spirits via BP comparison, and the mental pressure it gives the opponent for a sudden pump of BP. In addition, when compared to the original {{tk|Awaken}}, {{tk|Re Awaken}} also comes with an original line of "give all your "[[Red Cloud]]" family Spirits +1000 BP". As BP line has been very important in the Standard format, the turn-lasting BP pump could bring significant changes to the battle. In general, while it is more or less a simple keyword, the effect is surpsingly solid in the Standard format. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31868 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Re Awaken}}? |It is an effect that allows you to target one of your Spirits, and send any number of cores from it to the Spirit with {{tk|Re Awaken}}. If core is put during Your Attack Step, during this turn, all your "[[Red Cloud]]" family Spirits gain +1000 BP. {{tk|Re Awaken}} is not treated as {{tk|Awaken}}. |} == Trivia == * It is the first Standard-original keyword for [[Red]], a matching description for that [[The DragonEmperor Siegfried]] was the first X-Rare in the game. == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Re Awaken|List of cards with Re Awaken]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Buddy.fullContent:
[[File:CB26-CX01.png|thumb]] == Introduction == '''Buddy''' (バディ) is a special ability that debut in [[CB26]], and primarily owned by the Contract Spirits in the set. The effect name and the effect itself is a reference to the Buddy system in the show, '''Tiger & Bunny''', and the system refers to how two heroes with superpowers work together as partners. In game, the ability allows two Spirits to {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto '''the same Contract Spirit''', one on the left and one on the right, functioning like an [[Advent]] version of [[Imagine Brave]]. Contract Spirits with this effect have the following text: {{Buddy|"XXXX"/"YYYY"}}
You can {{tk|Contract Advent}} one of each target on the left and right of this card. This pre-advent card turns into refreshed state, and won't exhaust. (Including the cards that stacked, these cards can't be braved/advented on/switched in places with non-target cards.) "XXXX" and "YYYY" are specific names that are usually a part of the card name of the designated cards. Example: [[File:Buddy intro 1.jpg|600x400px]] ^ For [[Kaburagi T. Kotetsu & Barnaby Brooks Jr.]]'s case, you can {{tk|Contract Advent}} "WILD TIGER"-named and "BARNABY BROOKS Jr."-named Spirit cards, one of each, onto the left and right of the Contract card. While having the benefit of allowing two different Spirits to advent onto the same card, there are also restrictions coming with it so that the system doesn't get abused such as disabling {{tk|Change}}/Brave/further {{tk|Advent}} that doesn't contain the target names. You also can't advent the same Spirit on both sides unless the name of both cards contain both "XXXX" and "YYYY" in name. == Actual Procedure == [[File:Buddy intro 2.jpg|600x400px]] (1) When the target cards are advented onto the Contract Spirit, you stack the card onto '''one of the two sides''' of the Contract card. (If two are advented at the same time, you stack the two on the two sides simultaneously) (2) When you advent onto a Contract card with Buddy, the Contract Spirit '''turns into refreshed state''' regardless of whether it is attacking or not, and would not become exhausted again as long as it remains to be a pre-advent card. (3) When you declare an attack with a Spirit that Contract Advents on top a Contract Spirit with Buddy, only the Spirit on top is exhausted, and the Contract Spirit as a pre-advent card would remain refreshed. == Official Q & A == {| class="article-table" |+ !No. !Question !Answer |- |1 |What does "Buddy" do? |You can {{tk|Contract Advent}} up to two designated Spirit cards onto a Spirit with '''Buddy''', one on the left and one on the right, and the two Spirit cards that advent must include the names specified in the effect. The card with '''Buddy''' that has become a pre-advent card would always be in refreshed state. Also, concerning the pre-advent card with '''Buddy''', and any Spirits that advent on top, you can't brave/advent/switch them in places with cards that don't include the names specified in the effect. |- |2 |Can you {{tk|Contract Advent}} both a "WILD TIGER"-named card and a "BARNARBY BROOKS Jr."-named card onto a card with: {{Buddy|"WILD TIGER"/"BARNABY BROOKS Jr."}}? |Yes, you can. The two Spirits that {{tk|Contract Advent}} on top are treated as two separate Spirits, while the card with '''Buddy''' would serve as a pre-advent card for both Spirits, and both Spirits can activate the {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}} effects of that card. |- |3 |Can you {{tk|Contract Advent}} '''two''' "WILD TIGER"-named cards, which only hold one of the two names specified in the effect, onto a card with: {{Buddy|"WILD TIGER"/"BARNABY BROOKS Jr."}}? |No, you can't do so. You can only {{tk|Contract Advent}} a "BARNARBY BROOKS Jr."-named card next to a "WILD TIGER"-named card that is during Contract Advent. |- |4 |You can only {{tk|Contract Advent}} '''one''' "[[WILD TIGER & BARNABY BROOKS Jr.]]", which holds both of the names specified in the effect, onto a card with: {{Buddy|"WILD TIGER"/"BARNABY BROOKS Jr."}}? |No. Since a card that holds both of the names specified in the effect can fulfill the condition of '''Buddy''' with either part of the name, you can {{tk|Contract Advent}} two of such cards onto the card with '''Buddy'''. |- |5 |While only one Cost 5 "[[WILD TIGER]]" is during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on your Cost 3 "[[Kaburagi T. Kotetsu & Barnaby Brooks Jr.]], can you {{tk|Contract Advent}} a "[[WILD TIGER & BARNABY BROOKS Jr.]]" with an advent condition that specifies "Cost 5 or more" next to that "[[WILD TIGER]]"? |No, you can't. When you would {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto the side that is currently not being advented on, you could only reference the cost of the pre-advent card, "[[Kaburagi T. Kotetsu & Barnaby Brooks Jr.]]". |- |6 |If it's just one, can you [[advent]] a card without the specified card names onto a Spirit with '''Buddy''' that is currently not being advented on by any cards? |No, you can't. Also, if there is any pre-advent card with '''Buddy''' under your Spirit, you can only brave/advent/switch that Spirit in places with cards that include the names specified in the Buddy effect. |- |7 |When you would {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto a Spirit with '''Buddy''' that is currently not being advented on, do you stack the card perfectly on top of the Spirit like regular advents? |No, you don't. Even if you are adventing the first card onto the Spirit, choose left or right of the Spirit to advent the card onto. If the Spirit with '''Buddy''' is in exhausted state, the advented Spirit would be in exhausted state, while the pre-advent card with '''Buddy''' alone is turned into refreshed state. |- |8 |When you would {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto a Spirit with '''Buddy''' that is currently not being advented on, can you put additional cores on it? |No, you can't. Like regular advents, the newly advented card would inherit the cores originally on the Spirit with '''Buddy''' (which becomes the pre-advent card now). |- |9 |If only one Spirit is during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on a card with '''Buddy''', when you would {{tk|Contract Advent}} next to that Spirit, where do you put cores on it from? |When you would {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto a card with '''Buddy''' that is currently being {{tk|Contract Advent}} on by another Spirit, you can put cores from your Reserve/Field onto the newly advented card, like what you do when you {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto a card in Soul State. |- |10 |If only one Spirit is during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on a card with '''Buddy''', and only Soul Core is placed on it, can you deplete that Spirit to {{tk|Contract Advent}} a card next to it? |Yes, you can. The Spirit to be depleted and the Spirit to be advented are treated as separated Spirits despite being next to each other. |- |11 |If two Spirits are during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on a card with '''Buddy''', but one of the Spirits left the Field, can the pre-advent card with '''Buddy''' enter Soul State? |No, it can't. It must remain to act as the pre-advent card of the remaining Spirit. |- |12 |If two Spirits are during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on a card with '''Buddy''', for {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}} effects written on the card that has the "once per turn" clause, can the two Spirits on the left and on the right activate the effect once per turn respectively? |Yes, each of them can activate the effect once respectively. |- |13 |If two Spirits are during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on a card with '''Buddy''', for {{tk|Contract Pre-Advent}} effects written on the card that has the "(Once per Turn: Same Name)" clause, can the two Spirits on the left and on the right activate the effect once per turn respectively? |No, they can't. Effects with (Once per Turn: Same Name) can only be activated once by either one of them. |- |14 |Can you add pre-advent cards without the names specified in the ''Buddy'' effect via an effect to a Spirit with a pre-advent card with '''Buddy''' effect? |Yes, you can. In that case, to show clearly which Spirit you are adding the pre-advent card to, put the newly added pre-advent card under the card with '''Buddy''', and slide it to the side which the Spirit you are adding pre-advent cards to is on. (i.e. Left or Right) |- |15 |When you activate an effect that allows you to {{tk|Contract Advent}} two Spirits that the same time, if both the advent condition of the card and the '''Buddy''' condition are met, can you {{tk|Contract Advent}} two cards onto a Spirit with '''Buddy''', or two Spirits that are have a pre-advent card with '''Buddy''' at the same time? |Yes, you can. When you do, for the card that advents onto a Spirit that is during {{tk|Contract Advent}}, the cores are inherited; For the card that advents onto the card with '''Buddy''' that is currently in Soul State/pre-advent condition, you can put any number of cores onto it from your field/reserve; If you are adventing two cards at the same time onto a Spirit with '''Buddy''', '''split the cores''' on the Spirit to the two newly advented cards. In such case, if there's only one core on that Spirit with '''Buddy''', you '''can't''' {{tk|Contract Advent}} two cards that the same time. |- |16 |When facedown cards are placed under a Spirit with '''Buddy''' that is not being advented on via effects like [[Poison Blade]], if you {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto that Spirit, what happens to the facedown cards? |Move the cards underneath to the side that the Spirit {{tk|Contract Advent}} onto to show that the card are added to that Spirit. When you later advent another Spirit next to that Spirit, the cards under would not move. |- |17 |While you only have one Spirit during {{tk|Contract Advent}} on your card with '''Buddy''', the opponent activates an effect: "Neither player can advent." In that case, if your Hand is unaffected by opposing effects, can you {{tk|Contract Advent}} on your pre-advent card with '''Buddy'''? |Yes, you can. Since pre-advent cards are only affected by effects that target pre-advent cards, just like cards in Soul State, they are unaffected by opposing "can't advent" effects. |- |} == List of Cards with Buddy == [[:Category:Buddy|List of cards with Buddy]] == Navigation == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Chou Henshin.title: Chou Henshin
Chou Henshin.contentSample:
[[file:CB34-X03.png|thumb]] '''Chou Henshin''' (超変身) is a keyword introduced in [[CB34]], possessed exclusively by various forms of [[Kamen Rider Kuuga Mighty Form ［4］|Kuuga]]. The general form of effect is read as follows: '''Flash -''' {{CHen|Cost XXX}}
[''Effect YYY''.] After this effect resolves, either discard this card or or replace a [Condition] "Kuuga" without {{tk|Advent}} you control, including those in Soul State, in refreshed condition. The name of the effect comes from Kamen Ri
Chou Henshin.fullContent:
[[file:CB34-X03.png|thumb]] '''Chou Henshin''' (超変身) is a keyword introduced in [[CB34]], possessed exclusively by various forms of [[Kamen Rider Kuuga Mighty Form ［4］|Kuuga]]. The general form of effect is read as follows: '''Flash -''' {{CHen|Cost XXX}}
[''Effect YYY''.] After this effect resolves, either discard this card or or replace a [Condition] "Kuuga" without {{tk|Advent}} you control, including those in Soul State, in refreshed condition. The name of the effect comes from Kamen Rider Kuuga's line in the series, and is thus unique to Kuuga. Game-wise, the effect is in essence a modified version of {{tk|Change}}, which also corresponds to how Chou Henshin is more of a unique way of describing the form changes but the core elements are not that different from other riders in other shows. When compared to {{tk|Change}}, the major difference is that Chou Henshin also covers targets in Soul State. This makes it a cross-over version of {{tk|Change}} and {{tk|Contract Advent}}, with the former being able to switch with cards on the Field, and the latter being able to revive Contract Cards that went into Soul State by stacking on it and adding cores to it. Hence, the actual operation of the keyword in game also works like a combination of the two. When switching with a Spirit on the Field, it works exactly the same as {{tk|Change}}. When switching with a card in Soul State on the Field, it works as follows: 1) You declare and use the {{tk|Chou Henshin}} of a card. 2) Activate all effects related to {{tk|Chou Henshin}} being used (e.g. the effect written in the Chou Henshin effect like "destroy an opposing Spirit/Ultimate", and effects like "When you use {{tk|Chou Henshin}}, draw a card.) 3) At the timing of "after this effect resolves", target your Contract Card in Soul State that meets the condition to switch with the card that has its {{tk|Chou Henshin}} used. 4) Switch the card with {{tk|Chou Henshin}} with your Contract Card in Soul State. When you do, put any number of cores from your Field/Reserve to the switched card. 5) {{tk|Chou Henshin}} is completed, and you can proceed to resolve effects like "when switched via {{tk|Chou Henshin}} etc. While a major downside of {{tk|Change}} is that you have to keep a target alive on the Field to switch if you don't want to just discard the card, {{tk|Chou Henshin}} allows you to switch with cards in Soul State. This means that you can use {{tk|Chou Henshin}} to generate a body directly after your entire Field is removed and Contract Spirit entering Soul State, without the need to use another effect to summon a Spirit first. When compared to {{tk|Contract Advent}} that requires Soul Core, {{tk|Chou Henshin}} could "revive" your Contract Card without the need to use Soul Core, which can be saved for other things. On the other hand, when it is used to switch with your Contract Card, since the Contract Card will go ''back to your Hand'', it loses the merit of Contract Card staying on Field in Soul State, and unless you summon the Contract Card from the Hand again, you can't keep reviving the card. Switching with the Contract Card or not hence require a player's accurate judgment. In addition, since {{tk|Chou Henshin}} is a new keyword, it can't be supported by effects that support {{tk|Change}}, which exist in considerable amount throughout the years. As a fun fact, cards with {{tk|Chou Henshin}} come with no flavor text. This is probably due to how the effect was designed to be comparable to {{tk|Contract Advent}}, and cards with {{tk|Contract Advent}} in general come with no flavor text. == Cards with Chou Henshin == * [[:Category:Chou Henshin|List of cards with Chou Henshin]] * [[:Category:Chou Henshin support|List of Chou Henshin support cards]] == Related Articles == {{Keywords Nav}}

Camouflage.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS02-048.png|thumb|200px]] '''Camouflage''' (迷彩; ''mei-sai'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS02]], the second booster set of Standard Format. Cards with the effect are primarily [[White]]. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * '''[Level]''' {{Camou|X}}
When the opponent would target this Spirit with a Spirit effect, unless they pay X costs, they can't target it. An actual example will be [[The Disguiser Camouflan]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV2]''' {{ST|True Release}}{{Camou|3}}
When the opponent would target this Spirit with a Spirit effect, unless they pay three costs, they can't target it. As the name implies, it is an effect that allows the owner to ''escape'' from the targeting of opposing effects. It is the first keyword in Standard that provides immunity, or pseudo immunity in this case, to Spirits. However, different from {{tk|Armor}}, the first immunity keyword in Eternal, {{tk|Camouflage}} is not deflecting the effect completely, and has much more limitations that {{tk|Armor}}. One of the greatest limitations is that the opponent can still get their effects through if they pay the designated cost. As most of the {{tk|Camouflage}} were {{Camou|1}} when the keyword was first introduced, the opponent actually had good chances of surpassing that. However, it does not mean that the effect is meaningless, as the one core paid can be what could originally be used for the summon of another Spirit. This is even bigger a decision than one might assume when considering that a second Main Step exists in Standard. The extra cost paid might contribute significantly to a tempo loss, after all. Another major limitation is that it is limited to Spirit effects, while Nexus and Magic effects could still affect the owner. However, as the major removal comes from Spirits in Standard, the "Spirit-only" pseudo-immunity is still very much enough most of the time. A third limitation, also closely related to the difference in nature between Camouflage and Armor-type of effects, is that it only applies to effect that actually "targets" the Spirit, and does not protect the Spirit from effects that target ''all'' Spirits, like [[The EruptingThunder Palecoeurl]]'s, and effects from Eternal that does not contain the word, "target (指定)", like "''destroy'' an opposing 5000 BP or less Spirit". As such, it is clearly different from how Armor-type of effects work in Eternal. Instead of being unable to touch the Spirit once it owns the immunity like Armor, one could still remove or affect the owners of Camouflage via other means. This contributes to a much more balanced protection effect in an environment where removal is not particularly easy to begin with when the BP is high or cost is high, and slows down the need to introduce "can't be prevented" effects just to make it balanced. In spite of all the limitations above, one might still find that the keyword is stronger than what they expected in actual battles, as it disturbs the opponent's calculations, and forces the opponent to chose spending extra resources on removing your Spirits or let them stay. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31749 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Camouflage}}? |It is an effect that means, when the opponent would target a Spirit with {{tk|Camouflage}} via a Spirit effect, unless they pay X cost as specified by {{Camou|X}}, they can't target it. |- |31750 |When I activate an effect of my Spirit that reads "The opponent target one of their Spirits. Exhaust it", can the opponent target a Spirit they control with {{Camou|X}} without paying X extra costs? |Yes, that is possible. In this case, from the point of view of the opposing Spirit with {{tk|Camouflage}}, it is "you (the opponent)" who chooses the target, and {{tk|Camouflage}} won't proc. |- |31751 |When targeting an opposing Spirit with {{tk|Camouflage}} via a Spirit effect, if I pay the extra cost specified by {{tk|Camouflage}} from the Spirit which activated the targeting effect, depleting it in the process, can that targeting effect still be activated? |No, it can't be activated. The same applies if the activating effect is LV2 only, and paying the cost for {{tk|Camouflage}} would level down the Spirit activating the effect from LV2 to LV1. |- |31752 |If the opponent only controls one Spirit, and it has {{Camou|1}}, when I activate a Spirit effect that says, "Target an opposing Spirit", must I pay the one cost and target that Spirit? |No, you can choose to pay the one cost or not. If you choose not to pay, since you would not be able to target the Spirit with {{Camou|1}}, it is treated as the effect being activated but no valid target. |- |31753 |If there is a Spirit effect that affects "every opposing Spirit", and the range covers a Spirit with {{tk|Camouflage}}, must I pay the specified extra cost to include it in the target? |No. Effects that affect "every opposing Spirit" do not actually "target" a Spirit, and {{tk|Camouflage}} would not activate. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Camouflage|List of cards with Camouflage]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Legacy.fullContent:
[[File:26RSD04-X01-Legacy.png|thumb|250px]] == Introduction == '''Legacy''' (''{{ruby|継|けい}}{{ruby|召|しょう}}; Kei-shou'') is a major gimmick introduced together with the Standard Format, and first premiered in the six Entry Decks 26RSD01-06. As the name implies, it is an effect that "inherits" the power of cards used before in the form of providing reduction for new cards. The actual effect reads: {{ST|Legacy}} In simple terms, when paying the cost for cards with Legacy, you can '''banish cards with EX Symbols in the Trash from game to fulfill the reduction symbols of the card''', as if those EX Symbols are on your Field. Legacy exists not only on Spirits, but also on Magic cards, and potentially Nexuses. Hence, it isn't only a gimmick corresponding to summon, but also "deploy" and "use". == EX Symbols == [[File:All EX symbols.png|300px]] Before understanding how Legacy actually works, one must know what an "EX Symbol" is. '''EX Symbols (EXシンボル)''' is another important concept introduced together with Standard Format. Each color has their corresponding EX Symbols, which are essentially the color symbols with a special golden frame. While they are no different from normal color symbols on Field, they serve as the base for Legacy in Trash. Due to that special use, they are printed not only on Spirits, but also on Magic cards and potentially Nexus cards. [[File:26RSD01-002.png|250px]][[File:26RSD04-013.png|250px]] == Application == Take [[The FlyingIron Akurai]] as an example. [[File:Akurai Legacy.png|300px]] Akurai is a Cost 7 card, with four Red reduction symbols. Assuming that you have two Red symbols on your Field. Under normal circumstances, you need to pay 7-2 = 5 cost to summon Akurai. However, by using Legacy, you can banish '''two cards with Red EX Symbols''' in your Trash. When you do, two out of four of Akurai's Red reduction symbols are fulfilled before you calculate the Field symbols. And after calculating the field symbols, the actual cost you have to pay becomes:
'''7 - 2 (from Legacy) - 2 (from Red symbols on Field) = 3. ''' == Notes == When using Legacy:

1) You use it '''before''' counting the reduction symbols on the Field

2) You '''can't''' banish a number of cards with EX Symbols from Trash that exceeds the max number of reduction symbols on the card to be used/summoned/deployed (e.g. If a card has four Red reduction symbols, you can't banish five cards with Red EX Symbols from the Trash)

3) You can only banish EX Symbols that share the '''same color''' as the reduction symbols of the card to be used/summoned/deployed == Merits & Demerits == The existence of Legacy allows disadvantaged players to comeback and build up their board at a reasonable cost even with an empty board as long as there are cards with EX symbols in Trash. It is particularly important in the game where core is a limited resources and affects every move of play afterwards. On the other hand, since you can't take back cards you banished, it is suggested to think carefully what to banish, and the amount of times you do so. This applies particularly to cases where, the deck itself revolves around trash manipulation. And by banishing cards from Trash, it contradicts with cards that return cards from Trash to the Hand, or deploy cards from Trash. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31541 |What kind of effect is Legacy? |It is a an effect that allows you to banish cards with EX Symbols in your Trash from game, and for each EX Symbol banished, you can fulfill one of the reduction symbols of the same color of the card to be summoned/deployed/used. Legacy can be activated even if there are other effects that treat reduction symbols as fulfilled or when all reduction symbols are fulfilled just by counting the symbols on Field. In such cases, Legacy activates before those effects/calculation of Field symbols. |- |31542 |When activating Legacy, can I banish EX Symbols with a color different from the reduction symbols' color? And can I banish more cards with EX Symbols than it takes to fulfill the reduction symbols? |You can't. |- |31543 |When activating Legacy, is it treated as being activated even if I banish no cards with EX Symbols from the Trash? |No. Legacy is not considered being activated unless you banish at least one card with EX Symbol from the Trash. |- |31620 |When using an effect that summons/uses a card with {{tk|Legacy}} without paying the cost, can I still activate that card's {{tk|Legacy}}? |No, you can't. When you're summoning/using a card with {{tk|Legacy}} via an effect that states a fixed cost, like "summon/use without paying the cost", or "by paying one cost", you can't activate {{tk|Legacy}} and banish cards with EX Symbols from your Trash. |- |31866 |Are Spirits with only {{Tk|Legacy}} treated as Spirits with no printed effects? |No, they aren't treated as Spirits with no printed effects. |} == Navigation == {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Soul Magic.fullContent:
[[File:26RSD01-014.png|thumb|200px]]

'''Soul Magic''' (ソウルマジック) is a special effect introduced together with the Standard Format, and serves as a major gimmick of the new battle format. While the actual release happened only until the six Entry Decks, 26RSD01-06, were released, cards with such effects were first teased as CP cards in [[BS75]], the last booster before the separation of formats.

As the name implies, it is an effect exclusive to '''Magic cards'''. The general form of the effect reads as follows: 

{{Soul Magic}}


In short, it is an effect that let you use the Magic card by paying the cost with just one [[File:Stan Soul Core.png|20px]] (Soul Core), as long as you have at least one symbol of the corresponding color on your Field. In the case of [[Flame Hurricane]], as long as you have any Red symbols on your Field, you can use the Magic card that originally costs 6 with just one [[File:Stan Soul Core.png|20px]].

It increased the possibilities for counter attack with minimal cores and resources by allowing players to use Magic cards with heavy costs with just the Soul Core. On the other hand, it means that the way a player places the Soul Core becomes even more important, and the attacking side must be aware of the possibilities of a sudden comeback.

Shamanism.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS01-030.png|thumb|200px]] '''Shamanism''' (操霊; ''sou-rei'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first booster set of Standard Format. It is the core effect of the [[Purple]] deck type newly introduced in the same set, and demonstrated [[Purple]]'s signature trait of reusing cards from the Trash. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * {{Shaman|XXX & Cost Y or less}} [Timing]
You can target a Cost Y or less "XXX" family Spirit card in your Trash. Summon it. An actual example will be [[The DancingFox Charles de Peta]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{Shaman|[[Dark Puce]] & Cost 7 or less}} {{ST|When Summoned}}
You can target a Cost 7 or less "[[Dark Puce]]" family Spirit card in your Trash. Summon it. In short, it is an effect that let you re-summon cards with the target family and cost from the Trash. And as there is no mention of "without paying the cost" in the effect, you are required to pay the cost to summon the card. While trash-summoning has always been a part of Purple's nature, it is actually rare where it is made into a keyword effect. As an early mechanic in Standard where re-summoning something which entered Trash and an extra body alone mean a lot, the effect requires the player to pay for the summon cost instead of summoning it without paying the cost. Despite such balancing measure, it doesn't prevent the player from activating any {{ST|When Summoned}} effect of the summoned card like some early Purple trash-summoning cards did in Eternal back then. As a keyword, it also means it comes with various direct supports from effects targeting the keyword itself, like [[The InsectLord Shi-Reizen]], or cards summoned via the effect, like [[The Penetrating Mountain Range]]. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31585 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Shamanism}}? |{{Shaman|XXX}} is an effect that allows you to summon a Spirit card of the designated cost and family as specified in XXX from the Trash. When you do, you pay the cost from Field/Reserve like what you do for normal summons. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Shamanism|List of cards with Shamanism]] * [[:Category:Shamanism support|List of cards that supports Shamanism]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

At the end of battle, discard X cards from the opposing decktop. For each cost of the Spir
Rumble.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS01-084.png|thumb|200px]] '''Rumble''' (地鳴; ''ji-nari'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first booster set of Standard Format. It is the core effect of the [[Blue]] deck type newly introduced in the same set, and demonstrated [[Blue]]'s signature trait of discarding cards from opposing deck. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * {{Rumble|X}} {{tk|During Attack}}
At the end of battle, discard X cards from the opposing decktop. For each cost of the Spirit card that blocked in the opposing Trash, it discards -1 card. An actual example will be [[Ganasha]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV2]''' {{Rumble|5}} {{tk|During Attack}}
At the end of battle, discard five cards from the opposing decktop. For each cost of the Spirit card that blocked in the opposing Trash, it discards -1 card. In short, it is an effect that let you discard the specified number of cards from the opposing decktop at the end of battle. Since the effect only works at the end of battle, the holder must survive until the end of battle, meaning that if it is removed from the Field due to opposing effects, or lost the BP comparison and destroyed by the opposing blocker, the effect doesn't work. On top of that, if the Spirit with {{tk|Rumble}} is blocked, even if it destroyed the opposing blocker, for each cost of that blocker which is now in Trash when this effect resolves, the amount you are originally discarding via {{tk|Rumble}} will get reduced by 1. For example, if you attack with [[Ganasha]] at LV2, who has {{Rumble|5}}, and you are blocked by opponent's LV1 [[Mushakko]]. By comparing BP, [[Mushakko]] is destroyed and enters the opposing Trash. Then at the end of [[Ganasha]]'s battle, you discard:
'''5 (the number specified by Rumble) - 3 (Cost of [[Mushakko]] in Trash) = 2 cards''' from the opposing decktop. While the effect does come with quite a lot of restrictions (time lag due to being activated at the end of battle, requires the attacker to survive, discards fewer cards if it is blocked, etc.), it isn't necessarily a weaker effect when compared to {{tk|Crush}}, the well-known deck-discarding effect in [[Blue]] in Eternal. For one, the specified number of {{tk|Rumble}} isn't capped at 3 like {{tk|Crush}} (as most Spirits only has LV3 at max), but is proportional to the cost of the {{tk|Rumble}} holder, which reaches {{Rumble|7}} in the first set. Even without effects that increase the number of cards to be discarded, the basic number is in general higher than {{tk|Crush}}. Another key benefit is the core requirement. As {{tk|Crush}}, or even {{tk|Great Crush}}, requires the Spirits to be at a high LV for more effective mill, keeping multiple Spirits at high level is needed to make them effective. In that regard, most {{tk|Rumble}} starts at LV1, and is at full power regardless of the LV the card is in. This makes it much easier to spread the board with {{tk|Rumble}} Spirits for milling. This typically means, without other cards, a cost 3 {{tk|Rumble}} Spirit is milling 3 cards when it has one core on it while a Cost 3 Spirit with {{tk|Crush}} is only milling 1, not to mention cards with higher Rumble numbers. Despite so, as {{tk|Rumble}} requires the Spirit to stay till the end of battle, the player can't declare an attack and self-deplete the attacker in Flash to prevent themselves from hitting opposing Life if the opponent is not blocking. Hence, from the perspective of using milling as the main win-con, while {{tk|Rumble}} is more "economical" when compared to usual milling effects, it is harder to resort to not reducing the opposing life, and has less the combo potential. On the other hand, one can also take {{tk|Rumble}} as an effect that forces opponent to think whether they are blocking or not, as the sudden mill can be critical if it sends their key cards to Trash, which is an indirect version of {{tk|Clash}} and removal in a sense. Another factor that comes in play in Standard for milling effects like {{tk|Rumble}} is EX symbol. While sending opposing key cards to Trash is a plus factor, especially when retrieval is not that common or effective as it is in Eternal, the existence of EX Symbol means milling cards with EX Symbols from opposing deck might be helping them to build up EX Symbols in their Trash, accelerating their summon/use of high cost cards with [[Legacy]]. As a compensation, there are cards supporting {{tk|Rumble}} that turn milling cards with EX Symbols into resources like draw or core boost. The name of the effect most probably originates from the image of rumbling earth, where a deck of cards on top would just fall apart, leaving the cards scattered on the floor. It links nicely with [[Blue]]'s new image in Standard as a color that associates with the earth and land. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31592 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Rumble}}? |At the end of battle, discard X cards from the opposing decktop, where X is the number specified in {{Rumble|X}}. If the opposing Spirit that blocked was depleted or destroyed in that battle, and entered the Trash, for each cost of such card, {{tk|Rumble}} discards 1 card fewer. If the cost is equal or higher than X, you discard no cards from the opposing decktop. |- |31593 |When your attacking Spirit with {{tk|Rumble}} is destroyed by BP comparison, or has left the Field due to opposing effects, can I activate {{tk|Rumble}} at the end of that battle? |No, you can't. |- |31594 |If an opposing Spirit that blocked your Spirit with {{tk|Rumble}} is returned to the Hand/Deck via an effect and left the Field, or sent to the Trash after being destroyed but returned to the opposing Hand from Trash via an effect, what would happen? |As long as the opposing Spirit that blocked doesn't exist in the opposing Trash at the end of battle, the number of cards to be discarded by {{tk|Rumble}} won't be reduced. |- |31621 |Under Eternal Format, if your Spirit with {{tk|Rumble}} was blocked by an opposing Ultimate or Spirit-condition Brave, and those cards are sent to the Trash, would the number of cards discarded via {{tk|Rumble}} be reduced? |No, the number of cards to be discarded by {{tk|Rumble}} won't be reduced, as {{tk|Rumble}} doesn't reference Ultimate cards, or Brave cards in Trash. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Rumble|List of cards with Rumble]] * [[:Category:Rumble support|List of cards that supports Rumble]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Current.title: Current
Current.contentSample: [[File:26RBS01-035.png|thumb|200px]] '''Current''' (水流; ''sui-ryu'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first booster set of Standard Format. It is the core effect of the [[Green]] deck type newly introduced in the same set, and demonstrated a different side of [[Green]], the control & OTK side, when compared to the aggro style introduced in [[26RSD03]]. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * {{Current|[Family X] & Cost Y}} {{ST|Your Attack Step}} {{Invoke|Flash}}
Current.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS01-035.png|thumb|200px]] '''Current''' (水流; ''sui-ryu'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first booster set of Standard Format. It is the core effect of the [[Green]] deck type newly introduced in the same set, and demonstrated a different side of [[Green]], the control & OTK side, when compared to the aggro style introduced in [[26RSD03]]. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * {{Current|[Family X] & Cost Y}} {{ST|Your Attack Step}} {{Invoke|Flash}}
'''Exhaust this Spirit ▶''' Target one of your Cost Y (or more) "X" family Spirits. During this battle, it gains an extra Green symbol. An actual example will be [[Alotoll]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV2]'''{{ST|True Release}} {{Current|[[Oceanic Green]] & Cost 8 or more}} {{ST|Your Attack Step}} {{Invoke|Flash}}
'''Exhaust this Spirit ▶''' Target one of your Cost 8 or more "[[Oceanic Green]]" family Spirits. During this battle, it gains an extra Green symbol. In short, it is an effect that centralizes your symbols by allowing you to exhaust your own Spirit with {{tk|Current}} during Flash Timing and add a symbol to the target Spirit. In the process, the total amount of potential life to be reduced actually doesn't change, as one is exhausting their next attacker which can deal one life on their own to add the amount of life the current attacker can deal to the opponent. One may then raise the question of "why doing this". And the answer comes in multiple aspects. First, by dealing more life in a single attack instead of making a different attack, it reduces the risk of the attacker being removed in the second attack during Flash Timing as the opponent has one extra core in the second attack. It also means that the opponent is forced to react if their life is at two to prevent a direct lethal. In the Standard Format where "if your Life was reduced this turn" is a major triggering condition for additional effects for a lot of cards (e.g. [[Flame Hurricane]]), by combining two attack into one and dealing two lives at once helped prevent unwanted counterplays from the opponent. Another point worth to note is, {{tk|Current}} as an effect doesn't come with conditions like {{ST|Once Per Turn}}. This means, you can activate {{tk|Current}} a multiple amount of times in the same turn, adding 3-4 symbols to the attacker. Without the need to reduce life at multiple instants through cheap attacks but instead through a single high-symbol attack at the end means the {{tk|Current}} side player doesn't have to give extra resources to the opponent in early-mid game. On top of that, as {{tk|Current}} doesn't require permeant removal of own Spirits as a price to add the symbol, but only "exhausting", it means when combined with "Spirit-refreshing" effects, one can add multiple symbols in one attack even if they don't control multiple Spirits with {{tk|Current}}. For example, with [[The DeepBlow Whala]], you can easily add 2 symbols to Whala by using its LV2 effect and it only requires one extra Spirit with {{tk|Current}} on Field. Another obvious point would also be that, by adding symbol to a bigger attacker with supposedly higher BP, it means the Spirits with {{tk|Current}}, which in general have lower BP, wouldn't need to break through the opponent's high BP Spirit in their attacks. Despite its merits mentioned above, {{tk|Current}} is ultimately a supporting effect, which has the limitation that Spirits with the keyword don't do anything alone. While it works together with effects that support the {{tk|Current}} effect holders, unlike effects like {{tk|Rumble}} or {{tk|Clash}}, when a Spirit with {{tk|Current}} is summoned to the Field on its own, it is more or less a Spirit with no effects apart from being the supporting target of cards like [[The Current Corridor]]. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31586 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Current}}? |By exhausting a Spirit with this effect, target a Spirit with the family X and cost Y specified in {{Current|X & Y}}, and during this battle, that targeted Spirit gains an extra Green symbol. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Current|List of cards with Current]] * [[:Category:Current support|List of cards that supports Current]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The general form of its wording reads as follows: 

* {{Amplify|[Family X] +1000}} {{ST|During Attack/Block}}{{Invoke|Flash}}{{S
Amplify.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS01-X11.png|thumb|200px]] '''Amplify''' (増幅; ''zou-fuku'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first booster set of Standard Format. It is the core effect of the [[White]] deck type newly introduced in the same set, and demonstrated a different side of Standard's [[White]], which specializes in winning BP battles instead of direct effect removals. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * {{Amplify|[Family X] +1000}} {{ST|During Attack/Block}}{{Invoke|Flash}}{{ST|Once Per Battle}}
'''Pay one cost''' ▶For each "X" family Spirit you control, during this battle, this Spirit gains +1000 BP. An actual example will be [[The ArgentIronDuke Lars-Beriberg]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{Amplify|Leucomyst +1000}} {{ST|During Attack/Block}}{{Invoke|Flash}}{{ST|Once Per Battle}}
'''Pay one cost''' ▶For each "[[Leucomyst]]" family Spirit you control, during this battle, this Spirit gains +1000 BP. While the effect comes with a lot of tags and is quite lengthy, the actual effect, in short, allows the holder to gain BP proportional to the number of Spirits with the target family on the Field by paying one cost. It takes place during Flash Timing for both attack and block, and is limited to once per battle. As the name implies, it is an effect that "amplifies" your BP, and the more "reactor" you got, the great the power amplifies. From an Eternal viewpoint, making BP increase effect into a keyword seems rather unnecessary. However, in Standard where the BP line is ultra important in battles or effect removals, the impact of such BP increase by {{tk|Amplify}} is much greater than what it let on. With the nature of {{tk|Amplify}}, the more Spirits you control with the same family, the stronger the BP buff is going to be. This means the effect shall work best in a family-dedicated deck, and would become stronger as the match proceeds if the opponent fails to remove the Spirits of the same family from the Field. Most importantly, as it is a {{ST|During Attack/Block}} effect, the longer the opponent spent in removal, the higher the wall it is going to be for them to overcome, making it a board that is almost invincible in BP battles. As the holder of {{tk|Amplify}} is often in the same family as what specified by {{Amplify|X}, one can assume the Spirits with such effect always own a "by paying one cost, gain +1000 BP" effect even when it is the only Spirit on the Field; which could affect a lot of calculations. This makes the deck revolving around such effect being particularly strong against decks that revolve around BP battles (e.g. {{tk|Clash}}) or medium size attackers. On the other hand, as {{tk|Amplify}} is a "Flash" effect, it can't prevent direct BP destruction effects, or those that brought their BP to 0 immediately before Flash. As it only lasts during the same battle, even if one tries to add its BP in first flash to prevent following up removals, it would only save that Spirit in its battle, but not the removals that come in during the next attack. As far as the price for such effect concerned, the one cost requirement means the owner of the {{tk|Amplify}} Spirits has to pay special attention regarding how much they spend during Main Step, and check with the other defense in their Hand, like Magic cards, to come up with the best timing of using {{tk|Amplify}}. Regardless of the restrictions, {{tk|Amplify}} is an effect unique to the Standard Format which brings BP battle back to the main deal. To maximize the power of {{tk|Amplify}}, a lot of {{tk|Amplify}} Spirits or their support come with refreshing effects to allow the players to block at ease, and effects that synergize with the increased BP like "when BP becomes X or more, do Y". == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31587 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Amplify}}? |An effect that increases the BP of a Spirit proportional to the number of Spirits in the "X" family as specified in {{Amplify|X}} if you pay one cost. |- |31588 |When I activate the {{tk|Amplify}} of a LV2 Spirit, and that Spirit is brought down to LV1 after paying one cost from it, would its {{tk|Amplify}} fail to activate? |No, as its BP will be increased at the same time when the cost is paid. |- |31589 |Assume that I control three Spirits of the family X specified in {{Amplify|X}}, and gained 3000 BP via {{Amplify|X}}. Afterwards, if one of such Spirit left the Field, and only two Spirit with family X remain on the Field, would the BP increased via {{Amplify|X}} be reduced? |No, the increased BP won't get reduced. The effect only references the number of Spirit when the effect resolves. After the effect has resolved, even if the number of Spirits in the specified family increase or decrease, it won't affect the amount of BP gain via the effect. |- |31590 |Assume that a LV2 5000 BP Spirit activated {{tk|Amplify}} by paying one cost from it, and there are two Spirits of the specified family, so it is gaining 2000 BP. Since it activates the effect on LV2, the effect will bring it to 7000 BP. However, at the same time, it is brought down to LV1 after paying the one cost, and its LV1 BP is 3000. Ultimately, its BP becomes 3000 + 2000 = 5000. In that case, can derivative effects like "when it becomes 6000 BP or more" activate? |No, those effects can't activate. For effects like "when it becomes 6000 BP or more", where BP has to reach a certain level, the Spirit must be of such BP when the effect actually resolves. |- |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Amplify|List of cards with Amplify]] * [[:Category:Amplify support|List of cards that supports Amplify]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

You can use the Flash effect of
Magirrate.fullContent:
[[File:26RBS01-X15.png|thumb|200px]] '''Magirrate''' (魔述; ''ma-jtsu'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first booster set of Standard Format. It is the core effect of the [[Yellow]] deck type newly introduced in the same set, and demonstrated [[Yellow]]'s signature trait of using various Magic cards to battle. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * {{Magirrate|[Family X]}} {{ST|During Attack}} {{Invoke|Flash}} {{ST|Once Per Battle}}
You can use the Flash effect of a "X" family Magic card from your Hand, without paying the cost. An actual example will be [[The ReturningThunder Embalmimer]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{Magirrate|Topaz}} {{ST|During Attack}} {{Invoke|Flash}} {{ST|Once Per Battle}}
You can use the Flash effect of a "[[Topaz]]" family Magic card from your Hand, without paying the cost. The Japanese name is a combination of "魔", which can refer to anything related to demon/devil, but also "magic", and "述", which refers to "narrate", "speak", and "recount". According to the effect and the context here, it is most probably a play of word, as "魔述" sounds exactly the same as "魔術" (Magic) in Japanese, making the effect name pointing towards a "casting magic" direction. Hence, the English translation incorporated both the literal and inside meaning of the name. As straightforward as the wording goes, the effect allows you to use the Flash effect of a Magic card of the specified family, without paying the cost, during the Flash Timing in its attack, and is limited to once per '''battle'''. Note that "by using Flash effect of a Magic card", you are essentially "using that Magic card", and the used Magic card will enter Trash normally after its effect resolves like how you normally use a Magic card. It is easier to think of it just as an effect that turns the "pay cost and use Magic" action into "pay no cost and use one Magic" scenario. As far as "using it without paying the cost" is concerned, it means that the higher the original cost of the Magic card is, the more cores you actually save when using it via {{tk|Magirrate}}. It is hence particularly recommended to pair it with high cost magics like [[Thunder Shutter]]. It is particularly worthy to note that with the introduction of {{tk|Soul Magic}}, the amount of high cost Magic cards actually increased, making them a good combination with {{tk|Magirrate}} as well as long as the family matches. While {{tk|Magirrate}} as an effect conjures various potential, as it doesn't change the timing of using Magic cards to the point of attack declaration, but staying in Flash Timing instead, it doesn't solve the issue if the opponent removes the Spirit with {{tk|Magirrate}} on their Flash Timing (as defense side has the first Flash Timing). The family restriction of the effect also prevents the effect from using powerful Magic cards from other colors or families, limiting the combo potential. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31591 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Magirrate}}? |It's an effect that allows you to use the Flash effect of a Magic card with the family X specified in {{Magirrate|X}}. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Magirrate|List of cards with Magirrate]] * [[:Category:Magirrate support|List of cards that supports Magirrate]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

MD Armor.fullContent:
[[File:BSCO-010.png|thumb|250x250px]] '''MD Armor''' ({{Ruby|MD|エムディー}}{{ruby|装|そう}}{{ruby|甲|こう}}, ''emudi-sōkō)'' is a keyword introduced in the game, [[Battle Spirits CrossOver]]. It is a CrossOver-only keyword for part of the Collaboration replacement cards (BSCO cards) in the game, and is never an actual keyword in the physical game. It is possessed exclusively by [[Argenic-One]] and [[Argenic-One Diffusion Rain]], the replacements card for [[Freedom Gundam]] and [[Freedom Gundam［HiMAT Full Burst］]], the owner of {{tk|PS Armor}} in the physical game. The keyword itself is hence also acting as a replacement for {{tk|PS Armor}}, as {{tk|PS Armor}} was a concept/term in the Mobile Suit Gundam: SEED universe. The name, MD Armor, comes from the family name of [[Argenic-One]] and [[Argenic-One Diffusion Rain]], [[MD]], which is short for '''Machine Deus'''. However, it is to note that "MD Armor" doesn't pronounce as "Machine Deus Armor", but "Emu-Di-Armor" even in Japanese. Since it is exactly the same as PS Armor, it is worded as: * {{MDa|Cost X or less}}
This Spirit is unaffected by opposing Cost X or less effects. == Also See == [[:Category:MD Armor|List of cards with MD Armor]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

The general form of its wording reads as follows: * '''[LVX]''' {{F Change|[Name] & [Cost Y]}} {{Invoke|Main}}
Return this exhausted Spirit to the Hand, and you must summon a Cost Y "[Name]" with a different name from your Hand, without paying the cost. You can only use thi
Form Change.fullContent:
[[File:26RSD07-005.png|thumb|200px]] '''Form Change''' ({{ruby|F|フォーム}}チェンジ; ''formu-chanji'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RSD07]] and [[26RBS01]], the first collaboration starter & booster set of Standard Format. The general form of its wording reads as follows: * '''[LVX]''' {{F Change|[Name] & [Cost Y]}} {{Invoke|Main}}
Return this exhausted Spirit to the Hand, and you must summon a Cost Y "[Name]" with a different name from your Hand, without paying the cost. You can only use this effect of the same card name once per turn. An actual example will be [[Kamen Rider Zeztz Physicam Transform]], whose effect reads: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{F Change|"Zeztz" & Cost 3}} {{Invoke|Main}}
Return this exhausted Spirit to the Hand, and you must summon a Cost 3 "Zeztz" with a different name from your Hand, without paying the cost. You can only use this effect of the same card name once per turn. As the name implies, it is an effect resembling how the Kamen Riders change into their different forms in the show. While the effect is pretty self-explanatory, it basically allows you to summon a target Spirit card from the Hand without paying the cost by returning an exhausted Spirit with the {{tk|Form Change}} effect from your Field to the Hand. When the effect was first introduced, all the {{tk|Form Change}} effects worked as {{Invoke|Main}} effects, meaning that it could only be used during Main Step. Since the effect requires the Spirit to be exhausted, unless your Spirit was somehow exhausted by your own effects or an opposing effect, it generally refers to the case where the Spirit attacked, became exhausted, and you activate the effect during the '''2nd Main Step''', a unique feature in Standard Format. As it requires the player to gather both the card with {{tk|Form Change}} ''and'' its {{tk|Form Change}} target on top of having the card with {{tk|Form Change}} exhausted, the "cost" of the effect is actually pretty heavy, and the consistency is not particularly high either. It also did not help that the condition for {{tk|Form Change}} was quite strict when the keyword was introduced, as it was either those with the same cost on top of having the same name, or those with a higher cost albeit the number of target cards was still limited. (e.g. 1-2 types) The "you can only use this effect of the same card name once per turn" part also means that the effect can only be once even if you have multiple copies of the same card. Despite all these limitation, however, a no-cost summon effect in Standard environment is still a very powerful effect, especially how it means that one could turn an exhausted attacker to a refreshed blocker without paying extra cost to summon a new Spirit. It also comes with the merit of "recycling" the card with {{tk|Form Change}} for one to summon it next turn, and works best when those {{tk|Form Change}} owners come with a (When Summoned) effect, like [[Kamen Rider Para-DX Fighter Gamer Level 50 (26RCB01-049)|Kamen Rider Para-DX Fighter Gamer Level 50]]. For those {{tk|Form Change}} that targets a higher cost, it means that you are summoning the high cost Spirits at an earlier stage as well. From an Eternal perspective, {{tk|Form Change}} is essentially an adjusted version of {{tk|Change}}, an effect introduced also with the first Kamen Rider collaboration set back then. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31730 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Form Change}}? |It is an effect that allows you to return the exhausted Spirit with {{tk|Form Change}} you control to the Hand, and summon a card from the Hand with a name different from the {{tk|Form Change}} holder's (which meets the specified condition) without paying the cost. If you cannot summon a target card, you also cannot return the {{tk|Form Change}} holder to the Hand. |- |31731 |If all the cores from the {{tk|Form Change}} holder is put onto the Spirit summoned via {{tk|Form Change}}, would the {{tk|Form Change}} holder be depleted and sent to the Trash? |It would be depleted, but since it is still under the effect of the hand-returning effect, it would return to the Hand instead. |- |31732 |Is {{tk|Form Change}} treated as {{tk|Change}}? |No, it is not. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Form Change|List of cards with Form Change]] * [[:Category:Form Change support|List of cards that supports Form Change]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]

Level Up.fullContent:
[[File:26RCB01-039.png|thumb|200px]] '''Level Up''' (レベルアップ; ''reberu-apu'') is a keyword introduced in [[26RBS01]], the first collaboration booster set of the Standard Format, and is exclusive to the [[EX-AID]] family cards. Its wording reads as follows: * '''[LV1-2]''' {{tk|Level Up}} {{ST|When Attacks/Blocks}}
If this is the first attack/block of the turn, during this battle, this Spirit is treated as LV2. As the name implies, it is an effect that allows the owner of the effect to "Level Up" and become LV2. The effect is themed/named after the same gimmick equipped in the rider system in the Kamen Rider Ex-Aid franchise, where the rider, who transformed using different rider gashats, can "Level Up" and change into a different form. (e.g. from level 1 to level 2) While being a very straightforward effect, it got two main uses in the game: (1) obtain the LV2 BP for attack/block; and (2) unlock effects that are only active from LV2, while only having one core on the Spirit. For (1), in the Standard environment where BP is very important, the impact of the effect is actually stronger than what it reads, especially when the effect is printed on the low cost Spirits. While the effect is only locked to the first attack/block of the turn, it means the opponent has to calculate their attack/response on top of the sudden high BP against a Spirit with only one core on it. For (2), it allows the player to activate effects that usually come with a higher price with just one core on them (e.g. [[Kamen Rider Brave Fantasy Gamer Level 50 (26RCB01-047)|Kamen Rider Brave Fantasy Gamer Level 50]]'s LV2 effect). Many of the cards in the [[EX-AID]] family with the {{tk|Level Up}} effect are designed in the way that while their effects are powerful and often superior to their cost-performance, have the downside of requiring quite many cores for LV2. Yet, with {{tk|Level Up}}, it won't be an issue. In essence, while limited to attack/block, it works a lot like the main gimmick of Standard, {{ST|True Release}}. But instead of Soul Core, it requires the Spirit to be the first one to attack/block in the turn. In a way different to "where I have to put my Soul Core", the effect is a simple but effective one that make the user think carefully the order of attack before making one, and matches a lot with the theme of "gamer" riders of Ex-Aid. == Official Q&A == {| class="fandom-table" |+ !'''No.''' !'''Question''' !'''Answer''' |- |31733 |What kind of effect is {{tk|Level Up}}? |It is an effect which allows the holder of such effect be treated as LV2 during the battle if it is the one that makes the first attack/block of the turn among your Spirits. |- |31734 |During the opposing Attack Step, if I chose not to block the first opposing attack, and chose to block the second attack with a Spirit with {{tk|Level Up}}, can I activate {{tk|Level Up}}? |Yes, you can. |} == Related Articles == * [[:Category:Level Up|List of cards with Level Up]] * [[:Category:Level Up support|List of cards that supports Level Up]] {{Keywords Nav}} [[Category:Keywords]]
